origins.en: Gerard de Lairesse (1641-1711), painter of allegories and of wall and ceiling paintings. He came to Amsterdam from Liège in 1667. His 'Groot schilderboek' (great book of painting) appeared in 1707.

origins.name: De Leeuw van Vlaanderenstraat
origins.en: After the novel of the same name (the Lion of Flanders) by the Flemish writer Hendrik Conscience (1838).

origins.name: De Leggende Osstraat
origins.en: A historical stolp farmhouse on the Kadoelenweg, rebuilt in 1983. 'Leggen' is colloquial here for liggen (to lie): the lying ox.

origins.name: De Lierhof
origins.en: Together with the villages of 's-Gravenzande, Heenweg, Honselersdijk, Kwintsheul, Maasdijk, Monster, Naaldwijk, Ter Heijde and Wateringen, De Lier is part of the municipality of Westland in Zuid-Holland, formed on 1 January 2004.

origins.name: De loper
origins.en: A loper (runner): a long narrow carpet laid out to welcome someone. The street leads to the nearby Amsterdam ArenA.

origins.name: De Mirandalaan
origins.en: Salomon (Monne) Rodrigues de Miranda (1875-1942), for 28 years a city councillor for the SDAP, sixteen of them as an alderman of Amsterdam, among other things for public housing. Murdered by the occupiers in a punishment camp.

origins.name: De passage
origins.en: The street (the entrance) leads to the nearby Amsterdam ArenA.

origins.name: De Peerelstraat
origins.en: A former farmstead in the Watergraafsmeer. It lay next to Zorgwijk on the Oosterringdijk.

origins.name: De Rijpgracht
origins.en: Jan Cornelisz de Rijp (1570-1630), navigator, who sailed at the same time as Heemskerk and Barentsz in search of a northern passage, but did not winter on Nova Zembla because he took a route around Spitsbergen. When the street was laid out, the council of the former municipality of Sloten named it Willem Barentsstraat (council decision of Sloten, 8 March 1910).

origins.name: De Rijpstraat
origins.en: Jan Cornelisz de Rijp (1570-1630), navigator, who sailed at the same time as Heemskerk and Barentsz in search of a northern passage, but did not winter on Nova Zembla because he took a route around Spitsbergen. When the street was laid out, the council of the former municipality of Sloten named it Willem Barentsstraat (council decision of Sloten, 8 March 1910).

origins.name: De Roos van Dekamaweg
origins.en: A historical novel by Jacob van Lennep from 1836, set in the fourteenth century.

origins.name: De Ruijterkade
origins.en: Michiel Adriaansz. de Ruyter (1607-1676), the renowned admiral of Holland and West Friesland. He was born in Vlissingen. In Amsterdam he lived on what is now the Prins Hendrikkade.

origins.name: De Savornin Lohmanstraat
origins.en: Alexander F. de Savornin Lohman (1837-1924), lawyer and statesman, at first Anti-Revolutionary and, after a conflict with Abraham Kuyper, Christian-Historical. Professor at the Vrije Universiteit and Minister of the Interior from 1890 to 1895.

origins.name: De Schaapherderstraat
origins.en: A historical novel from 1838 by J.F. Oltmans (the shepherd), about the Utrecht War of 1481-1483.

origins.name: De Schorrenstraat
origins.en: A nature reserve on the east side of Texel, where birds such as the spoonbill, eider and oystercatcher breed. Schorren are silted-up, vegetated stretches of land outside the dikes that no longer flood at ordinary high tide (salt marshes).

origins.name: De Sitterstraat
origins.en: Willem de Sitter (1872-1934), astronomer. Professor at Leiden and director of the Leiden Observatory. He wrote a study of the expanding universe.

origins.name: De Tourton Bruynsstraat
origins.en: Titus Willem de Tourton Bruyns (1898-1943), resistance fighter, born in Teteringen, died in the German concentration camp Buchenwald.

origins.name: De Wieden
origins.en: The Beulaker Wiede and the Belter Wiede, the lake district in north-west Overijssel between Giethoorn and Vollenhove.

origins.name: De Wittenkade
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis de Witt (1623-1672), burgomaster of Dordrecht, and Johan de Witt (1625-1672), Grand Pensionary of Holland, both murdered by the mob in The Hague on a false accusation. One side of the quay was first called Maljapenkade.

origins.name: De Wittenstraat
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis de Witt (1623-1672), burgomaster of Dordrecht, and Johan de Witt (1625-1672), Grand Pensionary of Holland, both murdered by the mob in The Hague on a false accusation. One side of the quay was first called Maljapenkade.

origins.name: De-Grote-Geusplein
origins.en: The nickname (the great Beggar) of Count Hendrik van Brederode (1531-1568), leader of the procession of the Nobles in 1566 and one of the first leaders in the Eighty Years' War against Spain.

origins.name: Deccaweg
origins.en: The Decca system is a navigation aid used in shipping and aviation. It is based on measuring the difference in arrival time of radio signals sent out simultaneously by two stations.

origins.name: Dekschuitstraat
origins.en: A flat-bottomed vessel with cargo space only on deck (a deck barge).

origins.name: Del Court van Krimpenstraat
origins.en: Golfer (1889-1944), the founder of golf in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Delflandlaan
origins.en: A water board (hoogheemraadschap) in Zuid-Holland, bordering Rijnland and Schieland.

origins.name: Delflandplein
origins.en: A water board (hoogheemraadschap) in Zuid-Holland, bordering Rijnland and Schieland.

origins.name: Delistraat
origins.en: A region on the east coast of Sumatra (Indonesia), long known for growing tobacco. Its capital is Medan.

origins.name: Deltastraat
origins.en: A delta is the land at the mouth of a river where it flows into the sea in two or more arms. The word comes from the Greek letter delta, which has the shape of a triangle.

origins.name: Demerarastraat
origins.en: A river in South America, along which the Dutch colony of the same name arose early in the seventeenth century. In 1814 the area passed to the United Kingdom, and in 1831 it became part of British Guiana.

origins.name: Demerhof
origins.en: A river in Belgium.

origins.name: Den Brielstraat
origins.en: In 1572 Den Briel was the first city the Beggars (geuzen) took from the Spanish.

origins.name: Den Burgstraat
origins.en: The main town of the Wadden island of Texel.

origins.name: Den Helderstraat
origins.en: The town on the northern tip of Noord-Holland.

origins.name: Den Texstraat
origins.en: Jonkheer Cornelis Jacob Arnold den Tex (1824-1882), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1868 to 1879.

origins.name: Denderhof
origins.en: A river in Belgium.

origins.name: Dennenhof
origins.en: A conifer (the pine). The native Scots pine is by far the most common species in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Dennenrodepad
origins.en: A farm near Grubbenvorst (Limburg). Rode is an old word for clearing woodland; compare the verb rooien (to grub up), still in use.

origins.name: Derde Egelantiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Derde Goudsbloemdwarsstraat
origins.en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

origins.name: Derde Helmersstraat
origins.en: Jan Frederik Helmers (1767-1813), Amsterdam broker who devoted himself to letters. His works include 'De Hollandsche Natie' (1813). The second part of the Eerste Helmersstraat lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 and was then called Hofdijkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 9 May 1890). The start of this street was originally a short side street of the Nassaukade called Sophiapark.

origins.name: Derde Hugo de Grootstraat
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

origins.name: Derde Kostverlorenkade
origins.en: After the Kostverlorenwetering, dug in 1413 to give a shorter waterway to the Haarlem and Leiden lakes. According to some, the name Kostverloren (cost lost) comes from the heavy legal costs of this channel, which was a bone of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609. The name Kostverloren occurs in several places in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Derde Leliedwarsstraat
origins.en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Derde Looiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

origins.name: Derde Marnixdwarsstraat
origins.en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568) and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Derde Oosterparkstraat
origins.en: Named after the nearby Oosterpark, and originally (council decision of 15 November 1882) named Eerste, Tweede and Derde Parkstraat. The Eerste Oosterparkstraat was earlier called Oetgenspad, after Frans Hendriks Oetgens, a sixteenth-century burgomaster over whose land several paths were laid. Until 1895 the street name applied as far as the Linnaeusstraat. In that year the stretch along the park was given the park's name.

origins.name: Derde Schinkelstraat
origins.en: A schinkel is a short connecting stretch between two weteringen (drainage channels), in this case the Nieuwe Meer and the Overtoom. It is thought the connection owes its name to its shape: 'schinkel' is a synonym of 'schenkel', the lower leg between foot and knee. The quay was earlier called Visserkade by Nieuwer-Amstel. The municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel had named the streets Visserstraat, Alexanderstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 20 October 1882) and Willemsparkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 30 January 1883), but in 1896 they were changed because of confusion with names that already existed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Derde Vogelstraat
origins.en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

origins.name: Derde Weteringdwarsstraat
origins.en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory.

origins.name: Derde Wittenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

origins.name: Derkinderenstraat
origins.en: Antonius Johannes Derkinderen (1859-1925), painter, known for his murals (the city hall in Den Bosch) and book decoration. Director of the Rijksakademie van Beeldende Kunsten (State Academy of Fine Arts).

origins.name: Des Présstraat
origins.en: Josquin des Prés or Després (1450-1521), French composer and choirmaster (masses and chansons).

origins.name: Descartespad
origins.en: René Descartes (1596-1650), also called Cartesius. French philosopher, natural scientist and mathematician, founder of modern philosophy. From 1629 to 1649 he lived on the Westermarkt (no. 6).

origins.name: Descartesstraat
origins.en: René Descartes (1596-1650), also called Cartesius. French philosopher, natural scientist and mathematician, founder of modern philosophy. From 1629 to 1649 he lived on the Westermarkt (no. 6).

origins.name: Desselstraat
origins.en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Deurloostraat
origins.en: One of the Zeeland sea inlets, at the mouth of the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Develstein
origins.en: The name of a manor house in Heerjansdam (Zuid-Holland).

origins.name: Dever
origins.en: A castle from about 1400 near Lisse (Zuid-Holland), of which the ruin of a massive semicircular tower remains. A manor house was built against it in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Deymanstraat
origins.en: Jan Deyman (1620-1666), professor of anatomy in Amsterdam. The street was earlier called Tweede Boerhaavestraat (council decision of 15 November 1882).

origins.name: Diaconessenbrug
origins.en: From 1884, for more than 100 years, a hospital stood very near this bridge: the LDI, the Lutherse Diaconessen Inrichting (Lutheran Deaconess Institution). The deaconesses, who were responsible for nursing the sick, mostly also lived in the building at Koninginneweg 1.

origins.name: Diamantstraat
origins.en: The hardest and most precious gemstone. Why this and other gemstones were used for names in the neighbourhood cannot be traced. It may be assumed that it was because of Asscher's diamond-cutting works, based in the Tolstraat since 1907. The street came over from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under the name Eerste De Ruyterdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 30 September 1890).

origins.name: Diatomastraat
origins.en: A microscopic water creature: one of the diatoms, a siliceous alga.

origins.name: Dichtershofje
origins.en: A reference to the overall theme of the street names in the neighbourhood (poets' courtyard). Many eighteenth- and nineteenth-century poets and writers in particular are commemorated in the immediate surroundings of this courtyard.

origins.name: Dick Greinerstraat
origins.en: Architect (1891-1964). His work includes the centre of Betondorp in Amsterdam's Watergraafsmeer, built in the 1920s. After the war he helped rebuild Middelburg and Ierseke.

origins.name: Dick Hilleniuspad
origins.en: Biologist, essayist and poet (1927-1987). All three sides can always be recognised in his wide-ranging work. He wrote about travel and art, among other things.

origins.name: Dickenslaan
origins.en: Charles John Huffam Dickens (1812-1870), English novelist. His work exposes social abuses, for example in 'Oliver Twist'. Author of the famous Christmas story 'A Christmas Carol'.

origins.name: Diderotstraat
origins.en: Denis Diderot (1713-1784), French philosopher who, with d'Alembert among others, compiled an encyclopaedia of 35 volumes from 1749.

origins.name: Diemerbospad
origins.en: The Diemerbospad is a cycle path between the Brasapark in Amsterdam Zuidoost and the Diemerbos in the municipality of Diemen.

origins.name: Diemerparklaan
origins.en: Named after the village of Diemen. The park is managed ecologically and links the nature areas on the south and north sides of the IJmeer.

origins.name: Diemerzeedijk
origins.en: This dike, only partly in Amsterdam, runs from Zeeburg past the village of Diemen to Muiderberg. It was built as early as the fourteenth century to hold back the water of the Zuiderzee. Before the Watergraafsmeer or Diemermeer was drained, the dike was Amsterdam's only link with Muiden and the area beyond.

origins.name: Diepen
origins.en: A corrupted spelling of the French port of Dieppe, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Diepenbeekplantsoen
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Diepenbrockstraat
origins.en: Alphonsus Joannes Maria Diepenbrock (1862-1921), a composer of international standing who wrote mainly church music.

origins.name: Dierenriem
origins.en: The zodiac: the belt of the sun and planets in the sky. In ancient times the zodiac was fixed as twelve signs (constellations) at equal distances.

origins.name: Diezestraat
origins.en: A river in Noord-Brabant formed where the Dommel and the Aa flow together.

origins.name: Digitaalstraat
origins.en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

origins.name: Dijkbraak
origins.en: Named after the wiel (a pool formed by a dike breach or left behind after a flood) inside the Oostzanerdijk, west of the Zuideinde towards Oostzaan. Braak is a Noord-Holland word for wiel.

origins.name: Dijkdwarsstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out as a dike at the end of the sixteenth century, after which the surroundings (long a marsh) were filled in with earth (aangeplempt).

origins.name: Dijkgraafplein
origins.en: A dijkgraaf (dike reeve) is the chairman of a dike board or water board.

origins.name: Dijkmanshuizenstraat
origins.en: A polder on the Wadden island of Texel, north of Oudeschild, now a nature reserve.

origins.name: Dijkmeerlaan
origins.en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and in the Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Dijkmeerstraat
origins.en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and in the Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Dijksgracht
origins.en: Named after the water of the same name, which runs along the inside of the railway embankment here. The embankment originally closed off the Oosterdok from the IJ, which was then still open.

origins.name: Dijkstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out as a dike at the end of the sixteenth century, after which the surroundings (long a marsh) were filled in with earth (aangeplempt).

origins.name: Dijkwater
origins.en: A nature reserve between Duiveland and Dreischor (Zeeland): a dammed tidal creek with its banks.

origins.name: Dijkwegpad
origins.en: An old local name from this part of Rijnland.

origins.name: Dijlehof
origins.en: A river in Belgium.

origins.name: Dijsselhofplantsoen
origins.en: Gerrit Willem Dijsselhof (1866-1924), impressionist painter. For some years the park was first called Breitnerplantsoen (council decision of 22 April 1925).

origins.name: Dikninge
origins.en: Originally an old abbey (1325-1602), now a late Empire-style country house on the Reest near De Wijk (Drenthe). Gateposts from 1817.

origins.name: Dilbeekpad
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Dillestraat
origins.en: A plant of the carrot family (dill), widely used as a kitchen herb in the northern half of Europe.

origins.name: Dilsenstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Dina Appeldoornstraat
origins.en: Christina Adriana Arendina Koudijs, née Van Appeldoorn (1884-1938), composer of chamber music and symphonic poems. She also composed Dutch dances and a suite for orchestra.

origins.name: Dinarpromenade
origins.en: A currency of the Arab world and the Balkans.

origins.name: Dintelstraat
origins.en: A river in Noord-Brabant that flows into the Volkerak at Dinteloord.

origins.name: Diopter
origins.en: Pseudonym of Arie Keppler (1876-1941); literally a spy, or also a sight (on a gun). The first director of Amsterdam's Municipal Housing Department (1915-1936), a great champion and promoter of social housing. The garden villages in Noord, among others, were built under his leadership.

origins.name: Diponegorostraat
origins.en: Diponegoro (Yogyakarta 1785 - Makassar 1855). The aristocrat Diponegoro, a 'prince' of a Javanese principality, led the Javanese uprising against Dutch colonial rule in the Java War (1825-1830). Dutch authority wavered, but won in the end. The fighting may have cost more than 200,000 lives. Diponegoro was exiled to Celebes. He is one of Indonesia's greatest 'national heroes'.

origins.name: Dirhampad
origins.en: In the Valutabuurt (currency neighbourhood) of Nieuw-West an unnamed cycle path runs parallel to the Guldenpromenade. It is named after the Moroccan currency, the dirham, which gives this important cycle path the name Dirhampad.

origins.name: Dirk Bonsstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1897-1945), born in Brandwijk, executed by firing squad at Zijpersluis.

origins.name: Dirk Deutekompad
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1895-1945), member of the clandestine CPN. Arrested in July 1944 for helping Jews and transported to the Neuengamme/Buchenwald camp, where he died on 20 April 1945. In the camp he looked after a group of Jewish children, all of whom were hanged by the camp command.

origins.name: Dirk Hartoghstraat
origins.en: Navigator who discovered the west coast of Australia in 1616.

origins.name: Dirk Schäferstraat
origins.en: Composer and pianist (1873-1931), a great interpreter of Chopin.

origins.name: Dirk Sonoystraat
origins.en: Diederick van Sonoy. Leader of the Sea Beggars (1529-1597), a nobleman who had fled Germany, sided with Prince William of Orange and was appointed governor of West-Friesland. Under Prince Maurice he fell into disgrace.

origins.name: Dirk van Hasseltssteeg
origins.en: Named after the skipper Dirk van Hasselt; archive records show that he himself owned a corner house in this alley. Under nos. 2 to 6 lie the remains of foundations, possibly of the thirteenth-century castle of the lords of Amstel.

origins.name: Dirk Vreekenstraat
origins.en: A participant in the February Strike of 1941.

origins.name: Dirk Wittehof
origins.en: A merchant by trade (1884-1932), and in his spare time a writer of sentimental songs (levensliedjes), which Pisuisse sang with great success.

origins.name: Dirkshornplantsoen
origins.en: A village south of Schagen (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Discusstraat
origins.en: A throwing disc, used in discus throwing at the Greek and Roman games.

origins.name: Disketteweg
origins.en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

origins.name: Displaystraat
origins.en: As a counterpart to the street names recalling Amsterdam-Noord's former shipbuilding industry, this name refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Distelachterstraat
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Distelkade
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Distelkruisstraat
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Distelplein
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Distelvoorstraat
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Distelweg
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Ditlaar
origins.en: The former farmstead of the dike reeve Ellard Ditelaar, which stood in the eighteenth century between the village of Sloten and the Slotermeer.

origins.name: Djakartaterras
origins.en: Also Jakarta (formerly Batavia), the capital of the Republic of Indonesia. This stretch of street was made by a break in the row of façades.

origins.name: Djambistraat
origins.en: A town and old residency on the east coast of Sumatra (Indonesia).

origins.name: Doblijn
origins.en: A corrupted spelling of the Irish port and capital Dublin, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Docklandsweg
origins.en: A former industrial port area on the Thames in south-east London, redeveloped since the 1980s into an area for living and working. Also a district of Dublin where large-scale renewal projects have begun.

origins.name: Doddendaal
origins.en: A castle near Ewijk (Gelderland), probably founded in the eleventh or twelfth century. The name Doddendaal dates from 1379. The building has been altered many times. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries its cellar served as a church for Roman Catholics.

origins.name: Doggersbankstraat
origins.en: A shoal in the North Sea where in 1781 the Dutch admiral Zoutman inflicted a defeat on the British fleet.

origins.name: Doggerstraat
origins.en: A ship that takes its name from the place where it went fishing, the Dogger Bank. The dogger fished for herring and cod, among other things.

origins.name: Dokter Meurerlaan
origins.en: Rudolf J.Th. Meurer (1866-1950), Amsterdam doctor, a very well-known rowing official and for many years coach of 'Nereus'. He promoted the Bosbaan (rowing course) and founded the Amsterdam Medical Sports Examination Bureau.

origins.name: Dolfijnhof
origins.en: A constellation (the Dolphin).

origins.name: Dolhaantjestraat
origins.en: The nickname of Adrianus van Berques, a Walloon nobleman who served the Sea Beggars as admiral. He was killed in Hainaut in 1572.

origins.name: Dolingadreef
origins.en: A state in Grou (Friesland). State is a Frisian word for a farmstead.

origins.name: Dollardpad
origins.en: A nature reserve in the arm of the Wadden Sea between Groningen and Germany. The area was formed in the Middle Ages.

origins.name: Dom H. van der Laanstraat
origins.en: Dom van der Laan (1904-1991), architect and Benedictine monk. In 1925, with fellow students at the Technische Hogeschool in Delft, he founded the 'Bouwkundige Studiekring' (architecture study circle), which often met at the home of Granpré Molière, the founder of the Delft School.

origins.name: Domela Nieuwenhuisstraat
origins.en: Ferdinand Domela Nieuwenhuis (1846-1919), Lutheran minister who left the church in 1879. A Dutch popular leader, pioneer of socialism in the Netherlands and founder of the Social Democratic League. Member of the House of Representatives from 1888 to 1891. He went from socialist to anarchist, which led to a break with Troelstra and his associates. The park was laid out on the site of the Maria Magdalenakerk, demolished in 1968. Nearby, on the Nassauplein, stands his statue, made by the sculptor Johan Polet in 1931.

origins.name: Domenico Scarlattilaan
origins.en: Italian composer (1685-1757), choirmaster in Rome and harpsichordist at the Spanish court, who composed more than five hundred works for keyboard.

origins.name: Domselaerstraat
origins.en: Tobias van Domselaer (1611-1685), historian. He compiled his 'Beschrijving van Amsterdam' (description of Amsterdam), published in 1665, from notes by Cornelis Dapper and Pontanus.

origins.name: Don Boscostraat
origins.en: Italian priest (1815-1888) who devoted his whole life to educating neglected young people.

origins.name: Donarstraat
origins.en: The Germanic god of thunder.

origins.name: Donauweg
origins.en: The second-longest river in Europe (the Danube). It rises in the Black Forest and flows into the Black Sea.

origins.name: Dongestraat
origins.en: A small river in Noord-Brabant.

origins.name: Donker Curtiusstraat
origins.en: Dirk Donker Curtius (1792-1864), liberal statesman, at first a journalist. He campaigned for revision of the constitution and was later Minister of Justice. He was responsible for the laws on ministerial responsibility and on the right of association.

origins.name: Doornburg
origins.en: The Doornenburgh, a seventeenth-century house on the Vecht near Maarssen, altered in 1721 and again in the twentieth century. (Not to be confused with Doornenburg castle in the Betuwe.)

origins.name: Dora Tamanaplein
origins.en: South African resistance fighter (1901-1983), very active in the women's movement. A member of the women's wing of the African National Congress (ANC) and one of the leading figures of the Federation of South African Women.

origins.name: Doris Lessingstraat
origins.en: Doris Lessing (1919-2013) was a British writer.

origins.name: Dorpsstraat Holysloot
origins.en: A village, part of Amsterdam since 1921. The origin of the name is unknown; the village appears as early as 1288 under the name Hoolesloot.

origins.name: Dorpsweg Ransdorp
origins.en: The village of Ransdorp was an independent municipality until 1 January 1921, when the municipality, with its villages of Durgerdam, Holysloot and Schellingwoude, was added to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Dortmuiden
origins.en: This is the English port of Dartmouth, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Dorus Rijkershof
origins.en: Coxswain of the lifeboat at Den Helder (1847-1928), who saved hundreds of shipwrecked people from death. The Dorus Rijkers Fund, which supports the families of lifeboatmen who die, is named after him.

origins.name: Dostojevskisingel
origins.en: Fyodor Mikhailovich Dostoevsky (1821-1881), one of the best-known Russian writers of the nineteenth century.

origins.name: Dotterbloemstraat
origins.en: The wild flower (marsh marigold), of the buttercup family.

origins.name: Douwes Dekkerstraat
origins.en: Eduard Douwes Dekker (1820-1887), pen name Multatuli. An Amsterdammer who went to the East Indies in 1838, where he became a colonial administrator, resigned after a conflict, and then devoted himself to writing. A forerunner of the Tachtigers (the Movement of the Eighties). His works include 'Max Havelaar' and 'Woutertje Pieterse'. The Multatuli Museum is in the house where he was born, on the Korsjespoortsteeg.

origins.name: Dovenetelstraat
origins.en: A plant genus (dead-nettle) of the mint family.

origins.name: Dr. C.W. Ittmannpad
origins.en: Cesar Willem Ittmann (1914-1945), assistant surgeon at the Binnengasthuis. He belonged to the Persoonsbewijzen-Centrale (identity card centre) group and the student resistance, and cared for sick and wounded resistance fighters. He took part in sabotage and was executed by firing squad at the former Rozenoord airfield on the Amstel.

origins.name: Dr. E. Boekmanstraat
origins.en: Emanuel Boekman (1889-1940), a leading social democrat and city councillor for the SDAP. From 1931 to 1940 he was alderman for education and the arts. His 1938 doctoral thesis 'Overheid en kunstbeleid' (government and arts policy) laid the foundations of post-war arts policy.

origins.name: Dr. J.A. Ringersstraat
origins.en: Johannes Aleidis Ringers (1885-1965), hydraulic engineer, director of Rijkswaterstaat and then an executive of the Indies railways. He was interned by the Germans during the war. After the war he was Minister of Public Works and Reconstruction in the Schermerhorn and Beel cabinets.

origins.name: Dr. Jan van Breemenstraat
origins.en: Jan Frans Leonard van Breemen (1874-1961), a pioneer in the fight against rheumatism. The Reumacentrum (rheumatism centre) was built on this street in 1965.

origins.name: Draaierweg
origins.en: The trade name of a metal and wood worker (a turner).

origins.name: Drachmesingel
origins.en: The currency of Greece (the drachma).

origins.name: Drakenstein
origins.en: A knightly manor (ridderhofstede) near Lage Vuursche (Utrecht), from 1640.

origins.name: Drie Burgpad
origins.en: A former country estate on the ring dike of the Watergraafsmeer, now the Weesperzijde.

origins.name: Driebanstraat
origins.en: A polder in West-Friesland.

origins.name: Driedistelstraat
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Drieharingenbrug
origins.en: This drawbridge takes its name from the three herrings above the door of the house 'De Drie Haringen' (the three herrings) at Vierwindendwarsstraat no. 1.

origins.name: Driehoekstraat
origins.en: Laid out in the middle of the seventeenth century. The name (triangle street) comes from the shape of the street.

origins.name: Driekoningenstraat
origins.en: Named after a shop sign of the corner building on the Singel (the Three Kings). The name is mentioned as early as 1608. Before that the little street was called Lijnbaanstraat.

origins.name: Driemondweg
origins.en: After the village of Driemond, added to Amsterdam when the municipality of Weesperkarspel was abolished on 1 August 1966.

origins.name: Drontermeerpad
origins.en: One of the Veluwe border lakes (randmeren).

origins.name: Droogbak
origins.en: The name appears as early as the first half of the seventeenth century and probably comes from the drying of cloth by the cloth weavers.

origins.name: Drostenburg
origins.en: A farm south of Borculo (Gelderland).

origins.name: Druivenbrug
origins.en: The fruit (grapes), grown in the Netherlands as table grapes, in Germany, France, Spain and Italy for winemaking, and in Greece, Asia Minor and California for raisins.

origins.name: Druivenstraat
origins.en: The fruit (grapes), grown in the Netherlands as table grapes, in Germany, France, Spain and Italy for winemaking, and in Greece, Asia Minor and California for raisins.

origins.name: Drusiushof
origins.en: Joannes van den Driesche or Drusius (1550-1600), orientalist, professor in the Netherlands and England.

origins.name: Du Perronstraat
origins.en: Charles Edgar du Perron (1899-1940), poet, writer and critic. His works include 'Land van herkomst' (country of origin).

origins.name: Duarte Pachecostraat
origins.en: Portuguese navigator (died 1533), a contemporary of Columbus and Bartolomeu Dias. In 1488 he joined Dias on the island of Príncipe in the Atlantic Ocean, as Dias was returning from exploring the route to India around the Cape.

origins.name: Dubbele Buurt
origins.en: Originally entirely in the municipality of Haarlemmerliede en Spaarnwoude; since a boundary correction in 1963 part of it has been on Amsterdam territory.

origins.name: Dubbelink
origins.en: A farm north of Delden (Overijssel).

origins.name: Dubbelinkdreef
origins.en: A farm north of Delden (Overijssel).

origins.name: Dubbelmondehof
origins.en: A church village in the former Zuid-Hollandse Waard drowned in the St Elizabeth's flood of 1421.

origins.name: Dudok de Withof
origins.en: Corneille Abraham Adrien (Bram) Dudok de Wit (1841-1911), a champion of sport. Nicknamed the 'sports minister', he served as a race official at all sorts of competitions. At the exhibition games in Paris in 1900 (the second Olympiad) he was general delegate for the Netherlands. His brother L.C. Dudok de Wit (1843-1913), better known as Kees de Tippelaar (Kees the walker), became a symbol of recreational walking.

origins.name: Dufaystraat
origins.en: Guillaume Dufay (1400-1474), musician from Hainaut, a well-known fifteenth-century composer, mainly of masses.

origins.name: Duffelhof
origins.en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Duinbeek
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Duindoornplein
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Duindoornstraat
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Duinluststraat
origins.en: A nature reserve near Overveen/Bloemendaal, made up of woodland and dunes.

origins.name: Duivelandstraat
origins.en: The southern part of the Zeeland island of Schouwen-Duiveland.

origins.name: Duivendrechtsekade
origins.en: The village of Duivendrecht in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. Duivendrecht comes from Doeve (a man's name) and drecht (a place where ships were hauled overland). When the Watergraafsmeer was still a lake, a ferry ran from where the village now lies to the far side, towards Oetewaal.

origins.name: Duivendrechtselaan
origins.en: The village of Duivendrecht in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. Duivendrecht comes from Doeve (a man's name) and drecht (a place where ships were hauled overland). When the Watergraafsmeer was still a lake, a ferry ran from where the village now lies to the far side, towards Oetewaal.

origins.name: Duizendschoonstraat
origins.en: The ornamental plant (sweet william).

origins.name: Dukdalfweg
origins.en: Named after the wooden pile structure (a dolphin), made of an upright pile in the middle and about four raking piles, that stops ships from hitting the quayside. The word comes from Duc d'Alve, the unyielding Duke of Alba.

origins.name: Duke Ellingtonstraat
origins.en: Edward Kennedy (Duke) Ellington (1899-1974), American jazz composer, pianist, bandleader and arranger, known for his various styles, including jungle and mood.

origins.name: Dulcie Septemberpad
origins.en: Representative of the African National Congress (ANC) in France and Switzerland. She was murdered in Paris in April 1988 for her struggle against apartheid.

origins.name: Dulongstraat
origins.en: Pierre Dulong (1785-1838), French physicist and chemist. He discovered that the atomic heat is the same for all solid elements.

origins.name: Durbanweg
origins.en: A port city in South Africa. The street lies near the Afrikahaven in the western port area.

origins.name: Durgerdammerdijk
origins.en: Named after the village that belonged until 1921 to the municipality of Ransdorp, abolished that year. The name arose by corruption of the oldest name, IJdoringherdam: the dam at the corner of the IJ. (The polder outside the dike here has kept the name IJdoorn.) The Durgerdammerdijk is the stretch of the Waterland sea dike on which Durgerdam lies.

origins.name: Durgerdammergouw
origins.en: Named after the village that belonged until 1921 to the municipality of Ransdorp, abolished that year. The name arose by corruption of the oldest name, IJdoringherdam: the dam at the corner of the IJ. (The polder outside the dike here has kept the name IJdoorn.) The Durgerdammerdijk is the stretch of the Waterland sea dike on which Durgerdam lies.

origins.name: Dusartstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Dusart (1660-1704), painter and engraver, a pupil of Van Ostade.

origins.name: Dwars Spinhuissteeg
origins.en: After the nearby Spinhuis (spinning house), a house of correction for women founded in 1596. From 1833 to 1941 the building housed the police headquarters.

origins.name: Dwarswatering
origins.en: A former watercourse where the De Eendracht sports park is now.

origins.name: Dwergpalmstraat
origins.en: A kind of fan palm (dwarf palm). It is one of the few palms that also grows in Europe.

origins.name: Dwergplanetenbaan
origins.en: Planet-like bodies, larger than asteroids but smaller than planets. Unlike planets, they have not cleared their orbits of other objects. In our solar system Pluto, Eris, Makemake, Haumea and Ceres fall into the dwarf-planet category.

origins.name: Dwergvinvisstraat
origins.en: A cetacean (the minke whale).

origins.name: Dynamostraat
origins.en: A machine that turns mechanical power into electrical power.

origins.name: Eastonstraat
origins.en: Charles Easton (1864-1920), journalist and astronomer, editor-in-chief of 'Het Nieuws van den Dag'. He wrote several meteorological studies.

origins.name: Echtenstein
origins.en: A manor house in Emmen (Drenthe).

origins.name: Eckeharthof
origins.en: Meister E.J. Eckhart (1260-1329), German mystic, a Dominican friar whose teaching was condemned after his death.

origins.name: Eclipshof
origins.en: An eclipse is the darkening of a celestial body when it passes behind another or into its shadow.

origins.name: Ecuplein
origins.en: The European Currency Unit (ecu), the unit of account of the European Community, also used as a currency in its own right.

origins.name: Edammerpad
origins.en: Named after the Noord-Holland town (Edam).

origins.name: Edammerstraat
origins.en: Named after the Noord-Holland town (Edam).

origins.name: Edenburg
origins.en: A South African place name.

origins.name: Edenville
origins.en: A town in South Africa: a small farming town in the north of the Free State province.

origins.name: Edisonstraat
origins.en: Thomas Alva Edison (1847-1931), North American inventor of the microphone, the megaphone, the phonograph and the electric light bulb.

origins.name: Edith Magnusstraat
origins.en: Edith Magnus (1925-1993) belonged in the 1960s to the women's core group of the Nederlandse Vereniging tot Integratie van Homoseksualiteit (Dutch Association for the Integration of Homosexuality), today's COC. She organised the first women's national days, which meant a great deal to lesbian women.

origins.name: Edmond Halleylaan
origins.en: English astronomer (1656-1742), Fellow of the Royal Society, appointed 'Astronomer Royal' in 1731. He wrote on magnetism and published a chart of the Atlantic Ocean and a world map on which he improved the courses. A comet and an observatory are named after him.

origins.name: Edmond Halleysteiger
origins.en: English astronomer (1656-1742), Fellow of the Royal Society, appointed 'Astronomer Royal' in 1731. He wrote on magnetism and published a chart of the Atlantic Ocean and a world map on which he improved the courses. A comet and an observatory are named after him.

origins.name: Edmund Gunterstraat
origins.en: English astronomer (1581-1626), inventor of the pleinschaal (Gunter's scale), a kind of slide rule with logarithmic divisions. His scientific work dealt with navigation and its problems.

origins.name: Eduard Hellendoornstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1912-1941), involved in the February Strike of 1941. One of the '18 dead of the Waalsdorpervlakte'.

origins.name: Eduard Jacobshof
origins.en: Amsterdam cabaret artist (1868-1914) who introduced the levenslied (the sentimental popular song) to the Netherlands.

origins.name: Eduard Meijerstraat
origins.en: Water polo and swimming champion (1878-1929).

origins.name: Eduard van Beinumstraat
origins.en: Eduard A. van Beinum (1901-1959), conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra from 1945 until his death, and also of the London Philharmonic Orchestra from 1949 to 1952.

origins.name: Eduard Vetermanstraat
origins.en: Man of letters, playwright and director (1901-1946). He adapted several of Timmermans's books for the stage.

origins.name: Edumbe
origins.en: A town in South Africa, in the province of KwaZulu-Natal.

origins.name: Edward Masseystraat
origins.en: English scientist who in 1802 developed the mechanical log, a device that shows a ship's speed. Between 1802 and 1848 he received six patents for various mechanical nautical instruments.

origins.name: Edward Wrightstraat
origins.en: English scholar (died 1615) whose findings were particularly important for navigation. In 1599 he published 'Certaine errors in navigation'.

origins.name: Eef Kamerbeekstraat
origins.en: Evert Kamerbeek (1934-2008), athlete, eleven times Dutch decathlon champion from 1954.

origins.name: Eemlandstraat
origins.en: A region in the north-east of the province of Utrecht, in the basin of the river Eem.

origins.name: Eemsstraat
origins.en: The sea inlet between Delfzijl and Germany (the mouth of the river Ems).

origins.name: Eendenstraat
origins.en: The water bird (the duck).

origins.name: Eendrachtstraat
origins.en: The water between Tholen and Noord-Brabant.

origins.name: Eenhoornhof
origins.en: A constellation (the Dolphin).

origins.name: Eensgevonden
origins.en: A South African place name.

origins.name: Eerste Amstelvlietpad
origins.en: Historic country house (estate) on the Amsteldijk. It was built after 1721 by Gerrit Nieuwenhuizen, who originally called it Meerhuizen. It has been known as Amstelvliet since 1784. It was demolished in or after 1916.

origins.name: Eerste Anjeliersdwarsstraat
origins.en: An anjelier (carnation) is a flower belonging to the pink family.

origins.name: Eerste Atjehstraat
origins.en: The northern part of the Indonesian island of Sumatra (Aceh), known above all for the Aceh War (1873-1904), with which the name of General Van Heutsz is linked.

origins.name: Eerste Bloemdwarsstraat
origins.en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion of 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which it is named. From 1614 to 1878 the windmill 'De Blom' stood on the bastion; it was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

origins.name: Eerste Boerhaavestraat
origins.en: Hermannus Boerhaave (1668-1738), professor of medicine at Leiden, internationally renowned. The street name Boerhaavestraat (Eerste to Vierde) has changed quite often: set as Boerhaavestraat on 15 November 1876, changed to Eerste Boerhaavestraat on 15 November 1882, a change reversed on 10 December 1884. On 13 October 1897 the street was extended under the same name, and finally on 19 February 1908 it was split into today's Eerste and Tweede Boerhaavestraat. The Tweede, Derde and Vierde Boerhaavestraat named in 1882 were replaced by the names Deymanstraat, Ruyschstraat and Blasiusstraat.

origins.name: Eerste Boomdwarsstraat
origins.en: In this part of the Jordaan, streets are named after flowers, shrubs and trees. In the seventeenth century, the street was also called Lindeboomstraat.

origins.name: Eerste Breeuwersstraat
origins.en: A trade name. A breeuwer (caulker) sealed the seams between the planks of a ship's hull. In the seventeenth century many caulkers lived in the Eerste Breeuwersstraat (formerly Breeuwersstraat), working at the shipyards on the Prinseneiland and Realeneiland. In 1895 the parallel street was given the same name, which made the additions Eerste and Tweede necessary.

origins.name: Eerste Ceramstraat
origins.en: An island in Indonesia.

origins.name: Eerste Coehoornstraat
origins.en: Menno Baron van Coehoorn (1641-1704), fortress builder, engineer-general of fortifications.

origins.name: Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat
origins.en: Poet and prose writer (1596-1687), whose works include 'Hofwijck' and epigrams (sneldichten). He was secretary to several successive stadholders. Before 1894 parts of these streets were called Eerste and Tweede Bilderdijkstraat (council decisions of 15 May 1878 and 19 December 1883).

origins.name: Eerste Disteldwarsstraat
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Eerste Egelantiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Eerste Goudsbloemdwarsstraat
origins.en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

origins.name: Eerste Helmersstraat
origins.en: Jan Frederik Helmers (1767-1813), Amsterdam broker who devoted himself to letters. His works include 'De Hollandsche Natie' (1813). The second part of the Eerste Helmersstraat lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 and was then called Hofdijkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 9 May 1890). The start of this street was originally a short side street of the Nassaukade called Sophiapark.

origins.name: Eerste Hugo de Grootstraat
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

origins.name: Eerste Jacob van Campenstraat
origins.en: Architect (1595-1659), designer of the city hall on the Dam, now the Royal Palace, though he was not allowed to finish the work. Van Campen also built the Heiligewegspoort in 1636, and a palace in Rijswijk for Prince Frederik Hendrik in 1657. The split into Eerste and Tweede came after the stretch of street between them was sold to the Heineken brewery in 1930.

origins.name: Eerste Jan Steenstraat
origins.en: Painter (1626-1679), mostly of domestic scenes: merry, untidy interiors. That gave rise to the expression 'a Jan Steen household' (een huishouden van Jan Steen).

origins.name: Eerste Jan van der Heijdenstraat
origins.en: Painter and engineer (1637-1712), inventor of the fire engine with a hose and of a new model of street lamp. Painter of portraits and townscapes.

origins.name: Eerste Keucheniusstraat
origins.en: Levinus W.C. Keuchenius (1822-1893), Anti-Revolutionary statesman and fierce opponent of the state school. Minister of the Colonies from 1888 to 1890.

origins.name: Eerste Kostverlorenkade
origins.en: After the Kostverlorenwetering, dug in 1413 to give a shorter waterway to the Haarlem and Leiden lakes. According to some, the name Kostverloren (cost lost) comes from the heavy legal costs of this channel, which was a bone of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609. The name Kostverloren occurs in several places in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat
origins.en: The southern European ornamental tree (the laurel).

origins.name: Eerste Leeghwaterstraat
origins.en: Jan Adriaanszoon Leeghwater (1575-1650), hydraulic engineer. As overseer and millwright he worked on many land reclamations, including the Beemster. He drew up the first plan to drain the Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Eerste Leliedwarsstraat
origins.en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Eerste Lindendwarsstraat
origins.en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

origins.name: Eerste Looiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

origins.name: Eerste Marnixdwarsstraat
origins.en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Eerste Marnixplantsoen
origins.en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Eerste Nassaustraat
origins.en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. Before it was named in 1879, the quay was called Buitensingel.

origins.name: Eerste Oosterparkstraat
origins.en: Named after the nearby Oosterpark, and originally (council decision of 15 November 1882) named Eerste, Tweede and Derde Parkstraat. The Eerste Oosterparkstraat was earlier called Oetgenspad, after Frans Hendriks Oetgens, a sixteenth-century burgomaster over whose land several paths were laid. Until 1895 the street name applied as far as the Linnaeusstraat. In that year the stretch along the park was given the park's name.

origins.name: Eerste Passeerdersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

origins.name: Eerste Ringdijkstraat
origins.en: After its position relative to the Watergraafsmeer. Before the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was annexed, the Ooster Ringdijk was called Noorder- and Zuider-Ringdijk. The Eerste Ringdijkstraat was then called Schoollaan, and earlier still the name Dielemanstraat seems to have been used. A Tweede Ringdijkstraat (formerly Dijklaan) has since disappeared entirely through demolition.

origins.name: Eerste Rozendwarsstraat
origins.en: The flower (the rose).

origins.name: Eerste Schinkelstraat
origins.en: The name recalls the old roadside inn Schinkelhaven. Before 1922 the street was part of the Schinkelkade.

origins.name: Eerste Sweelinckstraat
origins.en: Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck (1562-1621), a musician of great renown and organist of the Oude Kerk. He wrote many compositions on the psalms and love songs. Before 1896 part of the Tweede Sweelinckstraat lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel as the Tweede Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 22 August 1890).

origins.name: Eerste Tuindwarsstraat
origins.en: Tuin (garden) here means a yard or enclosed space. The street name comes from the Stadstimmertuin (the city's carpentry yard, the Stadswerf), which lay here from 1612 to 1660 (by the Lijnbaansgracht) and to which the street led.

origins.name: Eerste Van der Helststraat
origins.en: Bartholomeus van der Helst (1612-1670), painter of militia and regents' group portraits.

origins.name: Eerste Van Swindenstraat
origins.en: Jean Henri van Swinden (1746-1823), philosopher, mathematician and physicist, professor at Franeker and from 1785 in Amsterdam. He sat on the commission that fixed the metre, after which he worked out the metric system introduced in the Netherlands in 1816.

origins.name: Eerste Vogelstraat
origins.en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

origins.name: Eerste Weteringdwarsstraat
origins.en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory.

origins.name: Eerste Weteringplantsoen
origins.en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory.

origins.name: Eerstegeluk
origins.en: A South African place name.

origins.name: Eeuwige Jeugdlaan
origins.en: Probably named after the legendary spring, the 'Fountain of Eternal Youth'. The legend says that whoever drank from the fountain would look young. The avenue also borders the Jeugdland neighbourhood, built between 1995 and 1998, and the name can be derived from that too.

origins.name: Efua Sutherlandstraat
origins.en: Efua Theodora Sutherland-Morgue (1924-1996), Ghanaian writer, actress and social worker, head of the Ghana Experimental Theatre. In 1961 she founded the literary magazine 'Okyeame', and she was a researcher at the university's Institute of African Studies in Ghana. She contributed greatly to awareness of Ghanaian culture.

origins.name: Egelantiersgracht
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Egelantiersstraat
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Egeldonk
origins.en: A farm in Zundert (Noord-Brabant). In Noord-Brabant the ending donk is common and means a small rise.

origins.name: Egelenburg
origins.en: A former country house south-east of Heiloo (Noord-Holland), built by the lords of Warmenhuizen.

origins.name: Egellelie
origins.en: The egellelie is a plant native to the Cape in South Africa.

origins.name: Egelskopstraat
origins.en: A marsh plant (bur-reed) that grows well in small ponds.

origins.name: Eggertstraat
origins.en: Willem Eggert, Lord of Purmerland and Ilpendam (1340-1417), a very wealthy Amsterdammer, schepen (alderman) of the city and one of the founders of the Nieuwe Kerk. Before 1865 the street was called Ellendigesteeg (miserable alley).

origins.name: Egidiusstraat
origins.en: The person addressed in an anonymous medieval lament.

origins.name: EGoli
origins.en: eGoli is the Zulu name for Johannesburg, the largest city in South Africa, in the province of Gauteng. Literally: city of gold. Forty per cent of the world's gold has been found in or around this city.

origins.name: Egstraat
origins.en: The farm implement (a harrow). When first laid out, the street was part of the Zaaiersweg (council decision of 30 January 1924).

origins.name: Ehrlichstraat
origins.en: Paul Ehrlich (1854-1915), German physician who in 1910 discovered salvarsan, an arsenic preparation against syphilis. He received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1908.

origins.name: Eierlandstraat
origins.en: The northern part of Texel, originally a separate dune island, later joined to Texel by a sand dike, after which the Eierland polder was formed by enclosing the mudflats. Extensive nature reserves lie on both the sea side and the Wadden side. The Eierlandse Gat (between Texel and Vlieland) is a seal reserve.

origins.name: Eiger
origins.en: A mountain peak in Switzerland, 3970 metres high.

origins.name: Eijkmanstraat
origins.en: Christiaan Eijkman (1858-1930), physician and bacteriologist, professor at Utrecht University. He discovered the cause of beriberi and received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1929.

origins.name: Eikenplein
origins.en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

origins.name: Eikenweg
origins.en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

origins.name: Einthovenstraat
origins.en: Willem Einthoven (1860-1927), Leiden professor of physiology and heart specialist, inventor of the string galvanometer. He received the Nobel Prize in 1924.

origins.name: Eisdenstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Eisingastraat
origins.en: Eise Eisinga (1744-1828), Frisian amateur astronomer. He built a planetarium that still exists in Franeker.

origins.name: Ekangala
origins.en: A village in South Africa, in the KwaNdebele area (formerly Transvaal) in the province of Mpumalanga.

origins.name: EKapa
origins.en: A South African name for Cape Town (colloquial).

origins.name: Ekingenstraat
origins.en: A church village on Noord-Beveland (Zeeland) drowned in 1532.

origins.name: Eksteenfontein
origins.en: A South African place name.

origins.name: Eksterstraat
origins.en: The bird (the magpie).

origins.name: Elandsgracht
origins.en: This neighbourhood once had many tanneries, where the hides of elk (elanden), deer, bears and so on were worked.

origins.name: Elandsstraat
origins.en: This neighbourhood once had many tanneries, where the hides of elk (elanden), deer, bears and so on were worked.

origins.name: Elbaweg
origins.en: An Italian island in the Mediterranean. Napoleon was exiled to Elba in 1814.

origins.name: Elberveld
origins.en: A South African place name.

origins.name: Elckerlijcstraat
origins.en: A fifteenth-century morality play (Everyman), attributed to Petrus van Diest. Its full title is 'Den spieghel der Salicheyt van Elckerlijc'.

origins.name: Eldorado
origins.en: Spanish for 'the gilded one', after a myth about an initiation ritual of the Muisca people of Colombia, in which a new chief had himself covered entirely in gold dust and swam in a mythical lake. The legend slowly changed from a person into a land of gold, sought for centuries by conquistadors, the French, the English and the Dutch.

origins.name: Elegaststraat
origins.en: A character from the Middle Dutch chivalric romance 'Karel ende Elegast'.

origins.name: Elektronstraat
origins.en: The smallest quantity of negative electricity, one of the building blocks of the atom.

origins.name: Elementenstraat
origins.en: The unit (cell) in a galvanic battery.

origins.name: Elfendansstraat
origins.en: The name refers to the poem 'Elvendans' (elves' dance) by Jacqueline E. van der Waals (1868-1922), included in the collection 'Nieuwe Verzen' (1909).

origins.name: Elim
origins.en: Named after Elim, a village on the Agulhas Plain in the Western Cape of South Africa, founded in 1824 by German missionaries as a Moravian mission station. The street lies in a neighbourhood whose names come from South Africa.

origins.name: Elisabeth Adriaansestraat
origins.en: Elisabeth (Betsy) Adriaanse (Roermond, 1906 - Chur, 1939) was a pioneer as a lawyer and a campaigner for women's suffrage.

origins.name: Elisabeth Boddaertstraat
origins.en: Jonkvrouw Elisabeth Boddaert (1867-1948) founded homes for neglected children in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Elisabeth Samsonstraat
origins.en: Surinamese businesswoman (1715-1771) who belonged to the class of fairly well-off free mulattoes (people of mixed descent). Unlike many whites in the colony, she could read and write. She lived as an equal with the white Carl Otto Creutz. In the slave society, despite racist opposition, she won herself an important position.

origins.name: Elisabeth van Dorpstraat
origins.en: Elisabeth (Lizzy) van Dorp (Arnhem, 5 September 1872 - Banyubiru, 6 September 1945) was a pioneer as a lawyer, economist and politician, and a campaigner for women's suffrage.

origins.name: Elisabeth Wolffstraat
origins.en: Elisabeth Wolff, née Bekker (Betje Wolff) (1738-1804), writer. With Aagje Deken she wrote, among others, 'Sara Burgerhart' and 'Willem Leevend'.

origins.name: Eliza van Calcarstraat
origins.en: Eliza Carolina Ferdinanda van Calcar-Schiotling (1822-1904), educator and writer. In 'De dubbele roeping der vrouw' (the double calling of woman) she argued for education for women.

origins.name: Elizabeth Anscombestraat
origins.en: Elizabeth Anscombe (1919-2001) was a British analytic philosopher.

origins.name: Elizabeth Cady Stantonplein
origins.en: American activist (1815-1902) who campaigned for women's suffrage in the United States. She extended her activism to Europe too, and in 1888 helped found the International Council of Women.

origins.name: Ella Fitzgeraldstraat
origins.en: Ella Jane Fitzgerald (1917-1996), regarded as one of the most important American jazz singers in history. Her hallmarks included a range of four octaves, clear diction and a gift for scat singing.

origins.name: Ellert Vlieropstraat
origins.en: A captain of the Beggars' fleet who fought at the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Elpermeer
origins.en: A nature reserve in the Grollo forestry (Drenthe).

origins.name: Elpermeerpad
origins.en: A nature reserve in the Grollo forestry (Drenthe).

origins.name: Elsrijkdreef
origins.en: A former farm in Amstelveen.

origins.name: Elstarstraat
origins.en: A Dutch apple variety, yellow-green with a red blush, bred from a cross of Golden Delicious and Ingrid Marie.

origins.name: Elzenhagensingel
origins.en: The name of a farm on the Buikslotermeerdijk, demolished in 1964.

origins.name: Elzenstraat
origins.en: The tree (the alder).

origins.name: Emanuel van Meterenstraat
origins.en: Southern Netherlandish merchant and historian (1535-1612), whose works include 'Historie der Nederlandscher oorlogen' (history of the Netherlands wars).

origins.name: Emanzana
origins.en: A nature reserve in South Africa, east of Johannesburg, known for its sulphur spring, which the area's first inhabitants called Emanzana. The Zulu name Emanzana means 'healing water'.

origins.name: Emfuleni
origins.en: A municipality in South Africa, in the province of Gauteng. The Zulu name means 'place where there are many rivers'. The municipality got the name because it lies beside the Vaal river.

origins.name: Emilie Knappertstraat
origins.en: The founder of social work in the Netherlands (1860-1952).

origins.name: Emmalaan
origins.en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934), second wife of King Willem III, Queen Regent from 1890 to 1898, and mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

origins.name: Emmaplein
origins.en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934), second wife of King Willem III, Queen Regent from 1890 to 1898, and mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

origins.name: Emmastraat
origins.en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934), second wife of King Willem III, Queen Regent from 1890 to 1898, and mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

origins.name: Emmeline Pankhurststraat
origins.en: English campaigner for women's suffrage (1858-1928), among other things head of the English society for women's suffrage. In London she gave public lectures and organised protest marches. She was arrested several times for her militancy. Pankhurst died in 1928, the year the women of Great Britain got the vote.

origins.name: Emmikhovenstraat
origins.en: An area in the Land van Altena (Noord-Brabant) drowned in the St Elizabeth's flood.

origins.name: Emmy Andriessestraat
origins.en: Photographer (1914-1953). During the Second World War she joined a group of photographers later known as 'De Ondergedoken Camera' (the hidden camera) and made a photo report of the Hunger Winter in Amsterdam. After the war she concentrated mainly on portrait photography.

origins.name: Empangeni
origins.en: A town in South Africa, in the province of KwaZulu-Natal.

origins.name: Endumeni
origins.en: A town in South Africa, formerly Dundee, in the province of KwaZulu-Natal. The Zulu name means 'place of the thunderstorm'; lightning often strikes the Endumeni hill.

origins.name: Engcobo
origins.en: A town in South Africa, in the Eastern Cape province.

origins.name: Enge Kerksteeg
origins.en: After the Oude Kerk, which the alleys lead to from the Warmoesstraat, part of which was originally called Kerkstraat.

origins.name: Enge Lombardsteeg
origins.en: After the nearby lommerd, or Bank van Lening (pawnshop), founded in 1614.

origins.name: Engelsesteeg
origins.en: The alley was already called this in the sixteenth century. There used to be many inns here, which shows it was a popular neighbourhood, perhaps particularly with English sailors.

origins.name: Enkeldoorn
origins.en: A South African place name.

origins.name: Enkhuizerplein
origins.en: The Noord-Holland town of Enkhuizen.

origins.name: Enkhuizerstraat
origins.en: The Noord-Holland town of Enkhuizen.

origins.name: Ennemaborg
origins.en: A late-medieval Groningen borg (fortified manor) near Midwolde (Groningen), restored around 1700. In its present form a stately country house.

origins.name: Enny Vredestraat
origins.en: Enny Vrede, stage name of Maria Magdalena Müller (Utrecht, 3 November 1883 - 2 April 1919), Dutch actress. She made her debut in 1908 with Eduard Verkade's company De Hagespelers, studied in Berlin with Max Reinhardt, and made her name in English society plays as well as in leading roles such as Shakespeare's Juliet and Shaw's Candida. She and her second husband died on the way back from their honeymoon in Norway, when the SS Amstel sank between Gothenburg and Rotterdam; their bodies were never found.

origins.name: Entabeni
origins.en: A game reserve in South Africa, in the province of Limpopo. The name means 'the place of the mountain', after its position in the mountainous Waterberg region. The area is part of a World Heritage site.

origins.name: Entrepotdok
origins.en: Named after its function. The dock was built in 1827; imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid (a bonded warehouse, entrepot). The warehouses have lost their function as an entrepot, and in part of them the upper floors have now been converted into homes (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Entrepothof
origins.en: Named after its function. The dock was built in 1827; imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid (a bonded warehouse, entrepot). The warehouses have lost their function as an entrepot, and in part of them the upper floors have now been converted into homes (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Entrepotkade
origins.en: Named after its function. The dock was built in 1827; imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid (a bonded warehouse, entrepot). The warehouses have lost their function as an entrepot, and in part of them the upper floors have now been converted into homes (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Eosstraat
origins.en: A figure from Greek mythology, also known as Aurore or Aurora: the goddess of sunrise and the dawn.

origins.name: Epicurusstraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher (341-270 BC). His philosophy held that only insight and a moral life lead to happiness.

origins.name: Erasmusgracht
origins.en: Desiderius Erasmus (1467-1536), humanist, who fiercely attacked the abuses in the Roman Catholic Church. His best-known work is 'In Praise of Folly'.

origins.name: Ereprijsstraat
origins.en: Named after the speedwell, a plant.

origins.name: Erich Salomonstraat
origins.en: German-Jewish photojournalist (1886-1944), a pioneer of candid photography, in which people are photographed without their noticing. A grand master of political documentary and society photography.

origins.name: Erik de Roodestraat
origins.en: Also Eric the Red. A Norse navigator who settled in Iceland in 960 and from there discovered Greenland in 985.

origins.name: Ernest Staesplein
origins.en: The title of an 1874 prose collection by the Flemish writer Anton Bergmann (1835-1874).

origins.name: Ernest Staesstraat
origins.en: The title of an 1874 prose collection by the Flemish writer Anton Bergmann (1835-1874).

origins.name: Ernst Cahn en Alfred Kohnbrug
origins.en: Ernst Cahn, the man with whom Alfred Kohn (died 1941) ran the Koco ice-cream parlours, the home base of Jewish fighting squads in the Second World War.

origins.name: Ernst Cahnsingel
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1889-1941), owner of the ice-cream parlour 'Koco' on the Van Woustraat, from which resistance to anti-Jewish riots was organised in 1941.

origins.name: Ertskade
origins.en: Ore boats used to be unloaded at this quay.

origins.name: Escudolaan
origins.en: The escudo is the currency of Portugal.

origins.name: Eshowe
origins.en: Eshowe is a town in South Africa whose name was inspired by the sound of the wind blowing through the native Dlinza forest.

origins.name: Esmoreitstraat
origins.en: A fourteenth-century Flemish abel spel (a serious secular play).

origins.name: Esplanade de Meer
origins.en: The former Ajax stadium De Meer.

origins.name: Esther de Boer-van Rijkstraat
origins.en: Actress (1854-1937). She played the part of Kniertje in Herman Heijermans's 'Op hoop van zegen' more than a thousand times.

origins.name: Ethekwini
origins.en: A port city in South Africa, formerly Durban, in the province of KwaZulu-Natal. The Zulu name means 'place where the ocean and the earth meet'.

origins.name: Etnastraat
origins.en: A volcano on the Italian island of Sicily, the highest and most active volcano in Europe.

origins.name: Eudorinastraat
origins.en: A microscopic water creature, a flagellate alga. Because it contains chlorophyll it can assimilate carbon dioxide.

origins.name: Eurokade
origins.en: The name of the future European currency.

origins.name: Europaboulevard
origins.en: Named after the continent. The naming followed the resolution of the Consultative Assembly of the Council of Europe of 29 December 1957, which called on every municipality in Europe to give a square or street the name Europe, to help promote the idea of European unity. With this naming the name Westerscheldeplein (council decision of 30 January 1935) and the name Scheldestraat for part of that street (council decision of 16 February 1927) were abolished.

origins.name: Europaplein
origins.en: Named after the continent. The naming followed the resolution of the Consultative Assembly of the Council of Europe of 29 December 1957, which called on every municipality in Europe to give a square or street the name Europe, to help promote the idea of European unity. With this naming the name Westerscheldeplein (council decision of 30 January 1935) and the name Scheldestraat for part of that street (council decision of 16 February 1927) were abolished.

origins.name: Eva Besnyöstraat
origins.en: Hungarian-Dutch photographer (1910-2003), born in Budapest, who came to the Netherlands in the 1930s. Known for her socially engaged reportage, architectural photography and portraits.

origins.name: Eva Schalkbrug
origins.en: Eva Schalk (1890-1978) was the first woman on a water board. She was for 27 years a hoofdingeland (board member) of the Buikslotermeer polder and for 21 years a hoofdingeland of the Hoogheemraadschap (regional water board).

origins.name: Everard van Reijdhof
origins.en: Historian (1550-1602), councillor of the Frisian stadholder Willem Lodewijk. His works include 'Historie der Nederlandscher oorlogen' (history of the Netherlands wars), an important source for knowledge of the Dutch Revolt.

origins.name: Eversdal
origins.en: A South African place name.

origins.name: Evert Cornelisstraat
origins.en: Conductor and pianist (1884-1931). Second conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra from 1910 to 1919, then conductor of the Utrecht City Orchestra.

origins.name: Evert van der Wallbrug
origins.en: Evert van der Wall (1944-2003) was alderman for education and youth affairs in Amsterdam for the PvdA from 1979 to 1983. In 2002 he became chairman of the Oost-Watergraafsmeer district. He worked for the development of Oostpoort with a central district hall and a community school, and that is why this bridge is named after him.

origins.name: Evertsweertplantsoen
origins.en: A village near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland (Zeeland) drowned in 1530.

origins.name: Evertsweertstraat
origins.en: A village near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland (Zeeland) drowned in 1530.

origins.name: Ewoud Worststraat
origins.en: A Beggar admiral (died 1574) who took part in the uprising in Vlissingen in 1572 and the siege of Middelburg in 1573.

origins.name: Ezelsbrug
origins.en: The name of this bridge (donkey bridge) recalls the hard struggle the residents had to wage against the car lobby, which would rather have seen bridges for ordinary traffic here. They often felt like donkeys that kept stumbling over the same stone. The name also refers to the memory aid called an ezelsbruggetje (a mnemonic). The bridge was officially opened on 14 March 1987 by having a donkey walk across it.

origins.name: F.C. Dondersstraat
origins.en: Franciscus Cornelis Donders (1818-1889), world-famous ophthalmologist.

origins.name: Faas Wilkesstraat
origins.en: Servaas Wilkes (1923-2006), footballer. With his elegant play he was Johan Cruijff's great role model. He was the first Dutchman to play for a top foreign club. Until 1998 he held the Dutch national team record with 35 goals in 38 internationals.

origins.name: Fagelstraat
origins.en: Caspar Fagel (1629-1688), who in 1672 succeeded Johan de Witt as Grand Pensionary of Holland.

origins.name: Fahrenheitsingel
origins.en: Gabriel Daniel Fahrenheit (1686-1736), German by birth, who settled in the Netherlands as a physicist. In 1715 he set the freezing point of the thermometer at 32 degrees and the boiling point at 212 degrees. The Fahrenheitstraat was originally called De Wetstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 31 October 1901).

origins.name: Fahrenheitstraat
origins.en: Gabriel Daniel Fahrenheit (1686-1736), German by birth, who settled in the Netherlands as a physicist. In 1715 he set the freezing point of the thermometer at 32 degrees and the boiling point at 212 degrees. The Fahrenheitstraat was originally called De Wetstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 31 October 1901).

origins.name: Falckstraat
origins.en: Anton Reinhard Falck (1777-1843), statesman and lawyer, one of the leaders of the revolution of 1813. Under King Willem I he was Minister of Education, Industry and the Colonies. Founder of the Leesmuseum (reading society). The street was laid out on a filled-in part of the Achtergracht.

origins.name: Fannius Scholtenstraat
origins.en: Cornelis A. Fannius Scholten (1767-1832), lawyer in The Hague. During the revolution of 1813 he was, with Melchior Kemper, commissioner of the General Government in Amsterdam, and afterwards Councillor of State in extraordinary service.

origins.name: Fanny Blankers-Koenlaan
origins.en: Francina Elsje Blankers-Koen (1918-2004), athlete. She won four gold medals at the 1948 Olympic Games in London. In 1999 the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) named her 'Female Athlete of the Century'.

origins.name: Fanny Durackstraat
origins.en: Australian swimmer who won gold in the 100 metres freestyle at the 1912 Olympic Games in Stockholm, the first woman to win Olympic swimming gold.

origins.name: Fanny Mendelssohnstraat
origins.en: Fanny Mendelssohn was a German composer and pianist.

origins.name: Faradaystraat
origins.en: Michael Faraday (1791-1867), English physicist and chemist, founder of the electromagnetic theory of light.

origins.name: Fazantenweg
origins.en: The game bird (the pheasant).

origins.name: Februariplein
origins.en: After the February Strike of 25 and 26 February 1941, a protest strike against the first raids in the Jewish quarter.

origins.name: Feike de Boerlaan
origins.en: Feike de Boer (1892-1976), director of the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland' (Netherlands Steamship Company) from 1934 to 1946. He held countless other posts, among them board member of the N.V. Nederlandsch-Indische Steenkolen Handel Maatschappij and of the N.V. Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij. From 1945 to 1946, exactly three hundred days, he was burgomaster of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Ferdinand Bolstraat
