origins.en: Painter (1616-1680), a pupil of Rembrandt, who painted portraits and regents' group portraits, among other things. (The boundary with the Gerard Doustraat was set more precisely by council decision of 9 June 1921.)

origins.name: Ferdinand Huyckstraat
origins.en: A historical novel by Jacob van Lennep about life in Amsterdam in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Ferguutstraat
origins.en: A thirteenth-century Celtic (Arthurian) chivalric romance.

origins.name: Ferrarisstraat
origins.en: Galileo Ferraris (1847-1897), Italian mathematician and physicist, discoverer of the principle of rotating (three-phase) current.

origins.name: Ferry Ploegerstraat
origins.en: Ferdinand Ploeger (1915-1944), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Bloemendaal.

origins.name: Fibigerstraat
origins.en: Johannes Andreas Grib Fibiger (1867-1928), Danish physician, a well-known scientist in cancer research. He received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1926.

origins.name: Fijnje van Salverdastraat
origins.en: Johannes Gerardus Wijbo Fijnje van Salverda (1796-1889), water management and railway engineer and inventor. As chief engineer of Rijkswaterstaat he was put in charge of the improvement of the Nieuwe Waterweg.

origins.name: Filips van Almondestraat
origins.en: Naval hero (1646-1711), admiral in the Nine Years' War against France of 1688 to 1697.

origins.name: Finsenstraat
origins.en: Niels Finsen (1860-1904), Danish physician, inventor of the Finsen lamp named after him, for light therapy. He received the Nobel Prize in 1903. From 26 July 1939 until it was given this name, the street was part of the Bunsenstraat.

origins.name: Firststraat
origins.en: Ruth First (1925-1982), journalist, daughter of Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe who came to South Africa. She wrote about the evil consequences of apartheid. After several arrests she fled to England, where she kept working for the anti-apartheid movement. In 1982 she was murdered by the South African secret service.

origins.name: Fizeaustraat
origins.en: Armand Hippolyte Fizeau (1819-1896), French physicist, inventor of a method for measuring the speed of light.

origins.name: Flamingostraat
origins.en: A bird that lives in subtropical regions and occasionally appears in temperate zones too.

origins.name: Flammarionstraat
origins.en: Camille Flammarion (1842-1925), French astronomer and author of many popular works on astronomy and geology.

origins.name: Fleerde
origins.en: The name of a patrician house in Bergharen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Flevopark
origins.en: Named after Lake Flevo, from which the Zuiderzee formed.

origins.name: Flevoparkweg
origins.en: Named after Lake Flevo, from which the Zuiderzee (now the IJsselmeer) formed.

origins.name: Flierbosdreef
origins.en: The name of several farms, among them in Wouw (Noord-Brabant) and Stedum (Groningen).

origins.name: Florapad
origins.en: The collective name for the plant world. Originally the Roman goddess of spring and flowers.

origins.name: Floraparkweg
origins.en: The collective name for the plant world. Originally the Roman goddess of spring and flowers.

origins.name: Floraweg
origins.en: The collective name for the plant world. Originally the Roman goddess of spring and flowers.

origins.name: Florence Nightingalestraat
origins.en: British nurse (1820-1910), nicknamed the lady with the lamp, known from the Crimean War of 1854. She became the pioneer of modern nursing and was a forerunner of the Red Cross.

origins.name: Florijn
origins.en: The name of farms in Groenlo (Gelderland) and Wassenaar (Zuid-Holland). In Eibergen (Gelderland) it is the name of a hamlet.

origins.name: Floris van der Laakenstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1919-1945), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad at Hattem. He was commander of the radio service of the Raad van Verzet (Resistance Council).

origins.name: Floris Versterstraat
origins.en: Painter (1861-1927), a pupil of Breitner and at first an impressionist. He painted still lifes, portraits and landscapes.

origins.name: Fluessenlaan
origins.en: A lake in southern Friesland.

origins.name: Fluitschipstraat
origins.en: A seventeenth-century cargo ship (the fluyt), a three-master with a rounded hull.

origins.name: Foekje Dillemastraat
origins.en: Athlete (1926-2007), rival of Fanny Blankers-Koen over 200 metres. After a compulsory sex test in 1950 she was banned for life, on the grounds that she was not fully a woman. The criteria were later changed, and after her death she was rehabilitated.

origins.name: Foeliedwarsstraat
origins.en: One of the products, important at the time, brought from the East Indies and stored here in the East India Company's warehouses (foelie is mace).

origins.name: Foeliestraat
origins.en: One of the products, important at the time, brought from the East Indies and stored here in the East India Company's warehouses (foelie is mace).

origins.name: Foersterhof
origins.en: Friedrich Wilhelm Foerster (1869-1959), founder of the modern work school (arbeidsschool).

origins.name: Fogostraat
origins.en: A volcano in Cape Verde that is still active.

origins.name: Fokke Simonszstraat
origins.en: Arend Fokke Simonsz (1755-1812), Amsterdam bookseller, poet and prose writer, who lived on the Looierssloot. Fokke was for a time in charge of the archives and antiquities, of which he left descriptions. The street was laid out on the Nieuwe Looierssloot, filled in in 1873.

origins.name: Fokkemast
origins.en: One of the masts (the foremost) of a ship: the foremast.

origins.name: Fokkezeil
origins.en: One of the sails of a ship (the foresail).

origins.name: Fonteinkruidstraat
origins.en: The name comes from the pondweed genus, of the family of the same name. Its leaves lie on the water surface or float under water, and its flowers are in green spikes.

origins.name: Foppingadreef
origins.en: A state, or farmstead, near Dronrijp (Friesland).

origins.name: Forintplantsoen
origins.en: The currency of Hungary (the forint).

origins.name: Formosastraat
origins.en: The island of Formosa, or Taiwan, off the coast of China, occupied by Japan until 1945 and Chinese after that. Taiwan is now in effect an independent state, although China regards the island as a Chinese province. The name, incidentally, is Portuguese: 'ilha formosa' means 'the beautiful island'.

origins.name: Fortuinstraat
origins.en: Named after the shipyard Het Fortuin (fortune), which was on the island of Wittenburg in the second half of the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Fosfaatweg
origins.en: Named after the phosphate factory to which this road and quay lead. Before 1949 the road was part of the Ringweg in the Amsterdammer Polder.

origins.name: Foucaultstraat
origins.en: Jean B.L. Foucault (1819-1868), French physicist. He demonstrated the rotation of the earth with a pendulum hung in the Panthéon in Paris, and discovered the induction (eddy) currents named after him.

origins.name: Fraijlemaborg
origins.en: The name of an estate in Slochteren. A borg was originally a stone fortification; the province of Groningen once had many borgen. The Fraeylemaborg is now a museum with period rooms.

origins.name: Frambozenstraat
origins.en: The fruit of the raspberry bush.

origins.name: Frances Harperstraat
origins.en: Frances Ellen Watkins Harper (1825-1911) was an African-American poet and writer.

origins.name: Francisco Faleirostraat
origins.en: An exiled Portuguese scholar who entered Spanish government service. His scientific work dealt with navigation and its problems. He supported Ferdinand Magellan in finding the route around South America.

origins.name: Franciscus Claessenstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1894-1945), born in Helden, died in the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp.

origins.name: Frank Martinus Arionstraat
origins.en: Frank Martinus Arion, pen name of Frank Efraim Martinus (Curaçao, 1936 - Curaçao, 2015), was a writer, poet and linguist. He worked in the Netherlands, Suriname and the Netherlands Antilles, and wrote in Dutch and Papiamentu. In 1955 Martinus Arion left for the Netherlands to study Dutch language and literature at Leiden University. There he came into contact with Cola Debrot, with whom he published his first collection of poems in 1957. He then founded an Antillean magazine, Encuentro Antilliano, with others. His debut novel Dubbelspel (double play, 1973) was his greatest success. In 1975 he taught at the teacher-training institute in Paramaribo.

origins.name: Frank van der Goesstraat
origins.en: Journalist and writer (1859-1939), a well-known socialist theorist. Co-founder of 'De Nieuwe Gids', founder of the SDAP in 1894, and foreign editor of 'Het Volk'.

origins.name: Frankemaheerdpad
origins.en: Named after a farm in Warffum (Groningen).

origins.name: Frankenstraat
origins.en: The franc is the currency of France, Belgium, Luxembourg and Switzerland.

origins.name: Frans Bastiaansestraat
origins.en: W.A.F. Bastiaanse (1868-1947), poet and writer. He wrote the Geschiedenis der Nederlandsche Letterkunde (history of Dutch literature, 1927).

origins.name: Frans de Wollantstraat
origins.en: An eighteenth-century Dutch military engineer who made his name in Russia under Catherine the Great as a designer of hydraulic works and builder of the city of Odessa.

origins.name: Frans Duwaerstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1911-1944), born in Amsterdam and executed by firing squad there too.

origins.name: Frans Halsstraat
origins.en: Painter (1580-1666) of portraits and militia group portraits.

origins.name: Frans Naerebouthof
origins.en: A Vlissingen pilot, known as a rescuer at sea (1748-1818). He became famous above all at the wreck of the Woestduin in 1779.

origins.name: Frans van Mierisstraat
origins.en: Frans van Mieris the Elder (1635-1681), painter of genre and history pieces. His father and his son were also well-known painters.

origins.name: Franz Kafkastraat
origins.en: Franz Kafka (1883-1924) was a German-language writer regarded as one of the most important authors of the twentieth century.

origins.name: Franz Zieglerstraat
origins.en: Photographer (1893-1939) who photographed members of the royal house and Hague society. Official court photographer from 1929.

origins.name: Fraunhoferstraat
origins.en: Joseph Fraunhofer (1787-1826), German physicist. He improved many optical instruments and discovered the lines in the solar spectrum (the Fraunhofer lines).

origins.name: Fred Petterbaan
origins.en: Frederik Hermanus Petter was a trade unionist and one of the leaders of the railway strike of 1903.

origins.name: Fred. Roeskestraat
origins.en: Frederik J. Roeske (1868-1961), conductor of the Royal Male Choir Apollo from 1891 to 1953, and also composer of music for a great many songs. Before it got this name, the street was part of the Prinses Irenestraat.

origins.name: Fred. Thomasstraat
origins.en: Fredericus F.X.M.D. Thomas (1906-1959), journalist, editor of the daily 'De Tijd' and author of 'Amsterdam, stad van mijn hart' (Amsterdam, city of my heart).

origins.name: Frederik Hendrikplantsoen
origins.en: Prince Frederik Hendrik (1584-1647), son of Prince William of Orange's fourth marriage, half-brother of Prince Maurice, and stadholder from 1625. His success as a military commander earned him the name 'stedendwinger' (tamer of cities). For some years the Frederik Hendrikplantsoen was first called Frederik Hendrikplein (council decision of 20 January 1886).

origins.name: Frederik Hendrikstraat
origins.en: Prince Frederik Hendrik (1584-1647), son of Prince William of Orange's fourth marriage, half-brother of Prince Maurice, and stadholder from 1625. His success as a military commander earned him the name 'stedendwinger' (tamer of cities). For some years the Frederik Hendrikplantsoen was first called Frederik Hendrikplein (council decision of 20 January 1886).

origins.name: Frederik van Dorpstraat
origins.en: A member of the Compromise of Nobles, of East Frisian descent (1547-1612). He fought at Heiligerlee and took part in the capture of Den Briel and the relief of Leiden.

origins.name: Frederik van Eedenstraat
origins.en: Writer and psychiatrist (1860-1932), co-founder of the literary magazine 'De Nieuwe Gids'. From 1894 he went his own way and founded a cooperative commune in Bussum. His works include 'Van de koele meren des doods' (the deeps of deliverance).

origins.name: Frederiksplein
origins.en: Prince Frederik Willem Karel (1798-1881), second son of King Willem I. Partly through his support the building of the Paleis voor Volksvlijt was promoted (opened 1864, burnt down 1929).

origins.name: Frederiksstraat
origins.en: Around 1880 Frederik Schröder provided a building loan for the houses along this street, which was then to be laid out, and so the street was named after him. The street was taken over from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under this name.

origins.name: Freek Oxstraat
origins.en: Frederik Johannes Marius Ox (1920-1944), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, killed on 15 June 1944 in a gunfight with Germans in the Euterpestraat (now the Gerrit van der Veenstraat).

origins.name: Fregatstraat
origins.en: A fast-sailing three-masted ship (a frigate).

origins.name: Fregelaan
origins.en: Gottlob Frege (1848-1925), German mathematician and philosopher, professor in Jena. He was the first to give a consistently worked-out reduction of mathematics to logic, and designed the Begriffsschrift, a symbolic notation for logic.

origins.name: Fresiastraat
origins.en: Named after the freesia, a plant.

origins.name: Freule Wttewaalpad
origins.en: Freule Christine Wilhelmine Isabelle Wttewaal van Stoetwegen (1901-1986), politician, member of the House of Representatives for the Christian Historical Union from 1945 to 1971. She sat on the parliamentary inquiry committee (1949-1956) that investigated the policy of the Dutch government in London during the Second World War.

origins.name: Frida Katzstraat
origins.en: Frida Mackay-Katz (Amsterdam, 29 July 1885 - Aerdenhout, 30 March 1963) was a pioneer as a lawyer and as a municipal, national and local politician, and a campaigner for women's suffrage.

origins.name: Frieslandstraat
origins.en: The province. Several nearby streets are named after Frisian castles.

origins.name: Frissenstein
origins.en: The name of a manor house in Deil (Gelderland).

origins.name: Frissensteinpad
origins.en: The name of a manor house in Deil (Gelderland).

origins.name: Frits Rotganshof
origins.en: Photographer (1912-1978), a master of the panoramic photograph. During the Second World War he secretly photographed the German occupation. After the war he photographed the activity in the ports of Rotterdam and Amsterdam. In the 1960s Rotgans worked on aviation photography and photomontages.

origins.name: Fritz Conijnstraat
origins.en: Fritz Gerhard Marie Conijn (1923-1944), resistance fighter and student, born in Alkmaar, executed by firing squad in Vught.

origins.name: Fritz Dietrich Kahlenbergstraat
origins.en: Filmmaker (1916-1995), who also took many photographs during the Second World War. In 1944 he brought the Amsterdam group of photographers together to record the last year of the occupation. The group later became known as 'De Ondergedoken Camera' (the hidden camera).

origins.name: Fröbelstraat
origins.en: Friedrich Wilhelm August Fröbel (1782-1852), German educator, who founded the first kindergarten in 1827.

origins.name: Funenkade
origins.en: The strip of land on which the Czaar Peterstraat, among others, was laid out came inside the city with the expansion of 1658 and was afterwards called the Funen. The name recalled the Danish island of Funen, where Admiral De Ruyter won a naval battle against the Swedes in 1659.

origins.name: Funenpark
origins.en: The strip of land on which the Czaar Peterstraat, among others, was laid out came inside the city with the expansion of 1658 and was afterwards called the Funen. The name recalled the Danish island of Funen, where Admiral De Ruyter won a naval battle against the Swedes in 1659.

origins.name: Funke Küpperstraat
origins.en: Albert Funke Küpper (1894-1934), illustrator and caricaturist, who worked for the political-satirical weekly 'De Notenkraker'.

origins.name: G.J. Scheurleerpad
origins.en: Gerardus Jacobus Scheurleer (1886-1948), tennis player, many times Dutch doubles champion with, among others, Diemer Kool.

origins.name: G.J. Scheurleerweg
origins.en: Gerardus Jacobus Scheurleer (1886-1948), tennis player, many times Dutch doubles champion with, among others, Diemer Kool.

origins.name: G.J.M. Sarlemijnstraat
origins.en: Gerardus Josephus Maria Sarlemijn (1909-1993), Amsterdam architect. With Adriaan Evers he designed in the conservative Bossche School style. He received the city of Amsterdam's Golden Pin for listing the city's monuments.

origins.name: G.T. Ketjenweg
origins.en: Gerard Tileman Ketjen, dealer in drugs and paints and the original founder of AKZO Nobel. In 1835 he founded the Ketjen sulphuric acid works on what is now the Marnixstraat. From 1916 production was concentrated in Amsterdam-Noord. In 1969 the Ketjen works merged with the company AKU to form AKZO.

origins.name: Gaandeweg
origins.en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

origins.name: Gaasperdammerpad
origins.en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp.

origins.name: Gaasperdammerweg
origins.en: After the hamlet of the same name on the small river Gaasp.

origins.name: Gaasperparkpad
origins.en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp.

origins.name: Gaasperplaspad
origins.en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp. The Gaasperplas itself is an artificial lake up to 35 metres deep, created by digging sand for building the Bijlmermeer.

origins.name: Gaasperzoompad
origins.en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp.

origins.name: Gaaspstraat
origins.en: The small river Gaasp, the part of the Weespertrekvaart that was not dug.

origins.name: Gaasterlandpad
origins.en: The southern part of Friesland, between Stavoren and Lemmer. Here are the only places where the Frisian coast does not need dikes to protect it.

origins.name: Gaasterlandstraat
origins.en: The southern part of Friesland, between Stavoren and Lemmer. Here are the only places where the Frisian coast does not need dikes to protect it.

origins.name: Gabriël Metsustraat
origins.en: Painter (1629-1667), mainly of genre pieces, and a pupil of Gerard Dou. A street had already been named after Metsu on 10 June 1880, but that name was changed to Paulus Potterstraat in 1893.

origins.name: Gabriela Mistralstraat
origins.en: Gabriela Mistral (1889-1957) was a Chilean poet, the first Latin American to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

origins.name: Gaffelaarspad
origins.en: A ship with a flat bottom and a round stem, used mainly on inland waterways.

origins.name: Gaffelstraat
origins.en: A farm implement (a pitchfork) for pitching hay.

origins.name: Galantstraat
origins.en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

origins.name: Galastraat
origins.en: A sweet, juicy apple from New Zealand, a variety that arose in the first half of the twentieth century.

origins.name: Galgenbrug
origins.en: The name (gallows bridge) refers to the view from this bridge of the gallows of the Volewijk, which stood there until 1795.

origins.name: Galgenstraat
origins.en: The view from this street of the gallows of the Volewijk is the origin of this name. In 1662 the city council decided to change the name to Prinsendwarsstraat, but that name never caught on.

origins.name: Galggouw
origins.en: This gouw (village road), in the municipality of Broek in Waterland, owes its name to an old gallows field.

origins.name: Galileïplantsoen
origins.en: Galileo Galilei (1564-1642), Italian mathematician, professor at Pisa and Padua. He discovered the laws of falling bodies and of the pendulum, built the first telescope and discovered many celestial bodies.

origins.name: Galjoenstraat
origins.en: A heavy, cumbersome sailing ship of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries (a galleon), with three or four masts and a high forecastle and sterncastle.

origins.name: Galjootstraat
origins.en: A ship: a flat-bottomed merchant ship with leeboards for coastal trade (a galliot).

origins.name: Galvanistraat
origins.en: Luigi Galvani (1737-1798), Italian physicist, who discovered electricity generated by chemical action.

origins.name: Galwin
origins.en: A corrupted spelling of the Irish port of Galway, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Gamerenstraat
origins.en: The Gamerenstraat (formerly Van Gamerenstraat) is named after Virginie Gameren (Curaçao, 19 March 1833 - date and place of death unknown). Virginie was an enslaved woman who fought for her freedom by starting legal proceedings against her owner. She won, and so forced the Ministry of the Colonies to grant her freedom. She took the surname Gameren, which gave her and her children autonomy.

origins.name: Ganzebloemstraat
origins.en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

origins.name: Ganzenhoefpad
origins.en: The name of a farm on the Vecht near Maarsseveen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Ganzenveldstraat
origins.en: The Ganzenveld is part of the Schoorl dunes (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Ganzenweg
origins.en: The water bird (the duck).

origins.name: Garcia Lorcastraat
origins.en: Federico García Lorca (1898-1936) was a progressive Spanish poet and playwright.

origins.name: Gare du Nord
origins.en: A major railway station in the north of Paris, opened in 1864.

origins.name: Garstkamp
origins.en: The name of a farm near Beesd (Gelderland).

origins.name: Gasthuismolensteeg
origins.en: On the city rampart (the Singel), where the alley is now, stood the mill of the Sint Elisabethsgasthuis (fifteenth and sixteenth centuries). The Sint Elisabethsgasthuis was the city's oldest hospital, founded in the fourteenth century. In 1492 its building was added to the city hall. Both buildings were later demolished to build the new city hall (now the palace). Before 1913 this was the Wijde Gasthuismolensteeg; earlier still the names Molensteeg and Benninghstraat occur.

origins.name: Gatwickstraat
origins.en: The name of one of London's airports.

origins.name: Gebroeders A. en B. Wolfswinkelweg
origins.en: The brothers Antoon (1919-1942) and Bertus (1921-1942) Wolfswinkel, resistance fighters. They distributed clandestine material, collected money for the resistance and belonged to a sabotage group at the Fokker factory in Amsterdam-Noord, where they worked. They took an active part in the February Strike of 1941. On 19 November 1942 both were executed by firing squad at Soesterberg.

origins.name: Gedempt Hamerkanaal
origins.en: Refers to the former Hamerkanaal (gedempt: filled in).

origins.name: Gedempte Begijnensloot
origins.en: The hof (courtyard), founded in the fourteenth century, was built to house beguines (lay sisters). The Begijnhof, together with the Sint Luciënklooster, was originally surrounded entirely by water. Behind the houses of the Kalverstraat ran a ditch, the Begijnensloot, which led from the Spui, not yet filled in at the time, to the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. This ditch was neglected, and so what remained of it was filled in in 1865. It was given the name Gedempte Begijnensloot, a name made official by a council decision in 1914.

origins.name: Gedempte Insteekhaven
origins.en: This side basin (insteekhaven) was part of the shipyard of the Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij (ADM). Several floating dry docks lay in it. It was filled in to build housing on the site.

origins.name: Geduld
origins.en: The ability to wait a long time to reach a goal (patience).

origins.name: Geelbekstraat
origins.en: The songbird (the yellowhammer), of the finch family.

origins.name: Geelvinckssteeg
origins.en: On the corner of this alley there once stood two warehouses called De Geelvinck. The name first appears in the last years of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Geer Ban
origins.en: The Geer Ban, or Vrije Geer, was one of the four parts that made up the municipality of Sloten in earlier centuries. A ban was in the old days an administrative district; a number of bannen together formed a bailiwick.

origins.name: Geerdinkhof
origins.en: A very old name of a plot of land at Vasse near Tubbergen (Overijssel).

origins.name: Geerdinkhofpad
origins.en: A very old name of a plot of land at Vasse near Tubbergen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Geerdinkhofweg
origins.en: A very old name of a plot of land at Vasse near Tubbergen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Geert Grootestraat
origins.en: Philosopher (1340-1384), founder of the Brethren of the Common Life. He railed against the abuses in the church, but also against heretics. He founded the religious renewal known as the Modern Devotion.

origins.name: Geertje Wielemaplein
origins.en: Swimmer (1934-2009), who won a silver medal in the 100 metres backstroke at the 1952 Olympic Games in Helsinki. In 1954 she became the Netherlands' first Sportswoman of the Year.

origins.name: Geertruida van Lierstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1915-1969), involved in many clandestine activities and a member of the Amsterdam resistance group CS-6.

origins.name: Geervliet
origins.en: An old little town (town rights 1381) on the Brielse Maas and the now silted-up Bernisse (Zuid-Holland).

origins.name: Geldersekade
origins.en: At the city's second expansion on the east side, today's Geldersekade was the city moat. So the inner bank (on the Zeedijk side) is the oldest, built around 1500. The other side lay outside the city until 1585. In the seventeenth century the old side was called partly Keulse kaai (Cologne quay) and further on Gelderse kaai, and for a short time also Londense kaai or Engelse kaai. The names came from the landing stages here where ships moored that sailed to the towns of Gelderland, to Cologne, London and other English ports. Some remains of the city wall built here around 1500 between the Waag and the Schreierstoren can still be found in the quay wall and by the Bantammerbrug.

origins.name: Geldershoofd
origins.en: The name of a country estate near Brummen (Gelderland). Before their renovation in 1983, the buildings Geldershoofd and Gravestein together formed the Gliphoeve building.

origins.name: Geleenstraat
origins.en: A small river in South Limburg that flows into the Maas at Stevensweert.

origins.name: Geleyn Bouwenszstraat
origins.en: A captain of the Sea Beggars at the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Gelrestraat
origins.en: The old name of Gelderland. Also a county (1046-1339) and then, until 1795, a duchy, roughly matching today's Gelderland plus part of Limburg and Germany.

origins.name: Generaal Vetterstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Augustinus Vetter (1837-1907), military commander-in-chief of the expeditions to Lombok (1894) and Aceh (1896).

origins.name: Generatorstraat
origins.en: The machine for generating electric current.

origins.name: Genhoes
origins.en: Genhoes castle, or Oud-Valkenburg, near Valkenburg (Limburg), built around 1500: a late-Gothic main building of marlstone, altered and extended in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and restored from 1962.

origins.name: Gentiaanplein
origins.en: The plant family (gentians).

origins.name: Gentiaanstraat
origins.en: The plant family (gentians).

origins.name: George Balanchinestraat
origins.en: George Balanchine was an American choreographer of Georgian descent, regarded as one of the most important choreographers of twentieth-century classical ballet.

origins.name: George Gershwinlaan
origins.en: American composer and pianist (1898-1937) who worked jazz elements into classical music. He wrote the opera 'Porgy and Bess' and countless musicals, as well as piano works, orchestral works and concertos.

origins.name: George Gershwinplein
origins.en: American composer and pianist (1898-1990) who worked jazz elements into classical music. He wrote the opera 'Porgy and Bess' and countless musicals, as well as piano works, orchestral works and concertos.

origins.name: George Sandstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Aurore Dupin, Baroness Dudevant (1804-1876), French novelist. Through her free way of life and in her work she stood up for the unrestrained development of women. She counts as the first truly emancipated woman of the modern era.

origins.name: George Sliekerkade
origins.en: George Christiaan Slieker (1861-1945), the first Dutch film exhibitor, who toured fairs and markets with his travelling cinema.

origins.name: George Westinghousestraat
origins.en: American engineer (1846-1914) who invented the Westinghouse brake named after him: an air brake, used especially on the railways.

origins.name: Geraardsbergenstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of East Flanders.

origins.name: Geraniumweg
origins.en: The garden and house plant.

origins.name: Gerard Borstkade
origins.en: Jacobus Gerardus Gerbrant Borst (1902-1975), internist, for 35 years professor at the University of Amsterdam and head of the internal medicine clinic at the Binnengasthuis. During the war years he was, among other things, one of the leaders of the doctors' resistance. Founder of modern blood transfusion therapy.

origins.name: Gerard Brandtstraat
origins.en: Remonstrant theologian (1626-1685) who wrote church history at first and poetry later. Until 1896 the street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel and was called H.G. Kosterstraat, after a building contractor (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 5 October 1880).

origins.name: Gerard Callenburgstraat
origins.en: Fleet commander (1642-1722). Captain of Admiral De Ruyter's flagship, he took part in the naval battles of Solebay (1672) and off Etna (1676) and in the capture of Gibraltar (1704).

origins.name: Gerard Douplein
origins.en: Painter (1613-1675), a representative of the Leiden school, a pupil of Rembrandt and teacher of, among others, Metsu and Van Mieris.

origins.name: Gerard Doustraat
origins.en: Painter (1613-1675), a representative of the Leiden school, a pupil of Rembrandt and teacher of, among others, Metsu and Van Mieris.

origins.name: Gerard Hulst van Keulenstraat
origins.en: From 1756 Gerard Hulst van Keulen (1733-1801) ran the well-known firm of Van Keulen, which for two centuries (c. 1680-1885) was based in Amsterdam on the corner of the Nieuwebrugsteeg and the Prins Hendrikkade. The firm specialised in making and selling sea charts and nautical instruments, and published and sold books, mainly on nautical subjects.

origins.name: Gerard Revebrug
origins.en: Gerard Kornelis van het Reve (1923-2006), writer and poet. With Harry Mulisch (1927-2010) and Willem Frederik Hermans (1921-1995) he formed the Big Three of post-war literature. His works include 'De avonden' (the evenings, 1947), 'Werther Nieland' (1949) and 'Nader tot U' (nearer to thee, 1966). He received the P.C. Hooft Prize (1968) and the Prize for Dutch Literature (2001).

origins.name: Gerard Ruttenhof
origins.en: Film director (1902-1982). With 'Dood water' (dead water, 1934), about the building of the Afsluitdijk, and 'Rubber' (1935), about a planter's wife in Suriname, he made two important Dutch feature films of the 1930s.

origins.name: Gerard Schaepstraat
origins.en: Councillor and schepen (alderman) of Amsterdam (1594-1666), ambassador to the English and Danish courts.

origins.name: Gerard Terborgstraat
origins.en: Painter (1617-1681) of portraits and genre pieces.

origins.name: Gerardus van der Groeplaan
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1922-1945) who worked at the Fokker factory in Amsterdam-Noord and belonged to a sabotage group there. He distributed 'De Waarheid' and raised money for the resistance. Sentenced to death in 1942, a sentence commuted to life imprisonment with penal servitude. Freed by the French, he died on 16 July 1945.

origins.name: Gerda Brautigamstraat
origins.en: Gerarda Brautigam (1913-1982), politician and journalist. Editor at Het Vrije Volk from 1945 to 1967 and member of the House of Representatives for the Labour Party (PvdA) from 1963 to 1972. She worked above all for consumer affairs, which made her very well known.

origins.name: Gerrie Knetemannlaan
origins.en: Racing cyclist (1951-2004), nicknamed 'de Kneet'. His greatest success was the world road championship in 1978.

origins.name: Gerrit Bronkepad
origins.en: Gerrit Bronke (nineteenth century) designed the church in Holysloot (a national monument) in 1846. For this neighbourhood the chosen category was the names of Dutch architects involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

origins.name: Gerrit Mannourystraat
origins.en: Mathematician and philosopher (1867-1956), professor at the University of Amsterdam and one of the most important Dutch mathematicians of this century.

origins.name: Gerrit Stuyverstraat
origins.en: A Sea Beggar who fought at the relief of Haarlem in 1572.

origins.name: Gerrit van den Boschpad
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1911-1944) who played an important part in distributing the clandestine paper 'De Waarheid'. He died in the Dachau concentration camp.

origins.name: Gerrit van der Puijstraat
origins.en: A resident of Sloten (1915-1988) who worked for the Sloten community for many years.

origins.name: Gerrit van der Veenstraat
origins.en: Gerrit Jan van der Veen (1902-1944), resistance fighter and sculptor by profession, who won the Prix de Rome for his sculpture. He took an active part in the resistance. Van der Veen was one of the instigators of the attack on the population register (27 March 1943) and was executed by firing squad in the dunes near Overveen. The street was previously called Euterpestraat, after the muse of music and poetry, and during the occupation of 1940-1945 was notorious because the German Sicherheitsdienst (SD) was based in the girls' secondary school (Meisjes-HBS).

origins.name: Gerrit van Erkelstraat
origins.en: Gerrit van Erkel (1860-1937), leader of the radical-socialist trade union movement.

origins.name: Gerrit Versteegstraat
origins.en: Architect (1873-1938) who built part of Tuindorp Watergraafsmeer, worked with Hendrik Berlage on the western part of the Transvaalbuurt, and designed the housing blocks on the Koekoekstraat in Noord.

origins.name: Geschutswerf
origins.en: Geschut (ordnance) is the collective name for cannon and heavy machine guns. The street lies where the Ordnance Yard of the Admiralty of Amsterdam was; guns were made here in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Geulstraat
origins.en: A small river in South Limburg, a tributary of the Maas. The Geul valley forms part of the border with Belgium.

origins.name: Geurt Brinkgrevebrug
origins.en: Monument conservationist, sculptor and writer (1917-2005). An advocate for preserving the historic city centre, he eventually brought about a turning point in thinking about the old cultural heritage. He also played a major part in keeping the old street pattern of the Nieuwmarkt neighbourhood. He received the Silver Medal (Zilveren Penning) in 1982.

origins.name: Geuzenkade
origins.en: At first meant as a term of abuse (geuzen: beggars), but taken as a title of honour by the Confederated Nobles (verbonden edelen) in the fight against Spain. Later the fighting name of all opponents of Spain in the Eighty Years' War. The Korte Geuzenstraat was earlier part of the Geuzenstraat.

origins.name: Geuzenstraat
origins.en: At first meant as a term of abuse (geuzen: beggars), but taken as a title of honour by the Confederated Nobles (verbonden edelen) in the fight against Spain. Later the fighting name of all opponents of Spain in the Eighty Years' War. The Korte Geuzenstraat was earlier part of the Geuzenstraat.

origins.name: Gevlebrug
origins.en: The Swedish port of Gävle on the Gulf of Bothnia, an important timber export port and now one of Sweden's largest oil ports.

origins.name: Gibraltarstraat
origins.en: The southern tip of Spain, named here for the naval battle against the Spanish in 1607 in which Jacob van Heemskerck was killed.

origins.name: Giessenburg
origins.en: A lost castle at Giessen-Oudekerk, of which some remains survive.

origins.name: Gieterij
origins.en: This and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij (ADM). To recall that former use, the names of the various workshops were used for the streets, in this case the shipyard's foundry (gieterij).

origins.name: Gietersstraat
origins.en: Named after 't Giethuis, the city's gun and bell foundry, which stood here from 1614 to 1821. The street name first came into use in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Gijsbrecht van Aemstelstraat
origins.en: After Gijsbrecht IV (c. 1235-1303), the last lord of Aemstel to be Lord of Amsterdam, and bailiff of Amstelland. Made famous by Vondel's tragedy.

origins.name: Gijsbrecht van IJselsteinstraat
origins.en: Bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland from 1358 to 1361.

origins.name: Gillis Steltmanstraat
origins.en: A Sea Beggar who became known at the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Gillis van Ledenberchstraat
origins.en: Clerk of the States of Utrecht (1550-1618), a supporter of Van Oldenbarnevelt, imprisoned by Prince Maurice. The street was earlier called Tweede Hugo de Grootdwarsstraat (council decisions of 13 October 1897 and 1 September 1908).

origins.name: Glauberweg
origins.en: Johann Rudolf Glauber (1604-1670), German chemist and physician. He discovered the laxative effect of the Glauber's salt named after him, used against bile complaints.

origins.name: Glitterstraat
origins.en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

origins.name: Gloriantstraat
origins.en: A fourteenth-century abel spel (a serious secular play).

origins.name: Goed Geluimd hof
origins.en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

origins.name: Goeman Borgesiusstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Goeman Borgesius (1847-1917), liberal statesman, Minister of the Interior from 1897 to 1901 (Compulsory Education Act, Housing Act, Accidents Act).

origins.name: Goereestraat
origins.en: Part of the Zuid-Holland island of Goeree-Overflakkee.

origins.name: Golfbaanpad
origins.en: A path by the De Hoge Dijk golf course.

origins.name: Gooiluststraat
origins.en: An estate in 's-Graveland, of which the Corversbos was originally also part. 's-Graveland is a stretch of Gooi heath from which the sand was dug away (afzanding). Once the sand was removed, Amsterdam regents laid out country estates and nurseries here in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Gooioord
origins.en: The name of a manor house in Bussum (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Gooise Kant
origins.en: A neighbourhood access road that comes out on and connects to the K-buurt and the Gooiseweg.

origins.name: Gooiseweg
origins.en: The road leads towards Het Gooi.

origins.name: Gordijnensteeg
origins.en: Named after the sixteenth- and seventeenth-century residents Willem and Samuel du Gardijn. At that time the alley was also known as Bloeddwarsstraat.

origins.name: Gorontalostraat
origins.en: A town on the island of Sulawesi (Celebes) in Indonesia.

origins.name: Gorsstraat
origins.en: A name used in Zuid-Holland for vegetated land outside the dikes that floods only at high water (elsewhere called schor or kwelder: salt marsh).

origins.name: Gosschalklaan
origins.en: Isaac Gosschalk (1838-1907), one of the most important Dutch architects of the nineteenth century. In 1885 Gosschalk was commissioned by the Imperial Continental Gas Association to design the buildings of the Westergasfabriek.

origins.name: Goudbalpad
origins.en: An old Dutch pear variety. The street lies on the former De Bongerd allotment complex.

origins.name: Gouden Leeuw
origins.en: The name of a farm in the Haarlemmermeer (the golden lion). (The name also occurs in Hummelo and Leiden.)

origins.name: Goudestein
origins.en: A castle near Maarssen on the Vecht, dating from 1754, built for the Amsterdam burgomaster Huydecoper.

origins.name: Goudreinetstraat
origins.en: The fruit, a variety of apple (golden reinette).

origins.name: Goudriaanstraat
origins.en: Bernardus Hermanus Goudriaan (1796-1842), chief engineer of Rijkswaterstaat, appointed by the government to assess the first railway plans.

origins.name: Goudsbloemstraat
origins.en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

origins.name: Gouwenaarssteeg
origins.en: Named after the broker Willem Jac. Gouwenaar, who lived on the corner of the Stromarkt around 1600.

origins.name: Govert Flinckstraat
origins.en: Painter (1615-1660), a pupil of Rembrandt, known above all for his militia group portraits and portraits.

origins.name: Gowin Knightstraat
origins.en: English physician (1713-1772) who in the eighteenth century published on magnetic experiments relating to the compass used by sailors.

origins.name: Graaf Florisstraat
origins.en: Floris V (1254-1296), Count of Holland, murdered by the nobles. Count Floris granted Amsterdam its oldest known privilege, which in 1275 gave 'den luden bij Amstelredam' (the people near Amstelredam) exemption from tolls. It is also the oldest dated document in which the name Amsterdam appears.

origins.name: Graafschapstraat
origins.en: A much-used name for part of the Achterhoek in Gelderland, originally the old county (graafschap) of Zutphen. Part of the street was renamed Jacob Soetendorpstraat in 1978.

origins.name: Graanstraat
origins.en: The collective name for the farm crops that belong to the grass family (grain).

origins.name: Graftdijkerstraat
origins.en: A village in Noord-Holland between the Beemster and the Schermer.

origins.name: Graham Bellstraat
origins.en: Alexander Graham Bell (1847-1922), Scottish physicist, who built the first practical telephone.

origins.name: Gran Paradiso
origins.en: The highest mountain entirely within Italy, 4061 metres.

origins.name: Granaatstraat
origins.en: A semi-precious stone (garnet).

origins.name: Granidastraat
origins.en: A tragedy by P.C. Hooft (1602-1605).

origins.name: Grasrijk
origins.en: A former farm on the Uitweg, demolished to build the garden city of Osdorp.

origins.name: Grasweg
origins.en: The commonest and largest plant family (grasses).

origins.name: Gravenstraat
origins.en: The counts of the House of Hainaut (1299-1345). When they were in Amsterdam, they stayed at an inn that stood here at the time. The little street appears as early as the beginning of the fifteenth century as 's-Gravenstraat (the count's street).

origins.name: Gravestein
origins.en: Named after a Surinamese plantation. Before their renovation in 1983, the buildings Gravestein and Geldershoofd together formed the building called Gliphoeve.

origins.name: Grensstraat
origins.en: Before 1896 the street formed the boundary (grens) between Amsterdam and Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Grevelingenstraat
origins.en: A sea channel between the islands of Goeree and Schouwen, now closed off from the open sea by the Grevelingendam.

origins.name: Grianestraat
origins.en: A tragicomedy by Bredero from 1612.

origins.name: Griendstraat
origins.en: The collective name for a growth of woody plants (mostly willows) that are cut regularly (osier beds). Griend or grint land lies in or along water.

origins.name: Griftstraat
origins.en: A dug channel on the Veluwe that flows into the IJssel at Hattem.

origins.name: Grimbergenstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Grimburgwal
origins.en: After the water called the Grim, which formed the city's southern boundary from 1342 to about 1400 (grim = muddy ditch).

origins.name: Griseldestraat
origins.en: A sproke from 1393. A sproke is a medieval rhymed tale, comparable to a boert or farce.

origins.name: Groen van Prinstererstraat
origins.en: Guillaume Groen van Prinsterer (1801-1876), statesman and historian, leader of the Anti-Revolutionaries from 1849 to 1866, and a fierce opponent of liberals and Roman Catholics.

origins.name: Groenburgwal
origins.en: The land between the Kloveniersburgwal and the Zwanenburgwal, where the cloth-drying frames stood and which was added to the city in 1593, was then the site of the dye works. This canal was therefore originally called Verwersgracht (dyers' canal). Early in the seventeenth century the name Groenburgwal arose, because there were green dye works here in particular.

origins.name: Groene Ridderhof
origins.en: After Jan Claesz. Groene Ridder, properly Backer (1588-?). He owned the ship De Groene Ridder (the green knight), but around 1631 decided to run a skippers' inn by the Kadoelenbreek. Around 1538 he sold it again. On this spot, level with Landsmeerderdijk 195, there has been an inn or café ever since.

origins.name: Groene Ridderpad
origins.en: After Jan Claesz. Groene Ridder, properly Backer (1588-?). He owned the ship De Groene Ridder (the green knight), but around 1631 decided to run a skippers' inn by the Kadoelenbreek. Around 1538 he sold it again. On this spot, level with Landsmeerderdijk 195, there has been an inn or café ever since.

origins.name: Groenehuyzen
origins.en: A former farm in the old municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Groenendaalstraat
origins.en: An estate near Heemstede (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Groeneveen
origins.en: An old sixteenth-century patrician house in Velsen (also called Papenburg).

origins.name: Groenhoedenveem
origins.en: A veem is a company that stores goods in its warehouses and delivers them from there. Each veem had its own emblem, after which it was named. These could be hats of different colours and shapes (among them Groenhoeden, green hats, and Klapmutsen). They also took their names from where their workmen came from (among them the Vriesseveem and the Zeeuwse Veem).

origins.name: Groenhoven
origins.en: The name of several farms (Leiden, Loosduinen, Wassenaar and Kerkwijk).

origins.name: Groenlandia
origins.en: A whaler that sailed from Oostzanerwerf around 1759, owned by the shipowner Aard Speciaal (1717-1760).

origins.name: Groenlandstraat
origins.en: An island in the Atlantic Ocean, north-east of Canada. Greenland is part of the Kingdom of Denmark and is the largest island in the world.

origins.name: Groenlust
origins.en: A farm on the Noorderweg, against the Enge Wormer, in the Wijde Wormer.

origins.name: Groenmarktkade
origins.en: Groenmarkt is short for Groentemarkt (vegetable market), held here from 1896 to 1934. In 1934 the Centrale Markthallen opened on the Jan van Galenstraat, after which this vegetable market was closed.

origins.name: Groenpad
origins.en: A former lane in the old municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Groesbeekdreef
origins.en: The name of the dreef (avenue) above it.

origins.name: Groetstraat
origins.en: The Noord-Holland village on the edge of the dunes.

origins.name: Groezestraat
origins.en: Silted-up land outside the dikes with light vegetation, also known as kwelder, gors, schor or schol (salt marsh).

origins.name: Groningenstraat
origins.en: The province. The adjoining streets are named after Groningen castles (borgen).

origins.name: Groot Blankenberg
origins.en: A former castle, destroyed in 1381. On its site now stands the house Blankenberg, built as a convent in 1825, near Cadier en Keer (Limburg).

origins.name: Groot-Essenburg
origins.en: A building from 1652 near Hierden on the Veluwe, built on the foundations of a thirteenth-century castle and restored in 1929.

origins.name: Grootslagstraat
origins.en: A large polder west of Enkhuizen.

origins.name: Grootzeil
origins.en: One of the sails of a ship (the foresail).

origins.name: Grootzeilhof
origins.en: One of the sails of a ship (the foresail).

origins.name: Grossglockner
origins.en: The highest mountain in Austria, 3787 metres.

origins.name: Grote Beerstraat
origins.en: The constellation (the Great Bear).

origins.name: Grote Bickersstraat
origins.en: These streets are on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr Johan Bicker (1591-1653), a shipbuilder and merchant, and a schepen (magistrate) and burgomaster of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets later laid out on the island automatically took the name of its founder.

origins.name: Grote Diestraat
origins.en: Literally 'great water', to distinguish it from the Kleine Die further on. The overtoom (a place where boats were hauled over a dam) was level with the Nieuwendijk.

origins.name: Grote Ruwenberg
origins.en: Of this castle near Sint-Michielsgestel (Noord-Brabant) only a small tower with loopholes remains. The rest was altered and extended into a reformatory.

origins.name: Grote Wittenburgerstraat
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

origins.name: Grubbehoeve
origins.en: A farm near Albergen, in Tubbergen (Overijssel). It is named after the Grubbe family, mentioned as early as 1394.

origins.name: Guggenheimlaan
origins.en: The Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright and built in 1956, known for the gallery that spirals around the central hall. The core of its modern art collection was assembled by the multimillionaire Solomon Guggenheim.

origins.name: Guido Gezellestraat
origins.en: Flemish priest and poet (1830-1899) with a very large body of work, above all a nature poet.

origins.name: Guldehandsteeg
origins.en: The sign of the inn 'In de gulde Hant' (in the golden hand) gave the name here. The inn stood on the corner with the Warmoesstraat in the sixteenth century. The alley ends in water steps down to the Damrak, which is why the name Watersteeg also occurs in the Middle Ages. The present name was put back in the street register around 1980, after being left out for about a hundred years.

origins.name: Gulden Kruis
origins.en: The name of a patrician house in Beverwijk (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Gulden Kruispad
origins.en: The name of a patrician house in Beverwijk (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Gulden Winckelplantsoen
origins.en: After a poem by Vondel from 1613.

origins.name: Gulden Winckelstraat
origins.en: After a poem by Vondel from 1613.

origins.name: Guldenpromenade
origins.en: Until the euro was introduced on 1 January 2002, the guilder was the Dutch currency.

origins.name: Gunterstein
origins.en: A castle on the right bank of the Vecht near Breukelen, built in the thirteenth century and lived in by Johan van Oldenbarnevelt from 1611 to 1619. The present building was put up after the French destroyed it in 1672.

origins.name: Gustav Mahlerlaan
origins.en: Austrian composer and conductor (1860-1911), one of the most important conductors of his time. His compositions linked late Romanticism with the modern period of classical music. Mahler had a special bond with Amsterdam, which he first visited in 1903 at the invitation of Willem Mengelberg, conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra. That visit began a close relationship between the orchestra and the composer.

origins.name: Gustav Mahlerplein
origins.en: Austrian composer and conductor (1860-1911), one of the most important conductors of his time. His compositions linked late Romanticism with the modern period of classical music. Mahler had a special bond with Amsterdam, which he first visited in 1903 at the invitation of Willem Mengelberg, conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra. That visit began a close relationship between the orchestra and the composer.

origins.name: Gutserstraat
origins.en: Someone who cuts out wood, for example, with a gouge (guts: a chisel with a hollow blade). The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

origins.name: Guus Trestorffstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1905-1944), born in Amsterdam and executed by firing squad there.

origins.name: Gyroscoopweg
origins.en: A fast-spinning body built symmetrically around an axis of rotation, used for ship's compasses. The instrument was invented by Foucault.

origins.name: H. Cleyndertweg
origins.en: Hendrik Cleyndert A.zn (1881-1958), originally a grain merchant in Nieuwendam by trade. He founded government care for landscape and recreation, and was a board member of the Society for the Preservation of Nature Monuments in the Netherlands (Natuurmonumenten), Bond Heemschut and the Hendrick de Keyser Society.

origins.name: H. Diesveldsingel
origins.en: The name is misspelt. Johannes Henricus (Harry) Diesveldt (1918-1944), resistance fighter and Engelandvaarder (one who escaped to England). He returned from England as a secret agent and wireless operator, was arrested in Amsterdam and executed by firing squad in Vught.

origins.name: H. Gerhardstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Gerhard (1829-1886), Amsterdam tailor and one of the socialist pioneers, co-founder of De Dageraad in 1856. He represented the 'First Socialist International', founded in 1864, in the Netherlands.

origins.name: H. Stolleplantsoen
origins.en: Heinrich Wilhelm Christian Stolle (1924-2006), architect and furniture designer. He was in a partnership with Frans van Gool and Arnold Oyevaar that designed 1100 homes in the Buikslotermeer.

origins.name: H.A.J. Baanderskade
origins.en: Herman Ambrosius Jan Baanders (1876-1953), architect of the Amsterdam School. His designs include the Amsterdams Lyceum on the Valeriusplein and housing on the Rooseveltlaan and the Uiterwaardenstraat.

origins.name: H.J. Algrastraat
origins.en: Hendrik Algra (1896-1982), journalist and Anti-Revolutionary politician, editor-in-chief of the 'Friesch Dagblad'. From 1946 to 1969 he sat in the Senate (Eerste Kamer) for the Anti-Revolutionary Party, concentrating on defence, foreign affairs and education.

origins.name: H.J.E. Wenckebachweg
origins.en: Henri Johan Eduard Wenckebach (1861-1924), founder and director of the Koninklijke Nederlandsche Hoogovens en Staalfabrieken (Royal Dutch Blast Furnaces and Steelworks). The street's first name (Industrieweg, council decision of 2 October 1963) was withdrawn at the request of the municipality of Ouder-Amstel, because Duivendrecht already had an Industrieweg.

origins.name: H.J.M. Walenkampstraat
origins.en: Hermanus Johannes Maria Walenkamp (1871-1933), architect and graphic designer, who trained with P.J.H. Cuypers. His work includes the Zaanhof housing in the Spaarndammerbuurt.

origins.name: H.M. Kraaijvangerstraat
origins.en: Herman Kraaijvanger (1903-1981), architect, who set up an architectural practice with his brother. The firm's pre-war work belongs to the tradition of Dutch brick architecture and was built almost entirely for Catholic clients.

origins.name: H.T. Zwiersplantsoen
origins.en: Henri Tino Zwiers (1900-1992), architect, born in Amsterdam, a Dutch pioneer of building with prefabricated elements, as in Terrasdorp. From 1938 he was a professor in Delft.

origins.name: Haag en Veld
origins.en: A patrician house in Velsen (Noord-Holland), first mentioned in 1671.

origins.name: Haaksbergweg
origins.en: The name of a hill near Haaksbergen.

origins.name: Haardstee
origins.en: The name of a farm near Steenderen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Haarlemmer Houttuinen
origins.en: To extend the existing timber stores, some plots were set aside after 1612 for stacking timber (houttuinen: timber yards). They got this name from their position parallel to the Haarlemmerstraat and Haarlemmerdijk. It took on the character of a street when the quay was widened and built up with houses in the nineteenth century and the railway embankment was laid. Around 1970 that character changed again when most of the buildings were demolished and a wide road was built to take traffic off the Haarlemmerdijk and Haarlemmerstraat. The widening also removed the Westerdokstraat, the Korte Westerdokstraat and the Teerplein.

origins.name: Haarlemmerdijk
origins.en: The city of Haarlem. Before the city's expansion of 1593 the Haarlemmerpoort (Haarlem gate) stood at the end of the Nieuwendijk, so the Haarlemmerdijk lay outside the city. In 1593 the stretch as far as the Korte Prinsengracht was brought inside the city and named Haarlemmerstraat. Some years later (1612) the next stretch became city territory but kept the name Haarlemmerdijk. From about 1615 the Haarlemmerpoort (by Hendrick de Keyser) stood on the Haarlemmerplein. In 1837 that gate was pulled down and rebuilt, and at King Willem II's entry into the city in 1840 it was renamed Willemspoort.

origins.name: Haarlemmermeerstraat
origins.en: The municipality of that name, formed after the lake was drained in 1852.

origins.name: Haarlemmerplein
origins.en: The city of Haarlem. Before the city's expansion of 1593 the Haarlemmerpoort (Haarlem gate) stood at the end of the Nieuwendijk, so the Haarlemmerdijk lay outside the city. In 1593 the stretch as far as the Korte Prinsengracht was brought inside the city and named Haarlemmerstraat. Some years later (1612) the next stretch became city territory but kept the name Haarlemmerdijk. From about 1615 the Haarlemmerpoort (by Hendrick de Keyser) stood on the Haarlemmerplein. In 1837 that gate was pulled down and rebuilt, and at King Willem II's entry into the city in 1840 it was renamed Willemspoort.

origins.name: Haarlemmersluis
origins.en: This bridge is named after the Haarlemmerstraat, the road out of Amsterdam to Haarlem.

origins.name: Haarlemmerstraat
origins.en: The city of Haarlem. Before the city's expansion of 1593 the Haarlemmerpoort (Haarlem gate) stood at the end of the Nieuwendijk, so the Haarlemmerdijk lay outside the city. In 1593 the stretch as far as the Korte Prinsengracht was brought inside the city and named Haarlemmerstraat. Some years later (1612) the next stretch became city territory but kept the name Haarlemmerdijk. From about 1615 the Haarlemmerpoort (by Hendrick de Keyser) stood on the Haarlemmerplein. In 1837 that gate was pulled down and rebuilt, and at King Willem II's entry into the city in 1840 it was renamed Willemspoort.

origins.name: Haarlemmerweg
origins.en: The main road to Haarlem.

origins.name: Haarlerbergpad
origins.en: The name of a hill near Haarle (Overijssel), a rise in the push moraine from the penultimate ice age (200,000-130,000 years ago).

origins.name: Haarlerbergweg
origins.en: The name of a hill near Haarle (Overijssel), a rise in the push moraine from the penultimate ice age (200,000-130,000 years ago).

origins.name: Hacquartstraat
origins.en: Carolus Hacquart (1640-1730), musician, who wrote pieces for the viola da gamba and was a gamba player at the court of the Oranges.

origins.name: Hagedoornplein
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Hagedoornweg
origins.en: The shrub (hawthorn). Part of the square was renamed Plein Spanje '36-'39 in 1986.

origins.name: Hageland
origins.en: A region in Belgium, in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Hagenau
origins.en: The Hagenau estate on the Veluwe, originally owned by the stadholder Willem II.

origins.name: Hajo Brugmanshof
origins.en: Historian (1868-1939). His works include a history of Amsterdam in eight volumes (1933).

origins.name: Hakfort
origins.en: A sixteenth- and seventeenth-century castle, altered in 1788, near Vorden (Gelderland). It is named after the knight Bernt van Hackfort (died 1559).

origins.name: Halmaheirastraat
origins.en: One of the islands of the Moluccas (Indonesia).

origins.name: Halteriastraat
origins.en: A microscopic water creature, a ciliate. Large stiff hairs make it move in jumps; smaller hairs create a current in the water that wafts food inside.

origins.name: Halvemaansbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge takes its name from the Halvemaansteeg. The origin of that name may lie in the façade of Halvemaansteeg no. 18, marked 'Van Ouds de Halve Maan' (of old the Half Moon).

origins.name: Halvemaansteeg
origins.en: The origin of this name may lie in the façade of no. 18, marked 'van ouds de Halve Maan' (of old the Half Moon). It is also possible that the bridge gave the name: in 1626 the Halvemaansbrug was given a half-curved shape (now straight). But the alley's name is already mentioned at the beginning of the seventeenth century, so it would be older than the bridge.

origins.name: Hamerstraat
origins.en: Named after the hammer. The street lies in the industrial part of Amsterdam-Noord where streets are named after tools and workshop materials, such as the Aambeeldstraat (anvil) and the Hamerkanaal.

origins.name: Hammarbystraat
origins.en: A waterside district in south Stockholm that has been renovated and redeveloped since the 1990s.

origins.name: Hamontstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Han Hollanderlaan
origins.en: Hartog Hollander (1886-1943), legendary radio reporter, whose reports did much to popularise sport in the Netherlands. He died in the Sobibor extermination camp.

origins.name: Handbalstraat
origins.en: Refers to a handball club that was here.

origins.name: Handboogstraat
origins.en: In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries the Crossbow (Voetboog) and Longbow (Handboog) Doelen, militia halls, were built on the Singel. Both had a shooting orchard that stretched to behind the houses on the Kalverstraat. In 1649 two streets were laid out on the grounds of these orchards and named Handboogstraat and Voetboogstraat.

origins.name: Händelstraat
origins.en: George Frideric Handel (1685-1759), German-English composer. Besides operas he composed 32 oratorios, six concerti grossi, twenty organ concertos, chamber music, songs and festive music.

origins.name: Hanedastraat
origins.en: The name of one of Tokyo's airports.

origins.name: Hannie Dankbaarpassage
origins.en: Henriëtte Christine Jaqueline Dankbaar (1952-2007), politician, the first GroenLinks district chair in Amsterdam (Oud-West, 1990-2002). She came from the PSP and was loved for her great social commitment.

origins.name: Hans Katanhof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1919-1943), a student, born in Hilversum, executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Hans Meerum Terwogtweg
origins.en: Albert Hendrik Magdalus Meerum Terwogt (1883-1960), the doyen of sports journalists. For forty years he was sports editor of the 'Nieuwe Rotterdamsche Courant'.

origins.name: Hans Onversaagdstraat
origins.en: A Beggar captain at the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Haparandadam
origins.en: A Swedish port on the Gulf of Bothnia, a timber port.

origins.name: Haparandaweg
origins.en: A Swedish port on the Gulf of Bothnia, a timber port.

origins.name: Hardwareweg
origins.en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

origins.name: Haringbuisdijk
origins.en: A ship used for herring fishing (a herring buss).

origins.name: Haringvlietstraat
origins.en: A sea channel from the Hellegatsplein to the North Sea (between Voorne and Zuid-Beveland), now closed off from the open sea by a dam.

origins.name: Harkstraat
origins.en: The gardening tool (the rake).

origins.name: Harmoniehof
origins.en: A basic concept of music theory (harmony).

origins.name: Haroekoestraat
origins.en: An island of the Moluccas (Indonesia).

origins.name: Harriet Freezerstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Harriët Wilhelmina Vriesendorp-Eybergen (1911-1971), writer and journalist. She wrote for 'De Groene Amsterdammer' and 'Het Parool', was an editor of the monthly 'Opzij', and was involved in founding Man Vrouw Maatschappij. Her well-attended lectures made an important contribution to improving the position of women.

origins.name: Harry Banninkstraat
origins.en: Composer (1929-1999), arranger and pianist. His work includes the music for Annie M.G. Schmidt's musicals, among them 'Heerlijk duurt het langst' and 'Ja zuster, Nee zuster'.

origins.name: Harry Koningsbergerstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1924-1945), born in Blokzijl, executed by firing squad in Zeist.

origins.name: Hart Nibbrigstraat
origins.en: Ferdinand Hart Nibbrig (1866-1915), painter and lithographer of portraits and landscapes, a representative of neo-impressionism.

origins.name: Hartelstein
origins.en: A former castle near Itteren (South Limburg), of which a fortified farmstead with seventeenth-century remains survives.

origins.name: Hartenstraat
origins.en: Recalls the tanners and the hide trade once based in this neighbourhood. Hart is an old form of hert (deer).

origins.name: Hasebroekstraat
origins.en: Johannes Petrus Hasebroek (1812-1896), minister and writer. Under the pseudonym Jonathan he wrote, among other things, 'Waarheid en droomen' (truth and dreams).

origins.name: Haspelsstraat
origins.en: Abraham Haspels (1893-1942), resistance fighter, born in the municipality of Haarlemmermeer and executed by firing squad in Amersfoort. He was involved in, among other things, the February Strike of 1941.

origins.name: Hasselaerssteeg
origins.en: Pieter Dircks Hasselaer (1554-1616), merchant and regent. In 1587 he bought the brewery 'De Witte Arent' on the corner of the alley and the Prins Hendrikkade. Before he settled in Amsterdam he had won great fame as a militia ensign during the siege of Haarlem. The alley was earlier called the Trouweloossteegje (faithless alley), recalling the former St Jacob's chapel, where divorces were proclaimed.

origins.name: Hatostraat
origins.en: The name of the airport of Willemstad, Curaçao.

origins.name: Havankbrug
origins.en: Havank, pseudonym of Hendrikus Frederikus (Hans) van der Kallen (Leeuwarden, 19 February 1904 - Leeuwarden, 22 June 1964), was a Dutch writer. Havank began his career as a writer of detective novels in Amsterdam, where he wrote his first two novels. He is best known for his 'Schaduw' (Shadow) series.

origins.name: Havenstraat
origins.en: A mooring place for ships (harbour).

origins.name: Havikshorst
origins.en: An old havezate (now a country house) from 1753, surrounded by a wide moat, near De Wijk (Drenthe).

origins.name: Havikslaan
origins.en: The bird of prey (the goshawk).

origins.name: Haya van Someren-Downerstraat
origins.en: Haya Victoria van Someren-Downer (1926-1980), politician, a member of the VVD. From 1959 to 1968 she sat in the House of Representatives, where she dealt mainly with education, media, and transport and water management. From 1974 to 1980 she was a member of the Senate (Eerste Kamer), where she worked on education and Kingdom affairs.

origins.name: Hazelaarstraat
origins.en: The broadleaf tree that bears hazelnuts.

origins.name: Hazenstraat
origins.en: The hare, a rodent. The name was given because of this animal's skin. The street lies near the old tanners and the hide trade.

origins.name: Heathrowstraat
origins.en: The name of one of London's airports.

origins.name: Hebridenlaan
origins.en: A Scottish island group of about five hundred islands, of which about a hundred are inhabited. The main islands are Lewis and Skye.

origins.name: Hecht en Sterkhof
origins.en: Hecht en Sterk, also known as Storkoe, was a coffee plantation on the Commewijne river in the district of Commewijne in Suriname. At its height in 1819 it covered more than 1000 akkers (fields). After emancipation in 1863 the plantation recruited no contract labourers and probably went out of production soon after. In 1910 the government bought it to make it, together with Frederiksburg, a government plantation, set up to grant land to contract workers.

origins.name: Hechtelstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Hectorstraat
origins.en: A figure from Greek mythology: army commander, son of the king of Troy.

origins.name: Hederabrug
origins.en: Hedera is the scientific name for ivy.

origins.name: Heemstedestraat
origins.en: A town in Noord-Holland that has grown together with Haarlem.

origins.name: Heer Halewijnstraat
origins.en: A medieval song about a murderer of women who is himself killed by a princess.

origins.name: Heermoesstraat
origins.en: A plant of the horsetail family (field horsetail) that can store substances such as heavy metals from its surroundings in its own cells. Horsetail has long been used for many ailments, among them as a diuretic, for joint pain and to strengthen the skeleton and connective tissue.

origins.name: Heesterveld
origins.en: The name of a farm near Nuland (Noord-Brabant).

origins.name: Hegelhof
origins.en: Georg W.F. Hegel (1770-1831), German philosopher, who had a great influence on the development of philosophy. He was a professor in Berlin. One of his followers in the Netherlands was Bolland.

origins.name: Hegeraatstraat
origins.en: H.J. Hegeraat (1874-1919), schoolteacher and later a journalist on the daily 'Het Volk'. Author of several socialist battle songs.

origins.name: Heggerankweg
origins.en: The climbing plant (bryony) that grows in hedges and scrub.

origins.name: Heibrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the Heisteeg, on which it lies. The Heisteeg takes its name from a corner house called 't Hayblok, already mentioned at the beginning of the sixteenth century. Until 1606 an unofficial name for this bridge was Strontenburgerbrug (roughly, dung-town bridge), because of the nuisance caused by two nearby shipyards.

origins.name: Heidotistraat
origins.en: Heidoti is a village in the Boven-Saramacca resort in the northern part of Suriname, inhabited by Maroons of the Kwinti people.

origins.name: Heiligeweg
origins.en: After the Miracle of Amsterdam, the chapel 'Ter Heilige Stede' (later the Nieuwezijds Kapel) was founded between the Rokin and the Kalverstraat. For the pilgrims a road was then laid beside the Heiligewegsevaart (later the Overtoom) from Sloten to the Kalverstraat, called the Heiligeweg (holy way). Our street is what remains of that pilgrimage route. In old documents the Leidsestraat is also called Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Heiligewegsluis
origins.en: After the Miracle of Amsterdam, the chapel 'Ter Heilige Stede' (later the Nieuwezijds Kapel) was founded between the Rokin and the Kalverstraat. For the pilgrims a road was then laid beside the Heiligewegsevaart (later the Overtoom) from Sloten to the Kalverstraat, called the Heiligeweg (holy way). Our street is what remains of that pilgrimage route. In old documents the Leidsestraat is also called Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Heimansweg
origins.en: Eduard (Eli) Heimans (1861-1914), naturalist. An Amsterdam schoolteacher, he wrote a series of books on birds and flowers with J.P. Thijsse. Together they founded the Dutch Natural History Society and the magazine 'De Levende Natuur'. Heimans died on a geological excursion.

origins.name: Hein Donnerbrug
origins.en: Jan Hein Donner (1927-1988) was a chess grandmaster who was Dutch champion several times. He was also a polemicist and a columnist for NRC Handelsblad.

origins.name: Heining
origins.en: Named after a polder outside the dikes in the former IJ, which after the Grote IJ polders were made became a separately drained area within them. The name indicates land that yields little hay. It came to Amsterdam through the boundary settlement with Haarlemmerliede en Spaarnwoude in 1963.

origins.name: Heinzestraat
origins.en: Gustav Adolph Heinze (1820-1904), German by birth, conductor in Amsterdam of the German Opera, the Liedertafel Euterpe and the Vincentius concerts. From 1862 to 1885 director of the Toonkunst music school. He composed cantatas and oratorios.

origins.name: Hekelveld
origins.en: Probably, when this land still lay outside the walls, flax was hackled here (hekelen: combing flax), to be made into rope on the neighbouring ropewalks. In 1604 there were still two houses whose gable stones recalled this craft. The Hekelveld was originally a canal and was filled in around 1865.

origins.name: Hekla
origins.en: A volcano in Iceland, 1491 metres high.

origins.name: Helena Kuipers-Rietberghof
origins.en: Helena Theodora Kuipers-Rietberg (1893-1944), resistance fighter, born in Winterswijk, died in the Ravensbrück concentration camp. She was known as the mother of the 'Landelijke Organisatie voor hulp aan onderduikers' (the national organisation for help to people in hiding, the L.O.). She also had a part in distributing the clandestine paper 'Trouw'.

origins.name: Helena Mercierstraat
origins.en: A forerunner of the women's movement in Amsterdam (1839-1910), and a writer on social subjects.

origins.name: Helene Madisonstraat
origins.en: American swimmer who won gold in the 100 metres freestyle at the 1932 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

origins.name: Hélène Swarthstraat
origins.en: Hélène Lapidoth, née Swarth (1859-1941), poet of love poetry, for a time much admired by many and in later years a forgotten figure.

origins.name: Helicopterstraat
origins.en: A rotor aircraft that can rise and descend vertically, built in 1933 by the aircraft maker J. Sikorsky, an American born in Russia.

origins.name: Heliotroopstraat
origins.en: An ornamental shrub, originally from South America.

origins.name: Hella Haasseplein
origins.en: Hélène Serafia Haasse (1918-2011), writer of novels, essays, poetry and plays. She received the P.C. Hooft Prize in 1983 and the Prize for Dutch Literature in 2004. She wrote a record 3 Boekenweekgeschenken (Book Week gift books), among them 'Oeroeg' (1948), perhaps her best-known work. She is among the Dutch authors most read abroad.

origins.name: Hellenburg
origins.en: A lost castle in the area of Goes, whose foundations have now been uncovered.

origins.name: Hellingstraat
origins.en: The name refers to the two concrete slipways (hellingen) on the NDSM site, used to launch ships.

origins.name: Helmgrasstraat
origins.en: A native perennial pioneer plant of the grass family (marram grass), important in forming dunes.

origins.name: Helmholtzstraat
origins.en: Hermann von Helmholtz (1821-1894), German physician and physicist, inventor of the ophthalmoscope.

origins.name: Helsingforsbrug
origins.en: Helsingfors is the Swedish name for Helsinki, the capital of Finland. The names in the Houthavens are named after places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Hembrugstraat
origins.en: After the former railway bridge over the Noordzeekanaal, which obstructed the port of Amsterdam. The bridge was demolished after the railway tunnel (the Hemtunnel) came into use.

origins.name: Hemonylaan
origins.en: The brothers Frans Hemony (1609-1667) and Pieter Hemony (1619-1680), bell founders of the carillons in the Oude Kerk, the Zuiderkerk, the Westerkerk and the Munttoren.

origins.name: Hemonystraat
origins.en: The brothers Frans Hemony (1609-1667) and Pieter Hemony (1619-1680), bell founders of the carillons in the Oude Kerk, the Zuiderkerk, the Westerkerk and the Munttoren.

origins.name: Hemsterhuisstraat
origins.en: Tiberius Hemsterhuis (1685-1766), classical philologist, professor in Amsterdam (philosophy) and later at Franeker and Leiden (Greek and national history).

origins.name: Hemweg
origins.en: After a former islet, the Hem, in the old IJ. The Hem was at first a spit of land that only later became an island through erosion of its banks. The word is the same as 'ham', now known only in 'inham' (inlet). A last stretch of the Hemweg still exists; originally the road began at the Spaarndammerbuurt.

origins.name: Hendrik Bulthuisstraat
origins.en: Barber (1892-1948) from the Frisian village of Bergum, designer of the B.M. sailing dinghy and a pioneer of sailing as a popular sport.

origins.name: Hendrik de Bruynstraat
origins.en: Hydraulic engineer (1815-1885), known for the water-management works he built in Surabaya (Dutch East Indies).

origins.name: Hendrik Dienskestraat
origins.en: Resistance hero and office clerk, born in Schiedam in 1907, died in 1945 in Helmstedt (Germany).

origins.name: Hendrik Godfroidhof
origins.en: Hendrikus Godfroid (1899-1943), resistance fighter, born in Arnhem, died in Scheveningen prison. He worked on the clandestine paper 'De Waarheid'.

origins.name: Hendrik Hosstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Pieter Hos (1906-1944), resistance fighter, born in Haarlem and executed by firing squad in Scheveningen. He was in the leadership of the national network of the clandestine paper 'Vrij Nederland'.

origins.name: Hendrik Jacobszstraat
origins.en: Violin maker who made violins between 1690 and 1740 on the model of the Italian Amati.

origins.name: Hendrik Jonkerplein
origins.en: Amsterdam industrialist (1778-1843) who in 1806 founded the factory for steam engines and other machinery that once stood here. Before 1956 this was the Bickersplein. The naming followed a request from N.V. Hk. Jonker en Zn, which turned 150 that year.

origins.name: Hendrik Soeteboomstraat
origins.en: Historian (1616-1678) who wrote several books about Waterland, among them 'De historie van Waterland' and 'De Waterlanders' (1660).

origins.name: Hendrik van Wijnstraat
origins.en: Historian (1740-1831), founder of the General State Archives (1802). He wrote supplements and notes to the 'Vaderlandsche Historie' of the historian Jan Wagenaar.

origins.name: Hendrik Veldhuishof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1922-1944) who set up a printing works in Blaricum for the clandestine paper 'Trouw', where other clandestine printing was also done. He was arrested in June 1944 and executed by firing squad in Vught soon afterwards.

origins.name: Hendrik Werkmanstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Nicolaas Werkman (1882-1945), artist, printer and resistance fighter. Printer for the collective 'De Blauwe Schuit', which published critical pieces about the German occupation. Executed by firing squad in 1945.

origins.name: Hendrikje Stoffelsstraat
origins.en: Rembrandt van Rijn's life companion (1626-1663). Around 1647 she joined his household as a maidservant and soon lived with the painter. She probably modelled for several works. She was buried in the Westerkerk.

origins.name: Hendrikus Rempestraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1903-1944), born in Amsterdam, died in Bruttig (Germany).

origins.name: Henegouwenstraat
origins.en: A province in the south of Belgium (Hainaut).

origins.name: Henk Curièrekade
origins.en: Peter Heinrich Curière (1911-1981), a legendary figure in the Spaarndammerbuurt for his positive and active involvement in the neighbourhood's urban renewal and as chairman of the neighbourhood improvement committee.

origins.name: Henk Gortzakstraat
origins.en: Hendricus Gortzak (1909-1989), politician, member of the Communist Party Holland. During the occupation he was involved in the activities of the now illegal Communist Party of the Netherlands. In 1948 he entered the House of Representatives for the CPN, and from 1952 to 1958 he led its parliamentary group. In 1958 Gortzak was expelled after a conflict with the party leadership.

origins.name: Henk Henriëtstraat
origins.en: Painter and graphic artist (1903-1945).

origins.name: Henk Hienschstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Jan Hiensch (1912-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, died in the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp.

origins.name: Henk Sneevlietpad
origins.en: Hendricus J.F.M. Sneevliet (1883-1942), politician and an active figure in the trade union movement in the Netherlands and the former Dutch East Indies. Internationally known as a communist for his contacts with China and Russia. As a resistance man he was executed by the Germans.

origins.name: Henk Sneevlietweg
