origins.en: Hendricus J.F.M. Sneevliet (1883-1942), politician and an active figure in the trade union movement in the Netherlands and the former Dutch East Indies. Internationally known as a communist for his contacts with China and Russia. As a resistance man he was executed by the Germans.

origins.name: Henkenshage
origins.en: A castle in Sint-Oedenrode, founded in the fifteenth century and partly in the seventeenth, altered in the nineteenth century.

origins.name: Henri Bergsonstraat
origins.en: French philosopher and physicist (1859-1941), author of 'Creative Evolution' (1907). He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1927.

origins.name: Henri Berssenbruggehof
origins.en: Photographer (1873-1959) who photographed street life and the ordinary (working) man and portrayed the cultural elite of the Netherlands. Known for his harmonious compositions, strong contrasts of light and dark, and perfected printing methods.

origins.name: Henri Borelstraat
origins.en: Prose writer and playwright (1869-1933), author of stories of the Indies and novels set in The Hague.

origins.name: Henri Dunantstraat
origins.en: Jean Henri Dunant (1828-1910), Swiss writer and philanthropist, who founded the International Red Cross in 1864. In 1901 he received the first Nobel Peace Prize.

origins.name: Henri Polaklaan
origins.en: Trade union leader and politician (1868-1943), co-founder of the SDAP in 1894 and Amsterdam's first social-democratic city councillor. In 1894 he founded the General Dutch Diamond Workers' Union, which later took the initiative in founding the NVV (trade union federation). With this naming in 1945 the name Plantage Franselaan was dropped. Early in the eighteenth century it was called the Achterlaan.

origins.name: Henri Zagwijnstraat
origins.en: Composer (1878-1954) of chamber music and choral works.

origins.name: Henric van Veldekehof
origins.en: Flemish poet (second half of the twelfth century), whose works include 'De Legende van Sint-Servaes' and a great many 'Minnesangen' (love songs).

origins.name: Henrick de Keijserplein
origins.en: City architect and sculptor (1565-1621). In Amsterdam he built the first Exchange, the Westerkerk, Zuiderkerk and Noorderkerk, and the Montelbaanstoren and Munttoren. In Delft his work includes the tomb of William of Orange.

origins.name: Henrick de Keijserstraat
origins.en: City architect and sculptor (1565-1621). In Amsterdam he built the first Exchange, the Westerkerk, Zuiderkerk and Noorderkerk, and the Montelbaanstoren and Munttoren. In Delft his work includes the tomb of William of Orange.

origins.name: Henriëtte Bosmansstraat
origins.en: Pianist and composer (1895-1952), who composed songs, mostly to French texts, and performed as a pianist at home and abroad.

origins.name: Henriëtte Roland Holststraat
origins.en: Henriëtte Roland Holst, née Van der Schalk (1869-1952), poet. For many years a militant socialist, in her poems and verse dramas too.

origins.name: Henriëtte Ronnerplein
origins.en: Henriëtte Ronner, née Knip (1821-1909), painter, mainly of dogs and cats.

origins.name: Henriëtte Ronnerstraat
origins.en: Henriëtte Ronner, née Knip (1821-1909), painter, mainly of dogs and cats.

origins.name: Hensbroekerstraat
origins.en: A village in Noord-Holland, between Alkmaar and Hoorn.

origins.name: Herbert Spencerhof
origins.en: English philosopher and sociologist (1820-1903), a follower of Rousseau.

origins.name: Hercules Seghersstraat
origins.en: Hercules Pieterszoon Seghers (1589-1638), etcher and landscape painter. Seghers's influence can be seen in the works of Rembrandt and Ruisdael. Only in the twentieth century did his manner of painting come to be highly valued.

origins.name: Herculesstraat
origins.en: In Greek mythology Hercules is the strong hero, the son of the supreme god Zeus.

origins.name: Herderhof
origins.en: Johann Gottfried Herder (1744-1803), German philosopher and writer, who had a great influence on Goethe.

origins.name: Herengracht
origins.en: After the Heren Regeerders (the lords who governed the city; in the old days the city was not administered but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch when in 1612 it was widened into today's canal, the first of the three main canals. The stretch beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658, as does the Nieuwe Herengracht.

origins.name: Herenmarkt
origins.en: After the Heren Regeerders (the lords who governed the city; in the old days the city was not administered but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch when in 1612 it was widened into today's canal, the first of the three main canals. The stretch beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658, as does the Nieuwe Herengracht.

origins.name: Herenstraat
origins.en: After the Heren Regeerders (the lords who governed the city; in the old days the city was not administered but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch when in 1612 it was widened into today's canal, the first of the three main canals. The stretch beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658, as does the Nieuwe Herengracht.

origins.name: Herentalsstraat
origins.en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Herfststraat
origins.en: The autumn season. The street came over in 1966 from the abolished municipality of Weesperkarspel under the name Vechtstraat (council decision of Weesperkarspel, 29 November 1957), but that name could not be kept because of confusion with the existing Vechtstraat.

origins.name: Herikerbergweg
origins.en: A hill near the hamlet of Herike, municipality of Markelo (Overijssel).

origins.name: Heringa-State
origins.en: A castle in Marssum near Leeuwarden, also called Poptaslot, built in the sixteenth century and restored in 1908.

origins.name: Herinkhave
origins.en: Originally a fourteenth-century house near Tubbergen (Overijssel), now a simple moated havezate from 1723.

origins.name: Herman Bonpad
origins.en: Hermanus J. Bon (1873-1945), known to all as Pa Bon. For many years a champion and leader of school football matches in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Herman de Manstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of the Jewish novelist Salomon Hamburger (1898-1946), a convert to Roman Catholicism. His works include the novel 'Het wassende water' (the rising water).

origins.name: Herman Gorterstraat
origins.en: Poet (1864-1927) who made his name above all with his great nature poem 'Mei' (May, 1889). He wrote 'Kritiek op de Literaire beweging der Tachtigers' (a critique of the literary movement of the Eighties) and was for many years a militant Marxist socialist.

origins.name: Herman Heijermansweg
origins.en: Journalist, novelist and playwright (1864-1924). He wrote many novels set in Amsterdam, some under the pseudonym Samuel Falkland. His great success was the play 'Op hoop van zegen' (The Good Hope).

origins.name: Herman Hellingplantsoen
origins.en: A Beggar captain who served under Governor Diederik Sonoy during the siege of Amsterdam (1572-1578). Helling was killed in 1577, together with the captain Nicolaas Ruychaver, in a failed attempt to take the city hall on the Dam.

origins.name: Herman Poortstraat
origins.en: Poet and writer (1886-1933), known above all as a lecturer on literary subjects for the Volksuniversiteit (adult education) and as a theatre critic. His works include a study of Bredero.

origins.name: Herman Robbersstraat
origins.en: Man of letters (1868-1937), author of novellas and novels, and also editor-in-chief of Elsevier and a critic.

origins.name: Hermanus Coenradistraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1909-1941), an electrician, born in Amsterdam and executed by firing squad in The Hague.

origins.name: Hermietenstraat
origins.en: After a house that stood on the corner of the Rokin at the beginning of the seventeenth century, called 'De Heremyt'. Until 1912 this was the Hermietensteeg. That year the alley was widened to six metres and steeg (alley) was changed to straat (street). Hermiet comes from heremiet, meaning hermit.

origins.name: Hermitagelaan
origins.en: The Hermitage Museum in St Petersburg, one of the largest museum complexes in the world. Its collection began with the precious private imperial collection of paintings. It is famous for its works by Titian, Rubens and above all Rembrandt.

origins.name: Herschelstraat
origins.en: Friedrich W. Herschel (1738-1822), English astronomer. He made reflecting telescopes and discovered the planet Uranus.

origins.name: Hertingenstraat
origins.en: A church village in Zeeuws-Vlaanderen drowned around 1500.

origins.name: Hertspieghelweg
origins.en: A didactic poem by Spieghel (1549-1612), merchant and man of letters.

origins.name: Hertzogstraat
origins.en: James B.M. Hertzog (1866-1942), South African statesman and general in the Boer War of 1899 to 1902. Several times a minister, and in 1924 Prime Minister of the Republic of South Africa.

origins.name: Hertzstraat
origins.en: Heinrich Rudolf Hertz (1857-1894), German physicist, founder of radio telegraphy. The unit of frequency is named after him.

origins.name: Herwijk
origins.en: The English port of Harwich, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Hessenbergweg
origins.en: The name of a hill east of Heerlerheide (Limburg).

origins.name: Hestiastraat
origins.en: A figure from Greek mythology: the eldest daughter of Chronos and Rhea and sister of Zeus, goddess of the hearth and of hospitality.

origins.name: Het Breed
origins.en: These names were given for the meaning of the word (broad field), as a counterpart to Het Hoogt and Het Laagt.

origins.name: Het Dok
origins.en: The street was laid out on the site of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij (Amsterdam Dry Dock Company), which staff in the neighbourhood simply called Het Dok (the dock).

origins.name: Het Hoogt
origins.en: Named after its position (the high one), as a counterpart to Het Laagt.

origins.name: Het Laagt
origins.en: The name (the low one) was given to the path laid out at street level, so it describes its position. The residential street above it, at the level of the third storey, was named Het Hoogt (the high one).

origins.name: Hettenheuvelweg
origins.en: A hill near Bergh in Montferland (Gelderland).

origins.name: Heusdenstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Heverleestraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Hexaanweg
origins.en: A tropical product, a component of petrol (hexane), transhipped in the port of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Hilbert van Dijkhof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1906-1944), a milk seller by trade, born in Kampen, executed by firing squad in Bloemendaal.

origins.name: Hildebrandstraat
origins.en: The pseudonym of Nicolaas Beets.

origins.name: Hildegard von Bingenstraat
origins.en: Hildegard von Bingen was a German composer, but also a scientist (cosmology, botany), abbess and philosopher.

origins.name: Hildo Kropplein
origins.en: Hildebrand Lucien Krop (1884-1970), city sculptor and painter. His works include the Berlage monument in Amsterdam. His decorations and sculptures on Amsterdam's bridges and buildings made him very important to the 'Amsterdam School'.

origins.name: Hildsven
origins.en: The fen (ven) on the west side of the municipality of Moergestel in the province of Noord-Brabant, a nature reserve.

origins.name: Hillegomstraat
origins.en: A town in Zuid-Holland, on the border with Noord-Holland.

origins.name: Hillenraadt
origins.en: A moated sixteenth-century nobleman's house in Swalmen (Limburg), altered and enlarged in later centuries.

origins.name: Hilverbeekstraat
origins.en: An estate near 's-Graveland, founded in the seventeenth century by Amsterdam patricians.

origins.name: Hilversumstraat
origins.en: A town in Het Gooi.

origins.name: Hiridostraat
origins.en: A mountain in Somalia.

origins.name: Hirschpassage
origins.en: Named after the former fashion house Hirsch en Cie, which opened in 1882 on the corner of the Leidseplein and the Weteringschans. Its management had trained at Hirsch in Brussels, itself a branch of the German Hirsch concern, which was entirely oriented to French fashion.

origins.name: Hobaostraat
origins.en: A peak on Bonaire.

origins.name: Hobbemakade
origins.en: Meindert Hobbema (1638-1709), landscape painter, a pupil of Ruisdael.

origins.name: Hobbemastraat
origins.en: Meindert Hobbema (1638-1709), landscape painter, a pupil of Ruisdael.

origins.name: Hodenpijlkade
origins.en: A small village near Schipluiden in the Westland.

origins.name: Hoek van Hollandstraat
origins.en: A village at the mouth of the Nieuwe Waterweg, part of the municipality of Rotterdam since 1914.

origins.name: Hoekenes
origins.en: A small island in the former IJ. The word nes means a spit of land.

origins.name: Hoekenespad
origins.en: A small island in the former IJ. The word nes means a spit of land.

origins.name: Hoekenesplantsoen
origins.en: A small island in the former IJ. The word nes means a spit of land.

origins.name: Hoekenrode
origins.en: The name of an old farm in De Bilt (Utrecht).

origins.name: Hoekenrodepad
origins.en: The name of an old farm in De Bilt (Utrecht).

origins.name: Hoekschewaardplein
origins.en: The Zuid-Holland island (the Hoeksche Waard).

origins.name: Hoekschewaardweg
origins.en: The Zuid-Holland island (the Hoeksche Waard).

origins.name: Hoekslootstraat
origins.en: The name Hoeksloot appears on eighteenth-century maps of Rijnland and its surroundings. After about 1800 the ditch is called Hoornsloot. It still runs along the Amstelveenseweg and, in Amstelveen, along the Emmakade.

origins.name: Hoendiepstraat
origins.en: A canal in the province of Groningen.

origins.name: Hof van Eden
origins.en: The Garden of Eden was, according to the Hebrew Bible, a garden in or equal to the perfect and beautiful Paradise where Adam and Eve lived.

origins.name: Hof van Groenen
origins.en: Probably an earlier name of the seventeenth-century ridderhofstad (knightly manor) and manorial estate in Delfland that appears in 1771 as Groeneveld.

origins.name: Hof van Versailles
origins.en: The Palace of Versailles, south-west of Paris, one of the most impressive Baroque buildings in Europe, built for Louis XIV and largely completed between 1661 and 1690.

origins.name: Hofgeest
origins.en: The name of a patrician house in Velsen (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Hofmeesterstraat
origins.en: Someone on passenger boats who takes care of the meals and serves at the buffet (a steward).

origins.name: Hofmeyrstraat
origins.en: Jan Hendrik Hofmeyr (1845-1912), South African statesman, who campaigned to keep Dutch in use in South Africa.

origins.name: Hofwijckstraat
origins.en: An autobiographical work by Constantijn Huygens from 1651. It was also the name of his country house in Voorburg, which still exists.

origins.name: Hogeboomspad
origins.en: The name of a path that once lay north of Leimuiden and was swallowed by the Haarlemmermeer. A hogeboom is a high footbridge, in principle made of just one tree trunk or beam.

origins.name: Hogehilweg
origins.en: The Hoge Hil, a rise near Domburg (Zeeland).

origins.name: Hogelandplein
origins.en: The Hogeland (also written Hoogeland) is the region of the province of Groningen north of the Reitdiep and the Damsterdiep. The name refers to the relatively high ground, caused by silting from the sea; the soil is therefore sea clay.

origins.name: Hogendijk
origins.en: A region in Groningen north of the Reitdiep and the Damsterdiep. The name refers to the high position of its sea-clay soil compared with the peat areas to its south.

origins.name: Hogevecht
origins.en: A patrician house on the Vecht between Loenen and Breukelen.

origins.name: Hogeweg
origins.en: So named by the council of the former municipality of Watergraafsmeer because the road lies at the front of the polder.

origins.name: Hogewerf
origins.en: A former ridderhofstad (knightly manor), now a farm, near Oud-Beijerland, named after its former owner, Lord Hubrecht Hoogewerff.

origins.name: Holbeinstraat
origins.en: Hans Holbein the Younger (1497-1543), German painter and engraver.

origins.name: Holendrechtdreef
origins.en: A watercourse on the border of Noord-Holland and Utrecht.

origins.name: Holendrechterweg
origins.en: A watercourse on the border of Noord-Holland and Utrecht.

origins.name: Holendrechtplein
origins.en: A watercourse on the border of Noord-Holland and Utrecht.

origins.name: Holendrechtstraat
origins.en: A watercourse on the border of Noord-Holland and Utrecht. The Holendrechterweg runs along this water and used to lie entirely in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. With the annexation of 1966 part of the road came onto Amsterdam territory.

origins.name: Hollandia Kattenburgpad
origins.en: A raincoat factory that stood here until the end of the 1960s. A monument on this path commemorates the tragic events of 11 November 1942, when 367 Jewish employees of the Hollandia Kattenburg raincoat factory were arrested by the Germans and, with family members taken from their homes, deported to the concentration camps. Only eight of the employees survived the camps.

origins.name: Hollandse Tuin
origins.en: The name of one of the many shipyards along the Grote Bickersstraat in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Hollemanstraat
origins.en: Arnold F. Holleman (1859-1953), chemist, professor in Amsterdam from 1905 to 1926. His chemistry textbooks have been translated into many languages.

origins.name: Holterbergweg
origins.en: The name of a hill near Holten (Overijssel).

origins.name: Holtmeulen
origins.en: A castle in Tegelen, Frederik Hendrik's headquarters at the siege of Venlo in 1646.

origins.name: Holwerdahof
origins.en: Jan Hendrik Holwerda (1873-1951), archaeologist and historian, director of the National Museum of Antiquities in Leiden. His works include 'Nederland's vroegste beschaving' (the Netherlands' earliest civilisation, 1925).

origins.name: Holy
origins.en: A former ridderhofstad (knightly manor) north of Vlaardingen (Zuid-Holland).

origins.name: Homme Hettingastraat
origins.en: A Frisian grietman (district magistrate) and member of the Compromise of Nobles (1566), who joined the army of Louis of Nassau in 1568.

origins.name: Hondecoeterstraat
origins.en: Melchior d'Hondecoeter (1636-1695), painter of animals and still lifes.

origins.name: Hondiusstraat
origins.en: Jodocus de Hondt or Hondius (1563-1612), cartographer, engraver and publisher from Ghent working in Amsterdam, mainly of maps and atlases (including the Mercator atlas).

origins.name: Hondsrugweg
origins.en: A ridge of hills in Drenthe.

origins.name: Honingen
origins.en: Originally a thirteenth-century moated castle of the lords of Kralingen, east of Rotterdam. Lumey was imprisoned here in 1573.

origins.name: Honselersdijkstraat
origins.en: A village near Naaldwijk, in the Westland.

origins.name: Honthorststraat
origins.en: Gerard van Honthorst (1590-1656), painter of portraits and night scenes, court painter to Frederik Hendrik.

origins.name: Hoofddorpplein
origins.en: A village, the main town of the municipality of Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Hoofddorpweg
origins.en: A village, the main town of the municipality of Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Hoofdweg
origins.en: The former municipality of Sloten gave the name for its function: a wide central main road (hoofdweg). After the annexation of 1921 the road was extended north to the Bos en Lommerplein.

origins.name: Hooge Venne
origins.en: A former farm in the old municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Hoogheemraadweg
origins.en: A hoogheemraad is a board member of a hoogheemraadschap, a regional water board that oversees several water boards and polders. Amsterdam includes parts of the Amstelland, Rijnland and Waterland water boards; Amstelland and Waterland have since merged into a larger whole.

origins.name: Hoogoorddreef
origins.en: A manor house near Hilversum, built around 1900 (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Hoogoordplein
origins.en: A manor house near Hilversum, built around 1900 (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Hoogte Kadijk
origins.en: When a great deal of land had built up through silting outside the old sea dike (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike, or quay dike (kadijk), was built. It was originally called the new sea dike, but that name later fell out of use. When this new dike was raised further, people spoke of the Laagte (low part) and the Hoogte (high part) of the Kadijk. Until 1943 the Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat. This is because it lies in line with the Plantage Kerklaan, although it has never been connected to it.

origins.name: Hoogwoudstraat
origins.en: A village in Noord-Holland.

origins.name: Hooistraat
origins.en: Mown and dried grass (and some other crops), used as fodder in livestock farming (hay).

origins.name: Hooivletstraat
origins.en: A flat-bottomed boat used to carry hay.

origins.name: Hoopende Swaen
origins.en: A whaler of the Oostzaan shipowner Pieter Swan, which sailed the seas east of Greenland between 1759 and 1775.

origins.name: Hoorneboeg
origins.en: An estate near Hilversum (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Hoornsestraat
origins.en: After the Noord-Holland town of Hoorn, once an important Zuiderzee town, as its many monumental buildings still show.

origins.name: Hoptille
origins.en: A hamlet with a bridge of the same name west of Hijlaard (Friesland).

origins.name: Hoptillepad
origins.en: A hamlet with a bridge of the same name west of Hijlaard (Friesland).

origins.name: Hornweg
origins.en: The former island De Hoorn or Horn in the old IJ. After the Noordzeekanaal was built, the island could still be clearly made out in the landscape of the Grote IJpolder, but the extension of the Westhaven (around 1960) dug it away entirely. 'Horn' means corner and was given to coastal features similar to a 'nes' or 'ham'. This horn's full name was Zaanderhorn: a spit of land belonging to the western part of Zaanden, the forerunner of Zaandam.

origins.name: Hortensiastraat
origins.en: An ornamental shrub (hydrangea).

origins.name: Hortusplantsoen
origins.en: After the Hortus Botanicus opposite. The quay used to be called Muidergracht, but because of confusion with the Plantage Muidergracht this name was set in 1911.

origins.name: Houdringe
origins.en: A nature reserve in De Bilt (Utrecht).

origins.name: Houthalenstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Houthavenkade
origins.en: Goods that were and are shipped through the port of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Houthavenweg
origins.en: Goods that were and are shipped through the port of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Houtkopersburgwal
origins.en: Named after the many timber merchants (houtkopers) and their yards that settled along this water in the seventeenth century. Until 1878 the cross street was called Vlooienburgsteeg.

origins.name: Houtkopersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the many timber merchants (houtkopers) and their yards that settled along this water in the seventeenth century. Until 1878 the cross street was called Vlooienburgsteeg.

origins.name: Houtmandwarsstraat
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis (c. 1540-1599) and Frederik Houtman (died 1625), who in 1595/1597 made the first voyage under the Dutch flag to the East Indies for Amsterdam merchants. Cornelis made a second voyage; Frederik was governor on Ambon for six years and became governor of the Moluccas.

origins.name: Houtmankade
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis (c. 1540-1599) and Frederik Houtman (died 1625), who in 1595/1597 made the first voyage under the Dutch flag to the East Indies for Amsterdam merchants. Cornelis made a second voyage; Frederik was governor on Ambon for six years and became governor of the Moluccas.

origins.name: Houtmanstraat
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis (c. 1540-1599) and Frederik Houtman (died 1625), who in 1595/1597 made the first voyage under the Dutch flag to the East Indies for Amsterdam merchants. Cornelis made a second voyage; Frederik was governor on Ambon for six years and became governor of the Moluccas.

origins.name: Houtrijkstraat
origins.en: After the former village of Houtrijk en Polanen, now Halfweg. The street was earlier called Tweede Spaarndammerstraat (council decision of 30 March 1881). In 1978, because the street pattern changed, part of the street was renamed and added to the Assendelftstraat.

origins.name: Hoyerpad
origins.en: A character in the work of the writer Nescio. Nescio (Latin: 'I do not know') is the pseudonym of Jan Hendrik Frederik Grönloh (1882-1961), known above all for his stories 'De uitvreter' (the freeloader) and 'Titaantjes' (little titans).

origins.name: Huddekade
origins.en: Johannes Hudde (1628-1704), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1672 to 1704 and an expert in water management. The former Hogesluis (built 1662, demolished 1883) was built to his design.

origins.name: Huddestraat
origins.en: Johannes Hudde (1628-1704), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1672 to 1704 and an expert in water management. The former Hogesluis (built 1662, demolished 1883) was built to his design.

origins.name: Hudsonhof
origins.en: Henry Hudson (c. 1565-1611), English navigator, who sailed for the Dutch East India Company in 1609. On his last voyage, in 1610, he discovered the Hudson Bay, named after him, between Labrador and Canada.

origins.name: Hudsonstraat
origins.en: Henry Hudson (1550-1611), English navigator in the service of the Dutch East India Company. He discovered the Hudson Bay, named after him, between Labrador and Canada (1610).

origins.name: Hugo de Grootkade
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

origins.name: Hugo de Grootplein
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

origins.name: Hugo de Vrieslaan
origins.en: Botanist (1848-1935), professor at the University of Amsterdam from 1880 to 1918. He developed mutation theory, which holds that characteristics change in jumps. The theory applies to all living organisms, not only plants.

origins.name: Hugo Floris Ruysstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1924-1943), born in Bussum, executed by firing squad in Haarlem.

origins.name: Hugo Verriesthof
origins.en: Flemish priest and man of letters (1840-1922), a contributor to the literary magazine 'Van nu en straks'. His works include 'Twintig Vlaamsche koppen' (twenty Flemish heads).

origins.name: Huidekoperstraat
origins.en: Pieter Huidekoper (1798-1852), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1842 to 1849, who campaigned for better public housing. The text on a memorial plaque to him reads: 'Hij was der stede goed, hij deed den arme wel' (he was good to the city, he did well by the poor).

origins.name: Huidenstraat
origins.en: After the hide trade (huiden: hides) concentrated here in earlier centuries.

origins.name: Huifkarpad
origins.en: The type of caravan (a covered wagon, huifkar) in use around 1900. The street name refers to the caravan site here.

origins.name: Huigenbos
origins.en: The name of farms in Scherpenzeel (Gelderland) and Egmond-Binnen (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Huismanshof
origins.en: A huisman is the head occupant of a house in the countryside.

origins.name: Huiswoudhof
origins.en: Otto Huiswoud (Paramaribo, 1893 - Amsterdam, 1961) and Hermina Huiswoud, née Dumont (British Guiana, 1905 - Amsterdam, 1998). In New York Otto Huiswoud became involved in social issues, and in 1914 he joined the Socialist Party. In 1919 he was a co-founder of the Communist Party of the United States. In 1926 he married Hermina, who was also involved in the international communist movement: she worked as a translator for the Communist International (Comintern) and wrote for the monthly The Negro Worker. After the Second World War the couple moved to Amsterdam, where Otto Huiswoud was chairman of the Vereniging Ons Suriname from 1954 to 1961.

origins.name: Huiswoudstraat
origins.en: Otto Huiswoud (Paramaribo, 1893 - Amsterdam, 1961) and Hermina Huiswoud, née Dumont (British Guiana, 1905 - Amsterdam, 1998). In New York Otto Huiswoud became involved in social issues, and in 1914 he joined the Socialist Party. In 1919 he was a co-founder of the Communist Party of the United States. In 1926 he married Hermina, who was also involved in the international communist movement: she worked as a translator for the Communist International (Comintern) and wrote for the monthly The Negro Worker. After the Second World War the couple moved to Amsterdam, where Otto Huiswoud was chairman of the Vereniging Ons Suriname from 1954 to 1961.

origins.name: Hullenbergweg
origins.en: The name of a hill near Bennekom (Gelderland).

origins.name: Hulstweg
origins.en: The shrub with hard, prickly leaves and red berries (holly).

origins.name: Humberto Delgadoplein
origins.en: Portuguese general (1906-1965). In the presidential election of 1958 he was the opposition candidate against the official candidate of the dictator Salazar. He lost through large-scale electoral fraud and terror by the secret police. In 1965 he was murdered by the secret services of Spain and Portugal.

origins.name: Humberweg
origins.en: The broad estuary of the English rivers Trent and Ouse. The name is known in the coal trade, because English coal is shipped from the surrounding areas.

origins.name: Huntum
origins.en: A patrician house on the Vecht, south of Vreeland.

origins.name: Huntumdreef
origins.en: A patrician house on the Vecht, south of Vreeland.

origins.name: Huntumpad
origins.en: A patrician house on the Vecht, south of Vreeland.

origins.name: Hunzestraat
origins.en: A small river that rises in Drenthe and widens into the Zuidlaardermeer on the border of the province of Groningen.

origins.name: Hygiëaplein
origins.en: The goddess of health in Greek mythology.

origins.name: Hygiëastraat
origins.en: The goddess of health in Greek mythology.

origins.name: Ibizastraat
origins.en: A Spanish island in the Mediterranean, part of the Balearic Islands.

origins.name: Iepenplein
origins.en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

origins.name: Iepenweg
origins.en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

origins.name: IJ-tunnel
origins.en: The road through the tunnel under the IJ, opened on 30 October 1968.

origins.name: IJburglaan
origins.en: The name fits the Amsterdam tradition in which artificial islands and peninsulas have names ending in -burg. The name IJburg makes clear that the place lies in the IJmeer.

origins.name: IJdok
origins.en: Part of the Westerdokseiland.

origins.name: IJdoornlaan
origins.en: The polder outside the dike just east of the village of Durgerdam, a nature reserve of hay meadows and reed beds.

origins.name: IJplein
origins.en: After the buildings of the Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij were demolished, a square was planned at the start of the Meeuwenlaan, and the planners called it the IJplein in advance. The name IJplein stuck, but no square was made; instead there are three parallel streets that all bear the name: an example of an inaccurate name.

origins.name: IJpromenade
origins.en: The IJ was once an arm of the Zuiderzee. In 1865-1872 it was reclaimed when the Noordzeekanaal was built, and in 1872 it was closed off from the Zuiderzee by the IJdijk and the Oranjesluizen.

origins.name: IJsbaanpad
origins.en: Named after the ice rink on the IJsclub grounds, to which the road leads.

origins.name: IJselmondestraat
origins.en: One of the Zuid-Holland islands.

origins.name: IJselstraat
origins.en: The river IJssel, a branch of the Rhine, runs from Westervoort to the IJsselmeer.

origins.name: IJslandtpad
origins.en: The eighteenth-century farmstead on the Middenweg, later joined to the still existing Frankendael, and demolished early in the nineteenth century.

origins.name: IJsselmeerstraat
origins.en: Named after the IJsselmeer.

origins.name: IJzerhof
origins.en: A river in Belgium.

origins.name: IJzerwerkerstraat
origins.en: A craftsman who works iron and steel (ironworker). The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

origins.name: Ilpendammerstraat
origins.en: A village in Waterland on the Noordhollandsch Kanaal.

origins.name: Ilperveldstraat
origins.en: A nature reserve in the municipalities of Landsmeer and Waterland, a brackish peat area.

origins.name: Imbos
origins.en: A hilltop between Arnhem and Laag-Soeren, a nature reserve since 1937 and part of the Veluwezoom National Park.

origins.name: Immanuel Kanthof
origins.en: German philosopher (1724-1804), professor at Königsberg (Germany) and one of the greatest thinkers of his time. His works include the 'Critique of Pure Reason'.

origins.name: Imogirituin
origins.en: The Indonesian town of Imogiri, on a hill seventeen kilometres south-east of Yogyakarta. The town is famous for its seventeenth-century royal cemetery. In 1646 Sultan Agung was the first to be buried there.

origins.name: Imstenrade
origins.en: An old country house near Heerlen (Limburg).

origins.name: Inaristraat
origins.en: Lake Inari, in northern Finland near the Russian border.

origins.name: Ingelandenweg
origins.en: The ingelanden are the landowners in a polder, who are assessed for the polder charges and elect the polder board.

origins.name: Ingenhouszhof
origins.en: Jan Ingenhousz (1730-1799), physicist, discoverer of the respiration of plants.

origins.name: Ingogostraat
origins.en: A place in Natal (South Africa) where the Boer general Joubert defeated the British in 1881 (First Boer War).

origins.name: Inlaagstraat
origins.en: An inlaagdijk is a dike built further back because the original dike threatens to be undermined by the waves and has to be given up as the main defence. Here it refers to a former strip of land north-west of Sloterdijk.

origins.name: Insulindeweg
origins.en: The name Multatuli gave to what was then the Dutch East Indies, from the Latin 'insula' = island.

origins.name: Internetstraat
origins.en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

origins.name: Inzet
origins.en: Inzet, in the sense of dedication.

origins.name: Ir. B. Bijvoetbrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after the architect Bernard Bijvoet (1889-1979), a representative of the 'Nieuwe Bouwen' (Dutch modernism). His designs include the Zonnestraal Sanatorium and the Hotel Gooiland in Hilversum. He was closely involved in building the nearby Muziektheater on the Waterlooplein.

origins.name: Ir. Jakoba Mulderplein
origins.en: Jakoba Mulder (1900-1988), chief architect of the urban expansion section and later head of the urban development department of Amsterdam's Public Works Department. Her most important work was the design of the Amsterdamse Bos.

origins.name: Irawan Soejonostraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1919-1945), a member of an Indonesian resistance group in Leiden later named after him.

origins.name: Isaäc Asscherpad
origins.en: Founder of the Asscher diamond-cutting works in the Tolstraat. He lived from 1843 to 1902.

origins.name: Isaac Gogelweg
origins.en: Isaac Jan Alexander Gogel (1765-1821), statesman and Patriot, founder of several kinds of taxes. In 1814 King Willem I consulted Gogel on his financial affairs.

origins.name: Isaac Titsinghkade
origins.en: Lawyer (1744-1812), envoy in China and Japan, and also a physician, merchant, diplomat, philosopher and collector of Japonica. He worked for the Dutch East India Company for 32 years.

origins.name: Isaak Gosseshof
origins.en: Historian (1873-1940), professor in Groningen, who with N. Japikse wrote the 'Handboek tot de staatkundige geschiedenis van Nederland' (handbook of the political history of the Netherlands).

origins.name: Isabella Richaardsstraat
origins.en: Isabella Johanna Alyda Richaards (1904-1985), the first woman member of parliament in Suriname (1963-1969) since universal suffrage was introduced there in 1948. Suriname's Women's Day falls on the date she took her seat in parliament: 14 May.

origins.name: Isarweg
origins.en: A tributary of the Danube that flows past the German city of Munich.

origins.name: Iseoplantsoen
origins.en: The lake Lago d'Iseo, in the province of Lombardy in northern Italy.

origins.name: Isolatorweg
origins.en: An insulating material or body on which electrical conductors rest (an insulator).

origins.name: Israël Queridostraat
origins.en: Writer (1872-1932), originally a diamond worker. For many years literary contributor to the 'Algemeen Handelsblad', he wrote several novels about the life of ordinary Amsterdammers.

origins.name: Ite Boeremastraat
origins.en: Ite Boerema (1902-1980), surgeon, professor of surgery at the University of Amsterdam from 1946 to 1973. He built the hyperbaric pressure chamber in the Wilhelmina Gasthuis.

origins.name: Iwan Kantemanplein
origins.en: Iwan Hugo Kanteman (1908-1945), resistance fighter, born in Suriname. From 1940 until his arrest in 1944 he worked for the air-raid protection service in Amsterdam. From 1943 he worked clandestinely for the CPN and distributed 'De Waarheid'. After his arrest he was taken to several concentration camps and died of illness and exhaustion in Buchenwald.

origins.name: J. Calsstraat
origins.en: Jozef Maria Laurens Theo Cals (1914-1971), politician, member of the KVP. Among other posts he was Minister of Education, Arts and Sciences from 1952 to 1963, above all the man behind the Mammoetwet (mammoth law), which regulated all of secondary education. In 1965 he became Prime Minister. His cabinet fell in the 'night of Schmelzer' (22 November 1966).

origins.name: J. de Koostraat
origins.en: Jan de Koo (1841-1909), at first a minister and later an influential journalist, founder of 'De Groene Amsterdammer'.

origins.name: J. Drijverweg
origins.en: Jan Drijver (1896-1963), director and secretary of the Society for the Preservation of Nature Monuments (Natuurmonumenten) and secretary of the Dutch Society for the Protection of Birds.

origins.name: J. Dunnebierstraat
origins.en: Jacob Dunnebier (1904-1988), architect. With the architect Cees Ronstadt he was responsible for renovating several buildings in the city centre.

origins.name: J.A. dèr Mouwstraat
origins.en: Johan Andreas dèr Mouw (1862-1919), man of letters and doctor of classics, who wrote under the pseudonym Adwaita. His poetry holds Eastern mysticism in Western forms.

origins.name: J.C. Breenstraat
origins.en: Johannes C. Breen (1865-1927), historian and city archivist of Amsterdam.

origins.name: J.C. Schröderstraat
origins.en: Jan Christiaan Schröder (1871-1938), journalist, for many years editor-in-chief of the daily 'De Telegraaf', where he wrote among other things the column 'Dagboek van een Amsterdammer' (diary of an Amsterdammer).

origins.name: J.C. van Epenstraat
origins.en: Johannes Christiaan van Epen (1880-1960), architect of the Amsterdam School, whose designs include housing on the Amsteldijk, the Saffierstraat and the Harmoniehof.

origins.name: J.F. Ankersmitstraat
origins.en: Johan Frederik Ankersmit (1871-1942), journalist. He began at 'De Telegraaf' and from its founding in 1900 until 1937 worked for the daily 'Het Volk'.

origins.name: J.F. Berghoefplantsoen
origins.en: Johannes Franciscus Berghoef (1903-1994), architect, professor at the Technische Hogeschool in Delft from 1947 to 1969, and one of the most important representatives of the Delft School. In 1939, with J.J.M. Vegter, he won the competition for Amsterdam's city hall.

origins.name: J.F. van Hengelstraat
origins.en: Johannes Frederik van Hengel (1887-1975), director of the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland' from 1919 to 1946. He held countless other posts, among them board member of the Amsterdam Port Authority and of the Maritime Museum in Amsterdam.

origins.name: J.G. Suurhoffstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Gerardus Suurhoff (1905-1967), politician. Except for the war years and a few months in 1946, he was a member of the House of Representatives for the SDAP and later the PvdA from 1939 to 1952 and from 1959 to 1961. From 1949 to 1952 he was second chairman of the Nederlands Verbond van Vakverenigingen (NVV, trade union federation). Minister of Social Affairs (1952-1958) and Minister of Transport and Water Management (1965-1966).

origins.name: J.H. Hisgenpad
origins.en: Julius Heinrich Hisgen (1875-1957), a well-known player in the Dutch national cricket team and one of the pioneers of Dutch cricket.

origins.name: J.H. van Heekpad
origins.en: Jan Herman van Heek (1873-1957), textile manufacturer from Twente, who did much for nature conservation and for the protection of medieval buildings, especially in Gelderland and Utrecht.

origins.name: J.H. van Heekweg
origins.en: Jan Herman van Heek (1873-1957), textile manufacturer from Twente, who did much for nature conservation and for the protection of medieval buildings, especially in Gelderland and Utrecht.

origins.name: J.J. Cremerplein
origins.en: Jacobus Johannes Cremer (1827-1880), man of letters, whose works include 'Fabriekskinderen' (factory children, a plea for child protection) and 'Overbetuwsche Novellen'.

origins.name: J.J. Cremerstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Johannes Cremer (1827-1880), man of letters, whose works include 'Fabriekskinderen' (factory children, a plea for child protection) and 'Overbetuwsche Novellen'.

origins.name: J.J. Viottastraat
origins.en: Joannes Josephus Viotta (1814-1859), physician in Amsterdam of Italian descent, and also a composer of church music and of popular songs to texts by J.P. Heije.

origins.name: J.J.M. Vegterstraat
origins.en: Architect (1906-1982), one of the most important representatives of the Delft School. In 1939, with J.F. Berghoef, he won the competition for Amsterdam's city hall.

origins.name: J.M. den Uylstraat
origins.en: Johannes Marten (Joop) den Uyl (1919-1987), social-democratic statesman. He was, among other things, alderman for economic affairs in Amsterdam, Minister of Economic Affairs in the Cals cabinet (1965-1966) and from 1967 leader of the Labour Party group in the House of Representatives, before he became Prime Minister in 1973. From 1977 to 1981 he led his party in opposition. In the second Van Agt cabinet (1981-1982) he was Minister of Social Affairs and Employment.

origins.name: J.M. van der Meylaan
origins.en: Johan Melchior van der Mey (1878-1949), architect of the Amsterdam School and one of the founders of expressionism in architecture. His designs include the Scheepvaarthuis.

origins.name: J.P. Kloosstraat
origins.en: Jan Piet Kloos (1905-2001), architect, who designed many schools, hospitals and centres for the elderly, such as the one on the Schoenerstraat in Noord. He worked uncompromisingly in the spirit of the Nieuwe Bouwen and functionalism.

origins.name: J.S. Ruppertstraat
origins.en: Johan Stephaan Ruppert (1877-1934), one of the leaders of the Amsterdam Christian federation of union executives and of the Christian trade union movement.

origins.name: J.W. Siebbeleshof
origins.en: He lived from 1904 to 1985 and for years worked for the interests of older residents of the Nieuwmarkt neighbourhood. The Centre for the Elderly for people from the neighbourhood is largely thanks to him.

origins.name: Jaagpad
origins.en: The name recalls the time of the trekschuit (towed passenger barge), when the barge driver used his horse to pull the boats along the canal. Many waterways (trekvaarten) had a towpath (jaagpad).

origins.name: Jaap Edenstraat
origins.en: Sportsman (1873-1925), the only person to have been world champion in both skating and cycling. He won his first world skating title in 1893, and was world cycling champion in 1894 and 1895. His world record over 5000 m skating, set in 1894, stood for seventeen years.

origins.name: Jaap Kunstbrug
origins.en: Jaap Kunst (Groningen, 12 August 1891 - Amsterdam, 7 December 1960), Dutch ethnomusicologist and one of the founders of the modern discipline. Kunst began studying the violin at an early age and became seriously interested in Dutch folk culture. After graduating from the University of Groningen in 1917, he joined a string trio that toured the Dutch East Indies. Kunst stayed on in Java (Indonesia) until the mid-1930s, working for the government, and collected and studied the indigenous music there, especially that of the Javanese gamelan. In 1930 his growing reputation as an authority on Indonesian music made him musicologist to the Dutch government.

origins.name: Jaap Nunes Vazstraat
origins.en: Jacob (Jaap) Nunes Vaz (Amsterdam, 20 September 1906 - Sobibor, 13 March 1943), Jewish journalist and one of the founders of the resistance newspaper Het Parool. Dismissed by the ANP press agency on the day the Netherlands surrendered in May 1940 because he was Jewish, he hosted Het Parool's first editorial meeting in his room on the Keizersgracht in December 1940. He refused to wear the yellow star, went into hiding in Wageningen in 1942. The Germans found his address; he was arrested in October 1942 and taken via the Oranjehotel prison and Westerbork to Sobibor, where he was murdered. The street was named after him in 1953.

origins.name: Jaap Speyerstraat
origins.en: Jaap Speyer (Amsterdam, 29 November 1891 - Amsterdam, 17 September 1952), Dutch film director. He learned film-making in Berlin, where he directed his first film in 1917, and returned to the Netherlands as the Nazis rose to power. His De Jantjes (1934) drew at least 100,000 Dutch cinema-goers, and his last film, Een koninkrijk voor een huis (1949), drew even more.

origins.name: Jaargetijden
origins.en: The seasons. Nearby lie the Winter-, Lente-, Zomer- and Herfststraat (winter, spring, summer and autumn streets). The municipality of Weesperkarspel had earlier called the street Schoolstraat. After that municipality was abolished the name had to be changed, because Amsterdam already had a Schoolstraat.

origins.name: Jac. P. Thijsseplein
origins.en: Jacobus P. Thijsse (1865-1945), primary and later secondary schoolteacher and a well-known botanist and zoologist. With Eli Heimans he founded the Dutch Natural History Society. He was co-founder and secretary of the Society for the Preservation of Nature Monuments in the Netherlands, and known as a writer for his 'Geïllustreerde Flora van Nederland' and the Verkade albums.

origins.name: Jachthavenweg
origins.en: The road runs past the marinas on the Nieuwe Meer.

origins.name: Jacob Bontiusplaats
origins.en: Physician in the service of the Dutch East India Company (1592-1631). He studied the flora and fauna around Batavia (now Jakarta), the administrative centre of the former colony of the Dutch East Indies.

origins.name: Jacob Burggraafstraat
origins.en: Partner of the shipbuilder Jan Witheyn, to whom in 1656 the first shipyard on the island of Wittenburg was leased.

origins.name: Jacob Cabeliaustraat
origins.en: A Sea Beggar of the Eighty Years' War, who fought at the capture of Den Briel (1572) and the defence of Alkmaar (1573).

origins.name: Jacob Catskade
origins.en: Jacob Cats (1577-1660), also known as Vadertje (Father) Cats, poet and statesman, among other things Grand Pensionary of Holland and West-Friesland under Frederik Hendrik. His didactic poetry made him hugely popular.

origins.name: Jacob de Rijkhof
origins.en: Amsterdam grain merchant (1541-1584) who joined the Sea Beggars and in 1572 took part in the capture of Den Briel. He then became commander of Veere.

origins.name: Jacob Frankhof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), a travelling salesman, born in Amsterdam, died in Sobibor (Poland).

origins.name: Jacob Geelstraat
origins.en: Man of letters and philologist (1789-1862) who campaigned against outdated art forms.

origins.name: Jacob Groenplantsoen
origins.en: Jacob Andries Groen Jr (1925-1987), historian, who wrote a great deal about the history of Amsterdam, especially Amsterdam-Noord. He is known among other things for his book 'Rondom Volewijck en Tolhuis' and his journalism for the daily 'De Noord-Amsterdammer'.

origins.name: Jacob Honigstraat
origins.en: Burgomaster of Zaandijk and founder of the antiquarian society for the Zaan region. Before 1930 the street was called Meijerstraat. It has been part of Amsterdam since 1 August 1966.

origins.name: Jacob Husleystraat
origins.en: Jacob Otten Husly (1730-1795), member of an Amsterdam family of architects. His buildings include Felix Meritis.

origins.name: Jacob Krausstraat
origins.en: Hydraulic engineer (1861-1951), Minister of Water Management in 1905 and 1908, who directed the building of harbour works in Chile.

origins.name: Jacob Krüsestraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1905-1944), born in Amsterdam, died in the Oranienburg concentration camp. Krüse worked for the clandestine paper 'Trouw' and for the 'Landelijke Organisatie voor hulp aan onderduikers' (the national organisation for help to people in hiding, the L.O.).

origins.name: Jacob Marisplein
origins.en: Painter (1837-1899), mainly of landscapes and Amsterdam street scenes.

origins.name: Jacob Marisstraat
origins.en: Painter (1837-1899), mainly of landscapes and Amsterdam street scenes.

origins.name: Jacob Melkmanstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1902-1943), a travelling salesman by trade, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

origins.name: Jacob Obrechtplein
origins.en: Composer (1430-1505), for many years active abroad, among other things as a choirmaster. He composed a great many masses and motets. The street was taken over in 1896 from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under the name Paviljoenstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 7 February 1896).

origins.name: Jacob Obrechtstraat
origins.en: Composer (1430-1505), for many years active abroad, among other things as a choirmaster. He composed a great many masses and motets. The street was taken over in 1896 from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under the name Paviljoenstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 7 February 1896).

origins.name: Jacob Paffstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1915-1966) who on 30 April 1944 took part in the raid on the remand prison (Huis van Bewaring) on Amsterdam's Weteringschans.

origins.name: Jacob Tilstraat
origins.en: A Beggar captain (1544-1584) who distinguished himself above all in the battle on the Zuiderzee against Bossu in 1573.

origins.name: Jacob van Arteveldestraat
origins.en: A novel by the Flemish writer Hendrik Conscience (1812-1883). Jacob van Artevelde lived from about 1290 to 1345 and was a Flemish popular leader.

origins.name: Jacob van Lennepkade
origins.en: Prose writer (1802-1868), mainly of historical novels, among them 'De roos van Dekama' and 'Ferdinand Huyck'.

origins.name: Jacob van Lennepstraat
origins.en: Prose writer (1802-1868), mainly of historical novels, among them 'De roos van Dekama' and 'Ferdinand Huyck'.

origins.name: Jacob van Maerlantstraat
origins.en: Flemish sexton (c. 1235 - c. 1300) from the village of Maerlant near Den Briel, later town clerk of Damme. The leading figure among the thirteenth-century Dutch (Diets) poets, known above all for his didactic poems.

origins.name: Jacob van Wassenaar Obdamstraat
origins.en: Jacob Baron van Wassenaer, Lord of Obdam (1610-1665), Dutch lieutenant-admiral, who was blown up with his ship at the Battle of Lowestoft in the Second Anglo-Dutch War.

origins.name: Jacob van Weesenbekestraat
origins.en: Secretary to William of Orange (1524-1575).

origins.name: Jacoba Mosselhof
origins.en: In the Dutch Protestant League, Jacoba Mossel started the discussion on whether women could work as religious teachers and preachers. She asked the executive to admit women to the training for religious teachers, and it agreed.

origins.name: Jacobus van Looystraat
origins.en: Man of letters and painter (1855-1930), known for his autobiographical cycle of novels 'Jaapje-Jaap-Jacob'. For some years he was on the editorial board of 'De Nieuwe Gids'.

origins.name: Jacques Oppenheimstraat
origins.en: Legal scholar (1849-1924), professor of constitutional and administrative law in Groningen and Leiden, and later also of international law. In 1913 he chaired the State Commission on proportional representation.

origins.name: Jacques Veltmanstraat
origins.en: Louis Jacques Veltman (1817-1907), actor. Besides the popular 'marqué', the villain in the melodramas, he was also a talented actor in the classical genre.

origins.name: Jaddanbaikade
origins.en: Jaddanbai was an Indian classical composer who, besides composing, also had talents for singing, dancing, acting and film production.

origins.name: James Bradleystraat
origins.en: English astronomer (1693-1762), Fellow of the Royal Society, appointed Savilian Professor of Astronomy at Oxford in 1721 and later Astronomer Royal. In 1728 he put the speed of light at 301,000 km/s, which mattered for navigation.

origins.name: James Cookstraat
origins.en: English explorer (1728-1779) whose discoveries include the east coast of Australia.

origins.name: James Rosskade
origins.en: James Clark Ross (1800-1862), English polar explorer, who led the Antarctic expedition of 1839-1843.

origins.name: James Wattstraat
origins.en: Scottish engineer (1736-1819), whose improvements made the steam engine practical. The unit of power of electric current is named after him. The street was earlier called Hans Lipperheijstraat (council decision of 10 January 1923).

origins.name: Jan Abelszstraat
origins.en: A Beggar captain of the Eighty Years' War, known from the battle on the Ems in 1568, who took part in the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Jan Beijerpad
origins.en: Jan (Johannes Hendrikus) Beijer (1944-1994), a birdwatcher who often visited the Diemerzeedijk.

origins.name: Jan Bernardusstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a resident or landowner of the time. Before the annexation of 1896 the street belonged, under the same name, to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Jan Bongastraat
origins.en: A Frisian grietman (district magistrate), member of the Compromise of Nobles in 1566 and a captain under Louis of Nassau. He was killed fighting Rennenberg in 1580.

origins.name: Jan Boterenbroodstraat
origins.en: Architect (1886-1936) of the Amsterdam School, whose designs include Huize Lydia on the Roelof Hartplein and housing in Tuindorp Nieuwendam.

origins.name: Jan Bottemastraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1908-1944) who played an important part in caring for people in hiding. He was commander of the Amsterdam-Noord knokploeg (K.P., armed resistance squad), and was executed by firing squad in Wormerveer.

origins.name: Jan C. de Voshof
origins.en: Jan Cornelis de Vos (1855-1931), actor and director, called Jan C. by his colleagues. For many years with the Vereeniging Het Nederlandsch Tooneel, he was a guide to many young actors and actresses.

origins.name: Jan Celestraat
origins.en: Johannes Cele (1347-1417), educator and school organiser, rector of the famous Zwolle town school, which with that of Deventer laid the foundation of early Dutch humanism.

origins.name: Jan Cupidohof
origins.en: The coxswain of the lifeboat Brandaris (1869-1938). Under his command 261 shipwrecked people were rescued.

origins.name: Jan de Greefstraat
origins.en: Architect (1784-1834), whose buildings include the warehouses on the Entrepotdok.

origins.name: Jan de Jonghkade
origins.en: Gerrit Jan de Jongh (1845-1917), director of Rotterdam's Public Works and one of the founders of modern Rotterdam. Under his leadership an electricity network, a water supply and modern sewers were built. He became known above all for his role in the city's development and the expansion of the Rotterdam harbours.

origins.name: Jan de Jonghstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1912-1945), born in Amsterdam and shot dead there.

origins.name: Jan de Louterpad
origins.en: Legal scholar (1847-1932), professor in Amsterdam and Utrecht, who taught international and constitutional law.

origins.name: Jan de Louterstraat
origins.en: Legal scholar (1847-1932), professor in Amsterdam and Utrecht, who taught international and constitutional law.

origins.name: Jan den Haenstraat
origins.en: One of the naval heroes of the Battle of Solebay in 1672. He was killed fighting the French off Palermo in 1676.

origins.name: Jan Eisenloeffelstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Johannes Wigbold (1876-1957), silversmith, who set up his own workshop in 1911. A representative of Dutch Art Nouveau and Art Deco.

origins.name: Jan Evertsenstraat
origins.en: Johan Evertsen (1600-1666), of a Zeeland family of naval heroes. As admiral he took part in several naval battles, including the Battle of the Downs (1639). He was killed in the Second Anglo-Dutch War.

origins.name: Jan Goeverneurhof
origins.en: Man of letters (1809-1889), known above all as a children's poet, who wrote under the pseudonym Jan de Rijmer. Founder and for many years editor of the family magazine 'De Huisvriend'.

origins.name: Jan Goldschmedingstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1921-1944), involved in organising the clandestine paper 'Trouw'.

origins.name: Jan Hanzenstraat
origins.en: A landowner who in 1564 bought a piece of land on condition that he maintain a path running along it, which was therefore called the Jan Hanzenpad. The path lay partly in Nieuwer-Amstel and ran from the Singel to the Kostverlorenwetering. Later its remnants were called Jan Hanzenstraat and Jan Hanzenkade. In 1904 the quay was renamed Agatha Dekenstraat.

origins.name: Jan Haringstraat
origins.en: A Sea Beggar from Hoorn who in 1573 held the Diemerzeedijk between the IJ and the Diemermeer (Watergraafsmeer) alone against the Spanish for a time.

origins.name: Jan Janzenstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1919-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in The Hague.

origins.name: Jan Kiststraat
origins.en: A skipper (died 1740) who sailed a transport barge for the Dutch East India Company (VOC).

origins.name: Jan Lelimanhof
origins.en: Architect (1829-1910) whose buildings include 'Arti et Amicitiae', the Prinsengracht hospital, several bread factories and some workers' housing (among others in the Valckenierstraat).

origins.name: Jan Lievensstraat
origins.en: Painter (1607-1674), a pupil of Rembrandt. His work includes murals in the city hall on the Dam.

origins.name: Jan Ligthartstraat
origins.en: Gerard Jan Ligthart (1859-1916), educator. With H. Scheepstra he wrote the once very well-known reading books for schoolchildren, 'Ot en Sien'.

origins.name: Jan Luijkenstraat
origins.en: Poet and engraver (1649-1712), popular above all for 'Het menselyk bedryf' (the human occupations), which he made with his son Caspar. By council decision of 27 February 1895 the street name was extended over a longer stretch, which was reversed by council decision of 3 April 1912.

origins.name: Jan Maijenstraat
origins.en: The Dutch navigator Jan Cornelisz May, who in 1611 discovered the Jan Mayen island named after him, between Spitsbergen and Iceland.

origins.name: Jan Mankesstraat
origins.en: Painter and etcher (1889-1920), mainly of animals.

origins.name: Jan Mensplein
origins.en: Jan Mens (Amsterdam, 18 September 1897 - Amsterdam, 31 October 1967) was a Dutch writer. In 1935 he came into contact with the former schoolmaster Theo Thijssen, who gave him recommendations and feedback. In 1938 he won the Komso first-work prize for his manuscript Mensen zonder geld (people without money), which was his breakthrough. In the early 1960s he was the best-selling writer in the Netherlands, known for De kleine waarheid (the little truth), a picture of the life of the 'ordinary' Amsterdammer.

origins.name: Jan Moretuspad
origins.en: Jan Moretus (1543-1610) was the son-in-law of Christoffel Plantijn and worked in his bookshop for a long time. After Plantijn's death Jan Moretus carried on the bookshop and its printing works until his own death in 1610.

origins.name: Jan Muschstraat
origins.en: Johannes Petrus Musch (1875-1960), actor, a brilliant interpreter of Shakespeare and Vondel, who played a long series of great roles (Lucifer, De wijze kater, Nathan the Wise, Molière's Miser). In 1952 he celebrated 60 years on the stage.

origins.name: Jan Nautahof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1917-1944), born in Almelo, died in Vught camp. Nauta worked for the clandestine paper 'Trouw'.

origins.name: Jan Olphert Vaillantlaan
origins.en: Naval officer (1751-1800) in the service of the Admiralty of Amsterdam, an expert on finding longitude at sea by lunar distances. In 1784 he published 'Verhandeling van de stuurmanskunst' (treatise on navigation).

origins.name: Jan Oudegeeststraat
origins.en: One of the founders of the Dutch trade union movement (1870-1950). Chairman of the NVV from 1909 to 1919 and secretary of the International Federation of Trade Unions from 1919 to 1926. He was also a member of Amsterdam's city council and of the Senate and the House of Representatives.

origins.name: Jan Peppinkstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1918-1942) involved in many clandestine activities, who led the espionage group 'Nederland Vrij'.

origins.name: Jan Pieter Heijestraat
origins.en: Amsterdam physician and poet (1809-1876). He founded the Society for Nursing in 1844, was for thirty years director of Toonkunst, and promoted community singing. He wrote the popular children's songs 'De Zilvervloot' (the silver fleet), 'Kabels los' and 'Vlaggelied'.

origins.name: Jan Postmahof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1895-1944), active in the labour movement, born in Amsterdam and, as a leader of the clandestine Communist Party, executed by firing squad in Vught.

origins.name: Jan Poytstraat
origins.en: Jan Poyt (years of birth and death unknown), a sixteenth-century designer, designed the striking tower of Ransdorp, which dates from the early sixteenth century. For this neighbourhood the chosen category was the names of Dutch architects involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

origins.name: Jan Puntstraat
origins.en: An eighteenth-century actor, much admired in his day and later fiercely criticised. Punt was also a skilled engraver.

origins.name: Jan Rebelstraat
origins.en: Jan Rebel was an islet in the old IJ. The name appears on old maps; how the islet got it is unknown.

origins.name: Jan Ringelstraat
origins.en: The Sea Beggar from Oostzaan who in 1576 sailed through the chain across the harbour of Muiden, so that Sonoy could sail in with his fleet.

origins.name: Jan Schaeferbrug
origins.en: Johannes Lodewijk Nicolaas Schaefer (1940-1994), politician for the Labour Party (PvdA). He sat in the House of Representatives from 1971, was state secretary for urban renewal at the Ministry of Housing and Spatial Planning in the Den Uyl cabinet from 1973 to 1977, and alderman in Amsterdam from 1978 to 1986 (housing, urban renewal, building control, land company). His are the winged words 'In gelul kan je niet wonen' (you can't live in hot air). He gave an enormous boost to urban renewal and housebuilding in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Jan Schaeferpad
origins.en: Johannes Lodewijk Nicolaas Schaefer (1940-1994), politician for the Labour Party (PvdA). He sat in the House of Representatives from 1971, was state secretary for urban renewal at the Ministry of Housing and Spatial Planning in the Den Uyl cabinet from 1973 to 1977, and alderman in Amsterdam from 1978 to 1986 (housing, urban renewal, building control, land company). His are the winged words 'In gelul kan je niet wonen' (you can't live in hot air). He gave an enormous boost to urban renewal and housebuilding in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Jan Sluijtersstraat
origins.en: Painter (1881-1957) who developed an entirely personal style in his portraits, still lifes and genre pieces.

origins.name: Jan Smitstraat
origins.en: Johannes Wilhelmus Smit (1851-1940), founder of the Roman Catholic Volksbond (people's league), who worked above all among the workers on the Eastern Islands.

origins.name: Jan Somerhof
origins.en: Jan Egbert W.H. Somer (1905-1945), resistance fighter and printer by trade, who for a long time printed the clandestine paper 'Het Parool'. Born in Hoorn, he was executed by firing squad in Zutphen on 13 April 1945.

origins.name: Jan Springerhof
origins.en: Jan L. Springer (1850-1915), architect, who with J.B. Springer and A.L. van Gendt built the Stadsschouwburg (completed 1894). He was also director of the Hague Academy of Fine Arts.

origins.name: Jan Swammerdambrug
origins.en: Jan Swammerdam (1637-1680), anatomist and naturalist, who made important microscopic studies, preserved in his 'Bybel der natuure' (Bible of nature).

origins.name: Jan Theuniszhof
origins.en: Linguist (1569-1638), specialising in Arabic.

origins.name: Jan Thoméepad
origins.en: Physician and football pioneer known far beyond the borders (1886-1954). Until his death he was medical attendant to the Dutch national football team.

origins.name: Jan Tooropstraat
origins.en: Painter and draughtsman (1858-1928), who developed an entirely personal style full of symbolism, later imbued with a religious mood. Fresco in the Beurs on the Damrak.

origins.name: Jan van Beersstraat
origins.en: Flemish man of letters (1821-1888), poet of Flemish everyday life.

origins.name: Jan van Boendalestraat
origins.en: Flemish poet (c. 1280 - c. 1365), town clerk of Antwerp and a renowned didactic poet.

origins.name: Jan van der Neuthof
origins.en: Jan Tijmen van der Neut (1921-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, died in Siegburg prison (Germany). In 1941 he was arrested by the occupiers for distributing the clandestine paper 'Vrij Nederland'.

origins.name: Jan van Duivenvoordestraat
origins.en: Lord of Warmond (1547-1610), who fought on the side of the Sea Beggars and defeated the Spanish in the harbour of Cádiz (1596).

origins.name: Jan van Eijckstraat
origins.en: Southern Netherlandish painter (1386-1440), court painter to John of Bavaria and later to Philip of Burgundy. He used oil paint in a way entirely new for the time.

origins.name: Jan van Galenstraat
origins.en: Fleet commander (1604-1653), killed in the Battle of Livorno against the English.

origins.name: Jan van Goyenkade
origins.en: Painter (1596-1656), mainly of landscapes.

origins.name: Jan van Houthof
origins.en: Man of letters (1542-1609), the first scholarly archivist, who wrote the first Dutch alexandrines.

origins.name: Jan van Riebeekstraat
origins.en: Jan Anthonie van Riebeeck or Riebeek (1618-1708), who in 1652, in the service of the Dutch East India Company, founded the Cape Colony at the Cape of Good Hope.

origins.name: Jan van Schaffelaarplantsoen
origins.en: A cavalry captain in the struggle between the Hooks and the Cods, who jumped from the tower of Barneveld to save the lives of his men. The main character of 'De Schaapherder', a historical novel by J.F. Oltmans.

origins.name: Jan van Zutphenplantsoen
origins.en: Amsterdam diamond worker (1863-1958), who in 1894 founded the General Dutch Diamond Workers' Union (ANDB) with Henri Polak, and later did important social and humanitarian work.

origins.name: Jan van Zutphenstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam diamond worker (1863-1958), who in 1894 founded the General Dutch Diamond Workers' Union (ANDB) with Henri Polak, and later did important social and humanitarian work.

origins.name: Jan Vethstraat
origins.en: Painter and draughtsman (1864-1925), and also an art historian, who campaigned to preserve the beauty of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Jan Voermanstraat
origins.en: Painter of landscapes and flowers (1857-1944), who illustrated many Verkade albums.

origins.name: Jan Vrijmanstraat
origins.en: Jan Hulsebos (1925-1997), journalist and filmmaker, who changed his name to Jan Vrijman during the Second World War. He was involved in the clandestine paper 'De Waarheid', and co-founded and co-directed the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA).

origins.name: Jan Vroegopsingel
origins.en: Amsterdam police sergeant (1877-1946), co-founder and from 1917 to 1946 chairman of the Allotment Holders' League (Bond van Volkstuinders).

origins.name: Jan Willem Brouwersstraat
origins.en: Joannes Wilhelmus Brouwers (1831-1893), Roman Catholic priest, journalist and writer, co-editor of the daily 'De Tijd' from 1863 to 1870 and parish priest in Bovenkerk from 1870.

origins.name: Jan Wilsbrug
origins.en: Named after Jan Wils (1891-1972), architect of the Olympic Stadium and the two Citroën buildings on the Stadionplein. He also designed the City Theatre on the Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen.

origins.name: Jan Witheijnstraat
origins.en: Shipbuilder (1610-1662). In 1656 he was the first to be leased a shipyard on the island of Wittenburg.

origins.name: Jan Zijvertszstraat
origins.en: A Beggar captain, known for the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Jan Zwanenburghof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1921-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

origins.name: Janna van der Weglaan
origins.en: Janna Rinske van der Weg (1893-1974), skater. In 1917 she was the first woman ever to finish the Elfstedentocht, and the second woman in the event's history to take part. In daily life she was a domestic servant.

origins.name: Janusz Korczakstraat
origins.en: Polish-Jewish doctor (1878-1942), educator, children's author and director of an orphanage. On 6 August 1942 he was deported with two hundred children from the orphanage to the Treblinka extermination camp and murdered there together with the children.

origins.name: Jarasingel
origins.en: Víctor Jara (1938-1973), Chilean singer, who on international tours represented the voice of the opposition. For Chilean television he made programmes about the horrors of civil war and fascism. He was murdered by the junta in 1973.

origins.name: Jarmuiden
origins.en: The English port of Yarmouth, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Jasmijnstraat
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Jasonstraat
origins.en: A figure from Greek mythology, leader of the Argonauts around 1350 BC.

origins.name: Jasper Leijnsenstraat
origins.en: The heroic sailor in a naval battle against the Spanish near Reimerswaal in 1574.

origins.name: Jasper Warnerstraat
origins.en: A pioneer of football (1870-1924), who in 1897 succeeded Pim Mulier as chairman of the Dutch Football Association.

origins.name: Javakade
origins.en: The island (Java), one of the Greater Sunda Islands (Indonesia). For many years the premises of the Stoomvaart Maatschappij Nederland stood on this quay; the company handled a large share of shipping to the former Dutch East Indies.

origins.name: Javaplantsoen
origins.en: The island (Java), one of the Greater Sunda Islands (Indonesia). For many years the premises of the Stoomvaart Maatschappij Nederland stood on this quay; the company handled a large share of shipping to the former Dutch East Indies.

origins.name: Javaplein
origins.en: The island (Java), one of the Greater Sunda Islands (Indonesia). For many years the premises of the Stoomvaart Maatschappij Nederland stood on this quay; the company handled a large share of shipping to the former Dutch East Indies.

origins.name: Javastraat
origins.en: The island (Java), one of the Greater Sunda Islands (Indonesia). For many years the premises of the Stoomvaart Maatschappij Nederland stood on this quay; the company handled a large share of shipping to the former Dutch East Indies.

origins.name: Jean Desmetstraat
origins.en: Film distributor and cinema owner (1875-1956), who began as a fairground and travelling cinema operator. By bringing foreign films to the Netherlands he contributed substantially to the radical changes in the film industry between 1907 and 1916.

origins.name: Jekerstraat
origins.en: A small river that flows into the Maas at Maastricht.

origins.name: Jelle Posthumapad
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1906-1943), born in Amsterdam and executed by firing squad in Scheveningen in 1943. He was active in distributing the clandestine paper 'De Waarheid'.

origins.name: Jeltje de Bosch Kemperpad
origins.en: Jonkvrouw de Bosch Kemper (1836-1916), the driving force behind several associations that organised nursing courses, and co-founder of the Tesselschade association. She promoted, among other things, the founding of the Amsterdam School of Domestic Science and the drawing school for girls.

origins.name: Jennerstraat
origins.en: Edward Jenner (1749-1823), English physician, who improved cowpox inoculation against smallpox so that it could be used on a mass scale. The street's name was earlier set as Emmalaan (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 15 March 1904).

origins.name: Jephtastraat
origins.en: A tragedy by Vondel, dating from 1659. By council decision of 6 October 1948 the street name was extended southwards, but on 18 February 1970 that stretch was added to the Gulden Winckelplantsoen.

origins.name: Jeroenensteeg
origins.en: Probably named after the former Sint Jeroenentoren, one of the small towers on the fifteenth-century city wall, to which the little street led. Jeroen was parish priest of Noordwijk and was killed by the Norsemen in the ninth century; he was later canonised.

origins.name: Jisperveldstraat
origins.en: A nature reserve near the Noord-Holland village of Jisp, a botanically important peat area.

origins.name: Joan Melchior Kemperstraat
origins.en: Legal scholar (1776-1824), professor in Amsterdam and Leiden, who campaigned against the rule of the regents and for constitutional government.

origins.name: Joan Muyskenweg
origins.en: Amsterdam industrialist (1866-1928), director of Werkspoor, who played an important part in the company's development.

origins.name: Joannes de Swaefhof
origins.en: A seventeenth-century schoolmaster from Middelburg, whose treatise on upbringing is considered the first complete work of pedagogy published in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Joannes Reddingiusstraat
origins.en: Poet (1873-1944), part of the late flowering of the Tachtigers (the Movement of the Eighties).

origins.name: Jodenbreestraat
origins.en: This street, laid out on part of the Sint Antoniesdijk, was part of the Sint Antoniesbreestraat until the second half of the seventeenth century. At that time the Jewish population began to grow considerably, and this part of the Breestraat became the main street of the 'Jodenbuurt' (Jewish quarter). From then on the name Jodenbreestraat came into use. After the occupiers had deported the Jewish residents in the war years 1940-1945, and much of the odd-numbered side had been demolished (and burnt in stoves), the rest of that row of façades was demolished in the 1960s.

origins.name: Joes Kloppenburgbrug
origins.en: Joes Kloppenburg (1970-1996) was beaten to death by Richard L. on 17 August 1996 when he intervened in a street fight in the Voetboogsteeg with the words 'Kappen nou!' (stop it now!). This bridge is fairly close to where he died and is meant as a symbol against senseless violence.

origins.name: Joh.M. Coenenstraat
origins.en: Johannes Meinardus Coenen (1825-1899), musician, who composed choral works, ballets and operas, and conducted concerts in Felix Meritis and the Paleis voor Volksvlijt.

origins.name: Johan Braakensiekhof
origins.en: Illustrator and caricaturist (1858-1940), who for many years drew a weekly cartoon for 'De Groene Amsterdammer'. Also an illustrator of children's books.

origins.name: Johan Broedeletstraat
origins.en: Novelist and playwright (1877-1947), and also a critic for 'De Haagsche Post'.

origins.name: Johan Coltermanpad
origins.en: A Beggar captain of the Eighty Years' War and delegate of the Prince of Orange, who fought at Enkhuizen and Haarlem in 1572.

origins.name: Johan Cruijff Boulevard
origins.en: Johan Cruijff, born 25 April 1947 in Amsterdam, died 24 March 2016 in Barcelona. Forward for Ajax 1964-1973.

origins.name: Johan de Meesterstraat
origins.en: Man of letters (1860-1931), novelist, editor of 'De Nieuwe Gids' and contributor to the 'Nieuwe Rotterdamsche Courant'.

origins.name: Johan Greivestraat
origins.en: Johan Conrad Greive (Amsterdam, 2 April 1837 - Amsterdam, 14 May 1891) was a Dutch artist, known above all for his realist views of distant landscapes. During his career he was a member of the artists' society Arti et Amicitiae and taught at the Rijksakademie. His work can be seen in the Rijksmuseum and the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam, among other places.

origins.name: Johan Herman Doornstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1910-1944), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Ede.

origins.name: Johan Hofmanstraat
origins.en: Probably named after J. Hofman, chairman of the Dutch Christian Typographers' Union (NCTB) and editor of its journal. He wrote several articles in Eltheto and Stemmen des Tijds, and the memorial book for the NCTB's jubilee is his work. In 1945 Hofman became second chairman of the re-founded CNV executive.

origins.name: Johan Huijsenstraat
origins.en: Photographer (1877-1959), a versatile portrait photographer who also made townscapes.

origins.name: Johan Huizingalaan
origins.en: Historian (1874-1945), professor at Groningen and Leiden, with many publications to his name, including 'Herfsttij der Middeleeuwen' (The Waning of the Middle Ages).

origins.name: Johan Jongkindstraat
origins.en: Landscape painter and engraver (1819-1891), who lived most of his life in France. A representative of impressionism.

origins.name: Johan Kernstraat
origins.en: Linguist (1833-1917), professor of Sanskrit at Leiden, and an expert on Indian and Malayo-Polynesian languages and literatures.

origins.name: Johan Limpersstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1915-1944), a sculptor by profession (Prix de Rome 1940), born in Haarlem, executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Johan Lulofsstraat
origins.en: Professor of astronomy, mathematics and philosophy at Leiden (1711-1768), an expert on the chronometer method and as such an adviser to the States of Holland and the States General. In 1750 he published his 'Inleiding tot eene natuur- en wiskundige beschouwing des aardkloots' (introduction to a physical and mathematical study of the globe).

origins.name: Johan Ramaerstraat
origins.en: Hydraulic engineer (1852-1932) who built the Merwedekanaal.

origins.name: Johan Rijnjastraat
origins.en: Architect (1870-1941) whose designs include the first buildings in Noord, between 1911 and 1915.

origins.name: Johan Schamppad
origins.en: Johan Frederik Jeremias Schamp (1899-1943), resistance fighter, active in distributing the clandestine paper 'Vrij Nederland'. He died in Amsterdam after being mistreated by the occupiers.

origins.name: Johan Schippersplantsoen
origins.en: Johan Godefridus Schippers (1923-1945), resistance fighter, born and executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Johan van der Keukenstraat
origins.en: Photographer and filmmaker (1938-2001). He trained in film in Paris and became famous in the Netherlands at a young age with his photo book 'Wij zijn 17' (we are 17). From the 1960s he worked mainly as a filmmaker, making dozens of short and longer films that won many awards at home and abroad.

origins.name: Johan van Hasseltkade
origins.en: He lived from 1850 to 1916 and was director of Public Works from 1900 to 1907, and before that director of the Waterworks.

origins.name: Johan van Hasseltweg
