origins.en: He lived from 1850 to 1916 and was director of Public Works from 1900 to 1907, and before that director of the Waterworks.

origins.name: Johan van Kuyckstraat
origins.en: A Beggar captain who fought the Spanish near Vlissingen in 1572.

origins.name: Johann Keplerstraat
origins.en: German astronomer (1571-1630), who worked in Prague for many years;, one of the founders of modern astronomy, who discovered the laws governing the motion of the planets. A forerunner of Newton.

origins.name: Johann Siegerstraat
origins.en: Johann Gerhard Wilhelm Sieger (1856-1942), founder of the Amsterdam Quinine Factory.

origins.name: Johanna Naberstraat
origins.en: Feminist (1859-1941), co-founder of the International Archive for the Women's Movement, secretary of the Association for Women's Suffrage, board member of the International Woman Suffrage Alliance and member of Amsterdam's city council. Besides studies of feminism she wrote historical works.

origins.name: Johanna Schouten-Elsenhoutstraat
origins.en: Johanna Isidoro Eugenia Schouten-Elsenhout (1910-1992) was a Surinamese poet.

origins.name: Johanna Westerdijkstraat
origins.en: Botanist (1883-1961), from 1906 director of the Willie Commelin Scholten phytopathology laboratory in Amsterdam. In 1917 she became the first woman in the Netherlands to be appointed professor. The universities of Uppsala and Giessen gave her honorary doctorates.

origins.name: Johannes de Bekahof
origins.en: A fourteenth-century chronicler, whose works include the 'Great Chronicle of the Bishops of Utrecht'.

origins.name: Johannes Hilverdinkstraat
origins.en: Painter (1813-1902), mainly of landscapes.

origins.name: Johannes J. Glasweg
origins.en: Johannes Jacob Glas (1917-1942), resistance fighter. He kept up the links between the Waarheid resistance groups in the factories of Amsterdam-Noord, made explosives and had a part in the February Strike (1941). He was arrested in 1941 and executed by firing squad at Soesterberg on 19 November 1942.

origins.name: Johannes Jelgerhuishof
origins.en: Actor, draughtsman and painter (1770-1836), who excelled as a character actor.

origins.name: Johannes Meewisstraat
origins.en: Johannes Adriaan Meewis (1905-1948), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, died in Davos as a result of his imprisonment.

origins.name: Johannes Poststraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1906-1944), a farmer by trade, born in Hoogeveen, who played a leading role in the resistance, especially in the national knokploegen (armed squads). After a failed raid on the remand prison in Amsterdam he was executed by firing squad in Bloemendaal in 1944.

origins.name: Johannes van der Steurstraat
origins.en: Philanthropist (1865-1945), head of a children's home in Magelang (Indonesia) and a campaigner for child protection in the former Dutch East Indies, widely known as 'Pa van der Steur'.

origins.name: Johannes van der Waalsstraat
origins.en: Formerly Van der Waalsstraat. Physicist (1837-1923), professor in Amsterdam, who made a special study of the properties of gases and improved the Boyle-Gay-Lussac law. In 1910 he received the Nobel Prize in Physics. The name was changed in 1955 because of confusion with the Waalstraat in the Rivierenbuurt.

origins.name: Johannes van Meurshof
origins.en: Historian (1579-1639), professor of history and Greek at Leiden, who wrote important historical works on the Netherlands and Denmark.

origins.name: Johannes Verhulststraat
origins.en: Composer and conductor (1816-1891) of masses, overtures and songs. Conductor of the Caecilia concerts and of Felix Meritis, and around 1870 the undisputed leader of Amsterdam's musical life.

origins.name: Johannes Vermeerplein
origins.en: Painter (1632-1675), mainly of domestic interiors.

origins.name: Johannes Vermeerstraat
origins.en: Painter (1632-1675), mainly of landscapes and interiors.

origins.name: Johannes Worpstraat
origins.en: Organist and composer (1821-1891), author of the textbook 'Muziekleer' (music theory).

origins.name: Johannis de Rijkestraat
origins.en: Hydraulic engineer (1842-1913). In 1865 he was overseer in the building of the Oranjesluizen at Schellingwoude, and in 1872 he went to Japan, where in government service he improved harbours and major waterworks. From 1891 to 1903 he was a kind of state secretary at the Japanese Ministry of Transport and Water Management. He was knighted for his work in both the Netherlands and Japan.

origins.name: John Blankensteinstraat
origins.en: Football referee (1949-2006), one of the few openly gay people in the football world, who campaigned for gay emancipation.

origins.name: John Campbellstraat
origins.en: An eighteenth-century English captain, commander of the yacht Chatham, who in 1757 designed the sextant, a measuring instrument for finding position at sea.

origins.name: John Coltranestraat
origins.en: John William Coltrane (1926-1967), American jazz saxophonist, inspired by Indian and Arabic music.

origins.name: John Fernhouthof
origins.en: Photographer, cameraman and director (1913-1987), trained by the filmmaker Joris Ivens. Like Ivens he made several politically committed left-wing films. His most famous film is 'Sky over Holland' (1967), which shows the kinship between Dutch art and the Dutch landscape.

origins.name: John Franklinstraat
origins.en: English naval officer (1786-1847) who explored the Northwest Passage, but whose expedition perished in the polar ice.

origins.name: John Hadleystraat
origins.en: English physicist and mathematician (1682-1744), inventor of the octant, an angle-measuring instrument for finding position at sea.

origins.name: John Lockehof
origins.en: English philosopher (1632-1704), founder of a new approach to education and a forerunner of Kant.

origins.name: John M. Keynesplein
origins.en: John Maynard Keynes (1883-1946), British economist, known for his book 'The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money', which argues that government should play an active role in the economy and counter economic stagnation through investment. The book is often seen as the foundation of modern macroeconomics.

origins.name: John Motleyhof
origins.en: John Lothrop Motley (1814-1877), American historian of the Netherlands, whose works include 'The Rise of the Dutch Republic' (1856) and 'The Life and Death of John of Barneveld' (1875).

origins.name: John Napierstraat
origins.en: Scottish scholar (1550-1617), inventor of calculation with logarithms and so a pioneer of modern astronomy. His invention was of great importance for navigation.

origins.name: Joke Smitstraat
origins.en: Campaigner for women's emancipation (1933-1981), critic and writer. She founded the movement 'Man Vrouw Maatschappij' and was a member of the Emancipation Committee. From 1970 to 1971 she sat on Amsterdam's city council for the PvdA. She floated the idea of a political party of women's own.

origins.name: Jolicoeurstraat
origins.en: One of the leaders of the uprising of enslaved people in Suriname. The escaped enslaved people, also called Maroons, waged a guerrilla war against their oppressors, plundering the plantations and dealing heavy blows to the economy.

origins.name: Jollenpad
origins.en: A jol (dinghy) is a small keelboat.

origins.name: Jonagoldstraat
origins.en: An apple variety from the United States, known for its good taste and its equally good keeping qualities.

origins.name: Jonas Daniël Meijerplein
origins.en: Secretary of the committee that drafted the constitution of 1813 (1780-1834). The square was made by filling in parts of the Houtgracht and the Muidergracht. The name was given to this square between the synagogues because in 1810 J.D. Meijer, as peacemaker, drew up the concordat between the two Jewish congregations.

origins.name: Jonathanhof
origins.en: An apple, also known as the Ulster Seedling, the parent of the Jonagold and from the United States.

origins.name: Joop Eijlstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1896-1941), a warehouseman by trade, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in The Hague.

origins.name: Joop Gerritzestraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1913-1942), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad at Soest.

origins.name: Joop IJisbergstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1900-1942), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad at Soest.

origins.name: Joop van Weezelhof
origins.en: Joseph Jacques van Weezel, resistance fighter (1909-1945), active in the CPN from 1930. In 1941 he was arrested by the Nazis on suspicion of organising the February Strike. He died in the Dachau concentration camp in 1945.

origins.name: Joos Banckersplantsoen
origins.en: Fleet commander (1599-1647), who had a part in the capture of the Silver Fleet under Piet Hein and in the Battle of the Downs under Cornelis Tromp.

origins.name: Joos Banckersweg
origins.en: Fleet commander (1599-1647), who had a part in the capture of the Silver Fleet under Piet Hein and in the Battle of the Downs under Cornelis Tromp.

origins.name: Joos de Moorstraat
origins.en: Vice-admiral of Zeeland (1548-1618), known from the Eighty Years' War, who fought the Dunkirk privateers.

origins.name: Joost Bilhamerstraat
origins.en: Architect (1541-1590), also a surveyor and cartographer. His works include the tower of the Oude Kerk. His map of 1575 is one of the oldest known maps of Holland.

origins.name: Joris Ivensplein
origins.en: Filmmaker (1898-1989), one of the most important documentary makers in film history. He became known for avant-garde documentaries such as 'De brug' (the bridge, 1928) and 'Regen' (rain, 1929), in which he experimented with movement and rhythm. Later he became more and more interested in social issues and a convinced communist, and made films commissioned by various communist regimes. Because of his films about the 'police actions' in Indonesia he became persona non grata in the Netherlands. He received countless awards for his films.

origins.name: Joris Ivensstraat
origins.en: Filmmaker (1898-1989), one of the most important documentary makers in film history. He became known for avant-garde documentaries such as 'De brug' (the bridge, 1928) and 'Regen' (rain, 1929), in which he experimented with movement and rhythm. Later he became more and more interested in social issues and a convinced communist, and made films commissioned by various communist regimes. Because of his films about the 'police actions' in Indonesia he became persona non grata in the Netherlands. He received countless awards for his films.

origins.name: Joris van Andringastraat
origins.en: A seventeenth-century naval commander, died 1676, and secretary to Admiral Michiel de Ruyter.

origins.name: Joris van den Berghweg
origins.en: Sports journalist (1882-1953), especially of cycling.

origins.name: Joseph Haydnpad
origins.en: Joseph Haydn (1732-1809), Austrian composer.

origins.name: Joseph Scaligerstraat
origins.en: Joseph Justus Scaliger (1540-1609), classical philologist and professor in Geneva. As a Huguenot he fled after the St Bartholomew's Day Massacre and later came to Holland, where he became a professor at Leiden. He taught Hugo de Groot and founded the Leiden school of philology.

origins.name: Joseph Schumpeterstraat
origins.en: Joseph Alois Schumpeter (1883-1950), Austrian economist, who fled to America because of the rise of the Nazis. Known for his theory of 'creative destruction': old ways of working and old structures are constantly replaced by new ones.

origins.name: Josephus Jittastraat
origins.en: Abraham Carel Josephus Jitta (1887-1958) was a Dutch legal scholar and professor at the Technische Hogeschool in Delft.

origins.name: Joubertstraat
origins.en: Petrus Joubert (1831-1900), commander-in-chief of the Boers in the Transvaal wars of independence.

origins.name: Jouke Zietsmastraat
origins.en: Jouke Zietsma (1893-1962) was involved in Tuindorp Nieuwendam, a high point of the rural variant of the Amsterdam School. For this neighbourhood the chosen category was the names of Dutch architects involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

origins.name: Jozef Israëlskade
origins.en: Painter (1824-1911), a pupil of J.W. Pieneman and J.H. Kruseman, who became known for his socially engaged scenes, among them scenes from the lives of poor fishermen.

origins.name: Juliana van Stolbergstraat
origins.en: Juliana of Stolberg (1506-1580), wife of William of Nassau and mother of Prince William of Orange. Princess Juliana is named after her.

origins.name: Julianaplein
origins.en: Juliana Louise Emma Marie Wilhelmina, born 30 April 1909, married in 1937 to Prince Bernhard of Lippe-Biesterfeld, Queen of the Kingdom of the Netherlands from 1948 to 1980.

origins.name: Julius Pergerstraat
origins.en: Photographer (1840-1924), a contemporary of Pieter Oosterhuis, who like Oosterhuis photographed engineering works, including bridges and railways.

origins.name: Jungfrau
origins.en: A mountain peak in Switzerland, 4158 metres high.

origins.name: Jupiterstraat
origins.en: The largest planet in our solar system.

origins.name: Justus Halbertsmastraat
origins.en: Frisian writer, philologist and historian (1789-1869).

origins.name: Justus Lipsiusstraat
origins.en: Linguist (1547-1606), professor at Leiden and later at Leuven.

origins.name: Justus van Maurikstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam cigar manufacturer (1846-1904), who became very popular as a writer about the life of ordinary Amsterdammers. He was co-editor of 'De Groene Amsterdammer'.

origins.name: Juttepeerpad
origins.en: An old Dutch pear variety. The street lies on the former De Bongerd allotment complex.

origins.name: Kaapstadweg
origins.en: With Bloemfontein and Pretoria, one of the capitals of South Africa (Cape Town).

origins.name: Kaasjeskruidstraat
origins.en: A plant family (mallows) named for its fruit, shaped somewhat like a little cheese. The common mallow, which also grows in the Netherlands, was used in classical antiquity against all sorts of ailments, from bowel and womb complaints to wasp and scorpion stings.

origins.name: Kabelgaststraat
origins.en: A trade name: someone who splices and joins cables. The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

origins.name: Kabelweg
origins.en: The insulated bundle of wires carrying electricity under water or underground (a cable). The road follows the strip of land along which, around 1950, the high-voltage cables were laid from the Hemweg power station to the western garden cities then being built, to supply them with power.

origins.name: Kadijksplein
origins.en: When a great deal of land had built up through silting outside the old sea dike (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike, or quay dike (kadijk), was built. It was originally called the new sea dike, but that name later fell out of use. When this new dike was raised further, people spoke of the Laagte (low part) and the Hoogte (high part) of the Kadijk. Until 1943 the Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat. This is because it lies in line with the Plantage Kerklaan, although it has never been connected to it.

origins.name: Kadoelenbrug
origins.en: The name of the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was added to Amsterdam on 1 August 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) appears as early as 1375. In 1429 the manors of Landsmeer and Quadolen are mentioned, which then shared one lord. Old maps show Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterland sea dike (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1 August 1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed because of confusion with the Zuideinde (formerly Oostzaan).

origins.name: Kadoelenpad
origins.en: The name of the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was added to Amsterdam on 1 August 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) appears as early as 1375. In 1429 the manors of Landsmeer and Quadolen are mentioned, which then shared one lord. Old maps show Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterland sea dike (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1 August 1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed because of confusion with the Zuideinde (formerly Oostzaan).

origins.name: Kadoelenweg
origins.en: The name of the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was added to Amsterdam on 1 August 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) appears as early as 1375. In 1429 the manors of Landsmeer and Quadolen are mentioned, which then shared one lord. Old maps show Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterland sea dike (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1 August 1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed because of confusion with the Zuideinde (formerly Oostzaan).

origins.name: Kagelinkkade
origins.en: The name of an old farm east of Diepenheim (Overijssel), by the Kagelink wood.

origins.name: Kajuitpad
origins.en: A part of a ship (the cabin).

origins.name: Kajuitweg
origins.en: A part of a ship (the cabin).

origins.name: Kalfjeslaan
origins.en: The former eighteenth-century inn on the Amsteldijk (demolished 1967), later the café-restaurant Het Kalfje.

origins.name: Kalkmarkt
origins.en: The lime market (kalkmarkt) was held on this quay from about 1663 until the end of the eighteenth century. The quay was made when the Nieuwe Waalseiland was filled in with earth in 1644.

origins.name: Kalkoenstraat
origins.en: The game bird (the pheasant).

origins.name: Kalmoesstraat
origins.en: A water plant (sweet flag).

origins.name: Kalverstraat
origins.en: After the calf market (kalvermarkt) held here until the seventeenth century. The name already occurs as such in 1393. However, no proof has been found that a cattle market was really held here, only that there was a calf market on the Dam in 1586. When it came inside the city, the stretch between the Spui and the Munt was called Byndewyck, that is, Binnenwijk (inner quarter). This southern part had the cattle market from 1486 to 1629 and was also called Ossemarkt (ox market). After that the name Kalverstraat spread over the whole street.

origins.name: Kamerlingh Onneslaan
origins.en: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes (1853-1926), physicist and professor at Leiden, who liquefied helium. In 1913 he won the Nobel Prize in Physics.

origins.name: Kamerpalmhof
origins.en: A kind of palm related to the succulents, with thick, leathery leaves (aspidistra).

origins.name: Kamillestraat
origins.en: A strongly scented meadow plant (camomile) of the daisy family, found not only in meadows but also often on waste ground.

origins.name: Kamperfoelieweg
origins.en: The climbing shrub (honeysuckle).

origins.name: Kampervenuspad
origins.en: An old Dutch pear variety. The street lies on the former De Bongerd allotment complex.

origins.name: Kampina
origins.en: A nature reserve east of Oisterwijk (Noord-Brabant), made up of fens, the Kampina heath and the valley of the Beerze stream.

origins.name: Kanaaldijk West
origins.en: Named after the Kanaaldijk: the west side of the dike.

origins.name: Kanaalpost
origins.en: Named after the Kanaaldijk.

origins.name: Kanaalstraat
origins.en: The kanaal (canal) meant here is the nearby Jacob van Lennepkanaal.

origins.name: Kanariestraat
origins.en: The songbird (the canary).

origins.name: Kaneelappelstraat
origins.en: A tropical fruit (sugar apple), originally from South America. Its skin is usually green, and its very soft flesh is white, with a sweet, aromatic taste.

origins.name: Kanteel
origins.en: The raised part of a crenellated defensive wall, with arrow slits (a merlon). The name refers to the rectangular shape of the neighbouring buildings.

origins.name: Kantershof
origins.en: The name of a farm in Bunde (Limburg).

origins.name: Kantershofpad
origins.en: The name of a farm in Bunde (Limburg).

origins.name: Kantershofstraat
origins.en: The name of a farm in Bunde (Limburg).

origins.name: Kapkarpad
origins.en: The very first type of caravan (a hooded cart). The street name refers to the caravan site here.

origins.name: Kapoeasweg
origins.en: A navigable river in Indonesia, on Kalimantan (Borneo).

origins.name: Kapteynstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Cornelis Kapteyn (1851-1922), astronomer and professor at Groningen, known for his research on star streams. He also lectured in the United States and South Africa.

origins.name: Karel Doormanstraat
origins.en: Karel Willem Frederik Marie Doorman (1889-1942), naval officer. During the Second World War he was rear admiral in the Dutch East Indies. In 1942 he was given the impossible task of preventing the Japanese from landing on Java, and was killed in this famous Battle of the Java Sea. The street came onto Amsterdam territory in 1921 under the name Houtmanstraat (council decision of Sloten, 8 March 1910), and by council decision of 22 March 1922 was named Zeven Provinciënstraat, after Admiral De Ruyter's flagship. After some changes to its boundaries (council decisions of 27 April 1933 and 10 June 1936), its present name was set in 1946.

origins.name: Karel du Jardinstraat
origins.en: Painter of landscapes and animals (1622-1678).

origins.name: Karel Klinkenbergstraat
origins.en: Painter of townscapes (1852-1924).

origins.name: Karel van de Woestijnestraat
origins.en: Flemish man of letters (1878-1929), professor at Ghent from 1921, one of the greatest Flemish poets after Guido Gezelle, and also known as a critic.

origins.name: Karel van het Revebrug
origins.en: Karel van het Reve (1921-1999) was a professor of Russian literature and a man of letters, widely regarded as one of the most important non-fiction writers in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Karimatastraat
origins.en: An Indonesian island group off the west coast of Kalimantan (Borneo).

origins.name: Karl Grögersingel
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), one of the nine involved in the attack on the Amsterdam population register on 27 March 1943. He was also involved in the attack on the railway near Sloterdijk and in founding the seditious magazine 'Rattenkruid' (rat poison).

origins.name: Karl Marxpad
origins.en: Karl Heinrich Marx (1818-1883), German philosopher and economist, who believed that capitalism would necessarily perish through its own development. Founder of Marxism, in which class struggle and the overthrow of the ruling class are central.

origins.name: Karlskrona-eiland
origins.en: A Swedish port on the Baltic from which much potash, timber and iron used to be shipped to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Karnstraat
origins.en: A dairy implement for making butter from milk (a churn).

origins.name: Karpatastraat
origins.en: Karpata, nicknamed Bastian, one of the leaders of the slave revolt that broke out on Curaçao in August 1795. He was captured in September that year and executed.

origins.name: Karperstraat
origins.en: The freshwater fish (the carp).

origins.name: Karperweg
origins.en: The freshwater fish (the carp).

origins.name: Karspeldreef
origins.en: The name recalls the former municipality of Weesperkarspel. Karspel or kerspel is an old word for a rural municipality, and earlier still for a church village or parish.

origins.name: Karthuizersdwarsstraat
origins.en: The streets were laid out where the monastery of the 'Carthuysers ter saliger havene' (Carthusians of the blessed haven) stood from 1394 to 1578. Until 1892 the cross street was called Blindemansteeg, but the name was changed because of confusion with the other Blindemansteeg. The path and playground are on the site of the monastery's former graveyard, which is why the park was called Karthuizer Kerkhof until 1889.

origins.name: Karthuizersplantsoen
origins.en: The streets were laid out where the monastery of the 'Carthuysers ter saliger havene' (Carthusians of the blessed haven) stood from 1394 to 1578. Until 1892 the cross street was called Blindemansteeg, but the name was changed because of confusion with the other Blindemansteeg. The path and playground are on the site of the monastery's former graveyard, which is why the park was called Karthuizer Kerkhof until 1889.

origins.name: Karthuizersstraat
origins.en: The streets were laid out where the monastery of the 'Carthuysers ter saliger havene' (Carthusians of the blessed haven) stood from 1394 to 1578. Until 1892 the cross street was called Blindemansteeg, but the name was changed because of confusion with the other Blindemansteeg. The path and playground are on the site of the monastery's former graveyard, which is why the park was called Karthuizer Kerkhof until 1889.

origins.name: Karveelstraat
origins.en: A fast sailing ship (caravel), carrying mainly a mainsail. The type dates from the late Middle Ages: two of Columbus's three ships in 1492, the Niña and the Pinta, were caravels.

origins.name: Kastanjeplein
origins.en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

origins.name: Kastanjeweg
origins.en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

origins.name: Kastelenstraat
origins.en: The name was given because the street runs right through the neighbourhood of castle names. The last stretch of the Kastelenstraat was renamed Zwaansvliet on 3 February 1965.

origins.name: Kasterleepark
origins.en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Kastrupstraat
origins.en: The name of Copenhagen's airport.

origins.name: Katrijpstraat
origins.en: A hamlet, also spelt Catrijp, at the foot of the dunes near Schoorl (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Kattenburgergracht
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. No explanation for the name has been found so far. There was a house called 'de Cat', but that name is only recorded in the eighteenth century. After many buildings had been demolished during the occupation, the rest were demolished in 1965-1968. Rebuilding then began on a new street plan. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

origins.en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. No explanation for the name has been found so far. There was a house called 'de Cat', but that name is only recorded in the eighteenth century. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

origins.en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. After many buildings had been demolished during the occupation, the rest were demolished in 1965-1968. Rebuilding then began on a new street plan. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

origins.name: Kattenburgerplein
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. No explanation for the name has been found so far. There was a house called 'de Cat', but that name is only recorded in the eighteenth century. After many buildings had been demolished during the occupation, the rest were demolished in 1965-1968. Rebuilding then began on a new street plan. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

origins.name: Kattenburgerstraat
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. No explanation for the name has been found so far. There was a house called 'de Cat', but that name is only recorded in the eighteenth century. After many buildings had been demolished during the occupation, the rest were demolished in 1965-1968. Rebuilding then began on a new street plan. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

origins.name: Kattengat
origins.en: Originally this was a narrow little canal running from the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal (now the Spuistraat) to the Singel. There is no agreement about the origin of the name. A narrow passage used to be called, figuratively, a kattegat: a gap so narrow that not even a cat could get through. The name may also come from the old nature of the ground: marshy land where catmint grows. The little canal was filled in during the second half of the nineteenth century. Part of it is now called Koggestraat. The remaining little street was widened considerably by demolition in 1936.

origins.name: Kattenlaan
origins.en: The origin and age of the name are unknown. The street came over under the same name from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel in 1896.

origins.name: Katwijkstraat
origins.en: The Zuid-Holland fishing village and seaside resort.

origins.name: Kazernestraat
origins.en: After the Oranje-Nassau barracks (kazerne), built in 1811.

origins.name: Kea Boumanstraat
origins.en: Kornelia Bouman (1903-1998), tennis player. Until 1996 she was the only Dutch Grand Slam winner (French Championships, 1927). She won bronze in the mixed doubles at the 1924 Olympic Games.

origins.name: Keerpunt
origins.en: The name came out of conversations with residents: a keerpunt (turning point) in the city council's thinking, to build homes instead of office buildings, the result of the neighbourhood's participation.

origins.name: Keerwal
origins.en: A place where you can go no further and have to turn back (keren). The buildings on the Keerwal screen the homes by the railway in the Funenpark.

origins.name: Kees Abspoelstraat
origins.en: Kees Abspoel (1899-1970) was Shell's in-house architect, and as such designed Shell's Great Laboratory in Amsterdam-Noord, on the Overhoeks site.

origins.name: Kees Boekestraat
origins.en: For this neighbourhood the chosen category was the names of Dutch architects involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

origins.name: Kees Broekmanstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Broekman (1927-1992), speed skater. In 1952 he was the first Dutchman to win a Winter Olympics medal, silver in the 5000 metres. He was also second in the 10 km.

origins.name: Kees Fensbrug
origins.en: Kees Fens (1929-2008) was an Amsterdam literary critic, essayist and man of letters. He received the P.C. Hooft Prize in 1990 and an honorary doctorate from the University of Amsterdam in 2004. From his house he looked out on this bridge, and in 2008 he published the book 'Het geluk van de brug' (the happiness of the bridge).

origins.name: Kees Schererhof
origins.en: Christoffel Johannes Scherer (1920-1993), photographer, who made his breakthrough with reportage on the North Sea flood of 1953, among other things. Two years later he co-founded World Press Photo. He portrayed Amsterdam poetically.

origins.name: Keienbergweg
origins.en: The name of a hill in Gelderland, between Velp and Beekhuizen.

origins.name: Keizersbrug
origins.en: It takes its name from the nearby Keizersstraat.

origins.name: Keizersgracht
origins.en: After Emperor Maximilian, Archduke of Austria, who in 1489 granted Amsterdam the privilege of bearing the imperial crown on its coat of arms.

origins.name: Keizersstraat
origins.en: On the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Kelbergen
origins.en: The name of a manor house in Brummen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kelbergenpad
origins.en: The name of a manor house in Brummen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kemangiestraat
origins.en: A herb, also called lemon basil or Thai basil.

origins.name: Kemiriestraat
origins.en: A nut. A kemiri (candlenut) is a kind of almond with a very strong taste.

origins.name: Kemminkhorstweg
origins.en: Named after the old farm Kemminckhorst near Dalfsen (Overijssel).

origins.name: Kempenlaan
origins.en: The border region of Belgian and Dutch Brabant (the Kempen).

origins.name: Kempering
origins.en: The name of a farm at Reutum, in Tubbergen (Overijssel).

origins.name: Ken Saro-Wiwastraat
origins.en: Nigerian writer (1941-1995), politician and businessman. As leader of MOSOP, the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People founded in 1990, he campaigned for more autonomy for the Ogoni. In 1995 he was sentenced to death after a show trial by the dictatorial regime, and on 10 November 1995 he was hanged together with eight other Ogoni activists.

origins.name: Kennemerduinstraat
origins.en: The Kennemerduinen national park, a nature reserve north of the Bloemendaalse Zeeweg.

origins.name: Keratellastraat
origins.en: A microscopic water creature (a rotifer) with two fast-spinning crowns of cilia and strong chewing parts for grinding its food. The keratella lives in a small case marked by spines.

origins.name: Kerdijkhof
origins.en: Arnoldus Polak Kerdijk (1846-1905), politician and journalist, who as a progressive liberal worked for the emancipation of workers. He was also a director of the Rijkspostspaarbank (post office savings bank).

origins.name: Kerkepad
origins.en: The Kerkepad is named after its position and purpose: the path from the dike village of Nieuwendam to the village church.

origins.name: Kerklaan Zunderdorp
origins.en: The main street of Zunderdorp, leading towards the village church.

origins.name: Kerkstraat
origins.en: The Kerkstraat was laid out in 1665 and named for the plan to link four churches (kerken) with it: the Amstelkerk, the Oosterkerk and two others that were never built, one by the Molenpad and one by the Weesperstraat. Later the street got various names: Kerkstraat (to the Amstel), Nieuwe Kerkstraat (to the Roetersstraat), Plantage Kerklaan (in the Plantage) and Korte Kerkstraat, which was renamed Tussen Kadijken in 1943.

origins.name: Kermispad
origins.en: The fair (kermis) with its attractions. The name is linked to the world of travelling people and refers to the caravan site here.

origins.name: Kerriestraat
origins.en: A spice mix (curry), originally from India, where the word 'kari' means sauce. The English corrupted 'kari' into 'curry'. Kerrie came to the Netherlands by way of Indonesia.

origins.name: Kersenstraat
origins.en: The fruit of the cherry tree.

origins.name: Kerstomaatplantsoen
origins.en: A kind of tomato, also called cocktail or cherry tomato.

origins.name: Kervelplantsoen
origins.en: A herb (chervil). In the Middle Ages the plant was often found in monastery gardens.

origins.name: Ketelhuisplein
origins.en: The very striking boiler house of the former Wilhelmina Gasthuis.

origins.name: Ketelmakerij
origins.en: The street lies on the site of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij. Ketelmakerij (boilerworks) refers to one of the workshops that were here.

origins.name: Ketelmakerstraat
origins.en: This trade name (boilermaker) recalls the old boilerworks that was here.

origins.name: Ketelstraat
origins.en: The machine part, the steam boiler (ketel): a closed vessel in which water is turned into steam by heating.

origins.name: Keurenplein
origins.en: Keuren are the ordinances of any public authority before 1795. The name is linked to the verb 'keuren' in the sense of 'choosing': originally these were the rules to be observed, or laid down, on the day new officials were chosen.

origins.name: Keverberg
origins.en: A castle in Kessel (Limburg), also called Kessel castle, built on the foundations of an eleventh-century stronghold and destroyed by German troops in 1944.

origins.name: Kiefskamp
origins.en: One of the best-preserved eighteenth-century country houses, from about 1770, near Vorden (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kiekstraat
origins.en: Israël David Kiek (1811-1899), photography pioneer. In the Netherlands his surname has become a byword for the unpretentious, off-the-cuff photo: the kiekje (snapshot). He had a photo studio in Leiden and photographed Leiden student life.

origins.name: Kierkegaardstraat
origins.en: Søren Kierkegaard (1813-1855), Danish preacher and philosopher, whose work centres on his personal view of life. He rejected the state church and institutional Christianity.

origins.name: Kievitstraat
origins.en: The meadow bird (the lapwing).

origins.name: Kijkduinstraat
origins.en: The former fort south of Huisduinen near Den Helder, known for the naval battle of 1673 in which Admiral De Ruyter defeated the combined Anglo-French fleet.

origins.name: Kikkenstein
origins.en: The name of a patrician house in Loenen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kikkensteinhof
origins.en: The name of a patrician house in Loenen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kikkensteinstraat
origins.en: The name of a patrician house in Loenen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kimpoweg
origins.en: The name of the airport of Seoul, South Korea.

origins.name: Kinderdijkstraat
origins.en: The river dike along the Noord, in the Alblasserwaard (Zuid-Holland).

origins.name: King's Cross
origins.en: A major railway station in north London.

origins.name: Kingsfordweg
origins.en: The name of the airport of Sydney, Australia.

origins.name: Kinkerstraat
origins.en: Johannes Kinker (1764-1845), poet, philosopher and lawyer in Amsterdam and The Hague. From 1817 until the Belgian Revolution of 1830 he was professor of Dutch language and literature at the new university of Liège, and argued for the unity of the northern and southern Netherlands. He was one of the first to introduce Kant's philosophy in the Netherlands, and was best known as a poet for his parodies. The street was named after him in 1881.

origins.name: Kinrooistraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Klaas Geertsplantsoen
origins.en: Klaas Geerts (1932-2002) founded the architectural practice INBO. He played an important part in the post-war reconstruction of the Netherlands and designed the Molenwijk. For this neighbourhood the chosen category was the names of Dutch architects involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

origins.name: Klaas Katerstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam bricklayer (1833-1906), who in 1876 founded the Christian association Patrimonium in Amsterdam and chaired it until 1899. From 1880 to 1900 he led the Christian Workers' League.

origins.name: Klaas Wannen
origins.en: Named after the ditch between the Twiske and the Gouw, probably named after a farmer. It disappeared when the Twiske was turned into a polder and laid out as woodland.

origins.name: Klapmutsenveem
origins.en: A veem is a company that stores goods in its warehouses and delivers them out again. Each veem had its own badge, after which it was named. These could be hats of different colours and shapes (Klapmutsen, Blauwhoeden and others). Some took their name from where their workmen came from (Vriesseveem, Zeeuwse Veem and others).

origins.name: Klaprozenweg
origins.en: The klaproos (corn poppy), a plant of the poppy family.

origins.name: Klarenburg
origins.en: The former farm Karenburg on the Uitweg, demolished to build the Osdorp garden city. The l in the street name is therefore a mistake, but the burgomaster and aldermen later judged the difference not important enough to change the council decision.

origins.name: Klaroenstraat
origins.en: A leaf vegetable with red-flamed leaves, also known as amaranth or Chinese spinach.

origins.name: Klaverbladstraat
origins.en: The name refers to the leaf of the native edible plants of the pea family (clover).

origins.name: Kleefkruidstraat
origins.en: An edible plant of the bedstraw family (cleavers), which owes its stickiness to the many little hooks that cover it.

origins.name: Kleiburg
origins.en: A former farm in the Bijlmermeer, on the Weespertrekvaart.

origins.name: Kleine Beerstraat
origins.en: A constellation (the Dolphin).

origins.name: Kleine Bickersstraat
origins.en: These streets are on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr Johan Bicker (1591-1653), a shipbuilder and merchant, and a schepen (magistrate) and burgomaster of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets later laid out on the island automatically took the name of its founder.

origins.name: Kleine Diestraat
origins.en: The nearby waters of the Kleine Die and the Grote Die. 'Die' is a contraction of 'de' (the) and 'ie'. 'Ie' in turn is a Noord-Holland variant of 'aa', meaning water, which in Frisian-speaking areas is written 'ee'. The spelling 'IJ' is actually incorrect.

origins.name: Kleine Houtstraat
origins.en: Recalls the timber trade that used to be concentrated around the Haarlemmer Houttuinen. (The Grote Houtstraat was abolished in 1973.)

origins.name: Kleine Pimpernelstraat
origins.en: A perennial with edible leaves (salad burnet). Its round flower head carries small greenish-purple flowers.

origins.name: Kleine Wittenburgerstraat
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

origins.name: Kleine Zonneplein
origins.en: The central body of the planetary system to which the Earth belongs (the sun).

origins.name: Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen
origins.en: Maria Johanna Kleine née Gartman (1818-1885), actress. As the first woman teacher at the Drama School she trained many actors and directors. Before it was named in 1915, the square was part of the Lijnbaansgracht and the Weteringschans.

origins.name: Klieverink
origins.en: Het Klieverink or Klievering, the name of a farm in Losser (Overijssel).

origins.name: Klieverinkweg
origins.en: Het Klieverink or Klievering, the name of a farm in Losser (Overijssel).

origins.name: Klimopbrug
origins.en: The climbing shrub (ivy).

origins.name: Klimopstraatje
origins.en: The climbing shrub (ivy).

origins.name: Klimopweg
origins.en: The climbing shrub (honeysuckle).

origins.name: Klinkerweg
origins.en: A metalworker who fastens iron parts together with rivets (a riveter). The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

origins.name: Klipperstraat
origins.en: A long, narrow, fast-sailing three-master (a clipper).

origins.name: Kloekhorststraat
origins.en: The name of an old farm in the hamlet of Klein Dochteren, in Lochem (Gelderland).

origins.name: Klokkenbergweg
origins.en: The name of a hill near Nijmegen.

origins.name: Klönne plein
origins.en: The gasholder specialists August Klönne built the Westergasfabriek's new telescopic gasholder in 1902. The gasholder is the landmark of the former works site.

origins.name: Kloveniersburgwal
origins.en: The Kloveniersburgwal owes its name to a part of the civic guard called kloveniers, after the firearm its men used, a culverin.

origins.name: Klovenierssteeg
origins.en: After the Kloveniersdoelen, the meeting place of the old civic guard, where the Doelen Hotel now stands. The old civic guard originally used the crossbow, but in 1522 the guardsmen were given guns, or kloveren, and were named kloveniers after them. Until the end of the sixteenth century this burgwal was the outermost city moat. Before 1909 the alley was called Watersteeg, but this caused confusion with the Watersteeg by the Rokin.

origins.name: Kneppelhoutstraat
origins.en: Johannes Kneppelhout (1814-1885), pseudonym Klikspaan, writer of realistic, humorous sketches and stories.

origins.name: Kneppelweg
origins.en: The name of an old farm near Eefde (Gelderland).

origins.name: Knokkestraat
origins.en: A Belgian coastal town in the province of West Flanders (West-Vlaanderen).

origins.name: Knollendamstraat
origins.en: A village in the Zaan region. The street was originally named Derde Spaarndammerdwarsstraat (council decision of 30 March 1881).

origins.name: KNSM-laan
origins.en: The Koninklijke Nederlandsche Stoomboot-Maatschappij (Royal Netherlands Steamship Company), founded in 1856 and one of the largest Dutch shipping companies. It ran scheduled services to the West Indies, Central America, the west and north coasts of South America, the Levant and European ports, and also sailed between North and South America. In 1981 the KNSM was absorbed into the Koninklijke Nedlloyd group.

origins.name: Koekoeksplein
origins.en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

origins.name: Koekoeksstraat
origins.en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

origins.name: Koen Limpergstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1908-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Haarlem.

origins.name: Koenenkade
origins.en: After a former resident.

origins.name: Koerierstersplein
origins.en: Girls who were active in the resistance in the Second World War. They handed out ration cards, false papers and money, and escorted Jewish children by bicycle or train. The street name is also a tribute to the couriers Miep Gies and Elly Voskuijl, who looked after the people hiding in the Secret Annex, among them Anne Frank.

origins.name: Koestraat
origins.en: The street ran along the cowshed (koestal) of the former Bethany convent, which stretched between this street and the Bethaniënstraat.

origins.name: Koffieweg
origins.en: The ground powder of roasted coffee beans. Coffee is handled in the port of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Kofschipstraat
origins.en: A round-built two-master with a broad stern (a kof), a slow sailer.

origins.name: Kogeldistelstraat
origins.en: An akkerdistel (creeping thistle) is a species of thistle.

origins.name: Koggestraat
origins.en: An old type of ship (the cog), after which the traditional Amsterdam Koggeschip is named. Before it was filled in in the nineteenth century, the water was part of the Kattengat.

origins.name: Koivistokade
origins.en: A large Russian oil port on the Baltic, today known as Primorsk. Koivisto, Finnish for 'birch grove', belonged to Finland from 1918 to 1944.

origins.name: Kokmeeuwpad
origins.en: A bird of the gull family (the black-headed gull).

origins.name: Kokospalmhof
origins.en: A kind of palm. The inside of the fruit of this palm looks like the face of a monkey, which in Portuguese is called 'coco'.

origins.name: Kolbergbrug
origins.en: Kolberg was the German name for the Polish Baltic port of Kołobrzeg. The names in the Houthavens are taken from places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Kolfschotenstraat
origins.en: An estate with a house near Scherpenzeel (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kolibristraat
origins.en: A very small tropical bird (the hummingbird).

origins.name: Kolksluis
origins.en: Bridge 302 lies in the Zeedijk over the Oudezijdskolk. The kolk of a lock is the chamber between its two pairs of gates. This was where the Oudezijds Voorburgwal and Achterburgwal drained into the IJ. The lock dates from the early fifteenth century.

origins.name: Kolksteeg
origins.en: This was where the Oudezijds Voorburgwal and Achterburgwal drained into the IJ. The lock dates from the early fifteenth century.

origins.name: Kollenbergweg
origins.en: The name of a hill east of Sittard (Limburg).

origins.name: Kölpinstraat
origins.en: The lake, the Kölpinsee, in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, northern Germany.

origins.name: Kombuisweg
origins.en: A kombuis is a ship's kitchen (galley).

origins.name: Kometensingel
origins.en: Small celestial bodies made of ice, gas and dust (comets).

origins.name: Komijnstraat
origins.en: A culinary herb (cumin) of the carrot family, native to the Middle East and India.

origins.name: Kompasweg
origins.en: Named after the navigational instrument (the compass).

origins.name: Konijnenstraat
origins.en: The rodent (the rabbit). The name arose from the trade in hides and skins carried on in this part of the city.

origins.name: Koningin Wilhelminaplein
origins.en: Wilhelmina Helena Pauline Maria, Princess of Orange-Nassau (1880-1962), daughter of King William III and Queen Emma, Queen of the Netherlands from 1898 to 1948.

origins.name: Koninginneweg
origins.en: Named after the queen of the time, Queen Emma.

origins.name: Koningsbergenbrug
origins.en: Koningsbergen was the Dutch name for Königsberg, now the Russian Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad. The names in the Houthavens are taken from places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Koningslaan
origins.en: After the kings of the House of Orange-Nassau.

origins.name: Koningspalmplein
origins.en: A kind of palm, considered by many the most beautiful palm in the world, hence the name royal palm.

origins.name: Koningsplein
origins.en: In the first years of the seventeenth century part of the Singel was called Koningsgracht, in honour of the allied King Henry IV of France. The square on this Koningsgracht was therefore named Koningsplein. The name Koningsgracht did not last, but the name of the square survived.

origins.name: Koningsstraat
origins.en: The streets lie on the old Lastage and were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Koogstraat
origins.en: The village of Koog aan de Zaan (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Koolpalmhof
origins.en: A tree, also called cabbage tree or grass palm. Although its shape recalls a palm tree, it does not belong to the palm family. Its young, soft leaves used to be eaten instead of cabbage (kool).

origins.name: Koolrabistraat
origins.en: A vegetable (kohlrabi), probably from northern Europe, whose swollen stem is eaten.

origins.name: Koopvaardersplantsoen
origins.en: A collective name for former merchant ships.

origins.name: Koornhorst
origins.en: The name of a farm in Bergh-Montferland (Gelderland).

origins.name: Koos Vorrinkweg
origins.en: Jacobus Johannes Vorrink (1891-1955), teacher and politician, founder and leader of the AJC (Workers' Youth Federation), chairman of the SDAP and member of parliament. He played an active part in founding the Labour Party (PvdA).

origins.name: Koperslagerij
origins.en: The street lies on the site of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij. Koperslagerij (coppersmithy) refers to one of the workshops that were here.

origins.name: Kopjachtplein
origins.en: A sailing yacht with a high stem.

origins.name: Koppelingpad
origins.en: A machine part (the coupling or clutch).

origins.name: Koppenburglaan
origins.en: The name of an old farm in Lathum, in the municipality of Angerlo (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kopraweg
origins.en: Copra is the dried flesh of the coconut. Copra used to be made by traders who travelled from port to port in the Pacific.

origins.name: Korenbloemstraat
origins.en: The plant (cornflower), of the daisy family.

origins.name: Korfbalstraat
origins.en: Named after the korfball that was played here on the former sports ground.

origins.name: Korianderstraat
origins.en: A plant (coriander) of the carrot family, also called ketumbar, from the Mediterranean and the Middle East.

origins.name: Kormelinkweg
origins.en: An old farm south-west of Eibergen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Korrelbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the Korrel family, who ran a dairy shop at Eerste Jan Steenstraat 4 from 1947 to 1985. The bridge is also meant as a tribute to the many small shopkeepers of the 1950s, 60s and 70s who have disappeared, a time when you could still buy on tick.

origins.name: Korsjespoortsteeg
origins.en: After the timber merchant Corsgen Jacobszoon, who in the fifteenth century had an orchard on the Singel, outside the city. The bridge over the Singel was therefore called the Korsjesbrug. Later the name passed to the gate and to the street leading to it. In the sixteenth century a new, longer alley was laid out in line with the first. Both were then called Korsjespoortsteeg, but the older one was given the prefix 'Korte' (short).

origins.name: Korte 's-Gravesandestraat
origins.en: Willem Jan van 's-Gravesande (1688-1742), professor of mathematics and astronomy at Leiden. He was the first follower of Newton in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Korte Amstelstraat
origins.en: The Korte Amstelstraat was made around 1670 by partly filling in the Nieuwe Achtergracht. A church was planned in the middle of the Amstelveld, so in 1669 a temporary church was built in a corner. The church was never built; the temporary church still stands.

origins.name: Korte Blekersstraat
origins.en: Called Korte Blekerspad before 1911, after the bleaching fields (blekerijen) there in the eighteenth century, along the Blekerssloot.

origins.name: Korte De Wittenstraat
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis de Witt (1623-1672), burgomaster of Dordrecht, and Johan de Witt (1625-1672), Grand Pensionary of Holland, both murdered by the mob in The Hague on a false accusation. One side of the quay was first called Maljapenkade.

origins.name: Korte Dijkstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out as a dike at the end of the sixteenth century, after which the surroundings (long a marsh) were filled in with earth (aangeplempt).

origins.name: Korte Distelstraat
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Korte Geuzenstraat
origins.en: At first meant as a term of abuse (geuzen: beggars), but taken as a title of honour by the Confederated Nobles (verbonden edelen) in the fight against Spain. Later the fighting name of all opponents of Spain in the Eighty Years' War. The Korte Geuzenstraat was earlier part of the Geuzenstraat.

origins.name: Korte Keizersdwarsstraat
origins.en: On the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Korte Keizersstraat
origins.en: On the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Korte Kolksteeg
origins.en: Originally the water from the peatland behind, which came by way of the now filled-in Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal, flowed through this kolk (basin) into the Damrak. Around 1350 the Martelaarsgracht was dug and this outlet fell out of use. The kolk was filled in towards the end of the fifteenth century.

origins.name: Korte Koningsdwarsstraat
origins.en: On the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Korte Koningsstraat
origins.en: The streets lie on the old Lastage and were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Korte Korsjespoortsteeg
origins.en: After the timber merchant Corsgen Jacobszoon, who in the fifteenth century had an orchard on the Singel, outside the city. The bridge over the Singel was therefore called the Korsjesbrug. Later the name passed to the gate and to the street leading to it. In the sixteenth century a new, longer alley was laid out in line with the first. Both were then called Korsjespoortsteeg, but the older one was given the prefix 'Korte' (short).

origins.name: Korte Leidsedwarsstraat
origins.en: The city of Leiden.

origins.name: Korte Lijnbaanssteeg
origins.en: The ropewalks (lijnbanen) of the ropemakers. The Lijnbaanssteeg dates from the fifteenth century, when the Singel was the outermost canal. A ropemaker needed a fairly large site for his trade, which could only be found on the edge of the city. The ropewalks lay on the city side of the moat, so inside the rampart. The Lijnbaansgracht ran right round the city. It has since been filled in in several places and there has taken other names, such as Leidseplein, Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen, Frederiksplein, Maarten Jansz. Kosterstraat, Valckenierstraat and Plantage Muidergracht.

origins.name: Korte Marnixkade
origins.en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Korte Marnixstraat
origins.en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Korte Meerhuizenstraat
origins.en: A former country house on the Amstel, where the Amstelkade now meets the Amsteldijk, demolished around 1914. In the seventeenth century the poet Hendrik Laurensz Spiegel lived here.

origins.name: Korte Niezel
origins.en: The name is a corruption of liesdel, a del or dale where lies (irises) grow. It was marshy land north of the higher ground on which the Oude Kerk was built. In the second half of the fourteenth century this hollow was raised and built on. In one of the streets the old name Liesdel lived on. In later centuries it became Niesdel, and in the eighteenth century officially Niezel. In the sixteenth century a little street was laid out in line with it, which after various other names finally became Korte (short) Niezel, while the oldest part was given the prefix Lange (long).

origins.name: Korte Ouderkerkerbrug
origins.en: Named after the village of Ouderkerk aan de Amstel, to which these roads lead. The prefix Korte (short) dates from 1956, after the dike was cut through for the industrial estate.

origins.name: Korte Ouderkerkerdijk
origins.en: The name of the dike in which this bridge lies.

origins.name: Korte Papaverweg
origins.en: The plant (poppy), wild and cultivated, also called klaproos.

origins.name: Korte Prinsengracht
origins.en: After 'the princely title', meaning that of the Princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and the plainest in the character of its buildings. It was dug in the expansion of 1612 and built up from the Brouwersgracht to the Leidsegracht. In the expansion of 1658 this canal too was extended across the Amstel (as far as the Entrepotdok). The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for today's Noordermarkt never caught on with the citizens.

origins.name: Korte Reguliersdwarsstraat
origins.en: All these names recall the Reguliers monastery (of the Canons Regular), which stood from 1394 to 1532 outside the city gate of the time, where the Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now cross. The city gate, of which the Munttoren is a remnant, was once called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht then ended at that gate. Parts of it were filled in in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Before 1909 the Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

origins.name: Korte Schimmelstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Jan Schimmel (1825-1906), bank director, known as a novelist and playwright and also editor of 'De Gids'. These streets came into Amsterdam in 1896 with the names set by Nieuwer-Amstel, Van Speyckstraat and Van Speyckdwarsstraat, but were renamed in 1922, after the annexation of Sloten brought a second Van Speyckstraat within the city boundary.

origins.name: Korte Spinhuissteeg
origins.en: After the nearby Spinhuis (spinning house), a house of correction for women founded in 1596. From 1833 to 1941 the building housed the police headquarters.

origins.name: Korte Stormsteeg
origins.en: Because this part of the city lay on its outermost edge until the sixteenth century, it took the full brunt of storms. The alley's name probably arose from this.

origins.name: Korte Tolstraat
origins.en: After the toll gate (tol) on the corner of today's Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was levied from about 1780 until the area was annexed in 1896, for the upkeep of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 11 February 1886).

origins.name: Korte van Eeghenstraat
origins.en: Like the Van Eeghenstraat, named after Christiaan Pieter van Eeghen (1816-1889), Amsterdam merchant, president-commissioner of De Nederlandsche Bank and the man behind the Vondelpark. When the street was laid out, the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel named it Heemskerkstraat on 7 February 1896 (after the minister J. Heemskerk Az.). After the annexation of 1896 the name was changed to Van Eeghendwarsstraat, because Amsterdam already had a Van Heemskerckstraat (council decision of 13 June 1896). The residents and owners, however, asked for the name to be changed: in their view 'dwarsstraat' (cross street) lowered the tone. The city council then set the present name.

origins.name: Korte Vogelstraat
origins.en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

origins.name: Korte Water
origins.en: A historical name from old Sloten/Osdorp. According to Jan Dou's map of 1687, the Korte Water lay south of the Ookmeertje.

origins.name: Korte Zoutkeetsgracht
origins.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the salt works (zoutketen) stood on both sides of this canal. These were sheds where coarse salt was refined for household use.

origins.name: Kortenaerstraat
origins.en: Egbert M. Kortenaer, lieutenant-admiral, who took part in the naval battles of Ter Heijde (1653) and the Sound (1658). He was killed in 1665 in the Battle of Lowestoft against the English.

origins.name: Kortenakenstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Korteweghof
origins.en: Diederik Johannes Korteweg (1848-1941), mathematician and astronomer, professor in Amsterdam, who edited the complete works of Christiaan Huygens.

origins.name: Kortrijk
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

origins.name: Kortvoort
origins.en: A hamlet and house near Oss (Noord-Brabant). A voort or voorde is a ford.

origins.name: Kortwoudepad
origins.en: Kortwoude is a hamlet in the Dutch province of Friesland, in the municipality of Achtkarspelen.

origins.name: Kostverlorenstraat
origins.en: After the Kostverlorenwetering, dug in 1413 to give a shorter waterway to the Haarlem and Leiden lakes. According to some, the name Kostverloren (cost lost) comes from the heavy legal costs of this channel, which was a bone of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609. The name Kostverloren occurs in several places in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Kotteraarstraat
origins.en: The metalworker who works with the kotter, a tool for reaming holes and making them cylindrical (a borer). The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

origins.name: Kotterspad
origins.en: A fast-sailing ship (cutter), used among other things for coastal shipping and fishing. Derived from the English 'to cut'.

origins.name: Kousenbandstraat
origins.en: A pod up to 90 centimetres long (yardlong bean), probably from tropical Africa, grown in South America and tropical Asia.

origins.name: Kouterstraat
origins.en: A kouter is the blade of a plough (coulter).

origins.name: Kouwenoord
origins.en: The name of several farms, among them one in Kesteren (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kouwenoordweg
origins.en: The name of several farms, among them one in Kesteren (Gelderland).

origins.name: Koxhorn
origins.en: An old country estate in Wassenaar (Zuid-Holland).

origins.name: Kraaiennest
origins.en: The name of a house and fort in Breukelen-Sint Pieter (Utrecht) and of a farm in Harmelen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kraaiennestpad
origins.en: The name of a house and fort in Breukelen-Sint Pieter (Utrecht) and of a farm in Harmelen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kraaienplein
origins.en: The bird (the crow).

origins.name: Kraailookstraat
origins.en: A plant, a rare wild garlic (crow garlic).

origins.name: Kraaipanstraat
origins.en: The place in the Transvaal (South Africa) where fighting against the British took place in the Boer War (1899-1902).

origins.name: Kraandrijverstraat
origins.en: The crane driver or crane operator works the crane that moves loads horizontally and vertically. The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

origins.name: Kraansluis
origins.en: The name of this fixed bridge recalls the Grote Kraan (great crane), which stood on the IJ from 1643 to 1841 and was used to step masts into ships and to unload blocks of stone and guns.

origins.name: Kraanspoor
origins.en: The name comes from the 1952 concrete structure (a crane track) on which the offices are built. Two large cranes used to stand here, hoisting cargo from the land onto the ships.

origins.name: Krabbendamstraat
origins.en: A village in the Kop van Noord-Holland (the northern tip of Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Kraijenhoffstraat
origins.en: Cornelis R.Th. Baron van Kraijenhoff (1758-1840), hydraulic engineer and Minister of War under King Louis Napoleon, who strengthened the fortifications around the city in 1815.

origins.name: Kramatplantsoen
origins.en: A suburb of Batavia (now Jakarta). Kramat is an Islamic term for something sacred (a grave, animal or object) to which miraculous power is attributed.

origins.name: Kramatweg
origins.en: A suburb of Batavia (now Jakarta). Kramat is an Islamic term for something sacred (a grave, animal or object) to which miraculous power is attributed.

origins.name: Krammerstraat
origins.en: The waterway between Overflakkee and Sint Philipsland.

origins.name: Kranenburg
origins.en: A former knightly manor on the Rottemeren, in Bleiswijk.

origins.name: Krasseurstraat
origins.en: A workman in a construction shop who scribes the working drawings onto metal plates. The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

origins.name: Kratontuin
origins.en: After the fortified, walled palace of Javanese rulers, the centre of political power and culture, which often formed a city within a city. Each dynasty founded a new kraton, where sometimes several thousand people lived. The most famous kraton on Java is that of Yogyakarta, founded in 1757.

origins.name: Kreeftstraat
origins.en: A constellation (Cancer, the Crab), also a sign of the zodiac.

origins.name: Krelis Louwenstraat
origins.en: A comedy by Pieter Langendijk, often performed with success.

origins.name: Kretaweg
origins.en: A Greek island (Crete).

origins.name: Kribbestraat
origins.en: A stone dam built across part of a river to guide the current (a groyne).

origins.name: Krijn Breurstraat
origins.en: Krijn Martinus Breur (1917-1943), resistance fighter, born in Dordrecht, executed by firing squad in Leusden.

origins.name: Krijn Taconiskade
origins.en: Photojournalist (1918-1979), who during the Second World War joined the photographers' group 'De Ondergedoken Camera' (the camera in hiding), which photographed clandestinely during the Hunger Winter. After the liberation he worked in international photojournalism, including a reportage on a famine in Haiti. He was a member of the famous photographers' collective Magnum.

origins.name: Krimpertplein
origins.en: The name of a farm on the Verwolde estate near Laren (Gelderland).

origins.name: Krom Boomssloot
origins.en: A side canal of the Recht Boomssloot, hence the prefix krom (crooked).

origins.name: Krombekstraat
origins.en: One of the few surviving varieties of the Dutch white bean.

origins.name: Kromme Distelstraat
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Kromme Leimuidenstraat
origins.en: A village between the Westeinder Plassen and the Braassemermeer in Zuid-Holland. The prefix Kromme (crooked) refers to the shape of the street.

origins.name: Kromme Palmstraat
origins.en: The tree (palm). The Palmgracht was filled in in 1895.

origins.name: Kromme Waal
origins.en: The walen were once (early seventeenth century) inlets of the IJ on the old side (Oude Waal) and the new side (Nieuwe Waal), where seagoing ships were laid up in winter. The Oude Waal silted up and became too shallow, and the Waalseiland was built up there in 1646. The quay on the city side kept the names Oude Waal and Kromme Waal (after its shape); on the Waalseiland came the names Binnenkant and Buitenkant (now Prins Hendrikkade). The Nieuwe Waal disappeared when the Westelijk Entrepotdok was built. Before 1912 the Waalsteeg was called Schippersstraatje; the name was changed because of confusion with the Schippersstraat.

origins.name: Kromme-Mijdrechtstraat
origins.en: The river in Zuid-Holland. Where it joins the Drecht, the Amstel begins. That the street is curved is a coincidence, or a joke by whoever named it.

origins.name: Krommehoekstraat
origins.en: Krommehoek, the name of a vanished farm.

origins.name: Krommeniestraat
origins.en: The village in the Zaan region. Because of building and demolition the street was shortened in 1978 and part of it was added to the Spaarndammerplantsoen.

origins.name: Krommertstraat
origins.en: The winding little canal the Krommert, already partly filled in before 1930. The rest was filled in in the 1950s.

origins.name: Kromwijkdreef
origins.en: The name of several patrician houses, among them ones in Tienhoven (Utrecht) and Maarsseveen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kronstadtbrug
origins.en: Kronstadt is a Russian port on the Gulf of Finland near Saint Petersburg. The names in the Houthavens are taken from places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Kroonweg
origins.en: The currency (crown) of Sweden, Denmark, Norway and the Czech Republic.

origins.name: Krooswijkhof
origins.en: Krooswijk or Crooswijk is a former sixteenth-century country estate on the Rotte, now a district of Rotterdam by the Crooswijk cemetery. This court was laid out, with other streets, on the route once planned for the Rotterdamseweg.

origins.name: Krootstraat
origins.en: The kroot or beetroot is a root crop, of the same family as the sugar beet.

origins.name: Kropaarstraat
origins.en: A grass (cock's-foot) found in Europe, Asia and North Africa.

origins.name: Krugerplein
origins.en: Johannes Stephanus Paulus Kruger, better known as Paul Kruger (1825-1904), president of the Transvaal from 1883. He sought support in Europe for his country's struggle against British rule, in vain, and died in Switzerland.

origins.name: Krugerstraat
origins.en: Johannes Stephanus Paulus Kruger, better known as Paul Kruger (1825-1904), president of the Transvaal from 1883. He sought support in Europe for his country's struggle against British rule, in vain, and died in Switzerland.

origins.name: Kruisbessenstraat
origins.en: The fruit of the shrub of the same name (gooseberry).

origins.name: Kruisherenpad
origins.en: In the early years of the garden city (around 1955) this path was the regular route of the fathers of the Roman Catholic church to their presbytery. They belonged to the order of the Crosiers (Kruisheren), so the path soon got this name.

origins.name: Kruislaan
origins.en: After its position: the road crosses (kruist) the Middenweg.

origins.name: Kruitberg
origins.en: An old patrician house near Santpoort (Noord-Holland), which in the seventeenth century belonged to Stadtholder William III.

origins.name: Kruitberghof
origins.en: An old patrician house near Santpoort (Noord-Holland), which in the seventeenth century belonged to Stadtholder William III.

origins.name: Kruitbergstraat
origins.en: An old patrician house near Santpoort (Noord-Holland), which in the seventeenth century belonged to Stadtholder William III.

origins.name: Kruithuisstraat
origins.en: A powder house (kruithuis) was built on this site in the seventeenth century. After some decades of use it was pulled down because the city's buildings were closing in on it.

origins.name: Kruldistelstraat
origins.en: An akkerdistel (creeping thistle) is a species of thistle.

origins.name: Krulslaplantsoen
origins.en: A variety of ordinary head lettuce with slightly curled leaves.

origins.name: Kruysweerstraat
origins.en: A former country house on the Amstel.

origins.name: ks. Ibisplantsoen
origins.en: The crane ship Ibis, built in 1982 at the NSM yard (the successor of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij). This crane ship, with a lifting capacity of 1600 tonnes, was used for hydraulic engineering works in the Persian Gulf.

origins.name: ks. Ibisweg
origins.en: The crane ship Ibis, built in 1982 at the NSM yard (the successor of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij) for Ballast-Nedam. This crane ship, with a lifting capacity of 1600 tonnes, was used for hydraulic engineering works in the Persian Gulf.

origins.name: Kuilsenhofweg
origins.en: The name of a farm at Beek near Nijmegen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kuinderstraat
origins.en: A small river in Friesland, which once flowed into the IJsselmeer at Kuinre.

origins.name: Kuiperbergweg
origins.en: A hill near Ootmarsum, the top of the eastern push moraine of Overijssel.

origins.name: Kuiperssteeg
origins.en: After the cooperage (kuiperij) here in the seventeenth century. Before that the alley appears as St. Clarensteeg, after the former St Clare convent.

origins.name: Kuipersstraat
origins.en: Named after the former Kuiperspad, which already existed in the seventeenth century and on which the street was laid out. Until 1896 the street belonged, under the same name, to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Kurk
origins.en: A corrupted spelling of the Irish port of Cork, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Kustvaarderstraat
origins.en: A ship built for coastal trade, usually of 500 tonnes at most, better known as a coaster.

origins.name: Kwadijkerstraat
origins.en: The village of Kwadijk, north of Purmerend.

origins.name: Kwadrantweg
origins.en: An instrument for measuring the altitude of celestial bodies, used in navigation (the quadrant).

origins.name: Kwakersplein
origins.en: After the former Kwakerspoel and Kwakerseiland, names first recorded here around 1680. The name probably comes from the sect of the Quakers (kwakers). Followers of this sect, whose principles were first preached in Amsterdam around 1656, were expelled from the city, so they met at this remote spot outside the city boundary. In 1674 they were allowed to meet in a house on the Keizersgracht. The name de Bijkerk (the side church), borne by one of the mills that stood here, also supports this explanation. Another explanation is the old word 'kwakel', the name for a high, narrow wooden bridge that still survives in Noord-Holland.

origins.name: Kwakersstraat
origins.en: After the former Kwakerspoel and Kwakerseiland, names first recorded here around 1680. The name probably comes from the sect of the Quakers (kwakers). Followers of this sect, whose principles were first preached in Amsterdam around 1656, were expelled from the city, so they met at this remote spot outside the city boundary. In 1674 they were allowed to meet in a house on the Keizersgracht. The name de Bijkerk (the side church), borne by one of the mills that stood here, also supports this explanation. Another explanation is the old word 'kwakel', the name for a high, narrow wooden bridge that still survives in Noord-Holland.

origins.name: Kwartelstraat
origins.en: A bird of the fowl family (the quail).

origins.name: Kwartiermeesterstraat
origins.en: An officer responsible for quarters and supplies (the quartermaster).

origins.name: Kwekerijlaan
origins.en: A place where plants are grown (a nursery). The street lies on the former De Bongerd allotment complex.

origins.name: Kwelderweg
origins.en: Vegetated land built up outside the dike, which usually no longer floods at high water (a salt marsh).

origins.name: Kwintsheulstraat
origins.en: A village in the Westland (Zuid-Holland).

origins.name: L. van Sonsbeeckstraat
origins.en: Lodewijk Hendrik van Sonsbeeck (1831-1903), burgomaster of Sloten from 1864 to 1868, and then of Vlagtwedde.

origins.name: L.J.M. Beelstraat
origins.en: Louis Jozef Maria Beel (1902-1977), statesman of the KVP (Catholic People's Party). In 1945 he became Minister of the Interior and in 1946 prime minister. From 1951 to 1956 he was again Minister of the Interior, and then prime minister once more in 1958-1959. He was also, among other things, a Minister of State.

origins.name: La Guardiaweg
origins.en: The name of one of New York's airports.

origins.name: La Meye
origins.en: A mountain peak in France (La Meije), 3987 metres high.

origins.name: Laagte Kadijk
origins.en: When a great deal of land had built up through silting outside the old sea dike (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike, or quay dike (kadijk), was built. It was originally called the new sea dike, but that name later fell out of use. When this new dike was raised further, people spoke of the Laagte (low part) and the Hoogte (high part) of the Kadijk. Until 1943 the Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat. This is because it lies in line with the Plantage Kerklaan, although it has never been connected to it.

origins.name: Laan der Hesperiden
origins.en: Figures from Greek mythology: seven nymphs who guard the tree with the golden apples in the land of Hesperia.

origins.name: Laan van Spartaan
origins.en: The grounds of the Amsterdam football club VVA/Spartaan, founded in 1901, are on this avenue.

origins.name: Laan van Vlaanderen
origins.en: The usual name for the Dutch-speaking part of Belgium, north of the language border (Flanders). Named after the former county, which takes its name from a Carolingian district, the pagus Flandrensis.

origins.name: Laanweg
origins.en: Originally this was a tree-lined road (laan). When the Buiksloterham was drained in 1851, three roads were made here: the 'weg' (along the canal), the 'dijk' (the former sea dike) and this 'laan'. The Laanweg disappeared around 1970 when its buildings were demolished and this little polder was raised. The old name has now been given to part of the service road of the Ranonkelkade and the Meidoornweg.

origins.name: Laarderhoogtweg
origins.en: The name of a hill near Laren (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Laboratoriumstraat
origins.en: After the nearby Aeronautical Laboratory (Luchtvaartlaboratorium), where scientific experiments and observations are made for aviation.

origins.name: Ladogameerhof
origins.en: Lake Ladoga (Ladozhskoye ozero), in northern Russia near the Finnish border.

origins.name: Laing's Nekstraat
origins.en: A mountain pass in South Africa, also called Langenek, known for Joubert's victory over the British in the First Boer War. The oldest part of the street (by the Ringvaart) has had various names over the years. Before 1896 it was Tweede Ringkadedwarsstraat, as named by Nieuwer-Amstel. By council decision of 16 October 1901 that name was changed to Meerstraat, and in 1912 this stretch was added to the Laing's Nekstraat.

origins.name: Lakenhalstraat
origins.en: The Stedelijk Museum De Lakenhal in Leiden, in a 1640 building by the city architect Arent van 's-Gravesande (originally the cloth hall). It opened as a museum in 1874 and is known for its historical collection of silver, glass, pewter and tiles, and for paintings by famous people of Leiden.

origins.name: Lamarckhof
origins.en: Jean de Monet de Lamarck (1744-1827), French biologist, who set out the first modern theory of evolution. A forerunner of Darwin.

origins.name: Lambert Rimastraat
origins.en: Lambert Gregoire Rima (1907-1943), resistance fighter, born in The Hague, executed by firing squad in Leusden. Rima was connected with the clandestine paper 'Het Parool'.

origins.name: Lamonggracht
origins.en: A river on the Indonesian island of Java.

origins.name: Lampenistenstraat
origins.en: A trade name: someone responsible for lighting and maintaining lamps (a lamplighter), for example on board a ship or at a station.
