origins.en: Picturesque castle in Renesse (Zeeland), severely damaged by water during the storm disaster of 1953. During the restoration, the foundations of a large castle from the early Middle Ages were uncovered.

origins.name: Moestuinlaan
origins.en: Vegetable garden. The street is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Moezelhavenweg
origins.en: Tributary that flows into the Rhine near Koblenz (Germany). Important river for the industries and mines in the Saar region.

origins.name: Mokerstraat
origins.en: A heavy blacksmith or breaking hammer.

origins.name: Molen 't Haasjepad
origins.en: Poldermolen, octagonal ground sluice gate. Kept the Wilmkebreek dry from the reclamation in 1633. The mill was seriously damaged during the 1916 flood disaster, and was subsequently replaced by an electric pumping station. Demolished in 1924.

origins.name: Molenaarsweg
origins.en: The miller is someone who operates a mill. The road runs along the Molenwijk park (see there). Before 1976, the road was part of the Stellingweg.

origins.name: Molenbeekstraat
origins.en: Name of various Dutch waterways, including in Limburg and along the Veluwezoom.

origins.name: Molengouw
origins.en: Named after the mill that stood near the current Nibbixwoudstraat, and where this street used to lead as a path to it.

origins.name: Molenpad
origins.en: This path was outside the city in the sixteenth century and led to a mill near the current Raamplein (Raamstraat was also called Molenpad until the seventeenth century). By the way, Molenpad is the only one of the many outer paths that retained the name path when it came to lie within the walls after 1612.

origins.name: Molenslootpad
origins.en: Name for a main waterway that leads to the polder mill.

origins.name: Molensteeg
origins.en: The alley dates back to the beginning of the fourteenth century, when the count of Holland had a mill built on the Zeedijk. This mill had disappeared by 1357, but the alley has retained its name to this day. In the sixteenth century, the alley was also called Minderbroederssteeg.

origins.name: Molenwerf
origins.en: This name was established in 1956, but already existed for a long time. The millyard is the piece of land on which a mill stands. In this case, the site where the mill stood in the old village of Sloterdijk.

origins.name: Molenwijk
origins.en: This is the name of a park. The residential buildings established in this park form a number of mill districts on the map and bear names of mill types.

origins.name: Molsteeg
origins.en: The name of this alley first appears in 1557 and refers to the house 'De Mol', which was already mentioned in 1533 and stood on the land where this alley is now located.

origins.name: Molukkenstraat
origins.en: Island group in Indonesia, located between Sulawesi and New Guinea, to which among others the islands of Ambon, Ceram and Halmaheira belong. (Indonesian name = Maluku).

origins.name: Mondlanestraat
origins.en: Eduardo Mondlane (1920-1969), leader of the liberation movement Frelimo in Mozambique. He was assassinated in 1969. It took until 1975 for Mozambique to become independent from Portugal.

origins.name: Monitorstraat
origins.en: Screen. As a counterpart to the street names that remind of the former shipbuilding industry in Amsterdam-North, this naming refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Monnikendammerplantsoen
origins.en: The place in North Holland, once a thriving Zuiderzee city.

origins.name: Monnikendammerweg
origins.en: The place in North Holland, once a thriving Zuiderzee city.

origins.name: Monnikendwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the Brothers of the Poor or Grey Monks monastery, founded in 1464, destroyed in 1578. The oldest name of the street is Grauwemonnikenstraat (1581).

origins.name: Monnikenstraat
origins.en: Named after the Brothers of the Poor or Grey Monks monastery, founded in 1464, destroyed in 1578. The oldest name of the street is Grauwemonnikenstraat (1581).

origins.name: Monnikskapstraat
origins.en: Plant genus from the ranunculus family. Blooms yellow, purple, blue, pink or white. The name is derived from the strikingly shaped upper petal. The monkshood mainly grows on alpine meadows on the northern hemisphere. Of the more than 250 species, only the yellow monkshood is native to the Netherlands.

origins.name: Monte Adi
origins.en: Mountain peak in Spain, 1453 meters high.

origins.name: Monte Perdido
origins.en: Mountain peak in Spain, 3355 meters high.

origins.name: Monte Viso
origins.en: Mountain peak in Italy, 3841 meters high.

origins.name: Montelbaanstraat
origins.en: Named after the Montelbaan Tower, built in the sixteenth century. The street was laid out after the renovation of the Jonker- and Ridderbuurt around 1930. As for the origin of the name Montelbaan, we are in the dark.

origins.name: Montferlandstraat
origins.en: The hilly landscape near 's-Heerenberg and Zeddam (Gelderland).

origins.name: Montfoorthof
origins.en: The place on the Hollandsche IJssel (Utrecht).

origins.name: Moreelsestraat
origins.en: Paulus Moreelse (1571-1638), painter, influenced by Titian. He painted, among other things, the archers of the Kloveniersdoelen.

origins.name: Morellenstraat
origins.en: The fruit, a kind of cherry.

origins.name: Morsestraat
origins.en: The North American Samuel Morse (1791-1872). Formed a system of symbols from a combination of dots and lines (Morse code).

origins.name: Mortelstraat
origins.en: Reference to the concrete company Albeton that was located on the Cruquiusterrein between 1977 and 2014.

origins.name: Mosplein
origins.en: The plants, spore plants, that are spread all over the world.

origins.name: Mosstraat
origins.en: The plants, spore plants, that are spread all over the world.

origins.name: Mosveld
origins.en: The plants, spore plants, that are spread all over the world.

origins.name: Motorkade
origins.en: A motor is a power machine, which provides moving force. Powered by electricity, gases or heat.

origins.name: Motorwal
origins.en: A motor is a power machine, which provides moving force. Powered by electricity, gases or heat.

origins.name: Mozartkade
origins.en: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756-1791), Austrian composer of church music, operas, symphonies, piano concertos, songs and chamber music. The greatest composer of the classical period.

origins.name: Mozes en Aäronstraat
origins.en: Named after the two Old Testament figures Mozes, leader during the exodus from Egypt, and Aaron, head of the priesthood. The street runs between the former town hall (worldly authority, Mozes) and the Nieuwe Kerk (spiritual authority, Aaron).

origins.name: Mr. P.N. Arntzeniusweg
origins.en: Pieter N. Arntzenius (1745-1799), lawyer and poet. Secretary of the former municipality of Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: ms. Oslofjordweg
origins.en: The motor ship Oslofjord. A passenger ship built at the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM) for a Norwegian shipping company and intended for the voyage between Norway and North America. At the christening in 1948, the ship was christened by the queen of Norway.

origins.name: ms. Tarnweg
origins.en: Motor ship (ms) Tarn, built at the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (later NDSM).

origins.name: ms. van Riemsdijkweg
origins.en: The motor ship Van Riemsdijk. A cargo and passenger ship, built in 1939 at the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (later NDSM) for the Koninklijke Pakketvaart Maatschappij (KPM) for use in Indonesia. When the war broke out in May 1940, the ship had not yet been completed. By the end of the war, the ship was sunk by the occupiers in the North Sea Canal and after the war was salvaged and dismantled.

origins.name: mt. Lincolnweg
origins.en: The turbinetanker Esso Lincoln was built in 1961 at the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM) on behalf of Esso. It was the hundredth ship to be launched after 1945, on December 15, 1962.

origins.name: mt. Ondinaweg
origins.en: Motor tanker, 6341 tons, built in 1939 at the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (later NDSM) on behalf of Anglo Saxon Petroleum Co.

origins.name: Muiderbergbrug
origins.en: Named after the town of Muiderberg

origins.name: Muiderlaan
origins.en: Runs in the direction of Muiden, just like Muiderstraat and Plantage Muidergracht.

origins.name: Muiderstraat
origins.en: The street runs in the direction of the city of Muiden (as well as the Plantage Muidergracht). The north side of this street was largely demolished during the hunger winter of 1944-45 and for the rest in the following years. After that, the street width was increased to 37 meters.

origins.name: Muntbergweg
origins.en: A hill west of Groesbeek (Gelderland).

origins.name: Muntendamstraat
origins.en: Pieter Muntendam (1901-1986), from 1953 professor of social medicine at Leiden. He has been intensively involved in public health in the Netherlands for sixty years, among other things as director-general and as state secretary. He had a forward-looking position on euthanasia and abortion. One of his many functions was that of chairman of the State Commission for Alternative Medicines.

origins.name: Muntplein
origins.en: The Amsterdammers simply call it the Mint. In the building next to the Mint Tower (remnant of the Regulierspoort), coins were minted for a period of time in the seventeenth century. Since then, the name Mint has remained associated with it. The official name Muntplein dates back to 1917. From 1-25-1877 to 1917, the square was called Sophiaplein (see at Sophialaan), and until 1877 Schapenplein.

origins.name: Murdoch Mackenziestraat
origins.en: Scottish cartographer (1712-1797), made maps of the Orkney Islands among other things. The sea book of the Orkney Islands that was given to her ships by the VOC after 1753 was a translation of Mackenzie's work.

origins.name: Murillostraat
origins.en: Bartholome Esteban Murillo (1618-1682), Spanish Baroque painter (Madonnas and saints).

origins.name: Museumbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the nearby Rijksmuseum, which was built in 1883 by Pierre Cuypers

origins.name: Museumplein
origins.en: Named after the nearby Rijksmuseum, built in 1883 by Pierre Cuypers. In 1883, 1887 and 1895 large exhibitions were held at the Museumplein, after which it was a skating club's ice rink until around 1940.

origins.name: Museumstraat
origins.en: Named after the nearby Rijksmuseum, built in 1883 by Pierre Cuypers. In 1883, 1887 and 1895 large exhibitions were held on Museumplein, after which it was a skating club's ice rink until around 1940.

origins.name: Mussenstraat
origins.en: The birds belonging to the finches.

origins.name: Muurbloemstraat
origins.en: The plant, of the cabbage family (crucifers).

origins.name: Muzenplein
origins.en: In Greek mythology, the muses (daughters of Zeus) are the goddesses of the arts and sciences.

origins.name: N. Lansdorpstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas Lansdorp (1885-1968), architect. Designer of the church on Mosstraat. In Amsterdam he built 2000 houses and 160 schools, such as the Vossiusgymnasium.

origins.name: Na Druk Gelukbrug
origins.en: is named after Dirk Beukeboom's farm on the then-current Brug is named after Dirk Beukeboom's farm on the then-current Oude Amstelveenseweg 255, which had to make way for the construction of the Olympic Stadium and the Olympic neighborhood The name of this farm refers to

origins.name: Naaldwijkstraat
origins.en: Name of a village in the Westland (South Holland).

origins.name: Naardermeerstraat
origins.en: The nature monument west of Naarden. In 1905, the municipality of Amsterdam's plan to purchase the area for landfill was rejected by the municipal council. This was the impetus for the establishment of the Association for the Preservation of Nature Monuments in the Netherlands, which purchased the Naardermeer in 1906.

origins.name: Nachtegaalstraat
origins.en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

origins.name: Nachtwachtlaan
origins.en: The famous painting by Rembrandt, depicting the corps of Captain Frans Banning Cock (1642). The name Night Watch was erroneously given to the painting by the fading of the paint.

origins.name: Nadezjda Mandelstamstraat
origins.en: Wife of the dissident Russian writer Osip Mandelstam. Nadezjda Mandelstam (1899-1980) risked her own life to promote the publication of poetry collections by her husband, who died during his internment in 1938.

origins.name: Nadia en Lili Boulangerplantsoen
origins.en: Nadia (Paris, September 16, 1887 - there, October 22, 1979) and Lili (Paris, 1893 - Mézy-sur-Seine, 1918) Boulanger were sisters and both composers. They meant a lot to classical music at the beginning of the 20th century. They were especially known in their native France but eventually also gained fame abroad. Nadia Boulanger's musical activity is closely linked to that of the American Fontainebleau Conservatory. She conducted here from 1949 until the end of her life and trained more than 600 students. Lili Boulanger was the first woman to win the Prix de Rome. After that, she was constantly ill and died at the age of only 24.

origins.name: Nadirstraat
origins.en: A concept in astronomy: the imaginary point on the celestial sphere, directly below the observer (opposite of zenith).

origins.name: Nadorststeeg
origins.en: According to old registers, in 1557 there was an inn on the corner of the Nes and this alley, where the 'Nadorst' was located.

origins.name: Nageljongenstraat
origins.en: Occupational name: young worker who makes the rivets glowing hot and hands them to the riveter. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Namenhof
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Namur.

origins.name: Nannie van Wehlstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Susanne J.A. Reys (1880-1944), children's book writer. Not only wrote girls' books but also essays on pedagogical and feminist issues.

origins.name: Nannoplein
origins.en: Name of an idyll by the writer Carel Vosmaer (1882).

origins.name: Naritaweg
origins.en: The name of one of Tokyo's airports.

origins.name: Narva-eiland
origins.en: City in Estonia near the border with Russia, as a historic export port of wood of importance to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Narwalstraat
origins.en: Cetacean, gray with brown spots on the upper side, only a few teeth in the upper jaw, does not grow longer than five meters. Found in the Arctic region.

origins.name: Nassaukade
origins.en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. Before it was named in 1879, the quay was called Buitensingel.

origins.name: Nassauplein
origins.en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. Before it was named in 1879, the quay was called Buitensingel.

origins.name: Nathan F. Israëlweg
origins.en: Nathan Frederik Israël (1904-1944), resistance fighter. Was involved in the preparation of the February Strike in 1941, participated in the armed resistance and produced the illegal newspaper 'De Waarheid' in Amsterdam Noord. Died in a firefight on August 15, 1944.

origins.name: Navigatiepad
origins.en: Fixing a position at sea. The streets in the area relate to shipping and seamanship.

origins.name: NDSM-kade
origins.en: Nederlandse Dok- en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, was founded in 1946 from a merger of the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). Located along the northern IJ coast and built cargo ships, among other things, and carried out repairs and ship modifications. The new shipyard closed in 1979; the repair part (a second NSM) went bankrupt in 1984.

origins.name: NDSM-pier
origins.en: Nederlands Dok- en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, was founded in 1946 from a merger of the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). Lived along the northern IJ coast and built cargo ships among other things and carried out repairs and ship modifications. The new shipyard closed in 1979

origins.name: NDSM-plein
origins.en: Nederlands Dok- en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, was founded in 1946 from a merger of the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). Lived along the northern IJ coast and built cargo ships among other things and carried out repairs and ship modifications. The new shipyard closed in 1979

origins.name: NDSM-straat
origins.en: Nederlands Dok- en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, was founded in 1946 from a merger of the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). Lived along the northern IJ coast and built cargo ships among other things and carried out repairs and ship modifications. The new shipyard closed in 1979

origins.name: Nederhoven
origins.en: Castle surrounded by a moat in Beegden (Limburg), with a date of construction 1614.

origins.name: Nedersticht
origins.en: Old name for the current province of Utrecht. Opposite Oversticht, which included the current provinces of Overijssel and Drenthe as well as Oost- and Weststellingwerf and the city of Groningen.

origins.name: Neerkanne
origins.en: Originally a medieval castle, near Canne near Maastricht, repeatedly destroyed. The current form dates from 1700, restored in 1955. It is also called Castle Agimont.

origins.name: Neerlandiaplein
origins.en: Name of the building built in 1888 by the Deaconry of the Reformed Church. It served as a home for married elderly people, and was part of the Amstelhoven complex where needy elderly people lived. Today it forms part of the Hermitage.

origins.name: Nellesteinpad
origins.en: Name of a house in Maarn (Utrecht). The name Nellestein has been used since 1976 for a residential area near the Gaasperplas Metro station.

origins.name: Nellie Bodenheimstraat
origins.en: Children's book writer (1874-1951), became especially known for the illustrations she made for children's books.

origins.name: Nelson Mandelapark
origins.en: Nelson Rolihlahla 'Madiba' Mandela (1918-2013). South African anti-apartheid fighter and politician, who is seen as the Father of the Fatherland in his home country. He was sentenced to life imprisonment in 1963 as leader of the military branch of the ANC, but was released in 1990. Received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993 with President F.W. de Klerk for their efforts to end the apartheid regime. Elected president in the first free elections of 1994, an office he held for 5 years.

origins.name: Neptunusplein
origins.en: Planet in our solar system.

origins.name: Neptunusstraat
origins.en: Planet in our solar system.

origins.name: Nepveustraat
origins.en: Jan Nepveu (1719-1779), governor of Suriname.

origins.name: Nes
origins.en: The toponym nes is an indication for a low-lying spit of land along a water. The name Nes, originally Nesse, indicates that there used to be swampy land here. Until the seventeenth century, the northern part was still called Gansoord. The word oord means roughly the same as nes, but is mainly found along the larger rivers.

origins.name: Nesciobrug
origins.en: Nescio was the pseudonym of the Amsterdam writer J.H.F. Grönloh, known for novellas such as De Uitvreter and Titaantjes. He enjoyed walking in the area around the neighboring Diemerzeedijk and the Buiten-IJ.

origins.name: Nesserhoek
origins.en: Named after the right-angle bend in the Waterlandse Zeedijk, now Buiksloterdijk, located freely in the IJ, strongly attacked by westerly wind and waves.

origins.name: Nesserland
origins.en: Named after the promontory, Nes, extending freely into the IJ from the Buiksloter Sea Wall.

origins.name: Nesserton
origins.en: Named after the end of the Nes, a spit in the IJ, on the northwest side of the Buiksloterham, marked with a ton on a stake, that disappeared due to the construction of the North Sea Canal.

origins.name: Netwerkweg
origins.en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

origins.name: Newtonstraat
origins.en: Isaac Newton (1642-1727), English mathematician and physicist. He discovered important laws in the field of gravity.

origins.name: Niasstraat
origins.en: Island group on the west coast of Sumatra (Indonesia).

origins.name: Nibbixwoudstraat
origins.en: Village between Hoorn and Medemblik (North Holland).

origins.name: Nic. de Roeverstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas de Roever (1850-1893), Amsterdam city archivist and historian. Author of 'In de oude Amstelstad'.

origins.name: Nickeriestraat
origins.en: River in Suriname.

origins.name: Nico Broekhuysenweg
origins.en: Nicolaas Broekhuysen (1876-1958). Initiator and pioneer of basketball in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Nico Jessekade
origins.en: Photographer (1911-1976), started as a doctor with his own general practice. Known for his loose way of photographing, characterized by blurriness, and the use of flash. His most famous book is 'Women of Paris', which has appeared in several countries

origins.name: Nico Snijdersstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

origins.name: Nico van Suchtelenhof
origins.en: Man of letters (1878-1949), initially wrote poetry, later novels. Director of the World Library in Amsterdam for many years.

origins.name: Nicolaas Anslijnstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas Anslijn education reformer (1778-1838) Writer of school reading books, including 'The Brave Hendrik' Born in Leiden, died in Alkmaar.

origins.name: Nicolaas Beetsplantsoen
origins.en: Man of letters and writer (1814-1903). As a student, he wrote the famous 'Camera Obscura' under the pseudonym Hildebrand.

origins.name: Nicolaas Beetsstraat
origins.en: Man of letters and writer (1814-1903). As a student, he wrote the famous 'Camera Obscura' under the pseudonym Hildebrand.

origins.name: Nicolaas Berchemstraat
origins.en: Painter (1620-1683), especially of landscapes.

origins.name: Nicolaas Hennemanhof
origins.en: Photographer (1813-1898). Settled in London around 1847. Was assistant to the famous English photographer William Henry Fox Talbot for many years, and was appointed court photographer at the court of Queen Victoria.

origins.name: Nicolaas Japiksestraat
origins.en: Historian (1872-1944), director of the royal house archive of the queen. He wrote historical studies, including 'History of the House of Orange-Nassau'.

origins.name: Nicolaas Maesstraat
origins.en: Painter (1632-1693), painted historical pieces and portraits. He was a pupil of Rembrandt.

origins.name: Nicolaas Ruychaverstraat
origins.en: Geuzen (Sea Beggar) captain during the capture of Den Briel and the siege of Alkmaar. Died in 1577 in a failed raid on Amsterdam, to get the city on the side of the Prince.

origins.name: Nicolaas Tetterodestraat
origins.en: Amsterdam industrialist (1816-1894), founder of the letter foundry 'Amsterdam'.

origins.name: Nicolaas Witsenkade
origins.en: Shipbuilder, cartographer, writer. Lived from 1641 to 1717. Studied law in Leiden and was an advisor to Tsar Peter the Great. His book on shipping from 1671 is one of the important sources on Dutch shipbuilding in the seventeenth century. He was Mayor of Amsterdam many times between 1682 and 1705.

origins.name: Nicolaas Witsenstraat
origins.en: Shipbuilder, cartographer, writer. Lived from 1641 to 1717. Studied law in Leiden and was an advisor to Tsar Peter the Great. His book on shipping from 1671 is one of the important sources on Dutch shipbuilding in the seventeenth century. He was mayor of Amsterdam many times between 1682 and 1705.

origins.name: Nida Senffstraat
origins.en: Dina Willemina Jacoba Senff (1920-1995), swimmer. Won gold in the 100-meter backstroke during the 1936 Berlin Olympic Games. First forgot to touch at the turn, swam back and still won.

origins.name: Niek Engelschmanbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after Niek Engelschman (1914-1988), who was also known as Bob Angelo. He was very active in the struggle for the emancipation of homosexuals and was the founder of the COC.

origins.name: Nienke van Hichtumstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Sjoukje Maria Diederika Troelstra-Bokma de Boer (1860-1939), wife of SDAP politician P.J. Troelstra. Juvenile book writer, became especially well known with 'Afke's tiental' (Afke's ten), in which she described the poverty and social abuses around the turn of the century.

origins.name: Nierkerkestraat
origins.en: A village that drowned in 1530 near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland.

origins.name: Niersstraat
origins.en: River in Limburg, which flows into the Maas near Gennep.

origins.name: Nieuw Herlaer
origins.en: Former castle in St. Michielsgestel. Later, a monastery with that name was built here. Of the original castle, only a tower with a spire remains.

origins.name: Nieuw-Zeelandweg
origins.en: Located east of the Australiëweg. Geographically, Nieuw-Zeeland is located east of Australia.

origins.name: Nieuwe Achtergracht
origins.en: Excavated at the same time as the Achtergracht, but on the other (new) side of the Amstel. Around 1670, a section was filled in, creating the Korte Amstelstraat. Also

origins.name: Nieuwe Akerweg
origins.en: Named after the Akerpolder in the former municipality of Sloten. Aker and Akerwatering are historical names that already appear on a 1687 map of Rijnland by Jan Dou.

origins.name: Nieuwe Amstelbrug
origins.en: When this double bascule bridge, designed partly by Berlage, opened in 1903, it was the newest bridge over the Amstel. The Hoge Sluis was also known as the Amstel Bridge, but this bridge was newer, hence the Nieuwe Amstelbrug

origins.name: Nieuwe Amstelstraat
origins.en: The river.

origins.name: Nieuwe Batavierstraat
origins.en: It is believed that the origin of the name must be sought at a facade stone or signboard in the former Batavierstraat. Batavier is most likely a corruption of Batavia. The Nieuwe Batavierstraat was created by reconstruction of the island of Uilenburg.

origins.name: Nieuwe Doelenstraat
origins.en: The targets were the places where the shooting guilds gathered and where they practiced shooting at a target. The Old Doelenstraat was laid out on the site of the oldest targets, which date back to the fifteenth century. The Nieuwe Doelenstraat derives its name from the Kloveniersdoelen, which stood on the site of the current Doelenhotel from 1522.

origins.name: Nieuwe Egelantiersstraat
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Nieuwe Foeliestraat
origins.en: One of the products, important at the time, brought from the East Indies and stored here in the East India Company's warehouses (foelie is mace).

origins.name: Nieuwe Gietersstraat
origins.en: Named after 't Giethuis, the city's gun and bell foundry, which stood here from 1614 to 1821. The street name first came into use in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Nieuwe Gouw
origins.en: Gouw is a Waterland term for road. The addition Nieuwe indicates that this road is slightly younger than the other Waterland roads. However, the road already appears on the map of Amstellandt and the surroundings of Covens from 1749. In 1957, the name was officially established again.

origins.name: Nieuwe Haagseweg
origins.en: The traffic road to The Hague. The old Haagseweg now has a secondary function.

origins.name: Nieuwe Hemweg
origins.en: Named after a former island called the Hem in the former IJ. The Hem was initially a spit of land that only later became an island as its shore washed away. The word is the same as 'ham', which is now only known as 'inham'. There is now only one last stretch of the Hemweg, originally this road began in the Spaarndammerbuurt. Due to the construction of some harbors, the road was dug through in 1947. Parts are now called Coenhavenweg and Archangelweg. The Nieuwe Hemweg was built to replace the Hemweg.

origins.name: Nieuwe Herengracht
origins.en: After the Heren Regeerders (the lords who governed the city; in the old days the city was not administered but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch when in 1612 it was widened into today's canal, the first of the three main canals. The stretch beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658, as does the Nieuwe Herengracht.

origins.name: Nieuwe Hoogstraat
origins.en: These streets are slightly higher than those in the immediate vicinity. The Oude Hoogstraat was laid out around 1490, the Nieuwe Hoogstraat a century later.

origins.name: Nieuwe Jonkerstraat
origins.en: The Jonker-, Ridder-, Koning- and Keizersstraten were laid out in the second half of the sixteenth century on originally reclaimed land outside the Zeedijk, officially drawn within the city in 1593 (see Lastage). Although the origin of the name is unknown, it is obvious to assume that the four groups of names were determined by the then municipal government. The Jonker- and Ridderbuurt was renovated in 1928. The Lastageweg was also built at that time. The Nieuwe Jonkerstraat is a remnant of the former Jonkerstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Keizersgracht
origins.en: After Emperor Maximilian, Archduke of Austria, who in 1489 granted Amsterdam the privilege of bearing the imperial crown on its coat of arms.

origins.name: Nieuwe Kerkstraat
origins.en: The Kerkstraat was laid out in 1665 and named for the plan to link four churches (kerken) with it: the Amstelkerk, the Oosterkerk and two others that were never built, one by the Molenpad and one by the Weesperstraat. Later the street got various names: Kerkstraat (to the Amstel), Nieuwe Kerkstraat (to the Roetersstraat), Plantage Kerklaan (in the Plantage) and Korte Kerkstraat, which was renamed Tussen Kadijken in 1943.

origins.name: Nieuwe Laan
origins.en: Former road in the Sloter Middelveldsche Polder, connecting road between Uitweg and Sloterdijkermeerweg. On a map of 1650 that old road is called Nieuwelaan, on later maps the name Malleweg appears. The current Nieuwe Laan was given the name Malleweg when it was built in 1958 (council decision, 1958), but due to objections the name was changed to Nieuwe Laan in 1967.

origins.name: Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg
origins.en: The arterial road north, leading over the Afsluitdijk to Leeuwarden. Before 1936 the Leeuwarderweg was part of the Buiksloterdijk. The Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg was built when the IJ tunnel was completed.

origins.name: Nieuwe Leliestraat
origins.en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Nieuwe Looiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

origins.name: Nieuwe Looiersstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

origins.name: Nieuwe Maanstraat
origins.en: The celestial body (the moon) that moves around the earth in an elliptical orbit.

origins.name: Nieuwe Meerpad
origins.en: The water surface was given this name to distinguish it from the Old Lake (see there). The Nieuwe Lake has been enlarged since the 1950s with part of the Riekerpolder and pumped to a depth of thirty meters for sand mining for the Western Garden Cities (westelijke tuinsteden).

origins.name: Nieuwe Nieuwstraat
origins.en: In a resolution of the city council (vroedschap) of 1550, it was decided to build a new street near the Korsjespoort, this street was simply called 'new street'. Thirty years later, the Sint Geertruidenklooster and the Lieve Vrouwengasthuis were demolished that stood between the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal and the Nieuwendijk. Here too, one of the newly laid streets was called 'the new street'. To distinguish the two new streets, the names in the first half of the seventeenth century were given the addition 'Old' and 'New', and they have retained these names to this day. The Nieuwe Nieuwstraat was initially also called Nieuwe Herenstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Oostenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to public traffic in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and formally abolished in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abolished in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Nieuwe Oostenburgerstraat
origins.en: Oostenburg was the easternmost of the three islands (with Kattenburg and Wittenburg) brought within the city by the expansion of 1658. Laying out streets and building began in 1664. At first three streets ran from the canal, named for their position Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to traffic for the growing Werkspoor works and abolished in 1957; the Oostenburgermiddenstraat followed in 1985, where the Compagniestraat now runs. Land freed by the disappearance of some shipyards took the Nieuwe Oostenburgerstraat and -dwarsstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Osdorpergracht
origins.en: Named after the neighborhood of Osdorp. On old maps, this neighborhood is mentioned as Oostdorp. In 1957, construction began on the garden city of Osdorp, which was practically completed in 1973. The Osdorperweg used to bear the names Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

origins.name: Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat
origins.en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

origins.name: Nieuwe Prinsengracht
origins.en: After 'the princely title', meaning that of the Princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and the plainest in the character of its buildings. It was dug in the expansion of 1612 and built up from the Brouwersgracht to the Leidsegracht. In the expansion of 1658 this canal too was extended across the Amstel (as far as the Entrepotdok). The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for today's Noordermarkt never caught on with the citizens.

origins.name: Nieuwe Purmerweg
origins.en: The polder, created by the draining of the lake between 1618 and 1622 near Purmerend.

origins.name: Nieuwe Ridderstraat
origins.en: The Jonker-, Ridder-, Koning- and Keizersstraten were laid out in the second half of the sixteenth century on originally reclaimed land outside the Zeedijk, officially drawn within the city in 1593 (see Lastage). Although the origin of the name is unknown, it is obvious to assume that the four groups of names were determined by the then municipal government. The Jonker- and Ridderbuurt was renovated in 1928. The Lastageweg was also built at that time. The Nieuwe Jonkerstraat is a remnant of the former Jonkerstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Schermerstraat
origins.en: Between 1631 and 1635 more were drained in North Holland.

origins.name: Nieuwe Spiegelstraat
origins.en: Named after a well-known Amsterdam family, mostly manufacturers, who had soap factories. In 1564 Lourens Pieters 'in den Spiegel' lived in the corner building of the Oude Spiegelstraat on the Singel and in 1608 Pieter Lourens Spiegel. The intended house is still called Hertspiegel in 1738. Construction of the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat begins in 1665. Again, it is likely that a resident from the Spiegel family was the namesake.

origins.name: Nieuwe Teertuinen
origins.en: When the old oil gardens (now Prins Hendrikkade) were moved to the Sloterdijksgracht and thus became the staging ground for the oil buyers there, the name of the quay there soon changed to Nieuwe Teertuinen.

origins.name: Nieuwe Tuinstraat
origins.en: Tuin (garden) here means a yard or enclosed space. The street name comes from the Stadstimmertuin (the city's carpentry yard, the Stadswerf), which lay here from 1612 to 1660 (by the Lijnbaansgracht) and to which the street led.

origins.name: Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat
origins.en: The island of Uilenburg, which together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken came to lie within the city in 1593. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known with certainty, but it is likely that the name comes from the marshland here, which was called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was formed by the merger of the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Utrechtseweg
origins.en: Named after the city of Utrecht. The street leads to the Frederiksplein, where the Utrechtsepoort used to stand (demolished in 1860). The Nieuwe Utrechtseweg is the new route to Utrecht. The old road ran via Duivendrecht and Abcoude.

origins.name: Nieuwe Vijzelstraat
origins.en: The name is probably derived from the former inhabitants Cornelis Arents Vijselaar (around 1600) and Jan Vijselaar (around 1632). Vijzelstraat was then a short street and ran to the current Reguliersdwarsstraat. When the street was extended, the name also passed on to this extension. Until the eighteenth century, people spoke of Oude and Nieuwe Vijzelstraat. The Vijzelgracht, dug between 1660 and 1670, was filled in 1934.

origins.name: Nieuwe Wagenstraat
origins.en: There was also a car park at the Haarlemmerpoort, and a Wagenstraat also came there. Due to confusion, the latter was changed to Nieuwe Wagenstraat in 1909. At the same time and for the same reason, the Schapensteeg was then changed to Korte Wagenstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Westerdokstraat
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was built and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Nieuwe Weteringstraat
origins.en: The streets are located in the Weteringbuurt. The names remind us of the Wetering, which originally flowed into the Spui from outside the city. The Boerenwetering is still a remnant of this. The Schans was formerly the wall on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century, the walls and embankments were demolished. Parts have been recreated in promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen) and a road has been built, which first went by the name of Schans in its full length, but was later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was built on the site that became available due to the demolition of the Flour and Bread Factory.

origins.name: Nieuwe Willemsstraat
origins.en: This is the extension of the Willemsstraat (see there). This name was also originally determined with one s.

origins.name: Nieuwe Zonneweg
origins.en: The central body of the planetary system to which the Earth belongs (the sun).

origins.name: Nieuwe-Wercksbrug
origins.en: Named after the original name for the current Jordaan.

origins.name: Nieuwebrugsteeg
origins.en: Named after the bridge where the alley leads. The first wooden bridge over the northern part of the Damrak was built between 1402 and 1421. When it was later replaced by a stone bridge, it was renamed Nieuwebrug. In old documents we also find the name Uiterstebrug.

origins.name: Nieuwegeinlaan
origins.en: Village south of Utrecht.

origins.name: Nieuwegrachtje
origins.en: At the beginning of the nineteenth century, an open street was laid out on the former wooden wall along the Rapenburgergracht, which was named 't Nieuwe grachtje.

origins.name: Nieuwendammer Sluispad
origins.en: Named after the nearby sluice gate. An old local name has thus been officially made.

origins.name: Nieuwendammerdijk
origins.en: The part of the Waterland sea wall that was in the former municipality of Nieuwendam until 1-1-1921. The name Nieuwendam originated when a new sea wall or dam was built here in 1516 after a break in the sea wall. That name was passed on to the later formed sea wall village.

origins.name: Nieuwendammerkade
origins.en: It is likely that the Nieuwendijk owes its name to a partial fortification along the Amstelmouth, in which the Amsteldam mentioned in 1275 also played a role.

origins.name: Nieuwendammerstraat
origins.en: Named after the former village of Nieuwendam. The first part of the street came under the name Nieuwstraat on Amsterdam's territory with the annexation of 1-1-1921.

origins.name: Nieuwendijk
origins.en: It is likely that the Nieuwendijk owes its name to a partial fortification along the Amstelmouth, in which the Amsteldam mentioned in 1275 also played a role.

origins.name: Nieuwenhuysenstraat
origins.en: Frederik Nieuwenhuysen (1905-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed in Haarlem.

origins.name: Nieuwerhoek
origins.en: Country house from the seventeenth century near Loenen aan de Vecht. One of the three corner houses (Ouder-, Middel- and Nieuwerhoek), founded by the Amsterdam family Van Hoek. Ouderhoek was demolished in 1838.

origins.name: Nieuwersluishof
origins.en: A village on the Vecht (Utrecht).

origins.name: Nieuwevaart
origins.en: Named after the Nieuwe Vaart, dug around 1650 to connect the IJ and the Oosterdok along the shortest possible route with the IJ mouth at Zeeburg.

origins.name: Nieuwevaartkade
origins.en: Named after the Nieuwe Vaart, dug around 1650 to connect the IJ and the Oosterdok along the shortest possible route with the IJ mouth at Zeeburg.

origins.name: Nieuwevaartweg
origins.en: Named after the Nieuwe Vaart, dug around 1650 to connect the IJ and the Oosterdok along the shortest possible route with the IJ mouth at Zeeburg.

origins.name: Nieuwezijds Armsteeg
origins.en: Arm has the meaning of bend here. The alley leads to the bend of Warmoesstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwezijds Kolk
origins.en: Originally the water from the peatland behind, which came by way of the now filled-in Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal, flowed through this kolk (basin) into the Damrak. Around 1350 the Martelaarsgracht was dug and this outlet fell out of use. The kolk was filled in towards the end of the fifteenth century.

origins.name: Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal
origins.en: For the origin of the name, see Oudezijds Voorburgwal. The Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal was filled in in 1884. Before the filling in, some sections had unofficial names of the markets held on site: Pijpenmarkt, Boommarkt, Bloemmarkt and Postzegelmarkt.

origins.name: Nieuwlandhof
origins.en: Name of the village in the Lower Betuwe, west of Leerdam (South Holland).

origins.name: Nieuwmarkt
origins.en: Created in 1614 by filling in and vaulting over a part of the Kloveniersburgwal. The new square that arose around the Waag as a result was initially called Sint Antoniesmarkt, later called Nieuwmarkt.

origins.name: Nieuwpoortkade
origins.en: The place in Belgium where Prince Maurice defeated the Spanish in 1600.

origins.name: Nieuwpoortstraat
origins.en: The place in Belgium where Prince Maurice defeated the Spanish in 1600.

origins.name: Niftrikhof
origins.en: Named after the village of the same name in the Land of Maas and Waal (Gelderland).

origins.name: Nigellestraat
origins.en: A garden plant, belonging to the ranunculus family, more commonly known as lady in green.

origins.name: Nigtevechthof
origins.en: The village south of Weesp, between the Vecht and the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal (Utrecht).

origins.name: Nijenburg
origins.en: One of the five thirteenth-century castles with which Floris V wanted to subdue the West Frisians. The castle destroyed in 1491, whose foundations can still be seen, is just east of Alkmaar near Oudorp (North Holland).

origins.name: Nijlpaardenbrug
origins.en: Refers to hippos in Artis

origins.name: Nilda Pintostraat
origins.en: Nilda Maria Geerding Jessurun Pinto (1918-1954), Curaçao writer. Especially known for the vivid way in which she recorded Curaçaoan folk tales in Papiamento.

origins.name: Nirwana
origins.en: In Buddhism, the highest spiritual state that a person can achieve, in which the soul has been freed from desire, aversion and delusion and he has come to rest as it were.

origins.name: Nisserstraat
origins.en: The Nissermeer, located in Telemark, southern Norway.

origins.name: Nobelweg
origins.en: Alfred Nobel (1833-1896), Swedish industrialist and chemist, inventor of dynamite and nitroglycerine. After his death, he bequeathed his fortune to a fund, from which six Nobel Prizes have been awarded annually since 1901 to those who make exceptional contributions to the following disciplines: physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, peace and economics.

origins.name: Nolensstraat
origins.en: Willem Hubertus Nolens (1860-1931) Roman Catholic clergyman and politician, after the death of Schaepman for many years the leader of the Roman Catholic State Party and member of parliament. From 1909 professor in Amsterdam in labor law.

origins.name: Nooit Dorstraat
origins.en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and in the Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Noord-Bevelandstraat
origins.en: Zeeuwse island.

origins.name: Noordbrabantstraat
origins.en: The province. The street is located in the middle of streets named after castles in this province.

origins.name: Noorder IJdijk
origins.en: North side of the IJ

origins.name: Noorder Valdeur
origins.en: Named after the drainage ditch between the Twiske and the Haal, which was presumably equipped with a wooden sluice gate. The sluices were raised with a rope, which hung over a block in a portal. Disappeared due to the flooding of the Twiske.

origins.name: Noorderakerweg
origins.en: The Akerpolder, where the road runs through, is the name giver here. The addition Noorder serves to distinguish it from the other, the Zuiderakerweg. The road came under the name Noorderakerweg in 1921 from the then dissolved municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Noorderbreedte
origins.en: The distance in degrees of a place north of the equator.

origins.name: Noorderdwarsstraat
origins.en: The names are derived from the Noordse Bos, in the seventeenth century a neighborhood of gardens, cut through by paths and canals, which stretched from the Reguliersgracht to the Spiegelgracht. The land was ceded by the city in 1670 to three charitable institutions, which built houses on it.

origins.name: Noorderhaakspad
origins.en: Sandbank near Texel, the western part of which serves as a resting area for birds and seals. Also known as Razende Bol.

origins.name: Noorderkerkstraat
origins.en: The Noorderkerk, a Protestant cruciform church, built in 1623 by Cornelis Danckertsz.

origins.name: Noorderkroonstraat
origins.en: The constellation (the Great Bear).

origins.name: Noordermarkt
origins.en: Named after the Noorderkerk (see at Noorderkerkstraat). Until 1655, the square was largely occupied by the cemetery attached to the church. In that year and the following year, the cemeteries were moved to a place outside the city. Officially, the market square first received the name Prinsenmarkt (after the Prinsengracht), but that name could not be maintained.

origins.name: Noorderpark
origins.en: It was created in 2014 by merging the Florapark and the Volewijkspark, two green areas on either side of the North Holland Canal. The park owes its name to its location in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Noorderstraat
origins.en: The names are derived from the Noordse Bos, in the seventeenth century a neighborhood of gardens, cut through by paths and canals, which stretched from the Reguliersgracht to the Spiegelgracht. The land was ceded by the city in 1670 to three charitable institutions, which built houses on it.

origins.name: Noordhollandschkanaaldijk
origins.en: The canal between Amsterdam and Den Helder, dug in the years 1818-1824 according to the design of Jan Blanken, because the port of Amsterdam became inaccessible due to the sandbanks at the mouth of the IJ. (The Willemssluizen are named after King William I, who stimulated the construction of the canal.)

origins.name: Noordhollandstraat
origins.en: The province. The surrounding streets are named after castles in this province.

origins.name: Noordkaapstraat
origins.en: The high rock formation, known as the northernmost point of Norway and Europe.

origins.name: Noordkaperweg
origins.en: Whale, black, sometimes with a white belly. Can reach a length of 15 meters. It lives in the temperate regions of the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and around the Southern Ocean.

origins.name: Noordplein
origins.en: The area around Noord metro station forms the high urban center of Amsterdam Noord. The name Noordplein tells about the geographical location in the city. The square forms the heart of Noord and connects Noord with Zuid via the metro line and the Zuidplein there.

origins.name: Noordsche Compagniebrug
origins.en: Named after the Noordsche or Greenland Company, which had its warehouses at Keizersgracht 40-44 in the so-called Greenland warehouses.

origins.name: Noordwal
origins.en: Named after the location, namely the north bank of the IJ.

origins.name: Noordzeekanaalweg
origins.en: Road named after the North Sea.

origins.name: Noordzeeweg
origins.en: Marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean

origins.name: Noordzijde
origins.en: Named after its location relative to the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Notarisappelstraat
origins.en: Apple variety that was first grown in 1890 by notary J.H.Th.W. van den Ham in Lunteren.

origins.name: Notenstraat
origins.en: The fruits of the nut tree.

origins.name: Notweg
origins.en: A former road between the Sloterdijkermeerweg and the Haarlemmerweg, disappeared before the construction of the Bos and Lommerbuurt. A notweg is a country road, intended for the transport of the harvest from the field. The Frisian word 'not' means 'harvest'. The term occurs frequently in North Holland above the IJ, also as a notsloot for a waterway with the same function.

origins.name: Nova Zemblastraat
origins.en: Island in the Arctic Ocean. Barentsz and Heemskerk overwintered there from 1596 to 1597 during their unsuccessful attempt to reach India via the northern route. This street first belonged to the Roggeveenstraat (council decision, 1878).

origins.name: Nuldernauwpad
origins.en: Veluwe border lake between Gelderland and Flevoland.

origins.name: Nydia Ecuryhof
origins.en: Nydia Maria Enrica Ecury (Oranjestad, 1926 - Willemstad, 2012) was a teacher, writer, translator and actress. Ecury studied English and journalism in Canada. In 1957 she settled in Curaçao where she taught at the Martinus-Mavo and at the Nilda Pinto-Household School. She also taught Papiamento privately. In 1967 Ecury was one of the founders of the theater group Thalia. In 1972 she debuted as a poet, after which she published several poetry collections. Ecury also played a role in the film Almacita di desolato in 1986. In 1995 she received the Pierre Lauffer Prize and in 2007 the Cola Debrot Prize.

origins.name: Nydia Ecurystraat
origins.en: Nydia Maria Enrica Ecury (Oranjestad, 1926 - Willemstad, 2012) was a teacher, writer, translator and actress. Ecury studied English and journalism in Canada. In 1957 she settled in Curaçao where she taught at the Martinus-Mavo and at the Nilda Pinto-Household School. She also taught Papiamento privately. In 1967 Ecury was one of the founders of the theater group Thalia. In 1972 she debuted as a poet, after which she published several poetry collections. Ecury also played a role in the film Almacita di desolato in 1986. In 1995 she received the Pierre Lauffer Prize and in 2007 the Cola Debrot Prize.

origins.name: Obiplein
origins.en: Island group in Indonesia, belonging to the Moluccas. The square was built in 1980 on the site of the former Obistraat (council decision, 1923).

origins.name: Oceanenweg
origins.en: The major world oceans: the Atlantic, the Indian and the Pacific.

origins.name: Ochtenhof
origins.en: Village on the Waal in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Octaanweg
origins.en: Hydrocarbon, a petroleum derivative.

origins.name: Oderweg
origins.en: The river on the border of Poland and Germany.

origins.name: Oermilla Tewariestraat
origins.en: Oermilla S. Radjaram Tewarie-Manichand (1922-1990), first Hindu female president of the women's organization of the Sanatan Dharm, an important religious movement of the Hindu Surinamese. Between 1944 and 1968 she gave several religious-cultural lectures in Suriname.

origins.name: Oesjesduiker
origins.en: The name of this diver comes from the signboard 't Osje, which was formerly attached to a butcher on the corner of the Oostenburgergracht

origins.name: Oetewalerpad
origins.en: The village of Oetewaal or Outewaal or Houtewaal, formerly located on the Zeedijk near the current Muiderpoort. The village, which is already mentioned in 1387, was burned down by the Spanish in 1575 and devastated by a storm surge in 1651, but was rebuilt again and again. In 1658 it was annexed by Amsterdam in its fourth expansion. Before 1878, Linnaeusstraat was called Oetewalerweg and was the road from Oetewaal to the Diemermeer (Watergraafsmeer). The current Oetewalerstraat came under the name Noordstraat (council decision of Nieuwe-Amstel, 1884) after the annexation of 1896.

origins.name: Oetewalerstraat
origins.en: The village of Oetewaal or Outewaal or Houtewaal, formerly located on the Zeedijk near the current Muiderpoort. The village, which is already mentioned in 1387, was burned down by the Spanish in 1575 and devastated by a storm surge in 1651, but was rebuilt again and again. In 1658 it was annexed by Amsterdam in its fourth expansion. Before 1878, Linnaeusstraat was called Oetewalerweg and was the road from Oetewaal to the Diemermeer (Watergraafsmeer). The current Oetewalerstraat came under the name Noordstraat (council decision of Nieuwe-Amstel, 1884) after the annexation of 1896.

origins.name: Oetgensdwarsstraat
origins.en: Frans Hendriks Oetgens (1559-1625), city factory master and mayor of Amsterdam on several occasions, was the owner of the land located here around 1600. The former street names Oetgenspad (now Eerste Oosterparkstraat) and Oetgensachterpad also remind us of this. The streets newly built in 1980 were laid out on the site where in 1864 the King. Beiersche Bierbrouwerij was built, in operation until 1927. Part of the stables still functioned as business spaces until around 1955.

origins.name: Oetgensstraat
origins.en: Frans Hendriks Oetgens (1559-1625), city factory master and mayor of Amsterdam on several occasions, was the owner of the land located here around 1600. The former street names Oetgenspad (now Eerste Oosterparkstraat) and Oetgensachterpad also remind us of this. The streets newly built in 1980 were laid out on the site where in 1864 the King. Beiersche Bierbrouwerij was built, in operation until 1927. Part of the stables still functioned as business spaces until around 1955.

origins.name: Oeverlandenweg
origins.en: A citizen has proposed naming an unnamed space Oeverlandenweg. The Oeverlandenweg runs from Adam Smithplein to the Oeverlanden and is therefore seen as an appropriate name for this public space.

origins.name: Oeverpad
origins.en: Named after the location: along and towards the bank of the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Oeverparklaan
origins.en: Refers to the Oeverpark where this lane runs along the entire length.

origins.name: Oeverzeggestraat
origins.en: Reed species, grows at the water edge of ponds and in slow-flowing waters.

origins.name: Ogentrooststraat
origins.en: Plant, belonging to the figwort family.

origins.name: Ohmstraat
origins.en: Georg S. Ohm (1787-1854), German physicist, who formulated the law of the strength of electric current (an ohm is a unit of electrical resistance).

origins.name: Okeghemstraat
origins.en: Johannes van Okeghem (1430-1495), Flemish composer, is considered the master of the Dutch School. He wrote masses, motets and chansons and was the teacher of Dufay and Obrecht.

origins.name: Oldambtstraat
origins.en: The eastern part of the province of Groningen. 'Old' is the North and East Dutch form for 'old'. The word 'ambt' or 'ambacht' means administrative district.

origins.name: Oldenaller
origins.en: Country house near Nijkerk (Gelderland), built in 1655 probably according to a design by Jacob van Campen, on the site of an earlier castle. The house was renovated around 1850 by K.G. Zocher.

origins.name: Oldengaarde
origins.en: Drenthe country house near Dwingelo from 1717.

origins.name: Oleanderstraat
origins.en: Named after the oleander, an ornamental shrub.

origins.name: Olga de Haasstraat
origins.en: Olga de Haas was a Dutch ballet dancer.

origins.name: Oliepalmstraat
origins.en: Palm species. The oil palm produces palm oil, which is used among other things in margarine, soap, biscuits and as fuel.

origins.name: Olifantswerf
origins.en: Named after the former shipbuilding yard 'De Olyphant' which was located here in Kattenburg.

origins.name: Olmenweg
origins.en: The deciduous tree, more commonly known as the elm.

origins.name: Olof Palmeplein
origins.en: Sven Olof Joachim Palme (1927-1986), Swedish politician of international allure. Founder and chairman of the Palme Commission for Disarmament and Security. He fought against the apartheid regime in South Africa. In the 1960s and 1970s, he campaigned with others against the U.S. actions in Vietnam. In 1986, he was murdered.

origins.name: Oltmansstraat
origins.en: Jan Frederik Oltmans (1806-1854), writer. Wrote historical novels, including 'The Shepherd'.

origins.name: Olympiakade
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Olympiaplein
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Olympiastraat
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Olympiaweg
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Olympisch Stadion
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Ombilinstraat
origins.en: River in Central Sumatra, Indonesia.

origins.name: Ommerenhof
origins.en: Location in the Neder-Betuwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Omval
origins.en: Landtong between the Amstel and the ring canal of the Watergraafsmeer. Since the seventeenth century or earlier so named after a 'wreck' located there, that is, a construction site or ruin. The name has been passed down with the transition on 1-1-1921 of this part of the municipality of Ouder-Amstel.

origins.name: Onbekendegracht
origins.en: The canal was dug as a diversion of the Nieuwe Achtergracht (see there). The name is said to have originated because, due to this diversion, the Nieuwe Achtergracht was no longer visible from the Amstel. In 1948, one of the residents made a request to the mayor and aldermen to change this name, because they found it a somewhat strange name. Fortunately, this request was not accepted.

origins.name: Onderlangs
origins.en: Named after its location relative to the ring road of the Watergraafsmeer (here Gooiseweg).

origins.name: Onkelboerensteeg
origins.en: Named after a resident from the seventeenth century, Dirk Honckelboer. The oldest spelling is therefore Onckelboerssteegje. Previously, the alley was called Pleytstraat and Kijffstraat.

origins.name: Onsenoort
origins.en: Castle from the fourteenth century in Nieuwkuyk near Vlijmen (North Brabant), of which only a heavy rectangular tower remains.

origins.name: Onstein
origins.en: A 1711 moat-surrounded country house, located near Vorden (Gelderland).

origins.name: Oogststraat
origins.en: The yield of the field crops.

origins.name: Ooievaarsweg
origins.en: The bird (the crow).

origins.name: Ookmeerweg
origins.en: Named after the former polder, a small lake pumped dry north of the hamlet of Osdorp.

origins.name: Oossaander Hoop
origins.en: Ship of the Oostzaanse shipowner Pieter Swan. Was engaged in whaling under the command of his brother Cornelis from 1769 to 1775.

origins.name: Oost-Indische Huisbrug
origins.en: Named after the nearby Oost-Indische House on the Kloveniersburgwal corner of Oude Hoogstraat

origins.name: Oostakkerstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of East Flanders.

origins.name: Oosteinde
origins.en: The name indicates the location relative to the Utrechtsepoort. That gate stood in the middle of the Frederiksplein, where later the Paleis voor Volksvlijt would stand. The street ran along the east side and at the end of the city (outside the gate, inside the city moat). The street on the other side was then given the name Westeinde.

origins.name: Oostelijke Handelskade
origins.en: The eastern harbor basin owes its origin to trade. The road was laid in 1875-1883. In 1919, a section was named Piet Heinkade (council decision, 1919). The reason why the word Oostelijke was added to the name is not clear from the correspondence that led to the naming. The road was already called Handelskade in 1883 for the naming. Originally it was a quay along the closure dike of the Oosterdok.

origins.name: Oostenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to public traffic in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and formally abolished in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abolished in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oostenburgergracht
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to public traffic in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and formally abolished in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abolished in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oostenburgermiddenstraat
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to public traffic in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and formally abolished in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abolished in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oostenburgerpark
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to public traffic in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and formally abolished in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abolished in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oostenburgervoorstraat
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middle street and -back street according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to public traffic in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and formally abolished in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abolished in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Ooster Ringdijk
origins.en: After its position relative to the Watergraafsmeer. Before the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was annexed, the Ooster Ringdijk was called Noorder- and Zuider-Ringdijk. The Eerste Ringdijkstraat was then called Schoollaan, and earlier still the name Dielemanstraat seems to have been used. A Tweede Ringdijkstraat (formerly Dijklaan) has since disappeared entirely through demolition.

origins.name: Oosterdok
origins.en: The Oosterdok was created by a seawall completed in 1832 on the east side of the city. The quay on and along this dyke was named Oosterdokskade and Oostelijke Handelskade.

origins.name: Oosterdoksdraaibrug
origins.en: This revolving bridge is located near the Oosterdok, hence the name.

origins.name: Oosterdokskade
origins.en: The Oosterdok was created by a seawall completed in 1832 on the east side of the city. The quay on and along this dyke was named Oosterdokskade and Oostelijke Handelskade.

origins.name: Oosterdoksstraat
origins.en: The Oosterdok was created by a seawall completed in 1832 on the east side of the city. The quay on and along this dyke was named Oosterdokskade and Oostelijke Handelskade.

origins.name: Oosterendstraat
origins.en: Village on the island of Texel.

origins.name: Oosterlengte
origins.en: The distance of a place in degrees east of the meridian, which was first assumed.

origins.name: Oostermeerstraat
origins.en: A former country house on the Amstel.

origins.name: Oosterpark
origins.en: Towards the location in the eastern part of the city. The name first only applied to the park, built in 1887 and in the following years. The road along the park was first named in 1895 and previously called Eerste Parkstraat (see Eerste Oosterparkstraat).

origins.name: Oostersekade
origins.en: The origin of this name is unknown. Since the description East Side of the Oudeschans also occurs, the explanation may be that Eastern was used for Eastern. (The Oosterkerk was also known as the Eastern church.) Another assumption for the origin of the name is that this may have been a docking place for ships for the Eastern trade (compare Texelse kade and Gelderse kade).

origins.name: Oosterspoorplein
origins.en: The Eastern Railway, the railway from Amsterdam to Amersfoort, opened in 1874 and extended in 1876 to Zutphen, thus creating the connection to North Germany.

origins.name: Oostertoegang
origins.en: Eastern access from the Oosterdok to the IJ

origins.name: Oosthuizenstraat
origins.en: Village northeast of the Beemster (North Holland).

origins.name: Oostoever
origins.en: Regarding the location relative to the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Oostzaanstraat
origins.en: The village of Oostzaan, located east of the Zaan.

origins.name: Oostzanerdijk
origins.en: The part of the Waterlandse sea wall that originally belonged to the municipality of Oostzaan.

origins.name: Opdijkstraat
origins.en: A dike that has been built 'higher up' as a kind of second defensive line against the water.

origins.name: Openhartsteeg
origins.en: Named after a facade stone, an open heart with orange apple. Already in the sixteenth century this was a sign of Orange sympathies. The alley was also formerly known as Pottenbakkerssteeg.

origins.name: Ophemerthof
origins.en: Village on the Waal, southwest of Tiel (Gelderland).

origins.name: Opheusdenhof
origins.en: Village in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Opijnenhof
origins.en: Village in the Tielerwaard on the Waal, northwest of Zaltbommel (Gelderland).

origins.name: Opmerkzaam
origins.en: The group of women, who regularly holds her silent march on Meiplein in Buenos Aires (Argentina). They want to know the truth about the fate of their men and children, who have disappeared under the general regime. In contrast to the weapons of violence and empty talk, they show in their collectivity and their persistence their struggle for truth, freedom and justice. Around this square, a number of streets are named after the virtues they represent.

origins.name: Opveld
origins.en: Castle in Heer (Limburg).

origins.name: Oranje Nassaulaan
origins.en: The House Oranje-Nassau is a branch of the House of Nassau.

origins.name: Oranje-Vrijstaatkade
origins.en: The Farmers' Republic, founded in 1842, which joined forces with the Transvaal in 1899 in the struggle against the English. Today, Oranje Free State is a province of the Republic of South Africa.

origins.name: Oranje-Vrijstaatplein
origins.en: The Farmers' Republic, founded in 1842, which joined forces with the Transvaal in 1899 in the struggle against the English. Today, Oranje Free State is a province of the Republic of South Africa.

origins.name: Oranjebrug
origins.en: This pick-up bridge derives its name from the street in which it lies. The origin of this street name is uncertain. It may refer to the house 'de Prins van Oranje', which used to stand here close to the Haarlemmerdijk.

origins.name: Orcastraat
origins.en: Also known as the killer whale (zwaardwalvis), black, with a white underside. Can grow six meters long and its dorsal fin is two meters long.

origins.name: Örehof
origins.en: The öre has the value of 1/100 of the standard coin of Sweden, Norway and Denmark (the crown).

origins.name: Orgeldraaierspad
origins.en: Basket-making was originally a typical travelling trade. The name is linked to the world of travelling people and refers to the caravan site here.

origins.name: Orionplantsoen
origins.en: Orion is a striking constellation on the ecliptic. In Greek mythology, Orion was a hunter who pursued the Pleiades, was accidentally killed by Artemis and then was elevated to a constellation.

origins.name: Orionstraat
origins.en: A constellation (the Dolphin).

origins.name: Orlyplein
origins.en: Name of the airport in Paris.

origins.name: Ornsteinstraat
origins.en: Leonard Salomon Ornstein (1880-1941), physicist, professor at Utrecht from 1915.

origins.name: Orteliuskade
origins.en: Abraham Ortelius (1527-1598), Flemish geographer, creator of a famous atlas.

origins.name: Orteliuspad
origins.en: Abraham Ortelius (1527-1598), Flemish geographer, creator of a famous atlas.

origins.name: Orteliusstraat
origins.en: Abraham Ortelius (1527-1598), Flemish geographer, creator of a famous atlas.

origins.name: Ortler
origins.en: Mountain peak in Italy, 3899 meters high

origins.name: Osdorper Ban
origins.en: Named after the neighborhood of Osdorp. On old maps, this neighborhood is mentioned as Oostdorp. In 1957, construction began on the garden city of Osdorp, which was practically completed in 1973. A ban is another word for governor.

origins.name: Osdorperweg
origins.en: Named after the neighborhood of Osdorp. On old maps, this neighborhood is mentioned as Oostdorp. In 1957, construction began on the garden city of Osdorp, which was practically completed in 1973. The Osdorperweg has always borne the names Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

origins.name: Osdorpplein
origins.en: Named after the neighborhood of Osdorp. On old maps, this neighborhood is mentioned as Oostdorp. In 1957, construction began on the garden city of Osdorp, which was practically completed in 1973. The Osdorperweg used to bear the names Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

origins.name: Ostwaldstraat
origins.en: Wilhelm Ostwald (1853-1932), German chemist. Made important inventions in the field of color theory. In 1909 he received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

origins.name: Oterleekstraat
origins.en: Village east of Alkmaar (North Holland).

origins.name: Otopeniweg
origins.en: Name of Bucharest airport.

origins.name: Ottho Heldringstraat
origins.en: Preacher (1804-1876), founder of an asylum for fallen women and founder of the homes for neglected youth named after him.

origins.name: Oturia
origins.en: Mountain peak in Spain, 1920 meters high.

origins.name: Ouborg
origins.en: Fourteenth-century castle on the Swalm near Swalmen (Limburg), of which only a ruin of a heavy octagonal tower remains today.

origins.name: Oud-Ehrenstein
origins.en: Once a strong castle, of which medieval parts still exist, located on the road Heerlen-Kerkrade (Limburg). Before 1363, this stein (fortified stone house) came into the possession of the noble family of Ederen. The name passed on to the castle and was shortened to Ehrenstein.

origins.name: Oudaen
origins.en: Ridderhofstad near Breukelen, on the right bank of the Vecht, partially still medieval, rebuilt in the seventeenth century. It is one of the few castles that escaped the arson by the French troops in 1672.

origins.name: Oude Doelenstraat
origins.en: The targets were the places where the shooting guilds gathered and where they practiced shooting at a target. The Oude Doelenstraat was built on the site of the oldest targets, which date back to the fifteenth century. The Nieuwe Doelenstraat takes its name from the Kloveniersdoelen, which stood on the site of the current Doelenhotel from 1522.

origins.name: Oude Haagseweg
origins.en: The traffic road to The Hague. The old Haagseweg now has a secondary function.

origins.name: Oude Hoogstraat
origins.en: These streets are slightly higher than those in the immediate vicinity. The Oude Hoogstraat was built around 1490, the Nieuwe Hoogstraat a century later.

origins.name: Oude Kinkerbrug
origins.en: Johannes Kinker (1764-1845) was a Dutch poet, philosopher and lawyer

origins.name: Oude Leliestraat
origins.en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Oude Looiersstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

origins.name: Oude Meerhof
origins.en: Named after the former Oude Lake that lay along the extension of the still existing New Lake.

origins.name: Oude Nieuwstraat
origins.en: In a resolution of the city council (vroedschap) of 1550, it was decided to build a new street near the Korsjespoort. This street was simply called 'new street'. Thirty years later, the Sint Geertruidenklooster and the Lieve Vrouwengasthuis were demolished that stood between the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal and the Nieuwendijk. Here too, one of the newly laid streets was called 'the new street'. To distinguish the two new streets, the names were given the addition 'Oude' and 'Nieuwe' in the first half of the seventeenth century, and they have retained these names to this day. The Nieuwe Nieuwstraat was initially also called Nieuwe Herenstraat.

origins.name: Oude Spiegelstraat
origins.en: Named after a well-known Amsterdam family, mostly manufacturers, who had soap factories. In 1564 Lourens Pieters 'in den Spiegel' lived in the corner building of the Oude Spiegelstraat on the Singel and in 1608 Pieter Lourens Spiegel. The intended house is still called Hertspiegel in 1738. The construction of the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat began in 1665. Again, it is likely that a resident from the Spiegel family was the name giver here.

origins.name: Oude Turfmarkt
origins.en: The peat market, which was held from 1564 to 1642 on this part of the former Amsteloever. In 1913 the name was declared obsolete and the quay near the Rokin was pulled back. In 1946 the quay regained its historic name.

origins.name: Oude Waal
origins.en: The walen were, in the early seventeenth century, inlets of the IJ on the old side (Oude Waal) and on the new side (Nieuwe Waal), where the sea ships were moored in winter. The Oude Waal silted up and became too shallow. The Waalseiland was then reclaimed in 1646. The quay on the city side retained the names Oude Waal and Kromme Waal (after the shape) on the Waalseiland the names Binnenkant and Buitenkant (now Prins Hendrikkade) came. The Nieuwe Waal disappeared due to the construction of the Western Entrepot Dock. The Waalsteeg was called Schippersstraatje before 1912. The name was changed due to confusion with the Schippersstraat.

origins.name: Oude-IJselstraat
origins.en: The Oude IJssel is a tributary of the IJssel River.

origins.name: Oudebrugsteeg
origins.en: The alley led to the oldest bridge that was built over the Damrak at the beginning of the fourteenth century as a connection between the old and the new side. The bridge deteriorated when this part of the Damrak was filled in. The two alleys still indicate the location of that old bridge.

origins.name: Oudekennissteeg
origins.en: Since the older spelling Oudekerksteeg is used, it is clear that there is a name alteration here, which dates back to the eighteenth century. The alley is named after the nearby Oude Kerk. Originally, the alley was called Barvoetsbroeders-, Minderbroeders- or Grauwmonnikensteeg.

origins.name: Oudekerksbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the nearby Old Church, the oldest church in Amsterdam. This church dates back to 1306 and is dedicated to Saint Nicholas.

origins.name: Oudekerksplein
