origins.en: Named after the Old Church located here. The square largely originated from the clearing of the cemetery surrounding the church, which was replaced in 1655 by a cemetery outside the city walls. The Old Church is the oldest church in Amsterdam, probably dating from 1306, and dedicated to Saint Nicholas. The current tower dates from 1566, built by Joost Bilhamer.

origins.name: Oudemanshof
origins.en: Corneille A.J.A. Oudemans (1825-1906), botanist, professor in Amsterdam from 1859. Wrote, among other things, the 'Flora of the Netherlands'.

origins.name: Oudenaardeplantsoen
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of East Flanders.

origins.name: Oudenrijnlaan
origins.en: Village west of Utrecht.

origins.name: Ouderkerkerdijk
origins.en: Named after the village of Ouderkerk aan de Amstel, to which these roads lead. The prefix Korte (short) dates from 1956, after the dike was cut through for the industrial estate.

origins.name: Oudeschans
origins.en: A rampart is an earthen wall and as such the Oudeschans was built around 1516 for defense against the Gelders. The concept of rampart has long since been lost here, but water and quay have retained the name. The addition 'Old' will have been given, when in the next century a new rampart was built around the enlarged city.

origins.name: Oudezijds Achterburgwal
origins.en: The canal behind the Voorburgwal on the old side. The square in front of the Oude Waalse Kerk (the old Walloon Church), which until then was part of this canal, was named Walenpleintje on 22-3-1978.

origins.name: Oudezijds Armsteeg
origins.en: Arm has the meaning of bend here. The alley leads to the bend of Warmoesstraat.

origins.name: Oudorperstraat
origins.en: The North Holland village of Oudorp.

origins.name: Ouwerdingenpad
origins.en: In 1532, land on South Beveland drowned.

origins.name: Overamstelstraat
origins.en: Named after the Overamstelsche Polder, which was located in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896. Compared to the center of that municipality, the polder was located on the other side of the Amstel. The street originally ran through to Linnaeusstraat and was called Korte en Lange Overamstelstraat. When, after the construction of the Transvaalbuurt, only Korte Overamstelstraat remained, the addition 'Korte' was declared obsolete in 1913.

origins.name: Overbrakerpad
origins.en: Named after the Overbraker Binnenpolder. From 1943 to around 1960 there was also an Overbrakerweg (in the Overbraker Buitenpolder), but that disappeared due to the construction of the Sloterdijk industrial area.

origins.name: Overdam
origins.en: Once a noble house, later a farm, located on the Vecht between Weesp and Nigtevecht (Utrecht).

origins.name: Overflakkeestraat
origins.en: Part of the Zuid-Holland island of Goeree-Overflakkee.

origins.name: Overhaalsgang
origins.en: Originally a lane (waaigat) on the Hoogte Kadijk, which provided access to the crossing over the Nieuwe Vaart in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, demolished around 1877 in connection with the construction of a railway line along the Wittenburgergracht. On the site of that old crossing is now a permanent embankment connection.

origins.name: Overhaalstraat
origins.en: In traffic engineering, an overhaal is a ferry crossing (overzetveer).

origins.name: Overhoeksparklaan
origins.en: On this site stands the eponymous high office tower designed by Arthur Staal for Shell in 1966. The term 'overhoeks', or 'diagonally placed', refers to the orientation of the building relative to the city and water.

origins.name: Overhoeksplein
origins.en: On this site stands the eponymous high office tower designed by Arthur Staal for Shell in 1966. The term 'overhoeks', or 'diagonally placed', refers to the orientation of the building relative to the city and water.

origins.name: Overijsselweg
origins.en: The province. In the vicinity, several streets are named after castles from Overijssel.

origins.name: Overleg
origins.en: Overleg with parties inside and outside the collective.

origins.name: Overpeltstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Overschiestraat
origins.en: The former village in South Holland, part of Rotterdam since 1941.

origins.name: Overslag
origins.en: Loading goods from sea vessels onto inland vessels and vice versa.

origins.name: Overslaghof
origins.en: Loading goods from sea vessels onto inland vessels and vice versa.

origins.name: Overtoom
origins.en: Named after the overtoom (a dam over which ships were pulled) that was built in the fourteenth century in the Schinkel. The Overtoom was a waterway before the filling in in 1904, the Heiligewegse- or Overtoomsevaart. The southern quay was called, as far as it was in Amsterdam, Vondelkade (council decision, 1875). The north side (the quiet side) has always had the name Overtoom.

origins.name: Overveenstraat
origins.en: Village near Haarlem (North Holland).

origins.name: Overvoorde
origins.en: Old noble house, located near Rijswijk (South Holland).

origins.name: Overzichtweg
origins.en: A former country house on the Schagerlaan, built around 1701 by Jacob Pauw, who gave it the name Groenhoven. A subsequent owner changed the name to Oversicht. The outside was demolished in 1804. The former Pauwenlaan, located west of the Schagerlaan, was named after the Jacob Pauw mentioned here.

origins.name: P. Dijkstraplein
origins.en: P. Dijkstra (1891-1957), director of the Royal Dutch Steam Boat Company from 1945 to 1955 director of the Holland Afrikalijn.

origins.name: P. Hans Frankfurthersingel
origins.en: P. Hans Frankfurther (1932-1996) has been committed to the village of Sloten and the Sloten-Oud Osdorp village council for more than thirty years. The Mill of Sloten returned to the district thanks in part to his efforts in 1991. In 1994 and 1995, he successfully coordinated the campaign around the referendum on the preservation of the Vrije Geer meadow.

origins.name: P. Lieftinckstraat
origins.en: Pieter Lieftinck (1902-1987), economist and politician, member of the Labour Party. Minister of Finance from 1945 to 1952. Famous for his money laundering in the summer of 1945. Initially erroneously named P. Lieftingstraat. By council decision in 1990 the error was corrected.

origins.name: P.E. Tegelbergplein
origins.en: Petrus Emelius Tegelberg (1838-1917), appointed co-director of the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland' in 1873. Board member of the Amsterdamse Droogdokmaatschappij and treasurer of the Amsterdamse Kamer van Koophandel.

origins.name: P.J. Oudstraat
origins.en: Pieter Jacob Oud (1886-1968), liberal statesman. Minister of Finance in the extraparliamentary crisis cabinets of Colijn, known for his austerity policy. In 1948 co-founder of the VVD, chairman of the House of Representatives faction. In the period 1938-1941 and 1945-1952 he was mayor of Rotterdam.

origins.name: P.L. Marnettestraat
origins.en: Pieter Lucas Marnette (1888-1948), Amsterdam architect. Much of his work, such as the school building on Schermerstraat, can be considered part of the Amsterdam School. At the Department of Public Works, he designed street furniture.

origins.name: Paalbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill between Ermelo and Speulde (Gelderland).

origins.name: Paardekraalstraat
origins.en: Location in Transvaal (South Africa), where in 1880 the Transvaal Farmers' National Council met and where it was decided to resist the impending English domination. The section between Transvaalkade and -straat was designated by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel as Eerste Ringkadedwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890), changed to Polderstraat on 16-10-1901, and moved to Paardekraalstraat in 1912.

origins.name: Paardenstraat
origins.en: This street and the nearby Wagenstraat were the home of draggers, stablekeepers and carriage drivers in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. They are located near Rembrandtplein, where markets used to be held, while earlier in the neighborhood near the Regulierspoort (Muntplein) there was a carriage square.

origins.name: Paasbergpad
origins.en: Refers to the Easter Mountain, a hill 80 meters high in the Twente municipality of Losser

origins.name: Paasheuvelweg
origins.en: Hill near Vierhouten (Gelderland).

origins.name: Pablo Nerudalaan
origins.en: Chilean poet (1904-1973). In 1971 he received the Nobel Prize for Literature.

origins.name: Pacayastraat
origins.en: Mountain in Guatemala

origins.name: Padangstraat
origins.en: Port city on the west coast of Sumatra (Indonesia).

origins.name: Paerlduiker
origins.en: derives its name from the brewery 'De Paerl', which was built in Wittenburg in the middle of the seventeenth century by Reinst and Grootenhuizen

origins.name: Pakingehof
origins.en: In 1377, the church village in the Braakman drowned, a now again reclaimed bay of the Westerschelde (Zeeuws-Vlaanderen).

origins.name: Paladruhof
origins.en: The lake, Lac de Paladru, located in southeastern France in the province of Isère.

origins.name: Palamedesstraat
origins.en: 'Palamedes or the murdered senselessness' a tragedy by Vondel, written in 1626 after the death of Maurits about Van Oldenbarneveldt. The part of the Overtoom, where this street is a side street, used to be called Vondelkade. Until 1890, the Palamedesstraat was a private street. The name was given by the construction company. With the takeover by the municipality, the name was also retained.

origins.name: Paleisstraat
origins.en: The name derives from the Town Hall, built in 1648, since 1808 Royal Palace. Before 1875 the street was called Gasthuisstraat, after the oldest hospital in the city, dating back to the fourteenth century, and Stilsteeg (no explanation can be given for this latter name). Another part was called Korte Gasthuismolensteeg before 1875.

origins.name: Palembangstraat
origins.en: City on Sumatra (Indonesia).

origins.name: Palestrinastraat
origins.en: Giovanni Palestrina (1525-1594), Italian composer of sacred music, organist and chapel master.

origins.name: Paletstraat
origins.en: Painter's tools, namely the board on which the painter mixes his colors.

origins.name: Palmdwarsstraat
origins.en: Refer to Palm Tree

origins.name: Palmgracht
origins.en: Refer to Palm Tree

origins.name: Palmstraat
origins.en: Refer to Palm Tree

origins.name: Pamirstraat
origins.en: Mountain in Tajikistan/Afghanistan

origins.name: Pampuslaan
origins.en: Name of an artificial island in the IJsselmeer east of Amsterdam. At low tide, ships often had to wait for a long time until the water was high enough to pass over the sandbank to Amsterdam. The expression 'lying before Pampus' comes from here.

origins.name: Panamakade
origins.en: Named after the Panama Canal, which was dug between 1900 and 1914 through the Isthmus of Panama (Central America).

origins.name: Panamalaan
origins.en: Named after the Panama Canal, which was dug between 1900 and 1914 through the Isthmus of Panama (Central America).

origins.name: Panchulisteeg
origins.en: Panchuli is a mountain in the Himalayas

origins.name: Pancrasstraat
origins.en: Gerbrand Claesz Pancras (1591-1649), Amsterdam soap maker, who was mayor of the city from 1639 to 1649. The name was established as Pancraskade during the construction (council decision, 1876). After the filling in in 1908, the name was changed.

origins.name: Pandimsteeg
origins.en: Pandim is a mountain in India

origins.name: Pandorinastraat
origins.en: Microscopically small aquatic plant. Colony-forming green seaweed, surrounded by a jelly sheath. Able to assimilate carbon dioxide due to the presence of chlorophyll.

origins.name: Pannerdenstraat
origins.en: Village on the Rhine (Gelderland).

origins.name: Papa Koendersstraat
origins.en: Julius Gustaaf Arnout Koenders, better known as Papa Koenders (Paramaribo, 1886 - Paramaribo 1957) was a teacher and an activist for the Sranantongo. In his own words, he was 'great-grandson of grandparents who were slaves'. With his association Pohama founded in 1944, he promoted Sranan and Creole culture. In addition, he founded the monthly magazine Foetoe-boi, which appeared from 1946 to 1956.

origins.name: Papaverhoek
origins.en: The plant (poppy), wild and cultivated, also called klaproos.

origins.name: Papaverweg
origins.en: The plant (poppy), wild and cultivated, also called klaproos.

origins.name: Papenbrugsteeg
origins.en: Named after the Papenbrug, which was here over the Damrak before the partial filling in and was built shortly before 1475. According to a sixteenth-century story, there was an old dilapidated bridge over the Damrak here, which was set on fire by some clergy at Shrovetide (Vastenavond). As a result, the restored or renewed bridge was named Papenbrug.

origins.name: Papendrechtstraat
origins.en: Village on the Beneden-Merwede, opposite Dordrecht (South Holland).

origins.name: Papiermolensluis
origins.en: The name of this fixed bridge is derived from the signboard 'De Papiermolen' on the corner house, where a paper seller lived.

origins.name: Papierweg
origins.en: The product, which is transhipped in the Amsterdam port.

origins.name: Paradijsappelstraat
origins.en: Very old apple from North Holland. The color is predominantly red.

origins.name: Paradijsplein
origins.en: The word, of Old Persian origin, means 'surrounded by a wall'. Often it refers to a garden, but above all it is a world where existence is peaceful and timeless.

origins.name: Paramariboplein
origins.en: The capital of Suriname.

origins.name: Paramaribostraat
origins.en: The capital of Suriname.

origins.name: Parelstraat
origins.en: Named after the former Pearl Bridge between Kattenburger- and Wittenburgergracht, and after the seventeenth-century brewery De Parel.

origins.name: Parkhof
origins.en: The green area in the vicinity of the palace.

origins.name: Parlevinker
origins.en: A parlevinker is a retail trader who sells with a small boat along the ships.

origins.name: Parlevinkerpad
origins.en: A parlevinker is a retail trader who sells with a small boat along the ships.

origins.name: Parmenidesstraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher (540-460 BC), the foremost of the Eleatic school, who taught the unity of all nature.

origins.name: Parnassusweg
origins.en: Mountain in Greece, in Greek mythology the residence of Apollo and the muses. Today figuratively used: the realm of poetic art.

origins.name: Parosstraat
origins.en: Greek island in the Aegean Sea, part of the Cycladic island group. All the islands of the Cyclades are located in a circle (ancient Greek: kyklos) around Delos, an important Greek sanctuary in antiquity.

origins.name: Parthenonhof
origins.en: The large Doric temple on the Acropolis of Athens, built from 447-432 BC in honor of the city goddess Athena. High point of Greek architecture, due to its unrivaled harmonious proportions.

origins.name: Pascalstraat
origins.en: Blaise Pascal (1623-1662), French philosopher and physicist. The hydraulic system is based on Pascal's Law.

origins.name: Passeerdersgracht
origins.en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

origins.name: Passeerdersstraat
origins.en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

origins.name: Passtukkenpad
origins.en: Probably named after the passtuk used to fill or measure spaces between objects.

origins.name: Pastelstraat
origins.en: A coloured crayon (pastel stick). The name is also given to the final product, the chalk drawing.

origins.name: Pasteurstraat
origins.en: Louis Pasteur (1822-1895), French chemist. Proved that various diseases are caused by bacteria. Found a serum against rabies and a method to kill bacteria (pasteurization). Before 1922, this was Prins Hendrikstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1902).

origins.name: Pasubio
origins.en: Mountain peak in Italy, 2236 meters high.

origins.name: Paterslaan
origins.en: According to old deeds of sale, the name of a meadow along the Wijkergouw near Schellingwoude.

origins.name: Patrice Lumumbastraat
origins.en: First prime minister of Congo, took office on June 23, 1960. Just a week later, the former Belgian colony was an independent republic. Lumumba was hated in Belgium and Congo for his fiery speech about the injustices of colonial rule. Lumumba only served his office until September 5, 1960. On January 17, 1961, he was murdered.

origins.name: Patroclosstraat
origins.en: Greek hero in the Trojan War, sung by Homer.

origins.name: Paul Christiaan Fluhof
origins.en: Paul Christiaan Flu (Paramaribo, 1884 - Leiden 1945) was a doctor, professor of tropical hygiene and rector magnificus of the University of Leiden. The very talented Flu obtained his medical degree at the Medical School in Paramaribo at the age of twenty, after which he left for the Netherlands to further his studies. He worked in Suriname, the Netherlands and Indonesia. He also achieved a lot in Suriname: he was the founder of the water supply network and helped many through his extensive knowledge of various tropical diseases. Flu's groundbreaking work was noticed: in 1911 he was appointed Knight of the Order of Orange Nassau.

origins.name: Paul Christiaan Flustraat
origins.en: Paul Christiaan Flu (Paramaribo, 1884 - Leiden 1945) was a doctor, professor of tropical hygiene and rector magnificus of the University of Leiden. The very talented Flu obtained his medical degree at the Medical School in Paramaribo at the age of twenty, after which he left for the Netherlands to further his studies. He worked in Suriname, the Netherlands and Indonesia. He also achieved a lot in Suriname: he was the founder of the water supply network and helped many through his extensive knowledge of various tropical diseases. Flu's groundbreaking work was noticed: in 1911 he was appointed Knight of the Order of Orange Nassau.

origins.name: Paul Hufkade
origins.en: Photographer (1924-2002), famous for his staged studio images, glamour portraits, advertising campaigns and glossy fashion reports.

origins.name: Paul Scholtenstraat
origins.en: Jurist (1875-1946), professor at the University of Amsterdam from 1907. Known for his edition of the Civil Law and the Commercial Law.

origins.name: Paul Schuitemahof
origins.en: Graphic designer and photographer (1897-1973). Known for his powerful typographic designs. After 1926 he introduced photographic elements into his designs. He was one of the first designers to use photo montage for industrial design. Representative of New Photography.

origins.name: Paul van Vlissingenstraat
origins.en: Paul Fentener van Vlissingen was a Dutch entrepreneur, columnist, publicist, conservationist and philanthropist. He was a member of the Van Vlissingen patrician family.

origins.name: Paulus Potterstraat
origins.en: Painter (1625-1654), mainly of landscapes and animals.

origins.name: Paulus van Hemertstraat
origins.en: Theologian and philosopher (1756-1825). Due to objections to the doctrine of predestination, he resigned as a preacher, after which he mainly dealt with Kant's philosophy.

origins.name: Pauwels-van Bienestraat
origins.en: The artist couple Désiré Pauwels (1861-1942) and Sophie van Biene (1854-1907). Pauwels was a famous singer, first at the French Opera in The Hague, later at the Dutch Opera. Sophie van Biene was associated with the Dutch Theater as an actress.

origins.name: Pauwenpad
origins.en: About this place used to run Pauwenlaan, named after Jacob Pauw who built a country house nearby around 1701. Pauwenlaan disappeared due to the construction of the railway line to Utrecht.

origins.name: Pazzanistraat
origins.en: Julius Pazzani, engineer. Director of the Imperial Continental Gaz-Association. Responsible for the technical design of the buildings of the Westergasfabriek. The street is located on the grounds of this former factory.

origins.name: Pedro de Medinalaan
origins.en: Spanish cosmographer (1493-1567). Published in 1545 the book 'Arte de Navegar'. In 1580 the Dutch translation appeared under the title 'De zeevaert oft conste van ter zee te varen'.

origins.name: Pedro Nunesstraat
origins.en: Portuguese mathematician (1502-1578), from 1529 royal cosmographer. Published on the degree arc. His findings were practically useful in navigation.

origins.name: Peelstraat
origins.en: Area on the border of North Brabant and Limburg, originally a poor area of heath and bog, now completely cultivated. The last remnant of Peel has been preserved as a nature reserve under the name Grote Peel.

origins.name: Pegasusstraat
origins.en: A constellation (the Dolphin).

origins.name: Pekelharingstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Adrianus Pekelharing (1848-1922), physician, professor at Utrecht from 1881, best known for his Beri-beri research.

origins.name: Pekkendam
origins.en: Former estate near Diepenheim (Overijssel).

origins.name: Pelerin
origins.en: Corrupted spelling of the French port city of Le Pellerin, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Pelikaanbrug
origins.en: Given the proximity of the d'Peliekaan warehouse at Hoogte Kadijk 51

origins.name: Pelikaanstraat
origins.en: The bird (the crow).

origins.name: Pelistersteeg
origins.en: Pelister is a mountain in North Macedonia

origins.name: Penninkshof
origins.en: Historical name from Rhineland. The name can still be found in Penningsveer aan de Liede (between Haarlem and Spaarnwoude).

origins.name: Pennyhof
origins.en: The penny has the value of 1/100 of the standard coin of Great Britain (the pound sterling).

origins.name: Penseelstraat
origins.en: Painting and drawing tools, a thin brush.

origins.name: Peperstraat
origins.en: Named after the Pepper Yard, which was located on the site of the current Peperstraat and belonged to the warehouses of the Dutch East India Company, where, among other things, the imported spices were stored.

origins.name: Perenpad
origins.en: The fruits of the pear tree.

origins.name: Pernaubrug
origins.en: Pernau was the German name for the Estonian port city of Pärnu on the Gulf of Riga. The names in the Shipyards are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Perseusstraat
origins.en: Constellation in the northern Milky Way.

origins.name: Persijn
origins.en: Castle from the sixteenth century, demolished in the eighteenth century, which was located near Wassenaar (South Holland). It was named after the Hague branch of the Persijns.

origins.name: Persstraat
origins.en: Reference to the paper recycling company that was located on the Cruquiusterrein until the redevelopment of the area in the twenty-first century.

origins.name: Perzikstraat
origins.en: The fruit of the peach tree.

origins.name: Pesetalaan
origins.en: The currency of Spain.

origins.name: Pestalozzihof
origins.en: Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi (1746-1827), Swiss pedagogue influenced by Rousseau. Innovator of methods for popular education.

origins.name: Pesthuysbrug
origins.en: Named after the old plague house, built in 1635 in the Stads- or Godshuispolder, initially only for plague sufferers, later also used for the care of dysentery and typhoid patients and the insane. In 1891, after various new and renovations, it became the Wilhelminagasthuis. In 1925, the last part of the old plague house was demolished.

origins.name: Petemayenbrug
origins.en: The name of this double lift bridge is probably a bastardization of Petemoeienbrug. A petemoei is a (godmother) aunt and was also used in the past as a term for an old woman.

origins.name: Peter Martensstraat
origins.en: Photographer (1937-1992). As a socially engaged photojournalist, he mainly photographed human suffering, where the form was subordinate to the content. A photo had to shock.

origins.name: Peter Schatstraat
origins.en: Composer (1935-2003), of operas, orchestral and choral works. He was considered the greatest talent of his generation for the development of Dutch tonal art. In 1973 he received the prestigious Matthijs Vermeulen Prize.

origins.name: Peter van Anrooystraat
origins.en: Conductor and composer (1879-1954). Was conductor of several orchestras, known as a composer for his Piet Hein rhapsody. Pioneer in the field of youth concerts.

origins.name: Peter Wotkehof
origins.en: Austrian photographer (1800-1870), settled in Rotterdam in 1854, made daguerreotypes as one of the first practitioners in the Netherlands, especially of musicians and panoramas of Rotterdam.

origins.name: Petroleumhavenweg
origins.en: Named after the port located here for unloading oil tankers and the areas for storing petroleum products. The port was put into use in 1888. The first part of the road was previously named Vlothavenweg (council decision, 1953).

origins.name: Petrus Blokhof
origins.en: Historian (1855-1929), Leiden professor, writer of 'History of the Dutch people' and of the 'Social history of Leiden'.

origins.name: Pettenstraat
origins.en: Village at the northern end of the Hondsbossche Zeewering (North Holland).

origins.name: Peursumstraat
origins.en: Village in the Alblasserwaard near the river Giessen (South Holland).

origins.name: Philip Vingboonsstraat
origins.en: Master builder (1613-1678), who applied the raised neck gable and pilasters. He built many fine canal houses (the Trippenhuis, often credited to him, was designed by his brother Justus) on Herengracht and Keizersgracht, Rokin and Singel.

origins.name: Piarcoplein
origins.en: Name of the Port of Spain, Trinidad airport.

origins.name: Pienemanstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas Pieneman (1810-1860), history and portrait painter. President of the association of visual artists and art-loving members "Maatschappij Arti et Amicitiae", founded in 1839, as successor to his father J.W. Pieneman.

origins.name: Pier Afrika
origins.en: The continent.

origins.name: Pier Azië
origins.en: The largest of the continents.

origins.name: Pier Europa
origins.en: The continent.

origins.name: Pier Panderstraat
origins.en: Frisian sculptor (1864-1919). A part of his work is collected in the Pier Pandertempel in Leeuwarden.

origins.name: Pierre Cuypershof
origins.en: Petrus J. Cuypers (1827-1921), architect and creator of Dutch Gothic Revival. His buildings include the Rijksmuseum (1885), Centraal Station (1889) and the Vondelkerk (1878).

origins.name: Pierre Lallementstraat
origins.en: French mechanical engineer (1843-1891). Lallement, a maker of prams, saw a passing draisine (a running machine without pedals) in 1862 and came up with the idea of adding pedals to the front wheel, a discovery that he patented four years later. Thus, he is considered the inventor of the bicycle with pedals.

origins.name: Pierre Laufferstraat
origins.en: Pierre A. Lauffer (Curaçao, 1920 - Curaçao, 1981) was a writer, poet and cultural activist for the preservation of his mother tongue, Papiamento. Lauffer wrote stories at a young age and remained active as an author. In 1944 his first poetry collection appeared, entirely in Papiamento, Patria (fatherland). In language and subject it represents a turning point in literature. Lauffer is indeed called the national poet of Curaçao, because he strongly advocated for the preservation of folklore and the history of his island. He considered Papiamento to be a carrier of culture with a fundamental role in Curaçao's quest for autonomy.

origins.name: Piet Dickentmanbrug
origins.en: Pieter Casper Johan Dickentman (1879-1950) was an Amsterdam cyclist. He was the first professional stayer in the Netherlands and became world champion in 1903

origins.name: Piet Gijzenbrugstraat
origins.en: Bridge over the Leiden Canal near Noordwijkerhout. The name Piet Gijzenbrug has been passed on to the neighborhood around that bridge.

origins.name: Piet Heinkade
origins.en: Pieter Pierszn Heijn (1577-1629), vice-admiral in service of the West India Company. Known for the conquest in 1628 of the Spanish silver fleet in the bay of Matanzas (Central America).

origins.name: Piet Heintunnel
origins.en: Pieter Pierszn Heijn (1577-1629), vice-admiral in service of the West India Company. Known for the conquest in 1628 of the Spanish silver fleet in the bay of Matanzas (Central America).

origins.name: Piet Kranenbergpad
origins.en: Named after Piet Kranenberg, one of the people who saved the Olympic Stadium beside this path. In 1996, with Bram Mulder and the stadium director Otto Roffel, he set up the rescue and operating plan that led to its renovation, begun in 1998.

origins.name: Piet Meerburgbrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after Piet Meerburg, who was born in De Bilt in 1919 and died in Amsterdam in 2010. He was involved in saving Jewish children during World War II, for which he received the Yad Vashem award. One of those children was the later mayor Ed van Thijn. He was also a prominent theater entrepreneur in Amsterdam. For example, he was director of the Nieuwe de la Mar theater for many years and produced the musical My Fair Lady.

origins.name: Piet Moeskopspad
origins.en: Pieter Daniel Moeskops (1893-1964), cyclist. In the 1920s, he was a five-time world sprint champion.

origins.name: Piet Mondriaanplein
origins.en: Painter (1872-1944), living in the United States after 1940. Pioneer in the field of abstract art, leader of neoplasticism.

origins.name: Piet Mondriaanstraat
origins.en: Painter (1872-1944), living in the United States after 1940. Pioneer in the field of abstract art, leader of neoplasticism.

origins.name: Piet Nakstraat
origins.en: Pieter Frederik Willem Nak (1906-1996), working at City Cleaning, central figure within the illegal communist party. Together with colleague Willem Kraan initiator of the February Strike in 1941. In the 1960s he managed to broaden the Vietnamese movement, which led to general rejection of the American actions there.

origins.name: Piet Peelenbrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after Piet Peelen (1922-1978), who worked at the Bridges Department. He made efforts to promote livability in Osdorp, especially in the field of traffic.

origins.name: Piet Wiedijkstraat
origins.en: Named after the pharmacist and writer Piet Wiedijk (died 1938), who wrote the first biography of Multatuli under the pseudonym J. Saks.

origins.name: Piet Zwarthof
origins.en: Photographer, typographer and industrial designer (1885-1977). Pioneer of 'New Photography' and modern typography. He rejected traditional typographic rules. Instead, he used the basic principles of constructivism. His work is recognizable by the primary colors, geometric shapes, repeated word patterns, tight diagonally placed lettering and an early use of photo montage.

origins.name: Pieter A. van Heijningestraat
origins.en: Pieter Adrianus van Heijninge (1903-1942), resistance fighter. Distributed illegal material, raised money for the resistance (illegaliteit) and instigated the February Strike in 1941. Was arrested in 1941 and executed on October 16, 1942 in Woudenberg.

origins.name: Pieter Aertszstraat
origins.en: Painter (1508-1575), painted genre pieces and church interiors. Before 1919 the street was called Nieuwe Tolstraat.

origins.name: Pieter Baststraat
origins.en: Pieter Bast (ca. 1550-1605) Dutch engraver and draughtsman. Child of the famous printing family Plantijn.

origins.name: Pieter Boorsmapad
origins.en: Amateur historian (1871-1951), interested in the history of the Zaanstreek. Laid the foundation for the systematic study of the Zaanse mill history.

origins.name: Pieter Borstraat
origins.en: Pieter Christiaan Bor (1559-1635), historian and Governor of Holland. Author of 'The Dutch Wars'.

origins.name: Pieter Buyskensstraat
origins.en: Geuzen (Sea Beggar) captain during the uprising in Enkhuizen (1534-1606).

origins.name: Pieter Calandlaan
origins.en: Water engineer (1826-1902). His name is mainly associated with the construction of the New Waterway from Rotterdam to Hoek van Holland (1866-1872).

origins.name: Pieter Cornelisz. Hooftstraat
origins.en: One of the great writers of the seventeenth century (1581-1647). He wrote poetry and plays, including 'Granida' and 'Warenar'. Prince Maurice appointed him Drost of Muiden. The Muiderslot was then the gathering place of intellectuals for many years.

origins.name: Pieter de Hoochstraat
origins.en: Painter (1639-1684), especially of interior scenes.

origins.name: Pieter Goosstraat
origins.en: Mapmaker (ca. 1616-1675) in service of the VOC. Made small-scale postage stamps, among other things, from which the course towards the Dutch East Indies could be plotted.

origins.name: Pieter Holmplein
origins.en: Swedish sailor (ca. 1686-1776), and master in the art of seamanship. Settled in Amsterdam, first in the Korsjespoortsteeg and later in the Kattegat. He was an expert in the field of course and navigation calculation. In 1748 he published his famous 'Seaman's sextant'.

origins.name: Pieter Holmstraat
origins.en: Swedish sailor (ca. 1686-1776), and master in the art of seamanship. Settled in Amsterdam, first in the Korsjespoortsteeg and later in the Kattegat. He was an expert in the field of course and navigation calculation. In 1748 he published his famous 'Seaman's sextant'.

origins.name: Pieter Jacobszdwarsstraat
origins.en: A landowner who lived here at the end of the fourteenth century, beginning of the fifteenth century. The alley was then called Gasthuissteeg, but was later named after him.

origins.name: Pieter Jacobszstraat
origins.en: A landowner who lived here at the end of the fourteenth century, beginning of the fifteenth century. The alley was then called Gasthuissteeg, but was later named after him.

origins.name: Pieter Langendijkstraat
origins.en: Man of letters and playwright (1683-1756). Writer of 'The mutual marriage fraud' and 'Krelis Louwen' among others. The street was first named without the addition of the first name (1900), but this was sometimes corrupted to Lange Dijkstraat.

origins.name: Pieter Lastmankade
origins.en: Amsterdam painter (1583-1633), among other things of biblical scenes, teacher of Rembrandt. By council decision of 10-1-1923, a part is named after him in Jan van Goyenkade.

origins.name: Pieter Lodewijk Takstraat
origins.en: Journalist and politician (1848-1907), one of the leaders of the SDAP, editor-in-chief of Het Volk. He was one of the founders of the General Workers' Cooperative De Dageraad.

origins.name: Pieter Nieuwlandstraat
origins.en: Poet, historian and astronomer (1764-1794), professor in Amsterdam and Leiden in astronomy and nautical science. At the age of 19, he had already been recommended for a professorship in Latin. This street was initially named Derde Van Swindenstraat (council decision, 1882).

origins.name: Pieter Oosterhuisstraat
origins.en: Photographer (1816-1885), originally a painter. Began with a portrait studio. Later made stereoscopic photographs and cartes-de-visite of cityscapes, which he sold in large quantities. Known for his industrial photographs, which recorded the construction of railway lines, bridges, harbors and canals.

origins.name: Pieter Oosterleehof
origins.en: Pedagogue and publicist (1863-1930), director of the Christian training school De Klokkenberg in Nijmegen. A well-known personality in the education world. He wrote, among other things, 'The History of Christian Education'.

origins.name: Pieter Pauwstraat
origins.en: Pieter Adriaensz Pauw (1552-1611), councilor and alderman of Amsterdam. His brother Reynier Pauw was mayor.

origins.name: Pieter Postpad
origins.en: Master builder (1608-1669), had a share in the construction of the town hall on the Dam. Other buildings: Mauritshuis and Huis ten Bosch in The Hague, town hall in Maastricht.

origins.name: Pieter Postsingel
origins.en: Master builder (1608-1669), had a share in the construction of the town hall on the Dam. Other buildings: Mauritshuis and Huis ten Bosch in The Hague, town hall in Maastricht.

origins.name: Pieter van den Heuvelpad
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1915-1942), distributed illegal material, was involved in the preparation of the February Strike in 1941 and was part of a sabotage group within the Fokker factory in Amsterdam-North, where he worked. On November 19, 1942, he was executed in Soesterberg.

origins.name: Pieter van der Doesstraat
origins.en: Commander of the Dutch fleet in the struggle against the Spanish (1562-1599).

origins.name: Pieter van der Meulenhof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1912-1944), born 1912 in The Hague, killed in prison in Scheveningen. Van der Meulen was active as a printer in the production of the illegal newspaper 'Het Parool'.

origins.name: Pieter van der Werfstraat
origins.en: Mayor of Leiden, who distinguished himself particularly during the siege of Leiden in 1572 by his perseverance.

origins.name: Pieter Vlamingstraat
origins.en: Historian (1686-1733). He wrote a 'Description of Amsterdam' that remained unfinished due to his sudden death and was later used by the historian Jan Wagenaar.

origins.name: Pieter Zeemanlaan
origins.en: Physicist (1865-1943), professor in Amsterdam. Especially known for his study of light (Zeeman effect). In 1902 he received the Nobel Prize in Physics.

origins.name: Pietersbergweg
origins.en: Named after the Sint-Pietersberg in Maastricht.

origins.name: Pigmentstraat
origins.en: Reference to the Vettewinkel paint factory, later Sigma, which was located on the Cruquiusterrein from 1934 to 2008.

origins.name: Pijlkruidstraat
origins.en: Aquatic plant. The name refers to the shape of the leaves.

origins.name: Pijnackerstraat
origins.en: Adam Pijnacker (1622-1673), painter, in particular of landscapes.

origins.name: Pikoletstraat
origins.en: Songbird, belonging to the finch family. Found in Suriname, among other places.

origins.name: Pilatus
origins.en: Mountain peak in Switzerland, 2129 meters high.

origins.name: Pilotenstraat
origins.en: A pilot is a captain. In this case, it refers to the aircraft pilot.

origins.name: Pina Bauschplein
origins.en: Pina Bausch was a German dancer and choreographer. One of the founders of neo-expressionist modern dance.

origins.name: Pinasstraat
origins.en: A seventeenth-century sailing ship with a square stern.

origins.name: Pinatuboplein
origins.en: Mountain in the Philippines

origins.name: Pindosweg
origins.en: Pindos is a mountain range in Greece

origins.name: Pinksterbloemstraat
origins.en: The meadow plant, belonging to the family of the cruciferous plants.

origins.name: Piraeusplein
origins.en: Greek port city, on which the former KNSM (see KNSM-laan) maintained a scheduled service.

origins.name: Piri Reisplein
origins.en: Hadji Muhiddin Piri Ibn Hadji Mehmed, better known as Piri Reis ('Army Captain Piri'). Ottoman sailor, navigator and cartographer from the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Creator of the Piri Reis map, a detailed world map that appeared in 1513.

origins.name: Pirinsteeg
origins.en: Pirin is a mountain in Bulgaria

origins.name: Pirolastraat
origins.en: Plant, mainly found in dune area.

origins.name: Pisuissehof
origins.en: Jean Louis Pisuisse (1880-1927), cabaret artist. Great artist in the world of folk art.

origins.name: Plaatwerkerstraat
origins.en: Occupational name: someone who processes sheet metal. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Planciusstraat
origins.en: Petrus Plancius (1550-1622), preacher and navigator. Designer of many voyages of discovery.

origins.name: Planetenplein
origins.en: Celestial bodies, which move in elliptical orbits around the sun. The earth is also a planet.

origins.name: Planetenstraat
origins.en: Celestial bodies, which move in elliptical orbits around the sun. The earth is also a planet.

origins.name: Plantage Badlaan
origins.en: Named after the bathhouse, which stood here from 1797 to 1820.

origins.name: Plantage Doklaan
origins.en: In 1682, the city government decided to build a 'plantation' in this area, which came within the city in 1658: a promenade only built with summer cottages, gardens and a few inns. A straight layout was cut across the entire area of the site. The avenue that this new plantation cut through in length was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were created. The summer houses were gradually replaced by residential houses, so today only the Wertheimpark still recalls the former purpose.

origins.name: Plantage Kerklaan
origins.en: In 1682, the city government decided to build a 'plantation' in this area, which came within the city in 1658: a promenade only built with summer cottages, gardens and a few inns. A straight layout was cut across the entire area of the site. The avenue that this new plantation cut through in length was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were created. The summer houses were gradually replaced by residential houses, so today only the Wertheimpark still recalls the former purpose.

origins.name: Plantage Lepellaan
origins.en: In 1682, the city government decided to build a 'plantation' in this area, which came within the city in 1658: a promenade only built with summer cottages, gardens and a few inns. A straight layout was cut across the entire area of the site. The avenue that this new plantation cut through in length was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were created. The summer houses were gradually replaced by residential houses, so today only the Wertheimpark still recalls the former purpose.

origins.name: Plantage Middenlaan
origins.en: In 1682, the city government decided to build a 'plantation' in this area, which came within the city in 1658: a promenade only built with summer cottages, gardens and a few inns. A straight layout was cut across the entire area of the site. The avenue that cut through this new plantation in length was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross lanes were created. The summer houses were gradually replaced by residential houses, so today only the Wertheimpark still recalls the former purpose.

origins.name: Plantage Muidergracht
origins.en: The place Muiden. The former Muidergracht began at the Leprozengracht. Part of it was renamed Jonas Daniël Meijerplein after filling in, the second part was later renamed Hortusplantsoen. The part of the Plantage Muidergracht parallel to Sarphatistraat was called Plantage Lijnbaansgracht before 1915.

origins.name: Plantage Parklaan
origins.en: The avenue ran along the former 'Park', a wide strip of land along the Nieuwe Herengracht. The Wertheimpark is the remainder of that. Where the sports field is now located, there was a concert hall with winter garden from 1849 and from 1883 to 1912 the Parkschouwburg.

origins.name: Plantage Westermanlaan
origins.en: The Nieuwe Prinsengracht originally ran through to the Entrepotdok. In 1864 it was partially drawn into Artis (recognizable by the ponds). The rest was filled in and on 19-11-1879 was named Plantage Prinsenlaan. On the occasion of the zoo's 125th anniversary, that name was changed in 1963 to the current name, named after Gerardus Frederik Westerman (1807-1890), the founder of 'Artis'.

origins.name: Plantagekade
origins.en: In 1682, the city government decided to build a 'plantation' in this area, which came within the city in 1658: a promenade only built with summer cottages, gardens and a few inns. A straight layout was cut across the entire area of the site. The avenue that this new plantation cut through in length was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were created. The summer houses were gradually replaced by residential houses, so today only the Wertheimpark still recalls the former purpose.

origins.name: Platanenweg
origins.en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

origins.name: Platenwagenweg
origins.en: The type of caravan, which was in use around 1930. The street name refers to the caravan camp on site.

origins.name: Platostraat
origins.en: Athenian philosopher (427-347 BC), student of Socrates. One of the greatest thinkers in history. Founded a philosophical school in Athens.

origins.name: Pleimuiden
origins.en: The English port city of Plymouth, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Plein '40-'45
origins.en: Recalls the years of German occupation (World War II). On the square stands the liberation carillon. The square is located on the edge of the resistance heroes' neighborhood.

origins.name: Plein Spanje '36-'39
origins.en: The name recalls the Spanish Civil War of 1936 to 1939, the futile struggle against Franco and his fascist regime. The name and the monument erected here are a tribute to a number of volunteers from the Netherlands who died in that struggle.

origins.name: Plejadenplein
origins.en: The star group, also known as the Seven Stars.

origins.name: Plejadenweg
origins.en: The star group, also known as the Seven Stars.

origins.name: Plesmanlaan
origins.en: Albert Plesman (1889-1953), aviation pioneer. Founded KLM in 1919, of which he was director until his death.

origins.name: Plesostraat
origins.en: Name of the airport in Zagreb, Croatia.

origins.name: Plimsollweg
origins.en: Plimsoll is the brand on the skin of a ship, which indicates up to what depth can be loaded under different conditions (named after the Englishman S. Plimsoll).

origins.name: Ploegstraat
origins.en: Agricultural machinery for loosening (plowing) the arable land.

origins.name: Plotterstraat
origins.en: Drawing machine controlled by a computer. As a counterpart to the street names that remind of the former shipbuilding industry in Amsterdam-North, this naming refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Plutarchusstraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher and writer (50-120), wrote biographies (Vitae) of a number of famous Greeks and Romans and philosophical writings (Moralia).

origins.name: Plutostraat
origins.en: The planet that is farthest from the sun.

origins.name: Pluvierplein
origins.en: The bird. In the Netherlands, the Kentish plover is best known.

origins.name: Pluvierstraat
origins.en: The bird. In the Netherlands, the Kentish plover is best known.

origins.name: Poederooienstraat
origins.en: Village on the Maas in the Bommelerwaard.

origins.name: Poeldijkstraat
origins.en: Village in the Westland.

origins.name: Poggenbeekstraat
origins.en: Georg Jan Poggenbeek (1853-1903), painter, mainly of landscapes.

origins.name: Polanenstraat
origins.en: The former village of Houtrijk and Polanen, now called Halfweg.

origins.name: Polderweg
origins.en: Back to the former state. Until around 1940, there was a polder here with the community garden complex Tuinwijk.

origins.name: Polijsterweg
origins.en: Occupational name of the person who polishes, that is, smooths an uneven surface of, for example, metal or wood.

origins.name: Polluxplein
origins.en: The star that together with the star Castor forms the main stars of the constellation Gemini.

origins.name: Polluxstraat
origins.en: The star that together with the star Castor forms the main stars of the constellation Gemini.

origins.name: Polonceau-kade
origins.en: Camille Polonceau (1813-1859), French railway engineer. Became known for his designs for girders and beams. The so-called Polonceauspant is one of the most important features of the purification plant, the boiler house and the water gas factory of the Westergasfabriek.

origins.name: Polsbroekstraat
origins.en: The rural village in the Lopikerwaard (Utrecht).

origins.name: Polygoongracht
origins.en: Film factory, founded in 1919 in Haarlem. Producer of commissioned films, documentaries and weekly cinema news bulletins.

origins.name: Pomonastraat
origins.en: Roman goddess of the fruit trees

origins.name: Pompmanstraat
origins.en: Job title: someone who is responsible for the pumps in the machine room of a ship.

origins.name: Pond Sterlinglaan
origins.en: The currency of Great Britain.

origins.name: Ponserstraat
origins.en: Occupational name: someone who punches, pressing holes into something with a machine, for example in metal. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Pontanusstraat
origins.en: Johannes Isaac Pontanus (1571-1639), historian in the service of the king of Denmark and the States of Gelderland. In 1611 a description of Amsterdam appeared from him.

origins.name: Pontplein
origins.en: This square owes its name to the IJplein ferry that docks there.

origins.name: Pontsteiger
origins.en: The departure point of the Distelweg ferry and the Houthaven ferry.

origins.name: Poolsterstraat
origins.en: The star that is exactly above the north and therefore remains unchanged in the same place for us.

origins.name: Poolstraat
origins.en: De Pool is the name of a former warehouse on Prins Hendrikkade, in which from 1719 until its demolition in 1878 the Roman Catholic secret church De Pool was located. In the later Roman Catholic Annakerk on Wittenburgergracht (now also demolished again), which became the successor of the secret church, the facade stone of that old warehouse was placed there, so that the name went with Wittenburg.

origins.name: Poortland
origins.en: Corrupted spelling of the English port city of Portland, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Poppendammergouw
origins.en: One of the quarters of the former Banne Ransdorp. The other quarters were Bloemendaal, Holysloot, Ransdorp and Durgerdam. The road came through the annexation of the municipality of Ransdorp in 1921 on Amsterdam's territory.

origins.name: Populierenweg
origins.en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

origins.name: Portengenstraat
origins.en: Village, west of Breukelen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Portsmuiden
origins.en: The English port city of Portsmouth, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Postjeskade
origins.en: Named after the former Postjeswetering. A postje is a freshwater fish.

origins.name: Postjesweg
origins.en: Named after the former Postjeswetering. A postje is a freshwater fish.

origins.name: Potgieterstraat
origins.en: Everardus Johannes Potgieter (1808-1875), merchant, writer, poet and critic, who became the center of a literary circle. Founded 'De Gids' in 1837, which he would edit for thirty years.

origins.name: Potvisstraat
origins.en: Cetacean, with a round, thick head and large teeth. The sperm whale lives scattered around the world.

origins.name: Pracanalaan
origins.en: The lake of Pracana, located in Portugal, in the province of Castelo Branco.

origins.name: Pradolaan
origins.en: Museo del Prado in Madrid, the national museum of Spain, opened in 1918. The foundation of the rich art collection was laid by the collection of Charles V, which was greatly expanded by Philip II and Philip IV. Famous for the paintings of Spanish, Italian and South Dutch artists.

origins.name: Pramenpad
origins.en: A flat-bottomed small inland vessel, is mainly used for the transport of livestock and manure.

origins.name: Praterlaan
origins.en: Stadion in Vienna. Ajax won the Champions League final against AC Milan (1-0) in this stadium on May 24, 1995.

origins.name: Preangerstraat
origins.en: Landscape near Bandung in western Java (Indonesia). Known for the cultivation of coffee, tea and tea plantations.

origins.name: Presanella
origins.en: Mountain peak in Italy, 3564 meters high.

origins.name: President Allendelaan
origins.en: Salvador Allende Gossens (1908-1973), president of the Republic of Chile from 1970, died during a coup. Allende brought a socialist government with a Marxist signature to the Chilean republic. The avenue was called West Shore before 1974 (council decision, 1948).

origins.name: President Brandstraat
origins.en: Jan Hendrik Brand (1823-1888), president of the Orange Free State (from 1864). His motto is well known: 'Everything will come right, if we all do our duty'.

origins.name: President Kennedylaan
origins.en: John Fitzgerald Kennedy (1917-1963), 35th president of the United States of North America from 1961, whose short reign was characterized by a firm approach, assassinated in Texas on November 22, 1963. Before 1964, the avenue was called Rivierenlaan.

origins.name: President Kennedyplantsoen
origins.en: John Fitzgerald Kennedy (1917-1963), 35th president of the United States of North America from 1961, whose short reign was characterized by a firm approach, assassinated in Texas on November 22, 1963. Before 1964, the avenue was called Rivierenlaan.

origins.name: President Steynplantsoen
origins.en: Martinus Theunis Steijn (1857-1916), president of Oranje Vrijstraat (1896-1902). Participated in the Second Boer War (1899-1902).

origins.name: President Steynstraat
origins.en: Martinus Theunis Steijn (1857-1916), president of Oranje Vrijstraat (1896-1902). Participated in the Second Boer War (1899-1902).

origins.name: Pretoriusstraat
origins.en: Andries Pretorius (1799-1853), one of the pioneers of the Transvaal Boers, defeated the Zulu king Dingaan in 1838. The city of Pretoria is named after him.

origins.name: Prins Bernhardplein
origins.en: Named after His Highness Prins Bernhard Lucas Emmanuel of Orange-Nassau, Van Vollenhoven (1969-).

origins.name: Prins Hendrikkade
origins.en: The youngest son of King William II, Prince William Frederick Hendrik (1820-1879), who had a warm interest in trade and shipping. The bust of the prince stands opposite the Shipping House and was made in 1885 by Professor F. Stracke. With the naming in 1879, a number of evocative names disappeared and with them a piece of memory of history. Calculated from the Singel, these were: the Herring Factory, derived from the herring trade established here in the late sixteenth century, on the site of the current Herring Factory Bridge stood the Herring Factory Tower.

origins.name: Prins Hendriklaan
origins.en: Hendrik, Duke of Mecklenburg-Schwerin, Prince of the Netherlands (1876-1934), married Queen Wilhelmina in 1901.

origins.name: Prinseneiland
origins.en: Probably named after the house 'The three Princes', which must have stood here in the seventeenth century. The house had busts of Prince William I, Prince Maurice and Prince Frederick Henry. However, it is not known where this house stood.

origins.name: Prinsengracht
origins.en: After 'the princely title', meaning that of the Princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and the plainest in the character of its buildings. It was dug in the expansion of 1612 and built up from the Brouwersgracht to the Leidsegracht. In the expansion of 1658 this canal too was extended across the Amstel (as far as the Entrepotdok). The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for today's Noordermarkt never caught on with the citizens.

origins.name: Prinsenhofssteeg
origins.en: The former St. Ceciliënsklooster was converted into a residence for royal persons visiting the city after 1578. This is why the building was named Prinsenhof. When the meetings of the Admiralty were later held here, in addition to the name Prinsenhof, the name Admiralty Hof was also created. In 1808, the town hall on the Dam was converted into a palace and the Prinsenhof became the town hall. This remained until 1988. In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries this was Ceciliënsteeg.

origins.name: Prinsensluis
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the street in which it is located and the canal over which it lies. Prince refers to the royal title here, which refers to that of the princes of Orange.

origins.name: Prinsenstraat
origins.en: Named after 'the princely title', which refers to that of the princes of Orange

origins.name: Prinses Amaliaplein
origins.en: Catharina-Amalia Beatrix Carmen Victoria of Orange-Nassau (December 7, 2003), heir princess of Orange, Prinses of the Netherlands, Prinses of Orange-Nassau, eldest daughter of Prince Willem-Alexander and Princess Máxima. Her nickname is Amalia.

origins.name: Prinses Irenestraat
origins.en: Irene Emma Elisabeth, second daughter of Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard, born 5-8-1939. She married in 1964 in Rome to the French nobleman Prince Carel Hugo of Bourbon Parma. For technical reasons, the western part of the Prinses Irenestraat near Rb. was renamed Fred. Roeskestraat on 27-4-1977.

origins.name: Prinses Margrietstraat
origins.en: Margriet Francisca, princess of the Netherlands, born 1943 in Canada, third daughter of Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard. In 1967 she married Pieter van Vollenhoven.

origins.name: Prinses Marijkestraat
origins.en: Maria Christina, princess of the Netherlands, born 1947. Fourth daughter of Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard. Was first called Princess Marijke, but has been calling herself Princess Christina since 1967.

origins.name: Printerstraat
origins.en: Device with which text and images, stored in a computer, can be printed. As a counterpart to the street names that remind of the former shipbuilding industry in Amsterdam-North, this naming refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Processorstraat
origins.en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

origins.name: Prof. H. Bavinckstraat
origins.en: Herman Bavinck (1854-1921), professor of theology at the Vrije Universiteit in Amsterdam. Due to his work in the field of pedagogy, he had a great influence on Christian education.

origins.name: Prof. Ph. Kohnstammstraat
origins.en: Philippus Abraham Kohnstamm (1875-1951), professor of pedagogy in Amsterdam and Utrecht. Had a great influence on the field of pedagogy at home and abroad.

origins.name: Prof. R. Casimirstraat
origins.en: Rommert Casimir (1877-1957), pedagogue, professor at Leiden, publicist.

origins.name: Prof. Tulpplein
origins.en: Nicolaas Tulp (1593-1674), Amsterdam physician, professor at the Athenaeum Illustre for the surgical guild. Also several times mayor of the city. The title Professor was added to the street name in 1946, because many were inclined to look for the street in the flower district.

origins.name: Prof. Tulpstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas Tulp (1593-1674), Amsterdam physician, professor at the Athenaeum Illustre for the surgical guild. Also several times mayor of the city. The title Professor was added to the street name in 1946, because many were inclined to look for the street in the flower district.

origins.name: Professor J.H. Gunningstraat
origins.en: Professor Johannes Hermanus Gunning (1859-1951), pedagogue. He was the first professor of pedagogy in government service and was the first in the Netherlands to advocate for the establishment of a high school.

origins.name: Profiltigracht
origins.en: Film factory, founded in 1929 in The Hague. Producer of (commissioned) films, documentaries and cinema newsreels. First counterpart, later partner of Polygoon.

origins.name: Programmeurstraat
origins.en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

origins.name: Propaanweg
origins.en: A petroleum derivative: gas used as motor fuel.

origins.name: Propellerstraat
origins.en: The common propulsion method for aircraft before the advent of jet engines.

origins.name: Provincialeweg
origins.en: Name determined by the municipality of Weesperkarspel for the road along the Weespertrekvaart and the Gaasp. Originally, the road was called the Weesperzandpad, built around 1640 by the cities of Amsterdam and Weesp. Until 1929, the road was managed by the Commissioners of the Zandpad. In 1929, management was taken over by the Province.

origins.name: Pruimenstraat
origins.en: The fruits of the plum tree.

origins.name: Ptolemaeusstraat
origins.en: Claudius Ptolemy (second century AD), Greek mathematician and astronomer. He first gave an overview of the longitudes and latitudes of the main cities of antiquity. Ptolemy's theorem: in a cyclic quadrilateral, the product of the diagonals is equal to the sum of the products of the opposite sides.

origins.name: Puiflijkpad
origins.en: Village in the Land of Maas and Waal (Gelderland).

origins.name: Pumoriplein
origins.en: Pumori is a mountain in the Himalayas

origins.name: Punterspad
origins.en: An open boat with flat bottom, particularly in use in the area around Giethoorn.

origins.name: Purmerhof
origins.en: The polder, created by the draining of the lake between 1618 and 1622 near Purmerend.

origins.name: Purmerplein
origins.en: The polder, created by the draining of the lake between 1618 and 1622 near Purmerend.

origins.name: Purmerweg
origins.en: The polder, created by the draining of the lake between 1618 and 1622 near Purmerend.

origins.name: Purperhoedenveem
origins.en: A veem is a company responsible for storing and delivering goods in and out of its warehouses. The veems each had their own license plate, after which they were named. These could be different colors and models of hats (e.g. Puper hats, Clogs). They also derived their name from the origin of the workers (e.g. Vriesseveem, Zeeuwse Veem).

origins.name: Putterplantsoen
origins.en: Songbird, also known as goldfinch (distelvink). Often kept as a cage bird.

origins.name: Putterstraat
origins.en: Songbird, also known as goldfinch (distelvink). Often kept as a cage bird.

origins.name: Pybo Steenstrastraat
origins.en: Scholar (died in 1788). Lecturer in mathematics, astronomy and nautical science at the Athenaeum Illustre in Amsterdam. Examiner of the navigators (stuurlieden) in service of the VOC in Amsterdam. He published among other things 'Grondbeginzels der Stuurmanskunst' (principles of navigation) (1766) and 'Public lessons on finding longitude at sea' (1770).

origins.name: Pyreneeën
origins.en: The mountain, located in France and Spain.

origins.name: Pythagorasstraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher and mathematician (582-507 BC), best known for the theorem named after him: the square of the hypotenuse of a right triangle is equal to the sum of the squares of the two right sides. The street was called Mr. Cornelis van Lennepstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1904) before 1922.

origins.name: Quashibastraat
origins.en: Quashiba lived in slavery on Saint Martin. In 1835 she managed to escape in a small boat with a few fellow slaves, including her two children Sammy and Jane, to the nearby British island of Anguilla. Five years later, her partner, Matthew Stancliff, dared to sail to Sint Maarten to pick up Quashiba's sister Minny and her children as well, so that they too could live freely. Quashiba and her family therefore stand for the struggle for freedom.

origins.name: Quellijnstraat
origins.en: Artus Quellijn or Quellinus (1609-1668), South Dutch sculptor. He made, among other things, the sculpture for the town hall on the Dam.

origins.name: Quinten Massijsstraat
origins.en: Flemish painter and goldsmith (1466-1530). The name is also written as Matsijs.

origins.name: R.J.H. Fortuynplein
origins.en: R.J.H. Fortuyn (born 1916) was appointed director of the Royal Dutch Lloyd in Amsterdam in 1956.

origins.name: R.J.H. Fortuynstraat
origins.en: R.J.H. Fortuyn (born 1916) was appointed director of the Royal Dutch Lloyd in Amsterdam in 1956.

origins.name: Raadhuisstraat
origins.en: Named after the town hall, designed in the seventeenth century by Jacob van Campen and built by Daniël Stalpaert. In 1808, ordered by King Louis Napoleon, it was evacuated and has since been used as a royal palace. The Raadhuisstraat was created in 1895 by widening the Huiszittensteeg and the Korte Huiszittensteeg, by filling in the Warmoesgracht and by a breakthrough of the canal wall.

origins.name: Raamdwarsstraat
origins.en: The lakenramen (tenter frames for stretching cloth), where the dyed cloth was hung to dry, had to be set up outside the city. When the Kloveniersburgwal was still the city moat, these frames could be found at the height of the current Raamgracht. The nearby Verversstraat also still reminds us of this old Amsterdam industry.

origins.name: Raamgracht
origins.en: The lakenramen (tenter frames for stretching cloth), where the dyed cloth was hung to dry, had to be set up outside the city. When the Kloveniersburgwal was still the city moat, these frames could be found at the height of the current Raamgracht. The nearby Verversstraat also still reminds us of this old Amsterdam industry.

origins.name: Raamplein
origins.en: The lakenramen (tenter frames for stretching cloth) were moved here during the sixteenth-century enlargements, when the area between Kloveniersburgwal and Zwanenburgwal was drawn into the city. The Raamplein was created by filling in a section of Lijnbaansgracht.

origins.name: Raampoort
origins.en: This bridge is named after the Raampoort, which was demolished in 1844

origins.name: Raamsteeg
origins.en: The lakenramen (tenter frames for stretching cloth) that were found on the outside of the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. This is the oldest place whose name is remembered by the cloth-dyeing houses.

origins.name: Raamstraat
origins.en: The lakenramen (tenter frames for stretching cloth), which were moved here, when the city was expanded in the sixteenth century, the area between Kloveniersburgwal and Zwanenburgwal was drawn closer to the city. Raamplein was created by filling in a section of Lijnbaansgracht.

origins.name: Raasdorperweg
origins.en: The former hamlet of Raasdorp, which was located on the edge of the Lutkemeer.

origins.name: Rachel Ruyschbrug
origins.en: Rachel Ruysch (The Hague, 1664 - Amsterdam, 1750) was one of the most successful still life painters of the 17th and 18th centuries. She is world famous for her colorful and lifelike floral paintings. As a married woman and mother of ten children, she continued her brilliant career unabated.

origins.name: Radarweg
origins.en: The navigation aid for ships and aircraft in the dark and poor visibility. The system is based on the reflection of radio waves. Radar is the abbreviation of Radio Detection and Ranging. The road was initially named Gyroscope Road.

origins.name: Radboud
origins.en: Square castle with round corner towers founded around 1289 by Floris V in Medemblik (North Holland). Partially demolished in the seventeenth century and rebuilt in 1890.

origins.name: Rademakerstraat
origins.en: Abraham Rademaker (1675,76-1735) was a Dutch engraver and draughtsman who became famous for his prints of castles, cities and country estates in the 17th and 18th centuries. He made dozens of images of existing country estates in the vicinity of Amsterdam, among other places.

origins.name: Raden Adjeng Kartinistraat
origins.en: Indonesian publicist and propagandist (1879-1904), advocate for human rights and pioneer of the Indonesian feminist movement. In 1903 her manifesto 'Give the Javanese education' appeared, followed in 1911 by her letters. In 1964 she was elevated to national heroine.

origins.name: Raderbootstraat
origins.en: Vessel propelled by paddle wheels.

origins.name: Radioweg
origins.en: The transmission of sound and signals through electrical waves, discovered by Hertz in 1888 and first applied by Marconi in 1900. At the time of the establishment of this street name, radio was one of the most important discoveries, through the application via the broadcasting associations.

origins.name: Ramskooi
origins.en: No explanation can be found for the name of this alley, which already existed around 1450. Some historians think of the name of a Norwegian woodcutter, while another assumption is that Jan Ran had a duck pond here. In the sixteenth century, the alley appears under the name Jan Ranskoy. The alley originally ran through to Prins Hendrikkade, which until 1879 was called Texelse kade for that part, and even earlier Nieuwezijds Houttuinen.

origins.name: Randwijkhof
origins.en: Location in Gelderland, located between Wageningen and Arnhem.

origins.name: Rangeerderstraat
origins.en: Railway worker, who is responsible for connecting and disconnecting train carriages and maneuvering the trains to the different tracks.

origins.name: Ranonkelkade
origins.en: Named after the buttercup (ranunculus), a plant.

origins.name: Raoul Wallenberghofje
origins.en: Swedish diplomat (1912-unknown), he advocated for peace and human rights. During World War II, he saved tens of thousands of Hungarian Jews from deportation. In 1945, he was captured by Soviet troops. In 1947, according to the Soviets, he died of a heart attack in captivity, but his death has never been confirmed.

origins.name: Raoul Wallenbergstraat
origins.en: Swedish diplomat (1912-unknown), he advocated for peace and human rights. During World War II, he saved tens of thousands of Hungarian Jews from deportation. In 1945, he was captured by Soviet troops. In 1947, according to the Soviets, he died of a heart attack in captivity, but his death has never been confirmed.

origins.name: Rapenburg
origins.en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now Oosterdok), Oudeschans, Rapenburgwal and Schippersgrachtje. The main street has taken the name of the island. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

origins.name: Rapenburgerplein
origins.en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now Oosterdok), Oudeschans, Rapenburgwal and Schippersgrachtje. The main street has taken the name of the island. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

origins.name: Rapenburgerstraat
origins.en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now Oosterdok), Oudeschans, Rapenburgwal and Schippersgrachtje. The main street has taken the name of the island. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

origins.name: Raphael Lemkinstraat
origins.en: Polish-Jewish lawyer (1901-1959), fought in the Polish resistance in 1939, fled to Sweden and later to the US. In the Holocaust he lost 49 family members. In 1944 he introduced the term genocide and in 1948 he was the driving force behind the UN negotiations on the Genocide Convention.

origins.name: Raphaëlplein
origins.en: Raffaëllo di Senti (1483-1520), Italian painter, leading figure of the Renaissance. Painted numerous madonnas, frescoes and portraits. Also worked as an architect on St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.

origins.name: Raphaëlstraat
origins.en: Raffaëllo di Senti (1483-1520), Italian painter, leading figure of the Renaissance. Painted numerous madonnas, frescoes and portraits. Also worked as an architect on St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.

origins.name: Ravensteinplein
origins.en: Old fortified town on the Maas (North Brabant).

origins.name: Ravensteinstraat
origins.en: Old fortified town on the Maas (North Brabant).

origins.name: Ravenstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out on the grounds of the shipyard 'De Raven' that was demolished in 1887. Marten Willems Raven is listed as the owner of this shipyard in 1692.

origins.name: Ravenswaaipad
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Maurik in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Ravenwerf
origins.en: The shipbuilding yard 'De Zwarte Raaf', which used to be located here between Kattenburgerstraat and -gracht.

origins.name: Realengracht
origins.en: Reynier Reael, in 1633 alderman (schepen) of the city. He was the owner of the entire Realeneiland.

origins.name: Réaumurstraat
origins.en: René Antoine F. de Réaumur (1683-1757), French physicist. In 1730 he constructed the thermometer named after him with an eighty-part scale. The street name was previously established by the municipality of Watergraafsmeer as Bothastraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1891).

origins.name: Recht Boomssloot
origins.en: The 16th-century shipbuilder Cornelis Pietersz Boom. To connect his shipyard on the Lastage with the surrounding water, he had a canal and a cross-channel dug. These were then named after him.

origins.name: Reesluis
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the Reestraat, in which it lies.

origins.name: Reestraat
origins.en: Deer species. The name recalls the hide trade, which was concentrated before the construction of the street in this neighborhood, and later in the nearby southern part of the Jordaan.

origins.name: Reewijkplein
origins.en: The South Holland village of Reeuwijk.

origins.name: Reggestraat
origins.en: Tributary of the Overijssel Vecht.

origins.name: Reguliersbreestraat
origins.en: All these names recall the Reguliers monastery (of the Canons Regular), which stood from 1394 to 1532 outside the city gate of the time, where the Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now cross. The city gate, of which the Munttoren is a remnant, was once called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht then ended at that gate. Parts of it were filled in in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Before 1909 the Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

origins.name: Reguliersdwarsstraat
origins.en: All these names recall the Reguliers monastery (of the Canons Regular), which stood from 1394 to 1532 outside the city gate of the time, where the Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now cross. The city gate, of which the Munttoren is a remnant, was once called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht then ended at that gate. Parts of it were filled in in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Before 1909 the Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

origins.name: Reguliersgracht
origins.en: All these names recall the Reguliers monastery (of the Canons Regular), which stood from 1394 to 1532 outside the city gate of the time, where the Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now cross. The city gate, of which the Munttoren is a remnant, was once called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht then ended at that gate. Parts of it were filled in in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Before 1909 the Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

origins.name: Reigersbos
origins.en: Name of a farm that stood on Abcouderstraatweg near the former Zwetskade.

origins.name: Reigersbosachterom
origins.en: Name of a farm that stood on Abcouderstraatweg near the former Zwetskade.

origins.name: Reigersbosdreef
origins.en: Name of a farm that stood on Abcouderstraatweg near the former Zwetskade.

origins.name: Reigersbospad
origins.en: Name of a farm that stood on Abcouderstraatweg near the former Zwetskade.

origins.name: Reigerweg
origins.en: The bird (the crow).

origins.name: Reijnier Vinkeleskade
origins.en: Etcher and draftsman (1741-1816), produced approximately three thousand prints, including many Amsterdam cityscapes. His work is therefore also important for topography.

origins.name: Reimersbeek
origins.en: Castle in Nuth (Limburg), founded in the sixteenth century, partially demolished and renovated in the eighteenth century. Today it is a rectangular house, consisting of three wings with a seventeenth-century gatehouse and accompanying farmhouse from 1705.

origins.name: Reimerswaalstraat
origins.en: Location on Zuid-Beveland near Yerseke. The land of Reimerswaal was completely swallowed up by a storm surge in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Reina Prinsen Geerligsstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1922-1943), born in Semarang (Indonesia), killed in the Oranienburg concentration camp (Germany).

origins.name: Reinaert de Vosstraat
origins.en: Medieval animal epic, probably of French origin, edited in Middle Dutch in 1260. Before 1939, this street was part of the Zeven Provinciënstraat (= Bestevâerstraat).

origins.name: Reinhard Dozyhof
origins.en: Historian (1820-1883), professor at Leiden. Famous orientalist.

origins.name: Reinier Claeszenplein
origins.en: Dutch vice-admiral. Was attacked by the Spanish fleet in 1606 at Cape St. Vincent (Portugal) and blew up his ship, instead of surrendering.

origins.name: Reinier Claeszenstraat
origins.en: Dutch vice-admiral. Was attacked by the Spanish fleet in 1606 at Cape St. Vincent (Portugal) and blew up his ship, instead of surrendering.

origins.name: Reinier Engelmanstraat
origins.en: Actor (1795-1845), pupil, later partner, of Andries Snoek.

origins.name: Reinveen
origins.en: A former farm on the Uitweg, demolished to build the garden city of Osdorp.

origins.name: Reinwardtstraat
origins.en: Caspar G.C. Reinwardt (1773-1854), professor of chemistry and pharmacy in Amsterdam. Director of the Royal Cabinet of Natural History in Amsterdam. Organized the medical service in Java in 1817.

origins.name: Reitdiepstraat
origins.en: Channel between the city of Groningen and Zoutkamp.

origins.name: Reitzstraat
origins.en: Francis William Reitz (1844-1934), South African statesman and writer. President of Oranje Vrijstraat from 1889 to 1896. Participated in the Second Boer War (1899-1902).

origins.name: Reizigersweg
origins.en: Travelling people. The name refers to the caravan park on site.

origins.name: Reling
origins.en: The railing of the fence that surrounds the ship deck.

origins.name: Rembrandtpark
origins.en: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn (1606-1669), the greatest Dutch painter of the Golden Age. The placement of his statue, first on the side in 1852, in the middle in 1875, was the reason why the square was renamed Rembrandtplein in 1876. Previously, the square was called Botermarkt, while the corner at Amstelstraat was unofficially called Kippenhoek because of the poultry market.

origins.name: Rembrandtplein
origins.en: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn (1606-1669), the greatest Dutch painter of the Golden Age. In 1852, the cast iron Rembrandt Monument, which was made by Louis Royer, was unveiled by King William III. This was first placed on the side of the square. In 1875, the monument was moved to the center, which was the reason for changing the name of the square to Rembrandtplein. Before that, the square was called Botermarkt after the market that took place here every Monday morning since the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Remijden
origins.en: Historical name of a piece of land in the old Sloten.

origins.name: Remmerdenplein
origins.en: Hamlet in the Gelderland municipality of Rheden.

origins.name: Rengerskerkestraat
origins.en: A village lost in a storm surge in the seventeenth century south of Schouwen (Zeeland).

origins.name: Renkumhof
origins.en: Place on the Rhine (Gelderland).

origins.name: Renooiplein
origins.en: Village on the Linge in the Betuwe.

origins.name: Renswoudestraat
origins.en: Village in the Gelderse valley, with a seventeenth-century castle of the same name (Utrecht).

origins.name: Resedastraat
origins.en: The garden plant. Found in the wild in dune area.

origins.name: Retiefstraat
origins.en: Pieter Retief (1788-1838), leader of the South African Boers during the Great Trek of 1835 and the following years.

origins.name: Retirobrug
origins.en: Station in Buenos Aires

origins.name: Revaleiland
origins.en: Nowadays Tallinn, the capital of Estonia. Amsterdam was the largest buyer of rye, grain and wood in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Reyer Anslostraat
origins.en: Poet (1625-1669), wrote among other things a laudatory poem on Amsterdam on the occasion of the laying of the first stone of the new town hall in 1648. Before 1896, this street was called Nieuwer-Amstel Parkstraat by the municipality.

origins.name: Rheastraat
origins.en: Figure from Greek mythology. One of the Titans, wife of Cronus, mother of Hestia, Hera, Demeter, Poseidon, Hades and Zeus.

origins.name: Rhenenhof
origins.en: City on the Rhine near the Grebbeberg (Utrecht).

origins.name: Rhijnestein
