origins.en: Ridderhofstad in Cothen near Jutphaas on the Kromme Rijn, consisting of a residential tower and a gate from the sixteenth century. The second tower and the central part date from around 1850.

origins.name: Rhijnspoorplein
origins.en: Named after the former Rhijnspoorwegmaatschappij, which opened the Weesperpoort station here in 1843. The company was later incorporated into the Dutch Railways.

origins.name: Rhijnvis Feithstraat
origins.en: Poet (1753-1824). Both in his poetry and his plays he was a great innovator. Loved by many during his lifetime. His evangelical New Year's carol is well known: 'Hours days months years, flying like a shadow away'.

origins.name: Rhodosweg
origins.en: Greek island in the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Rhôneweg
origins.en: The river, which springs in Switzerland and flows through Lake Geneva and France near Marseille into the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Ribesstraat
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Richard Holstraat
origins.en: Conductor, composer and pedagogue (1825-1904). Leader of the classical concerts in the Paleis voor Volksvlijt, teacher of Johan Wagenaar and Willem Mengelberg. Composed a number of symphonies.

origins.name: Richard Wagnerstraat
origins.en: German composer (1813-1883), creator of the nineteenth-century German musical drama ('Lohengrin', 'Tannhauser', 'Parsifal', 'Nibelungen').

origins.name: Ridderspoorweg
origins.en: Plant with purple, blue, red, yellow or white flowers. The scientific name, 'Delphinium', comes from the Latin word for dolphin, because the buds of the flower resemble a dolphin in some ways.

origins.name: Rie Mastenbroekstraat
origins.en: Hendrika Wilhelmina Kuypers-Mastenbroek (1919-2003), swimmer. Won three gold medals and one silver medal in 1936 during the Olympic Games, an unprecedented medal haul for a swimmer to date.

origins.name: Riekerweg
origins.en: Named after the Riekerpolder located here. The name comes from the former village of Rijk that was located south of the village of Sloten.

origins.name: Rietlandpark
origins.en: Until around 1880, an undeveloped, partly swampy and reed-covered area. After trade areas and sorting areas were built here at the end of the nineteenth century, the docks and roads were given their own names. The name Stads Rietlanden is still used today for the sorting area.

origins.name: Rietlandterras
origins.en: Until around 1880, an undeveloped, partly swampy and reed-covered area. After trade areas and sorting areas were built here at the end of the nineteenth century, the docks and roads were given their own names. The name Stads Rietlanden is still used today for the sorting area.

origins.name: Rietnesse
origins.en: The former castle of Costijn van Sirixe in Zierikzee on Schouwen-Duiveland (Zeeland).

origins.name: Rietveld Schröderpad
origins.en: The museum Het Rietveld Schröderhuis in Utrecht. The architect Gerrit Rietveld (1888-1964) designed the house for Truus Schröder-Schräder, whose contribution has been very decisive for the final result. The house, the interior and the furniture comply with the architectural principles of De Stijl. After the death of Truus Schröder in 1985, the house was opened to the public.

origins.name: Rietwijkerstraat
origins.en: A neighborhood that disappeared due to the construction of the Amsterdamse Bos near Amstelveen. Originally a village located further west, it was drowned in the Haarlemmermeer in the second half of the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Rietzangerweg
origins.en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

origins.name: Rigakade
origins.en: Port and capital of Latvia.

origins.name: Rigelstraat
origins.en: A star in the constellation Orion.

origins.name: Rijgersborgh
origins.en: Farm (also called Reigersbosch) on the Uitweg, demolished for the construction of the Slotermeer district.

origins.name: Rijnlandlaan
origins.en: An area around the Old Rhine from Katwijk aan Zee to Utrecht, mostly in the current province of South Holland.

origins.name: Rijnsburgstraat
origins.en: Location in South Holland. The street originally made up part of the Sloterweg, but this section was renamed in 1973, because due to urban expansion the Sloterweg was divided into two parts.

origins.name: Rijnstraat
origins.en: The river that springs in Switzerland, which comes into our country near Lobith.

origins.name: Rijsbesstraat
origins.en: Blue-black berry from the heath family, slightly more oval than the bilberry (bosbes), rare in the Netherlands. Grows in peat-rich soil near forest ponds. Tastes slightly sweet and is used to make jam, jelly or juice.

origins.name: Rijsdrechthof
origins.en: Old Rhine-Landish name: a water north of Leimuiden, disappeared due to the draining of the Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Rijssenburghof
origins.en: Drowned settlement between Leimuiden and Aalsmeer.

origins.name: Rijswijkstraat
origins.en: Village in South Holland, border municipality of The Hague.

origins.name: Rijtuigenhof
origins.en: This courtyard with the adjacent houses was laid out and built on a site that was occupied from 1910 until around 1980 by the company buildings of the Amsterdamse Rijtuig Maatschappij.

origins.name: Ringdijk
origins.en: After its position relative to the Watergraafsmeer. Before the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was annexed, the Ooster Ringdijk was called Noorder- and Zuider-Ringdijk. The Eerste Ringdijkstraat was then called Schoollaan, and earlier still the name Dielemanstraat seems to have been used. A Tweede Ringdijkstraat (formerly Dijklaan) has since disappeared entirely through demolition.

origins.name: Ringslangpad
origins.en: Harmless snake from the family of water snakes, native to Amsterdam. Can reach a length of up to one and a half meters. The color is brown to olive green, and the animal owes its name to the yellow neck spots that can merge into a ring.

origins.name: Ringvaartdijk
origins.en: The water along which the path runs. A ring canal (ringvaart) is the storage basin (boezem) of a polder, into which excess water from the polder is discharged.

origins.name: Ringweg-Noord
origins.en: Named after the function of this national road (A 10), whose parts have been localized by adding the wind direction. The western part of this Ringweg was previously named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten IJ via a tunnel.

origins.name: Ringweg-Oost
origins.en: Named after the function of this national road (A 10), whose parts have been localized by adding the wind direction. The western part of this ring road was previously named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten IJ via a tunnel.

origins.name: Ringweg-West
origins.en: Named after the function of this national road (A 10), whose parts have been localized by adding the wind direction. The western part of this Ringweg was previously named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten IJ via a tunnel.

origins.name: Ringweg-Zuid
origins.en: Named after the function of this national road (A 10), whose parts have been localized by adding the wind direction. The western part of this Ringweg was previously named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten IJ via a tunnel.

origins.name: Rini Ottehof
origins.en: Sara Catharina Otte (1917-1991), film actress, made a sensation as a young girl in 1935 with her leading role in the film 'Young Hearts'. Especially her appearance and her unpolished way of acting stood out.

origins.name: Rinus Michelslaan
origins.en: Marinus Jacobus Hendricus Michels (1928-2005), footballer and coach of Ajax. In 1971 he won the European Cup I with Ajax. Then achieved great success as coach of Barcelona and as national coach of the Dutch national team, during the World Cup in 1974 (second) and the European Championship in 1988 (first). Gained the nickname 'the General'. Founder of 'total football'.

origins.name: Riouwstraat
origins.en: The Riouw Archipelago, a group of islands in Indonesia near the east coast of Sumatra.

origins.name: Rita Reysbrug
origins.en: Maria Everdina Reys (1924-2013) is the most famous jazz singer in the Netherlands and perhaps in Europe, as evidenced by her nickname 'Europe's First Lady of Jazz'. She was married to Wessel Ilcken, who has a street name near this bridge. In the Park Haagseweg, all the streets are named after famous jazz musicians.

origins.name: Ritzema Bosstraat
origins.en: Jan Ritzema Bos (1850-1928), botanist, professor at Wageningen. Founder of plant pathology and of state supervision of it in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Robbert Cijferstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1919-1945), born in Amsterdam, executed at the Zijpersluis (North Holland).

origins.name: Robert Doumastraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

origins.name: Robert Fruinlaan
origins.en: Robert Jacobus Fruin (1823-1899), historian, professor at Leiden. Wrote a large number of historical studies, including 'Ten years from the Eighty Years' War'.

origins.name: Robert Kochplantsoen
origins.en: German bacteriologist (1843-1910), discoverer of the cholera bacterium (1883) and of the tuberculosis bacterium (1882). Won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1905. Part of the Robert Kochplantsoen was built on the former Meerlaan (council decision, 1923).

origins.name: Robert Scottstraat
origins.en: English South Pole traveler (1868-1912). Died during a second expedition, during which he reached the South Pole.

origins.name: Robijnstraat
origins.en: Hard, red gemstone. The municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel gave the street its name Tweede De when it was built.

origins.name: Rochussenstraat
origins.en: Jan Jacob Rochussen (1797-1871), statesman. successively Minister of Finance, Governor-General of Dutch East Indies and Minister of Colonies.

origins.name: Rocketstraat
origins.en: Name of the first English locomotive to run on a regular railway service.

origins.name: Rode Kruisstraat
origins.en: The street was thus named on the occasion of the centenary of the Dutch Rode Cross (founded in 1867). The adjacent streets are named after persons closely involved in this.

origins.name: Rodenrijsstraat
origins.en: Village north of Rotterdam.

origins.name: Roebelkade
origins.en: The currency of Russia.

origins.name: Roelantstraat
origins.en: Named after the Roelantslied. The epic from the thirteenth century that tells the story of Roelant, a knight of the Frankish prince Charlemagne. Before 1939, this street was part of the De Rijpstraat.

origins.name: Roelof Hartplein
origins.en: Amsterdam physician and philanthropist (1837-1892).

origins.name: Roelof Hartstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam physician and philanthropist (1837-1892).

origins.name: Roemer
origins.en: Named after a ditch between the Twiske and De Gouw. Disappeared due to the construction of the Twiske.

origins.name: Roemer Visscherstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam merchant and poet (1547-1620). Host for the artists Vondel, Hooft, Huygens and Brederode in his home on the Geldersekade.

origins.name: Roepie Kruizestraat
origins.en: Jan Hendrik Kruize (1925-1992), hockey player. Won bronze with his team at the 1948 Olympic Games in London and four years later in Helsinki silver.

origins.name: Roerdomppad
origins.en: Name of the underlying path.

origins.name: Roerstraat
origins.en: River that springs in the Eifel and flows into the Maas near Roermond.

origins.name: Roeselarestraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

origins.name: Roesiel
origins.en: Corrupted spelling of the French port city of La Rochelle, which appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Roetersstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Roeters (1617-1699), alderman of the city and owner of the land of the Roeterseiland named after him. The street was laid out on the Roetersburgwal, which was reclaimed in 1873.

origins.name: Roffart
origins.en: A seventeenth-century outdoor space with a gate from 1629 in Baarlo (Limburg).

origins.name: Roggeveenstraat
origins.en: Jacob Roggeveen (1659-1729), sailor, who made a trip to the East Indies around South America in 1721/1723. He discovered on that trip, on Easter 1722, the island that has since been called Easter Island.

origins.name: Rokin
origins.en: We must discard the long-standing theory that this name is a derivation from Rak-in (a rak within the Dam, such as the Damrak outside the Dam). This part of the Amstel, now partially filled in for 2/3 of its length, originally had no embankments. The buildings on Kalverstraat ran right down to the water. When in the sixteenth century the facade along the water of the first part was set back from the Dam (it had to 'ruck in'), a quay was built here, which was designated as Ruck-in in 1559. A few years later this became the Rock-in. With later extension, the entire quay was given this name.

origins.name: Rollemanstraat
origins.en: The street name refers to the caravan park on site. Rolleman is slang for caravan resident.

origins.name: Rombout Hogerbeetsstraat
origins.en: Pensioner of Leiden (1561-1626), supporter of Hugo de Groot. Imprisoned in 1619, but released in 1625 after the death of Prince Maurice. The name of the street had previously been established as Eerste Hugo de Grootdwarsstraat (council decision, 1897).

origins.name: Romeinsarmsteeg
origins.en: Named after an old signboard on which a hand with a sword could be seen. On the arm you could recognize a sleeve of Roman clothing. Such a signboard could also be seen on a house on the Vijgendam until 1847. Before the seventeenth century, this was the Nieuwe Kruissteeg.

origins.name: Romerostraat
origins.en: Oscar Arnulfo Romero (1917-1980), archbishop of San Salvador, capital of El Salvador. Spoke for the voice of the opposition. On March 24, 1980, he was murdered on the steps in front of the cathedral by right-wing paramilitary forces.

origins.name: Rondeel
origins.en: A semicircular, usually stone, bastion that was part of the city wall at the beginning of the sixteenth century. A rondeau is lower and made of heavier masonry than the older wall towers. Due to its meaning and due to the first syllable of the word, the name refers to the round shape of the new building.

origins.name: Röntgenstraat
origins.en: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen (1845-1923), German physicist. Discovered x-rays (X-rays) in 1895, applied in medicine for making photographs of internal body parts. He won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901. The municipality of Watergraafsmeer named the street during its construction Wilhelminastraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1904).

origins.name: Roomolenstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a facade stone. In the seventeenth century the street was called Molensteeg, later Roomolensteeg and in 1884 it was changed by the municipal council to Roomolenstraat. Perhaps the alley led to a (red) mill, which stood here outside the fortress before 1600.

origins.name: Roompotstraat
origins.en: Tidal channel in the mouth of the Oosterschelde, along the coast of Walcheren.

origins.name: Roomtuintjes
origins.en: Old roadside inn, formerly located on the Mauritskade, where Pieter Vlamingstraat now begins. Demolished between 1880 and 1884 for the construction of the Dapperbuurt.

origins.name: Rooseveltlaan
origins.en: Franklin Delano Roosevelt (1882-1945), president of the United States from 1932. Comes from a Dutch family that emigrated to America in 1649. He played a major role in the Allied victory in World War II, partly because he strongly opposed American neutrality. When the street was built, it was named Zuider Amstellaan (council decision, 1922).

origins.name: Roosje Vospad
origins.en: Socialist trade union leader and politician (1860-1932, married to M. Stel), fighter for universal suffrage. One of the first women to try to integrate her feminist views into a socialist position.

origins.name: Roosje Vosstraat
origins.en: Socialist trade union leader and politician (1860-1932, married to M. Stel), fighter for universal suffrage. One of the first women to try to integrate her feminist views into a socialist position.

origins.name: Rooswijck
origins.en: Eighteenth-century country house with later added towers, located between Santpoort and Velsen (North Holland).

origins.name: Rosa Luxemburgstraat
origins.en: German politician (1870-1919), representative of the radical-Marxist movement in the social democracy. During World War I imprisoned for anti-war agitation. In 1918 she was one of the leaders of the communist Spartacus League, which was soon transformed into the Communist Party of Germany. Killed by officers.

origins.name: Rosa Manusstraat
origins.en: Rosette Suzanne (Rosa) Manus (1881-1943), feminist and pacifist. She was the driving force behind the congresses of the League of Women for the Equal Suffrage Movement and devoted much of her work to the Peace Movement, also internationally. In 1941 she was arrested by the occupiers and in 1943 she died in the Ravensbrück concentration camp.

origins.name: Rosa Overbeekbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after Rosa Overbeek, a fictional character from the work of Theo Thijssen (1879-1943). She is the girlfriend of Kees the boy, who named bridge 123 after her.

origins.name: Roseboom
origins.en: Also known as 'The White rose tree'. Whale hunter, who sailed from Oostzanerwerf around 1726. The ship is named after its owner, shipowner Cornelis Roos (1691-1757).

origins.name: Rosendaalstraat
origins.en: Seventeenth-century inn on the Ringdijk (between Schagerlaan and Pauwenlaan), demolished around 1809.

origins.name: Rosmarijnsteeg
origins.en: Rosmarijn or rozemarijn (rosemary) is an evergreen, fragrant shrub. The alley was originally called Raamsteeg, but is already mentioned under the current name in 1616. This name is probably derived from a facade stone of one of the corner houses, on which a rosemary was depicted. An old note has been found in which there is talk of the decorators, who lived here and who made flowers and other decorations for baptism and wedding parties, which may have been the reason for the facade stone and for the naming of the alley.

origins.name: Rossinistraat
origins.en: Gioacchino Rossini (1792-1868), Italian opera composer.

origins.name: Rostockbrug
origins.en: Rostock is a port city in northeastern Germany. The names in the Houthavens are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Rosy Wertheimstraat
origins.en: Composer (1888-1949). Her compositions show the influence of Strawinsky and Debussy, among others.

origins.name: Rotterdammerbrug
origins.en: Named after the city of Rotterdam

origins.name: Rousseaustraat
origins.en: Jean Jacques Rousseau (1711-1778), French philosopher of the Enlightenment. One of the pioneers of the French Revolution, writer on education and composer.

origins.name: Rozenburglaan
origins.en: Country house between Kruislaan and Betondorp, built in 1642 and demolished in 1914 for the expansion of the Nieuwe Oosterbegraafplaats. The outside was originally called 'Het Vischkaantje', but was later called 'Rozenburg' after one of the owners David Rutgers van Rozenburg.

origins.name: Rozengracht
origins.en: The flower. The Rozengracht was filled in in 1895.

origins.name: Rozenoordpad
origins.en: Former nursery on the Amstel, located between Zorgvlied and the Kalfje. Also the location of the boat connection between Ouderkerk and Amsterdam.

origins.name: Rozenstraat
origins.en: The flower. The Rozengracht was filled in in 1895.

origins.name: Rozijnenstraat
origins.en: The fruits, dried grapes, from southern Europe, Central Asia, California and Australia.

origins.name: Rubensstraat
origins.en: Petrus Paulus Rubens (1577-1640), South Dutch painter of biblical scenes and historical paintings. Known for his lush female figures. He was the teacher of Anthonie van Dijck.

origins.name: Rudi Bloemgartensingel
origins.en: Jewish resistance fighter (1920-1943), one of the nine people involved in the attack on the Amsterdam Population Register on March 27, 1943. Also involved in the attack on the railway at Sloterdijk and in the establishment of the inciting magazine 'Rattenkruid'.

origins.name: Rudi van Dantzigstraat
origins.en: Rudi van Dantzig was a Dutch choreographer, ballet dancer and writer. He was artistic director of Het Nationale Ballet for twenty years.

origins.name: Rudolf Agricolastraat
origins.en: Philosopher (1443-1485), his real name was Roelof Huisman. From the province of Groningen. Renowned humanist, professor in Heidelberg.

origins.name: Rudolf Dieselstraat
origins.en: German engineer (1858-1913), inventor of the diesel engine named after him.

origins.name: Rudolf Nurejevstraat
origins.en: Rudolf Nureyev was a Russian-Austrian ballet dancer and choreographer.

origins.name: Ruigoord
origins.en: Former island in the IJ, after the reclamation a rise in the Houtrakpolder, on which the village of the same name was established. (Nowadays largely demolished.)

origins.name: Ruijgoordweg
origins.en: Former island in the IJ, after the reclamation a rise in the Houtrakpolder, on which the village of the same name was established. (Nowadays largely demolished.)

origins.name: Ruimzicht
origins.en: A former farm on the Uitweg, demolished to build the garden city of Osdorp.

origins.name: Ruisbeekhof
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Ruiseveenpad
origins.en: Named after a hamlet near Veenendaal (Utrecht).

origins.name: Ruisrietstraat
origins.en: Reed species, grows along water edges.

origins.name: Rumbeke
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

origins.name: Rumphiusstraat
origins.en: Georgius Everhardus Rumphius (1627-1702), born in Germany. In 1652 he embarked on a ship of the VOC. From 1662 he began systematically researching the flora and fauna on the Indonesian island of Ambon.

origins.name: Runstraat
origins.en: Fine ground oak bark, used for tanning leather.

origins.name: Rupelmonde
origins.en: One of the first country houses built by the Amsterdam patricians in the seventeenth century in Loenen aan de Vecht. It is still built in the style of an Amsterdam canal house.

origins.name: Rusland
origins.en: The oldest spelling, as it appears in a deed from 1403, is 'Willem Ruusschentuin'. The name was then shortened through ''t Ruyssenlandt', ''t Russeland' and ''t Ruslant' to the now incomprehensible Rusland. The street is so wide because the left part was a small canal (the Raamsloot), which was dug in 1537, but was still filled in in the same century.

origins.name: Rustenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out in 1878 on the Rustenburgerpad, which recalls the former Rustenburg country house from 1620.

origins.name: Rustenburgerstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out in 1878 on the Rustenburgerpad, which recalls the former Rustenburg country house from 1620.

origins.name: Rusthofstraat
origins.en: Former manor house on the Weesperzijde, near the Fahrenheitsingel, originally called Voorzigt, changed to Rusthof in 1807 and demolished around 1820.

origins.name: Rutherfordstraat
origins.en: Ernest Rutherford (1871-1937), English physicist and chemist. Gained fame in the field of radioactivity. Received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1908.

origins.name: Ruys de Beerenbrouckstraat
origins.en: Jonkheer Charles Joseph Marie Ruys de Beerenbrouck (1873-1936), Roman Catholic statesman. Minister of Justice and several times prime minister with the portfolio of Internal Affairs.

origins.name: Ruyschstraat
origins.en: Frederik Ruysch (1638-1731), professor in Amsterdam. Famous anatomist, surgeon and botanist. The street was previously called Derde Boerhaavestraat (council decision, 1882).

origins.name: Ruysdaelkade
origins.en: Seventeenth-century family of painters and engravers, of whom the most famous is Jacob Isaak Ruysdael (1628-1682), landscape painter. He was the teacher of Hobbema. The street already appears under this name in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1888.

origins.name: Ruysdaelstraat
origins.en: Seventeenth-century family of painters and engravers, of whom the most famous is Jacob Isaak Ruysdael (1628-1682), landscape painter. He was the teacher of Hobbema. The street already appears under this name in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1888.

origins.name: S. F. van Ossstraat
origins.en: S.F. van Oss (1868-1949), journalist, founder (1913) and editor-in-chief of the weekly magazine 'De Haagse Post'. Wrote weekly under the pseudonym Mr. Goeree d'Overflacque his humorous-satirical reflections.

origins.name: Saaftingestraat
origins.en: Region in the northeast of Zeelandic Flanders, in 1583 flooded for strategic reasons (the defense of Antwerp) and later not reclaimed.

origins.name: Saenredamstraat
origins.en: Pieter Jan Saenredam (1597-1665), painter. Painted among other things 'Face in the Sint Bavokerk' and 'The old town hall on the Dam'.

origins.name: Saffierstraat
origins.en: Hard blue gemstone.

origins.name: Sagittahof
origins.en: Constellation in the northern sky.

origins.name: Sallandstraat
origins.en: One of the three quarters of Overijssel, located between Gramsbergen and Deventer. The other quarters are Twente and Vollenhove.

origins.name: Saltetstraat
origins.en: Rudolph Hendrik Saltet (1853-1927), hygienist, professor in Amsterdam. Performed important work for public health.

origins.name: Salzmannhof
origins.en: Christiaan G. Salzmann (1744-1811), German pedagogue from the time of the Enlightenment.

origins.name: Sam de Wolffstraat
origins.en: Salomon de Wolff (1878-1960), economist and politician of Jewish descent. From 1909 to 1913 member of the Provincial States of North Holland, from 1930 to 1940 private lecturer at the University of Amsterdam. In 1943 he was arrested and deported to the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, from which he was allowed to go to Palestine (Israel).

origins.name: Sam van Houtenstraat
origins.en: Samuel van Houten (1837-1930), politician, initially liberal, later conservative. Minister of the Interior from 1894 to 1897. As a member of parliament, he submitted a proposal for the Children's Labor Act, the first social law, known as Van Houten's Children's Law (1874).

origins.name: Samosstraat
origins.en: Greek island in the east of the Aegean Sea.

origins.name: Sandenburch
origins.en: Former castle near Veere, built in the thirteenth or fourteenth century by a member of the old knightly family Van Sande. Inhabited for many years by the lords of Borssele. (Not to be confused with the still existing Sandenburg on the Langbroekerwetering.)

origins.name: Sanderijnstraat
origins.en: One of the main characters of the abel spel (secular play) 'Lanseloet van Denemerken' ('Lanseloet ende Sanderijn', from about 1400).

origins.name: Sandhorst
origins.en: Lost medieval castle in Wassenaar. Destroyed in 1818 after repeated renovations.

origins.name: Sandinostraat
origins.en: Augusto Sandino (1895-1934), resistance leader in Nicaragua. Fought from 1926 to 1934 with his guerrilla group in the mountains of Nicaragua against the American troops and the presidents held in their thrall by them. Arrested and murdered by the National Guard.

origins.name: Sandwijk
origins.en: Name of a country house with a large garden on the Oosterweg in the Purmer. Nowadays, there is a farm located there, called Abcoude.

origins.name: Sanne Sanneshof
origins.en: Photographer (1937-1967). His central theme is 'the woman'. He was looking for a new language of images and found it in the combination of photo and film. When he died in an accident at the age of thirty, he was a leading photographer in the Netherlands and was about to break through internationally.

origins.name: Santoriniweg
origins.en: Greek island in the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Sape Kuiperplantsoen
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1924-1943), born in Arnhem, executed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Sara Burgerhartstraat
origins.en: Named after the main character from the novella 'History of Miss Sara Burgerhart' from 1872.

origins.name: Sarah Vaughanstraat
origins.en: Sarah Lois Vaughan (1924-1990). Considered one of the most important American jazz singers in history. Known for her wide vocal range, expressive voice and strong vibrato.

origins.name: Sardiniëweg
origins.en: The Italian island in the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Sarphatikade
origins.en: Samuel Sarphati (1813-1866), Amsterdam doctor and pharmacist with many contacts in banking circles. Did much for the city. He made plans for the expansion of the city around Frederiksplein and outside the Singelgracht, among other things, for which he founded the Nederlandsche Bouwmaatschappij in 1864. Among the associations and buildings that came into being thanks to his efforts, we can mention: the Society for Agriculture (1848), the Association for Popular Industry (1852) with the Paleis voor Volksvlijt built by it (1864), the Trade School, the National Mortgage Bank, the Amstel Hotel (1866).

origins.name: Sarphatipark
origins.en: Samuel Sarphati (1813-1866), Amsterdam doctor and pharmacist with many connections in banking circles, who did much for the city. Among other things he drew up plans to expand the city around the Frederiksplein and beyond the Singelgracht, and founded the Nederlandsche Bouwmaatschappij for this in 1864. Societies and buildings that came about through him include the Maatschappij voor Landbouw (1848), the Vereeniging voor Volksvlijt (1852) with its Paleis voor Volksvlijt (1864), the Handelsschool, the Nationale Hypotheekbank and the Amstel Hotel (1866).

origins.name: Sarphatistraat
origins.en: Samuel Sarphati (1813-1866), Amsterdam doctor and pharmacist with many connections in banking circles, who did much for the city. Among other things he drew up plans to expand the city around the Frederiksplein and beyond the Singelgracht, and founded the Nederlandsche Bouwmaatschappij for this in 1864. Societies and buildings that came about through him include the Maatschappij voor Landbouw (1848), the Vereeniging voor Volksvlijt (1852) with its Paleis voor Volksvlijt (1864), the Handelsschool, the Nationale Hypotheekbank and the Amstel Hotel (1866).

origins.name: Saskia van Uijlenburgkade
origins.en: Wife of Rembrandt van Rijn (1612-1642). She probably knew Rembrandt through her uncle Hendrick, who was an art dealer. In 1634 the couple got married, in 1641 son Titus was born. Buried in the Old Church.

origins.name: Sassenheimstraat
origins.en: The South Holland village between Lisse and Warmond.

origins.name: Saturnusstraat
origins.en: The planet, one of the largest in our solar system.

origins.name: Sausalitolaan
origins.en: City on the Bay of San Francisco, where the pedestrian promenade is being renovated in the second decade of the twenty-first century.

origins.name: Savelsbos
origins.en: Nature reserve near Gronsveld (South Limburg), total 174 ha: a slope forest with a rare animal and plant world and a prehistoric flint workshop.

origins.name: Saxen-Weimarlaan
origins.en: The German royal family, related by marriage to the Dutch royal family Orange-Nassau.

origins.name: Saxenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: Former country house, later pottery factory, which stood here until 1879. The street has been passed down under this name from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Saxenburgerstraat
origins.en: Former country house, later pottery factory, which stood here until 1879. The street has been passed down under this name from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Scannerstraat
origins.en: Device with which a computer can read and store text and images. As a counterpart to the street names that remind of the former shipbuilding industry in Amsterdam-North, this naming refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Schaafstraat
origins.en: Woodworking tools.

origins.name: Schaarbeekstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Schaarsbergenstraat
origins.en: Village on the edge of the National Park De Hoge Veluwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Schaepmanstraat
origins.en: Herman Johan A.M. Schaepman (1844-1903), Roman Catholic priest, statesman and poet, professor at the Rijsenburg Seminary. From 1880 to 1903 member of parliament (advocate for expansion of suffrage and social legislation). Editor of the daily newspaper 'De Tijd', later of 'Het Centrum'. As a poet a follower of Bilderdijk and Da Costa.

origins.name: Schagerlaan
origins.en: Robert van Schager, resident of the manor house 't Roode Hart, the only manor house on this lane that survived the flood of 1651.

origins.name: Schaikstraat
origins.en: Village, south of Ravenstein (North Brabant).

origins.name: Schakelstraat
origins.en: The connection, in this case of electrical current.

origins.name: Schalk Burgerstraat
origins.en: Willem Schalk Burger (1852-1918), one of the folk leaders of the young Republic of South Africa. Boer general in the Second Boer War (1899-1902). After Paul Kruger left for Europe, he was acting president of Transvaal.

origins.name: Schalkwijkpad
origins.en: Village in the province of Utrecht, on the Utrecht-Culemborg railway line.

origins.name: Schapensteeg
origins.en: Named after the former landowner Jacob Schaap. The alleyway appears under the name Jacob Schapensteeg from the oldest mention (from 1595). Only in the course of the seventeenth century does the name appear only as Schapensteeg.

origins.name: Scharenburg
origins.en: The port city of Scarborough on the English east coast, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Scharenslijperspad
origins.en: Basket-making was originally a typical travelling trade. The name is linked to the world of travelling people and refers to the caravan site here.

origins.name: Scharrebiersluis
origins.en: Scharrebier was traditionally the drink for ordinary workers. This 'thin' beer type was formerly sold on this collection bridge, because there was often a lot of working people present there

origins.name: Scharwouderstraat
origins.en: This 'thin' beer type was formerly sold on this pick-up bridge, because there was often a lot of working people present there.

origins.name: Scheepmakerskade
origins.en: An unofficial name for this bridge is Rapenburgerschutsluis. The origin of the name Rapenburg is shrouded in mystery.

origins.name: Scheepsbouwkade
origins.en: Reference to the NSM and later NDSM shipyard on the north side of the IJ, where ships were built between 1922 and 1978. Also see: NDSM Square.

origins.name: Scheepsbouwweg
origins.en: The name recalls the shipyard, and in particular the new construction shipyard, where many ships were built until the 1970s of this century.

origins.name: Scheepstimmermanstraat
origins.en: Occupational name for shipbuilding.

origins.name: Scheldeplein
origins.en: River originating in France, which flows into our country past Antwerp and then discharges into the sea via the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Scheldestraat
origins.en: River originating in France, which flows into our country past Antwerp and then discharges into the sea via the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Schellingwouderdijk
origins.en: Village. The dike is part of the Waterland sea dike.

origins.name: Schelluinenstraat
origins.en: The village northwest of Gorinchem (South Holland).

origins.name: Schelvisch Hoofd
origins.en: Named after the place where the Noordhollandse tram station was located. Also the end point of the North-South Holland coffee shop-Central Station ferry.

origins.name: Schepenbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Meerssen (Limburg).

origins.name: Schepenlaan
origins.en: The streets in this district are named after ship types and ship parts.

origins.name: Schermerstraat
origins.en: Between 1631 and 1635 more were drained in North Holland.

origins.name: Scherpenzeelstraat
origins.en: Village in the Gelderse Valley (Gelderland).

origins.name: Schielandplein
origins.en: Place in South Holland

origins.name: Schiemanstraat
origins.en: Occupational name at sea: the petty officer on board responsible for supervising the rigging for the mast.

origins.name: Schiermonnikoogstraat
origins.en: Wadden island (Friesland).

origins.name: Schierstins
origins.en: Fourteenth-century defensible tower-shaped building, located in Veenwouden (Friesland) and restored in 1962. The building was already in the possession of the grey (schiere) monks of the abbey of Klaarkamp before 1439.

origins.name: Schillingdijk
origins.en: The currency of Austria.

origins.name: Schimmelstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Jan Schimmel (1825-1906), bank director, known as a novelist and playwright and also editor of 'De Gids'. These streets came into Amsterdam in 1896 with the names set by Nieuwer-Amstel, Van Speyckstraat and Van Speyckdwarsstraat, but were renamed in 1922, after the annexation of Sloten brought a second Van Speyckstraat within the city boundary.

origins.name: Schinkelhavenkade
origins.en: The name recalls the old roadside inn Schinkelhaven. Before 1922 the street was part of the Schinkelkade.

origins.name: Schinkelhavenstraat
origins.en: The name recalls the old roadside inn Schinkelhaven. Before 1922 the street was part of the Schinkelkade.

origins.name: Schinkelkade
origins.en: A schinkel is a short connecting stretch between two weteringen (drainage channels), in this case the Nieuwe Meer and the Overtoom. It is thought the connection owes its name to its shape: 'schinkel' is a synonym of 'schenkel', the lower leg between foot and knee. The quay was earlier called Visserkade by Nieuwer-Amstel. The municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel had named the streets Visserstraat, Alexanderstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 20 October 1882) and Willemsparkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 30 January 1883), but in 1896 they were changed because of confusion with names that already existed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Schipbeekstraat
origins.en: Built in the fifteenth century and extended in later centuries, shipping canal on the border of Gelderland and Overijssel. Flows into the IJssel near Deventer.

origins.name: Schipluidenlaan
origins.en: Village in the Westland, south of Delft.

origins.name: Schippersgracht
origins.en: In this neighborhood, on the harbor side, the shipowners and sailors made up the majority of the population, which is why the canal and street got this name.

origins.name: Schippersstraat
origins.en: In this neighborhood, on the harbor side, the shipowners and sailors made up the majority of the population, which is why the canal and street got this name

origins.name: Schoenerstraat
origins.en: Small merchant ship with sharp bow and with two or more masts.

origins.name: Schoffelstraat
origins.en: Named after the hoe, a gardening tool.

origins.name: Schokkerjachtdijk
origins.en: Ship, a fishing vessel related to the botter. The name probably comes from the island of Schokland. Schokkers were known for their enormous seaworthiness.

origins.name: Schokkerspad
origins.en: Small fishing boat, originally from the Netherlands.

origins.name: Schoklandstraat
origins.en: Former island in the Zuiderzee, now incorporated into the Noordoostpolder.

origins.name: Schollenbrugpad
origins.en: Named after the roadside inn that used to stand here, and which took its name from the old Schollenbrug in the Weesperzijde, which connected the Watergraafsmeer to the city. That bridge was previously called Schulpbrug, after the seventeenth-century inn the Schulp. This was on the other side of the bridge, so in the Watergraafsmeer (with a shell or shell in the facade).

origins.name: Schollenbrugstraat
origins.en: Named after the roadside inn that used to stand here, and which took its name from the old Schollenbrug in the Weesperzijde, which connected the Watergraafsmeer to the city. That bridge was previously called Schulpbrug, after the seventeenth-century inn the Schulp. This was on the other side of the bridge, so in the Watergraafsmeer (with a shell or shell in the facade).

origins.name: Schonerwoerdstraat
origins.en: Village in the so-called Five Brothers Countries (South Holland).

origins.name: Schoolmeesterstraat
origins.en: Named after the pseudonym 'De Schoolmeester' of the Dutch poet Gerrit van de Linde (1808-1858).

origins.name: Schoolstraat
origins.en: Named after the old municipal school of Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Schooltuinpad
origins.en: Refers to the nearby school garden complex.

origins.name: Schoonboomstraat
origins.en: Former church village on Zuid-Beveland, drowned by a storm surge in 1532.

origins.name: Schoonhovendreef
origins.en: City on the Lek, on the border of Utrecht and South Holland.

origins.name: Schoorlstraat
origins.en: Village at the foot of the dunes, north of Alkmaar.

origins.name: Schopenhauerhof
origins.en: Arthur Schopenhauer (1778-1860), German philosopher. Denied the existence of a causal free will.

origins.name: Schorpioenstraat
origins.en: Constellation, sign of the Zodiac.

origins.name: Schotse Hooglanden
origins.en: The mountain, located in Scotland.

origins.name: Schotse Huizenpad
origins.en: The mountain, located in Scotland.

origins.name: Schoutensteeg
origins.en: Named after a former resident, Jan Arentsz Schouten. In the fifteenth century, the alley was therefore fully called Jan Arentszn Schoutensteeg. He was the schout (sheriff) of Amsterdam from 1426 to 1430. Before that time, the name Willem Noirtsteeg was also used.

origins.name: Schouwstraat
origins.en: ''t Schouw' is a hamlet on the Noordhollandsch Kanaal, on the northern municipal border of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Schovenstraat
origins.en: Sheaves: corn stalks bound together.

origins.name: Schubertstraat
origins.en: Franz Schubert (1797-1828), Austrian composer. Wrote symphonies, chamber music and songs, including: 'Die Forelle', 'Erlkönig' and the cycle 'Die Winterreise'.

origins.name: Schuitenhuisstraat
origins.en: In general, a shooting house is a boat shelter (now boat house). The name appears on a historical map from 1659 (by Stevijn and Van Broeckhuysen) in the vicinity of the inn 'De drie Baarsjes'.

origins.name: Schurenbergweg
origins.en: A hill near Hoensbroek (Limburg).

origins.name: Schutterweg
origins.en: The zodiac sign Sagittarius or Sagittarius in the Zodiac.

origins.name: Schweigmannstraat
origins.en: Antonius Petrus Paulus Schweigmann (1893-1945), resistance fighter, born in Leeuwarden, killed in Sandbostel (Germany).

origins.name: Science Park
origins.en: Campus for international knowledge institutes in the field of ICT, exact sciences and scientific research.

origins.name: Sean MacBridestraat
origins.en: Irish politician (1904-1988). After World War II, he was Minister of Foreign Affairs and actively involved in the creation of the Geneva Conventions and the European Convention for Human Rights. In 1961, he was one of the founders of Amnesty International. He received both the Soviet Peace Prize and the Nobel Peace Prize.

origins.name: Seifertplein
origins.en: Jaroslav Seifert (1901-1986), Czech writer. After the Russian invasion, his strongly anti-fascist and patriotic work could only be distributed underground. In 1984 he received the Nobel Prize for Literature.

origins.name: Seineweg
origins.en: River in France.

origins.name: Seinwachterstraat
origins.en: Signalman, who operates the signals in a signal box along the railway track.

origins.name: Seizoenenhof
origins.en: The name fits the adjacent district with names of the four seasons.

origins.name: Semarangstraat
origins.en: City on the island of Java (Indonesia).

origins.name: Senecastraat
origins.en: Roman philosopher and poet (4 BC-65 AD). Teacher of Nero, who later forced him to commit suicide.

origins.name: Senefelderstraat
origins.en: Aloys Senefelder (1771-1834), Austrian typographer. Inventor of lithography.

origins.name: Seranggracht
origins.en: A river on the Indonesian island of Java.

origins.name: Serge Lifarsteeg
origins.en: Serge Lifar was a Russian-French dancer, choreographer, ballet director and author.

origins.name: Servaes Noutsstraat
origins.en: Michiel Servaes Nouts (1630-1693), the first bellringer of the Town Hall on the Dam.

origins.name: Servetsteeg
origins.en: This name already occurs here in the seventeenth century, but the original name Revet- or Ravetsteeg is also used until the eighteenth century. A Revet, Ravet or Rabat is a kaatsbaan (a court for the ball game kaatsen). This court was located at the corner of the alley and the city wall. It can therefore be assumed that Servet is a corruption of Revet.

origins.name: Sextantweg
origins.en: The navigation tool, an angle measuring instrument for determining position at sea using the stars.

origins.name: Shackletonstraat
origins.en: Sir Ernest Henry Shackleton (1874-1922), English South Pole researcher. Reached the magnetic South Pole in 1909.

origins.name: Sibogastraat
origins.en: Siboga or Sibolga is a city on the west coast of Sumatra (Indonesia).

origins.name: Sibrandus Stratinghstraat
origins.en: Inventor and chemist (1785-1841). Was a professor in Groningen, where he developed and tested motorized vehicles. In 1834, he made possible, as the first person in the Netherlands, a test drive with a steam carriage. Probably also built the first electromagnetic vehicle in the world.

origins.name: Siciliëweg
origins.en: An Italian island in the Mediterranean.

origins.name: Siebren van der Baanhof
origins.en: Resistance hero (1894-1944). Keeper of the Reformed Church on the Keizersgracht, where he hid weapons and other things of the resistance (illegaliteit). Upon discovery, by the occupiers in 1944, shot dead on the sidewalk in front of the building together with the pastor Ferwerda. Van der Baan was also active in the distribution of the illegal newspaper 'Trouw'.

origins.name: Sieg Vaz Diasstraat
origins.en: Journalist (1904-1943) and resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed on the Leusderheide.

origins.name: Sierenborch
origins.en: Corrupted spelling of the French port city of Cherbourg, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Sierplein
origins.en: Before houses were built on this square and the square was given an official name, the square was popularly called Sierplein due to the decorative paving.

origins.name: Sieverdinkpad
origins.en: Name of an old farm near Winterswijk.

origins.name: Sijlhoff
origins.en: Former castle in Leiderdorp, first built around 1292, destroyed in 1420, rebuilt during the Spanish period and finally demolished in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Sijpestein
origins.en: Castle, mentioned as early as 1288, that was destroyed and rebuilt several times. In 1911 the old foundations were exposed, after which the castle was rebuilt in its original style. It is located near Loosdrecht.

origins.name: Sijsjesbergweg
origins.en: Hill near Huizen (North Holland), north of the Table Mountain.

origins.name: Sijsjesstraat
origins.en: Songbird.

origins.name: Sikkelstraat
origins.en: Agricultural tools for cutting corn stalks.

origins.name: Silenestraat
origins.en: Plant, belonging to the pink (carnation) family, grows in dunes and along berms.

origins.name: Silodam
origins.en: The embankment in the IJ. Since the end of the nineteenth century, there has been a large grain silo here, which was later expanded with a second. Both silos are out of use and are being converted into houses.

origins.name: Silvoldestraat
origins.en: The Gelderland village on the Oude IJssel.

origins.name: Silvretta
origins.en: Mountain peak in Switzerland, 3411 meters high.

origins.name: Simon Carmiggeltstraat
origins.en: Simon Johannes Carmiggelt (1913-1987), writer and journalist, best known for his newspaper columns ('Kronkels'), which appeared under the pseudonym Kronkel in 'Het Parool'. In 1974 Carmiggelt received the P.C. Hooft Prize.

origins.name: Simon Stevinstraat
origins.en: Mathematician and engineer (1548-1620), head of Water Works and teacher of Prince Maurice. Inventor of the ten-part fractions and of the sailing cart. During the construction, the street was named Kerklaan by the Watergraafsmeer municipality (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1901).

origins.name: Simon van Gijnpad
origins.en: The Museum Mr. Simon van Gijn in Dordrecht. In 1925, the former 1729 residence of the banker and collector Simon van Gijn (1836-1922) was converted into a museum. In addition to the authentic interiors, the museum is known for its collection of national history prints and the collection of crafts and old toys.

origins.name: Simon van Woerdenstraat
origins.en: Simon van Woerden (1902-1998) designed the Bethel Church around 1958.

origins.name: Simone de Beauvoirstraat
origins.en: French writer (1908-1986), taught philosophy in Marseille, Rouen and Paris from 1931 to 1943. Her literary work is critical, sharp and imbued with her existentialist way of life.

origins.name: Simonshavenstraat
origins.en: Village on the South Holland island of Putten.

origins.name: Simonskerkestraat
origins.en: The village that drowned in 1484 on Schouwen-Duiveland (Zeeland).

origins.name: Simsonstraat
origins.en: The hero of the Israelites in the Old Testament (symbol of strength). Was stripped of his hair by his beloved Delilah, and therefore of his strength.

origins.name: Sinaasappelstraat
origins.en: Named after the orange, a citrus fruit.

origins.name: Sinderenstraat
origins.en: Hamlet near Varsseveld (Gelderland).

origins.name: Singel
origins.en: A singel is a waterway or a road along the outer edge of the city. In Amsterdam, the Singel (Amsterdammers say "het Singel") formed the city boundary in the second half of the fifteenth century, within which the walls with gates were built. At that time, that canal was called 't Singel or the Stedegracht (now Singel, Kloveniersburgwal and Geldersekade). The current Singel has retained the old name. However, in the seventeenth century, the city administration introduced the name Koningsgracht for it, but that name could not be maintained (see also Koningsplein).

origins.name: Singerstraat
origins.en: The Singer Museum in Laren. The American painter W.H. Singer Jr. (1868-1943) came to Laren around 1900 and had a villa built in 1911. In 1956, a new wing of the building was converted into a museum. The basis of the collection is the collection of the Singer couple: nineteenth and twentieth-century works by mainly Dutch and French artists.

origins.name: Sinjeur Semeynsstraat
origins.en: Named after the book 'Sinjeur Semeyns' by H.J. Schimmel

origins.name: Sint Agnietenstraat
origins.en: Here was formerly the Sint Augustinian Monastery, founded in 1397, destroyed in the great city fire in 1452 and rebuilt again. The still existing monastery church, the Sint Augustinian Chapel, dates from 1470 and housed the Athenaeum from 1632 to 1862.

origins.name: Sint Annendwarsstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a religious figurine, depicting Sint Anna.

origins.name: Sint Annenstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a religious figurine, depicting Sint Anna.

origins.name: Sint Antoniesbreestraat
origins.en: which in turn derives its name from the Sint Antoniesgasthuis or Leprosy House.

origins.name: Sint Antoniesluis
origins.en: Named after the Sint Antoniesdijk, the sea wall located outside the city until the seventeenth century, which in turn took its name from the Sint Antoniesgasthuis or Leprosy House. The Sint Antoniesluis was part of the Zwanenburgwal before 1976.

origins.name: Sint Jacobsdwarsstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a holy image, depicting the apostle James, who sat on the facade at one of the street corners. The Sint Jacob Chapel will not have been the namesake, as this chapel was located further north on the Nieuwendijk.

origins.name: Sint Jacobsstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a holy image, depicting the apostle James, who sat on the facade at one of the street corners. The Sint Jacob Chapel will not have been the namesake, as this chapel was located further north on the Nieuwendijk.

origins.name: Sint Jansstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a religious statue, depicting the apostle John, who sat on the facade at one of the street corners.

origins.name: Sint Jorisstraat
origins.en: Named after the Sint Joris guesthouse, which was located here, founded in the second half of the fourteenth century and demolished at the end of the sixteenth century for the expansion of the city.

origins.name: Sint Luciënsteeg
origins.en: The former Sint Lucian monastery that was moved to the complex of the Burgerweeshuis after 1578 (now Amsterdam Museum of History).

origins.name: Sint Nicolaasstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a small religious statue, which must have stood on the corner of the street on the facade.

origins.name: Sint Olofspoort
origins.en: The Sint Olofspoort was one of the oldest city gates and stood here from before 1380 to 1618. The gate got its name from the adjacent Sint Olofkapel, which still exists and is one of the oldest buildings preserved in Amsterdam. Foundation remains have been found from the gate. Sint Olofssteeg was called Oudezijds Wijde Kapelsteeg until 1914.

origins.name: Sint Olofssteeg
origins.en: The Sint Olofspoort was one of the oldest city gates and stood here from before 1380 to 1618. The gate got its name from the adjacent Sint Olof Chapel, which still exists and is one of the oldest buildings preserved in Amsterdam. Foundation remains have been found from the gate. The Sint Olofssteeg was called Oudezijds Wijde Kapelsteeg until 1914.

origins.name: Sint Pieterspoortsteeg
origins.en: The gate is a remnant of the Sint Pietersgasthuis, which already stood here in the second half of the fourteenth century. In 1578 the hospital was transferred to the Binnengasthuis and the buildings, with the exception of the gate, were demolished and rebuilt as a bank.

origins.name: Sint Willibrordusdwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the church of that name, dedicated to Sint Willibrordus, the Anglo-Saxon preacher and archbishop from the seventh century, who completely Christianized the Dutch area. The church was demolished in 1970 due to structural failure. The street and the cross street were taken over from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel in 1896 under the names Kerkstraat, Hoedemakerskade (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890 and 28-8-1891) and Eerste Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890).

origins.name: Sint Willibrordusstraat
origins.en: Named after the church of that name, dedicated to Sint Willibrordus, the Anglo-Saxon preacher and archbishop from the seventh century, who completely Christianized the Dutch area. The church was demolished in 1970 due to structural failure. The street and the cross street were taken over from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel in 1896 under the names Kerkstraat, Hoedemakerskade (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890 and 28-8-1891) and Eerste Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890).

origins.name: Sint-Hubertpad
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Luxembourg.

origins.name: Sint-Truidenstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Siriusstraat
origins.en: One of the largest and brightest stars in the constellation The Great Dog.

origins.name: Sixhavenweg
origins.en: Jonkheer Willem Six (1859-1919), from 1898 to 1919 chairman of the Royal Sailing and Rowing Association, a great promoter of the construction of the marina in Amsterdam North. Two months before the completion of the harbor, he died, after which the harbor was named after him.

origins.name: Sjai Agnonstraat
origins.en: Sjmoeël Joseef Agnon (1887-1970) was the first writer in Hebrew to win the Nobel Prize for Literature. He is known by the acronym Sjai as his first name.

origins.name: Skûtsjespad
origins.en: Traditional type of jolle. Sailing vessel for sea and river navigation with round bow, flat bottom and side sails.

origins.name: Slaakstraat
origins.en: Water between St. Philipsland and North Brabant, dammed in 1884.

origins.name: Slangenburg
origins.en: Fifteenth-century castle near Doetinchem, renovated in the seventeenth century under General Van Baer van Slangenburg.

origins.name: Slatuinenweg
origins.en: This is the remainder of the former Slatuinenpad, which ran from the Baarsjesweg to the Haarlemmerweg until 1927 and along willow groves (willow grove gardens). It was a popular walking path of the Amsterdamers.

origins.name: Slauerhoffstraat
origins.en: Jan Jacob Slauerhoff (1898-1936), doctor and poet. As a ship's doctor, he traveled around the world. His poetry therefore reveals a continuous restlessness.

origins.name: Sleewijkstraat
origins.en: The village of Sleeuwijk on the Merwede opposite Gorinchem (North Brabant).

origins.name: Slego
origins.en: The name is the Old Dutch rendering of the port town of Sligo, located on the northwest coast of Ireland.

origins.name: Sleutelbloemstraat
origins.en: Also known as primula. Plant that occurs in meadows and on old estates.

origins.name: Sleutelbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the seventeenth-century brewery 'De Sleutel' that belonged to Gerrit Bicker and which was located on the site of the current Binnengasthuisterrein.

origins.name: Slibveldenweg
origins.en: The road ends just after the Wijsentkade in a rectangular piece of land where the 'Slibvel- den' were built in the late 1950s. In popular parlance, the path is known as the "Slibveldenweg"

origins.name: Slichtenhorststraat
origins.en: Hamlet and estate near Nijkerk (Gelderland).

origins.name: Sliedrechtstraat
origins.en: Location on the Beneden-Merwede, formerly known for its dredging companies and shipyards.

origins.name: Slijkstraat
origins.en: Named after the soil conditions in the sixteenth century. In Amsterdam-Centrum, several street names indicate the former swampy ground (see Nes-Niezel). Only the main streets were raised at the time (Zandstraat-Dijkstraat).

origins.name: Slijperweg
origins.en: Metalworker, who smooths the surface of metal objects.

origins.name: Slikkerveerstraat
origins.en: Village on IJsselmonde, at the confluence of Lek and Noord.

origins.name: Slimmeweg
origins.en: This is the former name of the Osdorperweg, as found on old maps of this area.

origins.name: Slingerbeekstraat
origins.en: River in the Gelderse Achterhoek. Flows into the Oude IJssel near Doetinchem.

origins.name: Slochterweg
origins.en: The original name of the section located here of the North Holland Canal, which connected the Buiksloter Meer with the Broeker Meer. Before this naming, the road formed parts of the Canal Dyke (until 1966 Landsmeer) and the Leeuwarderweg.

origins.name: Sloestraat
origins.en: Former tidal current between Walcheren and Zuid-Beveland, now completely reclaimed.

origins.name: Slootdorpstraat
origins.en: The village in the Wieringermeerpolder.

origins.name: Slootstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out in 1660 on a filled in ditch near the Former City Timberyard.

origins.name: Sloterdijkerbrug
origins.en: The old dike village, of which only the church and a small part remain today. It belonged to the municipality of Sloten, which was annexed to Amsterdam in 1921. The village was originally called Sloterdam and had a harbor and a lock in earlier centuries.

origins.name: Sloterdijkerweg
origins.en: The old dike village, of which only the church and a small part remain today. It belonged to the municipality of Sloten, which was annexed to Amsterdam in 1921. The village was originally called Sloterdam and had a harbor and a lock in earlier centuries.

origins.name: Sloterdijkstraat
origins.en: Opinions differ on the naming of this street. According to some, a house called Sloterdijk at the corner of the street is the namesake, others look for a direct connection with the village of Sloterdijk on which one had the view through the street.

origins.name: Sloterkade
origins.en: Named after the village of Sloten, which was the main village of the municipality of Sloten until 1-1-1921, to which also the village of Sloterdijk and the hamlet of Osdorp belonged. The municipality extended from the Haarlemmermeer to the North Sea Canal and from the Schinkel to Halfweg.

origins.name: Slotermeerlaan
origins.en: The name is derived from Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk, which, after being drained more than once, was dug out again into a lake for sand extraction. This water is the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Sloterweg
origins.en: Named after the village of Sloten, which until 1-1-1921 was the main village of the municipality of Sloten, to which also the village of Sloterdijk and the hamlet of Osdorp belonged. The municipality extended from the Haarlemmermeer to the North Sea Canal and from the Schinkel to Halfweg. The Sloterweg originally ran to (or began at) the Schinkel. Due to the construction of the ring road, a part has disappeared and deteriorated (see also Rijnsburgstraat).

origins.name: Slufter
origins.en: Nature monument on the island of Texel. In the Slufter are some creeks, which are still in open connection with the sea. Breeding ground for seabirds and spoonbills.

origins.name: Sluispad
origins.en: The path runs along the sluice located here in the Gaasp.

origins.name: Sluisstraat
origins.en: Artificial dam. By opening and closing doors, the connection between two waters is regulated.

origins.name: Smaksteeg
origins.en: The name already appears in the sixteenth century and originates from a facade stone of a corner house. On it stood a taste, a kind of ship.

origins.name: Smalschipstraat
origins.en: Ship, flat-bottomed of Frisian origin with leeboards and a gaff-rigged mast. Very suitable for shallow waters. The narrow ship was used to load goods and unload larger ships.

origins.name: Smaragdplein
origins.en: These and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (ADM). As a reminder of that former purpose, the names of the various workshops were used for the naming, in this case the forge of the shipyard.

origins.name: Smaragdstraat
origins.en: Gemstone with grass green color.

origins.name: Smederij
origins.en: These and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (ADM). As a reminder of that former purpose, the names of the various workshops were used for the naming, in this case the forge of the shipyard.

origins.name: Smederij Meisterbrug
origins.en: Family business in the Bellamy neighborhood, founded in 1909.

origins.name: Smitstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas Jacobus Smit, general in the First Boer War of Independence (1880-1881) of the Transvaal Boers, where he defeated the English at Ingogo. In 1883 negotiator for the Boers in London.

origins.name: Sneeuwbalstraat
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Sneeuwbalweg
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Snellerwaardgracht
origins.en: Village on the Hollandse IJssel (Utrecht). The original spelling is Snelrewaard.

origins.name: Snelleveldplein
origins.en: Hamlet on the Waal near Waardenburg (Gelderland).

origins.name: Snelleveldstraat
origins.en: Hamlet on the Waal near Waardenburg (Gelderland).

origins.name: Snelliusstraat
origins.en: Willebrord Snellius (1580-1626), mathematician and physicist. Leiden professor, founded the first European observatory.

origins.name: Snijdersbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Geulle (Limburg).

origins.name: Snodenhoekpark
origins.en: Hamlet near EIst in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Snoekjesbrug
origins.en: After a resident from the sixteenth century, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a pike depicted on the facade of his house. Originally, the name was therefore Snoeksgracht/steeg.

origins.name: Snoekjesgracht
origins.en: After a resident from the sixteenth century, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a pike depicted on the facade of his house. Originally, the name was therefore Snoeksgracht/steeg.

origins.name: Snoekjessteeg
origins.en: After a resident from the sixteenth century, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a pike depicted on the facade of his house. Originally, the name was therefore Snoeksgracht/steeg.

origins.name: Snorrenhoefstraat
origins.en: Hamlet near Leusden (Utrecht).

origins.name: Socratesstraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher (469-399 BC), teacher of Plato. Was condemned as a freethinker to drink the cup of poison.

origins.name: Soembawastraat
origins.en: One of the Lesser Sunda Islands (Indonesia).

origins.name: Soendastraat
origins.en: Island group to which the main islands of Indonesia belong, divided into the Greater and Lesser Sundas. The Greater include Java, Sumatra, Kalimantan (Borneo) and Sulawesi (Celebes). The Lesser include Bali and the other series of islands east of Java. The Sundas are located in West Java.

origins.name: Soerabajastraat
origins.en: Port city on East Java (Indonesia).

origins.name: Soestdijkstraat
origins.en: Village, falls under the municipality of Soest. The royal palace Soestdijk is located in the municipality of Baarn.

origins.name: Soesterberghof
origins.en: Village, falls under the municipality of Soest. Especially known for the nearby military airfield.

origins.name: Soetendaal
origins.en: Former country house near Maarssen on the Vecht.

origins.name: Soewardistraat
origins.en: Soewardi Soerjaningrat (Jakarta 1889 - Jakarta 1959), later called himself Ki Hadjar Dewantoro. He was closely involved in the action of the multiracial Indische Partij (Indies Party) that sought an independent India. For this reason, he was exiled to the Netherlands (1913-1919). After his return, he was mainly engaged in educational work. In the first Indonesian cabinet, he was minister of education and culture (1945).

origins.name: Softwareweg
origins.en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

origins.name: Solebaystraat
origins.en: Location on the east coast of England. In the Battle of Solebay (1672), the Dutch-Zeeuw fleet under Admiral De Ruyter successfully fought against the English.

origins.name: Solitudobrug
origins.en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and in the Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Solitudolaan
origins.en: Former country house near the Amstel and the Weespertrekvaart, which was located approximately at this location. It was already mentioned in 1730, and still existed in 1798.

origins.name: Solitudopad
origins.en: Former country house near the Amstel and the Weespertrekvaart, which was located approximately at this location. It was already mentioned in 1730, and still existed in 1798.

origins.name: Solostraat
origins.en: The largest river on the island of Java (Indonesia).

origins.name: Somerlustpad
origins.en: Former country house on Kruislaan, where the Nieuwe Ooster Cemetery is now located.

origins.name: Sommelsdijkstraat
origins.en: Village on the island of Overflakkee (South Holland).

origins.name: Sonderbuur
origins.en: Name of a demolished farm on the Haarlemmerweg near Halfweg.

origins.name: Sonneveld
origins.en: Medieval house of the Van Zonneveld family in Valkenburg (Limburg), demolished in 1789.

origins.name: Sontvaarderstraat
origins.en: A southerner is an inland ship that sails between the Netherlands and the Swedish south coast.

origins.name: Sophialaan
origins.en: Queen Sophia Frederika Mathilda of Württemberg (1817-1877), the first wife of King William III.

origins.name: Sophie Redmondplein
origins.en: Jeanne Sophie Everdine Redmond (1907-1955), first female doctor in Suriname. She fought for the position of the woman and the preservation of the heritage of Surinamese culture. Her nickname was Datra Foe potisma, doctor for the poor. She wrote plays, which were compiled in 1972.

origins.name: Spaanse Brabanderstraat
origins.en: Based on the novel by Gerbrand Adriaensz. Bredero,'Spaanschen Brabander' from 1617.

origins.name: Spaarndammerdijk
origins.en: The place Spaarndam, northeast of Haarlem. The name is derived from the dam in the Spaarne.

origins.name: Spaarndammerplantsoen
origins.en: The place Spaarndam, northeast of Haarlem. The name is derived from the dam in the Spaarne.

origins.name: Spaarndammerstraat
origins.en: The place Spaarndam, northeast of Haarlem. The name is derived from the dam in the Spaarne.

origins.name: Spaarndammertunnel
origins.en: The place Spaarndam, northeast of Haarlem. The name is derived from the dam in the Spaarne.

origins.name: Spaarnwouderdijk
origins.en: Named after the village of Spaarnwoude. The old Spaarnwouderdijk that came into Amsterdam in 1921 by annexation of the municipality of Sloten, has practically disappeared completely, so that name has been discontinued. At the same time, a newly built bicycle path has taken on the old name Spaarnwouderdijk.

origins.name: Spadinalaan
origins.en: Area in South Toronto on Lake Ontario. There has been a redevelopment process underway here since the beginning of the twenty-first century.

origins.name: Spahof
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Liège.

origins.name: Spakenburgstraat
origins.en: Village on the Eem Lake (Utrecht).

origins.name: Spaklerweg
origins.en: The Spakler family, founders and owners of the sugar factory (a family business). Coenraad Hendrik Spakler (born around 1732 in Westphalia) owned a sugar refinery on the Rozengracht.

origins.name: Spanderswoudstraat
origins.en: Nature monument. It is an old 's-Gravelandse country house with forest, wood walls and meadows.

origins.name: Spangenhof
origins.en: The former Spangen castle, between Schiedam and Overschie. Today, Spangen is a district of Rotterdam.

origins.name: Spankerenkade
origins.en: Village near Dieren (Gelderland).

origins.name: Sparrenweg
origins.en: Coniferous tree.

origins.name: Spechtstraat
origins.en: Name of a bird family.

origins.name: Speelmanstraat
origins.en: Willem Pieter Speelman (1919-1945), resistance fighter, born in Vlagtwedde, executed by firing squad in Halfweg.

origins.name: Speerdistelstraat
origins.en: An akkerdistel (creeping thistle) is a species of thistle.

origins.name: Speerstraat
origins.en: Attribute for throwing the spear, already practiced by the ancient Greeks.

origins.name: Spelderholt
origins.en: Nature monument northeast of Hoenderlo (Gelderland).

origins.name: Spengenpad
origins.en: Hamlet near Kockengen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Sperwerlaan
origins.en: Predatory bird.

origins.name: Speuldestraat
origins.en: Hamlet near Ermelo (Gelderland).

origins.name: Spicastraat
origins.en: Star in the zodiac sign Virgo.

origins.name: Spiegelgracht
origins.en: Named after a well-known Amsterdam family, mostly manufacturers, who had soap factories. In 1564 Lourens Pieters 'in den Spiegel' lived in the corner building of the Oude Spiegelstraat on the Singel and in 1608 Pieter Lourens Spiegel. The intended house is still called Hertspiegel in 1738. The construction of the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat begins in 1665. Again, it is likely that a resident of the Spiegel family is the namesake.

origins.name: Spijkerkade
origins.en: The - usually metal - tool for wood connections.

origins.name: Spijtellaantje
origins.en: L.J. Spijdel (born 1844), who established a shipyard here in 1885. The lane came within Amsterdam with the annexation of Sloten and was so named in popular parlance. In 1949, the name was officially established.

origins.name: Spinaker
origins.en: A spinnaker is meant: a sail, which is deployed when a ship sails dead before the wind.

origins.name: Spinakerhof
origins.en: A spinnaker is meant: a sail, which is deployed when a ship sails dead before the wind.

origins.name: Spinhuissteeg
origins.en: After the nearby Spinhuis (spinning house), a house of correction for women founded in 1596. From 1833 to 1941 the building housed the police headquarters.

origins.name: Spinozahof
origins.en: Benedictus Spinoza (Baruch d'Espinoza) (1632-1677), Jewish philosopher, who after being expelled from the Jewish community, lived by grinding eyeglass lenses. One of the leading thinkers of the seventeenth century, best known for his 'Ethics'. From 1874 to 1966, the Spinoza Clinic for Eye Patients stood on this street. A part of the street was previously called Andrieszkade, after the oldest known mayor of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Spinozastraat
origins.en: Benedictus Spinoza (Baruch d'Espinoza) (1632-1677), Jewish philosopher, who after being expelled from the Jewish community, lived by grinding eyeglass lenses. One of the leading thinkers of the seventeenth century, best known for his 'Ethics'. From 1874 to 1966, the Spinoza Clinic for Eye Patients stood on this street. A part of the street was previously called Andrieszkade, after the oldest known mayor of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Spitsbergenstraat
origins.en: Island group in the Arctic Ocean, mostly covered by a permanent ice cap. It now belongs to Norway. Spitsbergen was discovered in 1596 by Willem Barentsz, who had the settlement of Smeerenburg built there for whaling purposes.

origins.name: Spitskopstraat
origins.en: Mountain in South Africa where the Boers defeated the English in the First Boer War (1880-1881).

origins.name: Spooksteeg
origins.en: The origin of the name is unknown. Before 1800, the name is not mentioned on maps or in registers.

origins.name: Sporadenlaan
origins.en: Greek island group.

origins.name: Sportpark de Weeren
origins.en: A weir is an elongated plot of land between two boundary ditches. The ditch between two posts is also called a weir ditch. By council decision in 1971, part of the road was added to Buikslotermeerplein.

origins.name: Sportpark Kadoelen
origins.en: The name of the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was added to Amsterdam on 1 August 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) appears as early as 1375. In 1429 the manors of Landsmeer and Quadolen are mentioned, which then shared one lord. Old maps show Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterland sea dike (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1 August 1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed because of confusion with the Zuideinde (formerly Oostzaan).

origins.name: Sportpark Oostzanerwerf
origins.en: Named after the Oostzanerwerf district, where the sports park is located. The district derives its name from the municipality of Oostzaan, to which this area belonged until 1-8-1966.

origins.name: Sportpark Sloten
origins.en: Named after the village of Sloten, which until 1-1-1921 was the main village of the municipality of Sloten, to which also the village of Sloterdijk and the hamlet of Osdorp belonged. The municipality extended from the Haarlemmermeer to the North Sea Canal and from the Schinkel to Halfweg. The Sloterweg originally ran to (or began at) the Schinkel. Due to the construction of the ring road, a part has disappeared and deteriorated (see also Rijnsburgstraat).

origins.name: Sportpark Spieringhorn
origins.en: The former inland polder, which already existed before the poldering of the IJ.

origins.name: Sportparklaan
origins.en: Refers to the former sports park

origins.name: Sportstraat
origins.en: The street is located in the middle of streets whose names are derived from the Greek plays and from figures from antiquity who are generally known for their power.

origins.name: Spreeuwenpark
origins.en: The bird (the crow).

origins.name: Spui
origins.en: Until the end of the fourteenth century, the water that formed the southern border of the city. This water was equipped with a lock when the Singel was dug, hence the name Spui. The Spui was filled in in 1882.

origins.name: Spuistraat
origins.en: Named after the Spui, where the street leads out. Before the filling in in 1867, this was the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal. This canal was dug around 1385, along the straight course of the street this can still be recognized.

origins.name: Spyridon Louisweg
origins.en: Greek athlete, won gold in the marathon at the Olympic Games in Athens in 1896.

origins.name: Srefidensiplein
origins.en: Srefidensi is an important concept in Surinamese history and means 'independence'. The word was invented by the Surinamese poet Henri Frans de Ziel, alias Trefossa (1916-1975). 'Srefi' means 'self' in Sranantongo and 'densi' something like 'do'. Trefossa also wrote the Surinamese national anthem

origins.name: Staalkade
origins.en: Named after the Staalhof around the corner on the Groenburgwal. The Staalhof was the seat of the Staalmeesters, a college that supervised the products of the cloth (laken) industry in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. The Staalkade first emerged around 1630 through the merger and bore the name Binnen-Amstel until 1913.

origins.name: Staalmeesterslaan
origins.en: One of Rembrandt's most famous paintings.

origins.name: Staalstraat
origins.en: Named after the Staalhof around the corner on the Groenburgwal. The Staalhof was the seat of the Staalmeesters, a college that supervised the products of the cloth (laken) industry in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. The Staalkade first arose around 1630 by embankment and bore the name Binnen-Amstel until 1913.

origins.name: Staatsliedenbrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after the neighborhood in which it is located, the Staatsliedenbuurt

origins.name: Stade de Colombes
origins.en: Stadium in Paris. Ajax won the quarter-finals of the European Cup for Champions on March 5, 1969 at this stadium.

origins.name: Stadhouderskade
origins.en: When this quay was to be named, it was two hundred years ago that stadtholder William III freed the country from the English, the French and the Münsterians. Although Amsterdam has never been very stadtholder-friendly, this was still a reason to name the stadtholders, namely William II (1626-1650) and William III (1650-1702), in addition to a Nassaukade and a Mauritskade.

origins.name: Stadionkade
origins.en: A stadium has been a playing field with eccentrically sloping seats since the time of the Greeks. The road runs along the place where the stadium stood during the inauguration in 1922 (at the current Amazonestraat). The Olympic Stadium (on the square) was built for the 1928 Olympic Games.

origins.name: Stadionplein
origins.en: A stadium has been a playing field with eccentrically sloping seats since the time of the Greeks. The road runs along the place where the stadium stood during the inauguration in 1922 (at the current Amazonestraat). The Olympic Stadium (on the square) was built for the 1928 Olympic Games.

origins.name: Stadionweg
origins.en: A stadium has been a playing field with eccentrically sloping seats since the time of the Greeks. The road runs along the place where the stadium stood during the inauguration in 1922 (at the current Amazonestraat). The Olympic Stadium (on the square) was built for the 1928 Olympic Games.

origins.name: Staghof
origins.en: The part of the rigging of a ship that must support the masts.

origins.name: Stammerlandweg
origins.en: The name recalls the Stammerlandpolder, an old polder name, now part of the Gemeenschapspolder.

origins.name: Stapels
origins.en: Corrupted spelling of the French port town of Etaples, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Staringplein
origins.en: Antoni Christiaan Winand Staring (1767-1840), poet of nature poetry. Lived at De Wildenborch castle near Vorden.

origins.name: Staringstraat
