origins.en: Antoni Christiaan Winand Staring (1767-1840), poet of nature poetry. Lived at De Wildenborch castle near Vorden.

origins.name: Starrenboschstraat
origins.en: The estate Starre-Bosch, which stood on Kruislaan from 1690 to around 1800, on the site of the current Oosterbegraafplaats.

origins.name: Statenjachtstraat
origins.en: The official name of the service vessel of the state colleges in the Seven Provinces.

origins.name: Stationsplein
origins.en: Named after the Central Station completed in 1889, designed by architect Pierre Cuypers. Despite the many objections of the municipal government and the Chamber of Commerce, construction of the station at this location was carried out by the then-government.

origins.name: Staverdenplein
origins.en: Hamlet in the municipality of Ermelo (Gelderland). The castle of Staverden, built around 1905 on medieval foundations, is also known as Pauwenhof.

origins.name: Steelvlietplein
origins.en: As a result of a storm surge in 1530, a church village near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland drowned.

origins.name: Steenbokstraat
origins.en: The constellation, also the sign of the Zodiac.

origins.name: Steenderenstraat
origins.en: Village north of Doesburg (Gelderland). The town of Bronkhorst is now also part of this municipality.

origins.name: Steengroevenpad
origins.en: Country house east of Winterswijk.

origins.name: Steenhouwerijbrug
origins.en: Named after the stonemasons who worked in the Stads Metseltuin on the Leidsegracht.

origins.name: Steenhouwerssteeg
origins.en: In 1557, the stonemason Jan Woutersz lived on the corner of the canal. Before that, this was the Schoolsteegje, because this was the exit of the O.Z.-school.

origins.name: Stekkenbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill northwest of Groesbeek (Gelderland).

origins.name: Stellendamstraat
origins.en: Fisherman's village on the island of Goeree-Overflakkee (South Holland).

origins.name: Stellingweg
origins.en: A stelling is a gallery on struts around a tall mill. From this gallery the cap is turned into the wind and the sails are taken in. In 1976, for traffic technical reasons, part of the Stellingweg was renamed Molenaarsweg, while another part was added to Appelweg.

origins.name: Stenen Beer
origins.en: Named after defensive work in the Amsterdam position, located between Buitendijk and Couhornerhoek during the Batavian Republic. Demolished in 1825.

origins.name: Stenendokweg
origins.en: The dug docks of the shipyard, which are closed with sluice gates. They are mainly used at the repair yard.

origins.name: Stenghof
origins.en: A mast is an extension of the ship's mast.

origins.name: Stentorstraat
origins.en: A microscopic aquatic creature, can attach itself to a substrate, with its body stretching enormously in length, with a mouth funnel at the end.

origins.name: Stephensonstraat
origins.en: George Stephenson (1781-1848), English engineer, inventor of the locomotive (1814).

origins.name: Sterappelstraat
origins.en: Apple variety, originating around 1830 in southern the Netherlands or Belgium. The fruits are quite small, round and have a dark red color.

origins.name: Sterkenburg
origins.en: Old knight's manor town in Driebergen (Utrecht), of which only the heavy round tower remained after the demolition in 1848 and against which a new house was built.

origins.name: Sterrenplein
origins.en: The celestial bodies, namely fixed stars, planets and comets. The square is the center of the oldest part of the garden village of Oostzaan, where the streets are named after celestial bodies.

origins.name: Sterrenstraat
origins.en: The celestial bodies, namely fixed stars, planets and comets. The square is the center of the oldest part of the garden village of Oostzaan, where the streets are named after celestial bodies.

origins.name: Stettineiland
origins.en: Important historical Swedish and Prussian export port of wood. The city is now Polish and called Szczecin; Originally council decision spelled 'Stennin', this was later restored.

origins.name: Steve Bikoplein
origins.en: Steve Biko (1946-1977), killed in the nonviolent resistance against racial discrimination in South Africa. From 21-9-1904 to 1-2-1978 this was Pretoriusplein.

origins.name: Steven Vennecoolstraat
origins.en: Master builder (1659-1719), built among other things the Deutzenhofje on the Prinsengracht.

origins.name: Stichtstraat
origins.en: The name for the entire worldly area of the bishop of Utrecht, which ran from Bodegraven to the city of Groningen. Amstelland also belonged to it. later the term was narrowed down to the current province of Utrecht.

origins.name: Stieltjesstraat
origins.en: Thomas Jan Stieltjes (1856-1894), mathematician. Made contributions to mathematical analysis and number theory.

origins.name: Stierstraat
origins.en: The constellation, also a sign in the Zodiac.

origins.name: Stoel en Spreehof
origins.en: Teunis Stoel (1852-1912) and Marius Spree (1875-1925), who together operated the Plantage Schouwburg in the Plantage. They brought real folk pieces, such as works by Justus van Maurik.

origins.name: Stoelenmatterspad
origins.en: Basket-making was originally a typical travelling trade. The name is linked to the world of travelling people and refers to the caravan site here.

origins.name: Stokerkade
origins.en: Occupational name for lighting fires or ovens, and especially on locomotives and ships.

origins.name: Stolwijkstraat
origins.en: Village east of Gouda (South Holland).

origins.name: Stompetorenstraat
origins.en: Village in the Schermer, near Alkmaar (North Holland).

origins.name: Stoofsteeg
origins.en: Probably named so, because there were some one-room houses here, where needy people lived. The alley is mentioned in 1464 under the name Stovestege. Stove means room (compare the German 'Stube'). The alley was also previously known as Sint Jans Molenpad.

origins.name: Stoombootweg
origins.en: The road leads to the place on the Landsmeerdijk of the former station of the steamboat service to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Stoomgemaalstraat
origins.en: The mill, which drained the polder and replaced the windmill in the course of the nineteenth century.

origins.name: Stormsteeg
origins.en: Because this part of the city lay on its outermost edge until the sixteenth century, it took the full brunt of storms. The alley's name probably arose from this.

origins.name: Stormvloedkeringstraat
origins.en: Hydraulic construction that must counteract extreme high water floods.

origins.name: Stoutenburggracht
origins.en: Village south of Hoevelaken (Utrecht). It is named after the former castle that belonged to Van Oldebarneveldt.

origins.name: Strackéstraat
origins.en: Johan Ph. Stracke (1817-1892), sculptor. Made statues of Tollens (Rotterdam), Boerhaave (Leiden), Jan van Nassau (Utrecht) and in Amsterdam, among other things, sculptures on the facade of the Sint Jacobsgesticht in the Plantage Middenlaan. (Not to be confused with F. Stracke who made the bust of Prince Henry.)

origins.name: Stralsundbrug
origins.en: Stralsund is a German port city on the island of Rügen on the Baltic Sea. The names in the Houthavens are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Strandboulevard
origins.en: Refers to the important beach where this street runs along. The beach that is also the namesake of Strandeiland.

origins.name: Strandeilandlaan
origins.en: Name refers to the future Beach Island

origins.name: Strandvlietpad
origins.en: Named after the subway stop, where this path leads to. Strandvliet was the name of an old farm near Duivendrecht.

origins.name: Strawinskylaan
origins.en: Igor Strawinsky (1882-1971), American of Russian birth. Conductor and composer of operas and ballet music, including 'Le sacre du printemps'.

origins.name: Strawinskypad
origins.en: Igor Strawinsky (1882-1971), American of Russian birth. Conductor and composer of operas and ballet music, including 'Le sacre du printemps'.

origins.name: Streefkerkstraat
origins.en: Village in the Alblasserwaard near the Lek (South Holland).

origins.name: Strekkerweg
origins.en: Occupational name for someone who deforms metal, for example by means of a series of successive upsetting blows perpendicular to the direction of tension as in blacksmithing. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Stromarkt
origins.en: Named after the function that this square-shaped piece of street had in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Stromboliweg
origins.en: Volcanic island northeast of Sicily, part of the Lipari archipelago.

origins.name: Struisgrasstraat
origins.en: Grass species, which occurs all over the world.

origins.name: Stuurmankade
origins.en: Someone who controls a vessel.

origins.name: Stuyvesantstraat
origins.en: Peter Stuyvesant (1592-1672), colonial administrator, governor of Curaçao. The last director of the colony of New Netherlands, which had to be ceded to the English with the Treaty of Breda (1667). He stimulated trade in America and the West.

origins.name: Subangstraat
origins.en: Name of the Kuala Lumpur airport, Malaysia.

origins.name: Suikerdiefjestraat
origins.en: Small bird. One of the most famous birds of the Netherlands Antilles.

origins.name: Suikerpeerpad
origins.en: Old Dutch pear variety. The path is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Suikerplein
origins.en: This square and the surrounding streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Westersuikerfabriek where many families used to live in the Spaarndammerbuurt neighborhood.

origins.name: Sumatrakade
origins.en: An island in Indonesia.

origins.name: Sumatraplantsoen
origins.en: An island in Indonesia.

origins.name: Sumatrastraat
origins.en: An island in Indonesia.

origins.name: Surinamekade
origins.en: Refers to the country of Suriname.

origins.name: Surinameplein
origins.en: Named after Suriname

origins.name: Surinamestraat
origins.en: Named after Suriname

origins.name: Suze Groenewegplantsoen
origins.en: Politician (1875-1940), teacher in Rotterdam. Since 1914 member of the party board of the SDAP. Member of the Provincial States of South Holland and of the municipal council of Rotterdam and the first female member of the House of Representatives (1918-1937). As a member of parliament, she has worked, among other things, for the possibility of also appointing women as mayors.

origins.name: Suze Robertsonstraat
origins.en: Painter (1856-1922) from the Breitner school. Primarily painted still lifes.

origins.name: Swammerdamstraat
origins.en: Jan Swammerdam (1637-1680), anatomist and naturalist, who made important microscopic studies, preserved in his 'Bybel der natuure' (Bible of nature).

origins.name: Taandwarsstraat
origins.en: Tannin is a yellowish-brown pigment, prepared from oak bark and used to make fishnets and sails durable. The tanneries, formerly spread throughout the city, were only allowed on the Realeneiland around 1623 due to fire danger.

origins.name: Taanstraat
origins.en: Tannin is a yellowish-brown pigment, prepared from oak bark and used to make fishnets and sails durable. The tanneries, formerly spread throughout the city, were only allowed on the Realeneiland around 1623 due to fire danger.

origins.name: Tafelbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Blaricum (North Holland).

origins.name: Tagorestraat
origins.en: Rabindranath Tagore (1861-1941) was the first Indian writer to win the Nobel Prize for Literature.

origins.name: Talbotstraat
origins.en: William Henry Fox Talbot (1800-1877), English philosopher, Egyptologist, mathematician, linguist, physicist and photographer. Founder of modern photography. Experimented in the 1930s of the nineteenth century with photographic processes. Developed a negative process that made it possible to make more than one print of a negative.

origins.name: Talmastraat
origins.en: Aritius Sybrandus Talma (1864-1916), Reformed minister, later anti-revolutionary statesman. Leader of the Christian Songwriters' Association and director of the Patrimonium Housing Foundation. From 1908 to 1913 Minister of Agriculture. He played an important role in improving the poor conditions in the field of housing.

origins.name: Taman Sapituin
origins.en: Taman Sari means flower garden in Indonesian

origins.name: Tamariskhof
origins.en: Evergreen shrub with (light) pink flowers, which grows well on the coast.

origins.name: Tan Malakastraat
origins.en: Tan Malaka (Suliki 1894 - Kediri 1949). Tan Malaka obtained a teacher's certificate in Haarlem. During his stay in the Netherlands (1913-1919), he became more active in the Communist Party. After returning, he joined the Communist Party founded by Henk Sneevliet. The colonial authorities arrested him and exiled him from India. Back in the Netherlands, he was the first Indonesian to stand for a seat in the House of Representatives (1922). He was not elected and left for the Soviet Union. He then served as an agent of the Communist International (Komintern) in Southeast Asia until 1927 and led a hidden and persecuted existence.

origins.name: Tartaud-Kleinhof
origins.en: The theater actors Frits Tartaud (1857-1946), actor-director, director of the Rotterdam Theater, and his wife Alida Klein (1873-1938), a gifted tragedienne.

origins.name: Tasmanstraat
origins.en: Abel Jansz. Tasman (1603-1659), sailor and explorer. Discovered in 1642 and 1644 the island of Tasmania and New Zealand named after him.

origins.name: Teerketelsteeg
origins.en: This alley, which originally ended dead on the water where Koggestraat is now, ran behind the house 'de Teerketel' on the current Spuistraat. Tar was cooked and sold in the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Tefelenstraat
origins.en: Village on the Maas, northwest of Oss.

origins.name: Tegenhouderstraat
origins.en: The metalworker, who works together with the bricklayer. With a chisel, he holds the nail head against it when it is hammered through the bricklayer. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Teilingen
origins.en: Thirteenth-century castle, now a ruin located in Sassenheim (South Holland). Became famous through Jacoba of Bavaria, who lived and died there.

origins.name: Teixeira de Mattosstraat
origins.en: Named after the originally Portuguese-Jewish family that later established a bank at number 746 Prinsengracht. The bank went bankrupt in 1966.

origins.name: Tekkopstraat
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Woerden (Utrecht).

origins.name: Teleportboulevard
origins.en: The office area around the Sloterdijk station, of which this road forms a central axis, had the unofficial name Teleport when it was built. This is an American term adopted for an area of work with high-quality internal and external communication systems. The original intention to develop this area in this way has only been partially realized.

origins.name: Telescoophof
origins.en: A pair of binoculars for astronomical observations.

origins.name: Tempelhofstraat
origins.en: Name of the Berlin airport.

origins.name: Ten Katestraat
origins.en: Jan Jacob Lodewijk ten Kate (1819-1889), preacher-poet also provided translations of Goethe, Dante and Andersen. Originally widely read, but since the movement of the Eighty-Eighters has been pushed back.

origins.name: Tenderstraat
origins.en: The wagon behind the steam locomotive, on which coal and water are transported.

origins.name: Tenerifestraat
origins.en: Spanish island off the African coast. One of the Canary Islands.

origins.name: Teniersstraat
origins.en: David Teniers the Younger (1610-1690), South Dutch painter. Founded the Brussels Academy in 1663. Known for his tavern scenes and farmer's fairs.

origins.name: Ter Boede
origins.en: Originally a medieval castle near Koudekerke (Walcheren), now a stately country house from around 1740.

origins.name: Ter Gouwstraat
origins.en: Jan ter Gouw (1814-1894), teacher. Well-known historian of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Ter Haarstraat
origins.en: Bernard ter Haar (1806-1880), preacher-poet from the school of Tollens. Wrote religious and domestic poems. From 1854 professor in Utrecht.

origins.name: Ter Hooge
origins.en: Medieval castle near Koudekerke (Zeeland), significantly renovated in 1755 and partly rebuilt.

origins.name: Ter Kleef
origins.en: Former castle, built at the end of the fourteenth century, blown up in 1572 after the siege of Haarlem by the Spanish. Today, only a farm-like building, a tower and a pile of stones remain in Haarlem-Noord.

origins.name: Terheideweg
origins.en: Village south of The Hague. Known in national history for the naval battle of 1653 against the English, in which Admiral Maarten Harpertszoon Tromp died.

origins.name: Terletstraat
origins.en: Hamlet on the Arnhem-Apeldoorn road.

origins.name: Termietergouw
origins.en: The farm 'de Termiet', where the road leads to it. (Termite comes from ter Miede, and ants are grasslands.)

origins.name: Termieterweg
origins.en: The farm 'de Termiet', where the road leads to it. (Termite comes from ter Miede, and ants are grasslands.)

origins.name: Termini
origins.en: Most important train station in Rome.

origins.name: Ternatestraat
origins.en: Island belonging to the Moluccas (Indonesia).

origins.name: Terpstraat
origins.en: Artificially raised residential hill, occurs under this name in Friesland. Terpen also occur in all kinds of shapes in other provinces under the name woerd, werd or wierd.

origins.name: Terschellingstraat
origins.en: Wadden island (Friesland).

origins.name: Tervurenpad
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Teslastraat
origins.en: Nikola Tesla (1856-1943), Yugoslav engineer and physicist. In 1884 he emigrated to America. A member of Edison's team made numerous inventions in the field of alternating current and high-frequency technology. The unit of magnetic induction is named after him.

origins.name: Tesselschadestraat
origins.en: Maria Tesselschade Visscher (1594-1649), poet. She adorned the Muiderkring with her sister. Daughter of Roemer Visscher, who gave her this name at her birth, because he had just lost many of his ships at Texel.

origins.name: Tetje de Jongbrug
origins.en: Theodora (Tetje) de Jong (Uithoorn, May 2, 1918 - Drachten, January 21, 1999) was the first paid female police commissioner in the Netherlands. In 1954, the same year in which the first women joined the uniform service at the Amsterdam police, De Jong was appointed chief inspector. On January 1, 1964, De Jong was officially appointed police commissioner in Amsterdam. In 1977, De Jong received a Royal award due to her great significance for the Amsterdam police: she was appointed Officer of the Order of Orange-Nassau.

origins.name: Teugestraat
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Voorst (Gelderland).

origins.name: Texelplein
origins.en: A Wadden island (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Texelweg
origins.en: A Wadden island (Noord-Holland).

origins.name: Teylerplein
origins.en: The oldest museum in the Netherlands: the Teylers Museum in Haarlem. The eighteenth-century merchant Pieter Teyler van der Hulst left his fortune to promote art and science. In 1784 the museum began with one room, where scientific instruments, extinct animals and drawings were exhibited. Over time, the collection has been expanded with paintings, coins and fossils, among other things.

origins.name: Th. J. Lammerslaan
origins.en: Theodorus Johannes Lammers (1890-1972), Amsterdam architect. Designer from the later period of the Amsterdam School, the man behind the Physiological Laboratory of the Vrije Universiteit on Valeriusplein.

origins.name: Th. K. van Lohuizenlaan
origins.en: Theodore Karel (1890-1956), architect and urban planner. He was at the basis of the General Expansion Plan for Amsterdam, which appeared in 1934. Worked closely with Cornelis van Eesteren.

origins.name: Th. Weeversweg
origins.en: Theo Weevers (1875-1952) professor of botany in Amsterdam. Founder of government care for nature conservation. Chairman of the State Committee on nature reserves and nature conservation.

origins.name: Theemsweg
origins.en: River in England.

origins.name: Theo Fransmanbrug
origins.en: Theo Frenchman, who was the first district chairman of Amsterdam-North from 1981 to 1990. He worked as such to find new destinations for the NDSM site after the closure of the shipyard.

origins.name: Theo Frenkelhof
origins.en: Theodorus Maurits Frenkel (1871-1956), actor, theater and film director, member of the famous theater family Bouwmeester. Directed about two hundred films in England, France and Germany. Between 1915 and 1922 he also directed a number of feature films in the Netherlands. Achieved international success with his adaptation of Heijermans' play 'Brand in De Jonge Jan', in which he also acted.

origins.name: Theo Mann-Bouwmeesterhof
origins.en: The actress Theodora Mann born Bouwmeester (1850-1939), sister of Louis Bouwmeester. She was one of the greatest tragedians. Her starring roles included Tosca, Lady Macbeth and Mary Stuart.

origins.name: Theo Thijssenhof
origins.en: Theodorus Thijssen (1879-1943), Amsterdam teacher and pedagogue. Wrote novellas and novels on the field of school and children's life, of which 'Kees the boy' is best known.

origins.name: Theo van Doesburgstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Christian E.M. Küpper (1883-1931), painter and designer of stained glass windows under the influence of Mondrian. Driving force of the 'Stijlgroep' (1917). As an architect, he worked with Rietveld.

origins.name: Theodoor van Hoytemastraat
origins.en: Painter (1863-1917), mainly painted animals, illustrator and lithographer.

origins.name: Theodorus Dobbestraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1901-1944), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Dieren.

origins.name: Theodorus Majofskistraat
origins.en: Theodorus Johannes Majofski (1770-1836), Polish-born actor, ancestor of a famous acting family. In his time, he was one of the most important figures in Amsterdam theater.

origins.name: Theophile de Bockstraat
origins.en: Painter (1851-1904), best known for his nature scenes.

origins.name: Theophilusstraat
origins.en: A rhymed Marian legend from the fourteenth century.

origins.name: Thérèse Schwartzeplein
origins.en: Therèse van Duijl-Schwartze (1852-1918), portrait painter. At the request of the painter Lizzy Ansingh, the first name is included in full in the name, to make it clear that it was a woman.

origins.name: Thérèse Schwartzestraat
origins.en: Therèse van Duijl-Schwartze (1852-1918), portrait painter. At the request of the painter Lizzy Ansingh, the first name is included in full in the name, to make it clear that it was a woman.

origins.name: Theseusstraat
origins.en: In Greek mythology the hero of Attica, who defeated the minotaur with the help of Ariadne.

origins.name: Tholenstraat
origins.en: One of the Zeeuwse islands, separated by water from the Eendracht of North Brabant.

origins.name: Thomas à Kempisstraat
origins.en: Thomas van Kempen (1380-1471), philosopher, from Kempen in the land of Cleve. Author of the famous work 'On the imitation of Christ'.

origins.name: Thomas Hoodstraat
origins.en: English scholar, lived at the end of the sixteenth century. He taught astronomy and navigation in London among other things and published about the use of sea charts. In 1602 a translation of his work appeared in Amsterdam under the title 'Tgebruijck vande zeecaarte'.

origins.name: Thomas Prinslaan
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1885-1942), carried out sabotage at the Kromhout-Motorenfabriek where he worked, participated in the preparation of the February Strike in 1941. On November 19, 1942, he was executed in Soesterberg.

origins.name: Thomas R. Malthusstraat
origins.en: Thomas Robert Malthus (1766-1834), British historian and economist. In 1798 his pamphlet 'An Essay on the Principle of Population' appeared, in which he demonstrates that the population is increasing faster than economic growth. This would lead to overcrowding and social misery.

origins.name: Thomas van Aquinostraat
origins.en: Italian theologian and philosopher (1225-1274), one of the greatest of the scholastics, who tried to make the Church's teachings understandable to the mind.

origins.name: Thomas van Erpehof
origins.en: Professor of Oriental languages (1584-1624) at the University of Leiden, close friend of Hugo de Groot.

origins.name: Thorbeckeplein
origins.en: Jan Rudolf Thorbecke (1798-1872), liberal statesman and professor in Leiden. Prime Minister and several times Minister of the Interior. His most important act was the revision of the constitution in 1848. Originally this was a part of the Reguliersgracht. After the filling in of this part in 1874, the name Reguliersplein was born. In 1876, the statue of Thorbecke was unveiled here, made by the sculptor F. Leenhoff. This was the reason for giving the square its current name. (The statue bears the inscription Optimo civi cives = the citizens to the best citizen.)

origins.name: Thorn Prikkerstraat
origins.en: Named after Johan Thorn Prikker (1868-1932) who worked in the Symbolist, Impressionist and Art Nouveau style.

origins.name: Tichelstraat
origins.en: Named after the many tile and brick bakeries established here in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Tidorestraat
origins.en: Island belonging to the Moluccas (Indonesia).

origins.name: Tielstraat
origins.en: The city in the Betuwe on the Waal, center of fruit and vegetable cultivation.

origins.name: Tienenpad
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Tiengemetenstraat
origins.en: The South Holland island in the Haringvliet.

origins.name: Tienraaikade
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Mierlo, east of Venray (Limburg).

origins.name: Tijl Uilenspiegelstraat
origins.en: Main character from a folk book from around 1500, who is seen as a personification of the Flemish folk character with his mischievous antics. The story was depicted in 1867 by Charles de Coster, and in a symphonic poem by Richard Strauss.

origins.name: Tijnmuiden
origins.en: The English port town of Tynemouth, near Newcastle, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Tilanusstraat
origins.en: Christiaan Bernhard Tilanus (1856-1943), professor of surgery in Amsterdam. Tilanus was born as the son of J.W. Tilanus, professor from 1867-1893 and grandson of the equally famous professor C.B. Tilanus (1828-1873). He was a specialist in bacteriology and later also in orthopedics. He soon saw the importance of first aid by laypeople in accidents. At his initiative, a brochure was distributed in 1893 that laid the foundation for the establishment of the first first aid association in the Netherlands, the 'Association for First Aid in Accidents', which later received the title of Royal. He also founded the Clinical School, the Training School for midwives and the Orthopaedic Association.

origins.name: Timo Smeehuijzenbrug
origins.en: Timo Smeehuijzen was a 20-year-old soldier who died in Afghanistan on June 15, 2007. Before that, he attended school at the nearby Fons Vitae high school, hence this location. This bridge is also a tribute to all other soldiers who died in Afghanistan.

origins.name: Timorplein
origins.en: Island belonging to the Lesser Sunda Islands in Indonesia. Half of the island was Portuguese territory.

origins.name: Timorstraat
origins.en: Island belonging to the Lesser Sunda Islands in Indonesia. Half of the island was Portuguese territory.

origins.name: Tintorettostraat
origins.en: Jacopo Robusti (1518-1594), calling himself Tintoretto, Italian painter. One of the main painters of the Venetian school.

origins.name: Tip Maruggstraat
origins.en: Silvio Alberto 'Tip' Marugg (Willemstad, 1923 - Willemstad 2006) was a writer and poet. After obtaining his Mulodiploma in 1942, he served in the military for five years. After that, he worked at Shell, where he discovered writing after working on the staff magazine Passaat. He debuted in 1958 with the novel Weekend Pilgrimage. For his third novel The morning is calling again from 1988 he was nominated for the AKO Literature Prize and in 1989 he received the Cola Debrot Prize. Island life played a major role in his books, which have been translated into several languages.

origins.name: Titiaanstraat
origins.en: Painter's name of Tiziano Vecellio (1477-1576), famous master of the Venetian school.

origins.name: Titus Brandsmabrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after Titus Brandsma (1881 - 1942). He was a Roman Catholic priest and professor of Theology in Nijmegen. As a spiritual advisor, he exerted influence in 1942 on the Catholic daily newspapers to avoid making propaganda for the NSB. The same year, he was deported to Dachau, where he died.

origins.name: Titus van Rijnstraat
origins.en: Son of Rembrandt van Rijn and Saskia van Uijlenburg (1641-1668). Modeled several times. After Rembrandt's death, he ran an art gallery with works by the painter with his stepmother Hendrikje Stoffels. Was buried in the Westerkerk.

origins.name: Tjalkstraat
origins.en: River sailing ship with flat bottom and round bow, gaff rigged.

origins.name: Tjepmapad
origins.en: Former country house near Vleuten (Utrecht), of which only the seventeenth-century gate building remains.

origins.name: Tjerk Hiddes de Vriesstraat
origins.en: Frisian admiral (1622-1666), died in the Second Anglo-Dutch War at Dunkirk.

origins.name: Tjeukemeerhof
origins.en: A lake in southern Friesland.

origins.name: Tjotterspad
origins.en: Inland waterway sailboat with low draft.

origins.name: Tobias M.C. Asserstraat
origins.en: Jurist (1838-1913). Known at home and abroad in the field of international private law. In 1862 he became a professor in Amsterdam, in 1893 a member of the Council of State. In 1911 he received the Nobel Peace Prize.

origins.name: Toetsenbordweg
origins.en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

origins.name: Tofana
origins.en: Mountain peak in Italy, 3243 meters high.

origins.name: Tolbrugstraat
origins.en: After the toll gate (tol) on the corner of today's Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was levied from about 1780 until the area was annexed in 1896, for the upkeep of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 11 February 1886).

origins.name: Toldwarsstraat
origins.en: After the toll gate (tol) on the corner of today's Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was levied from about 1780 until the area was annexed in 1896, for the upkeep of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 11 February 1886).

origins.name: Tolhuisweg
origins.en: Named after the Tolhuis, a roadside inn and once a popular spot. Construction dates back to 1662, when a highway was built here and a toll was established. In the garden, the famous concerts were held from 1887 to 1912 by the then popular seventh regiment under the leadership of organist Joh. Zaagmans.

origins.name: Tolkamerstraat
origins.en: The village with border office near Lobith (Gelderland) on the Rhine. The Rhine is the busiest border crossing in the world here.

origins.name: Tollensstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Frederik Tollens (1780-1856), Rotterdam merchant, who became known as a folk poet.

origins.name: Tolsendestraat
origins.en: Former church village, south of Yerseke (Zeeland), flooded in 1530.

origins.name: Tolstraat
origins.en: After the toll gate (tol) on the corner of today's Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was levied from about 1780 until the area was annexed in 1896, for the upkeep of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 11 February 1886).

origins.name: Tom Schreursweg
origins.en: Cornelis Petrus Antonius Schreurs (1896-1956), already took the initiative in 1923 for radio sports broadcasts, in particular of international football matches.

origins.name: Tomatenstraat
origins.en: Named after the tomato, a fruit.

origins.name: Toministraat
origins.en: Port city on the island of Sulawesi (Celebes) in Indonesia.

origins.name: Tommaso Albinonistraat
origins.en: Italian composer (1671-1750), probably self-taught. Worked as a chamber musician of Ferdinando Carlo, Duke of Mantua. Johan Sebastian Bach used themes by Albinoni three times as a starting point for his own compositions. Albinoni wrote instrumental works and about fifty operas.

origins.name: Ton de Leeuwstraat
origins.en: Composer (1926-1996), was associated with the Sweelinck Conservatory in Amsterdam from 1959 to 1987, first as head professor of composition and from 1984 as artistic director. He dealt with the relationship between the East and the West in music. He received many awards, including the Prix d'Italia and the Matthijs Vermeulen Prize.

origins.name: Tondenpad
origins.en: Hamlet in the municipality of Brummen, west of Zutphen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Tongelaer
origins.en: Former castle from the fifteenth century, located near MilI, municipality of Beers (North Brabant). Only a square gate tower remains.

origins.name: Tongerenstraat
origins.en: Hamlet and estate west of Epe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Tonia Stieltjesplein
origins.en: Tonia Stieltjes (1881-1932) was born in the Czaar Peterstraat, as the daughter of an Afro-Surinamese born into slavery. She campaigned for the improvement of the working and living conditions of domestic staff and is considered the first black trade unionist woman. She also lives on in the many portraits where she posed as a model.

origins.name: Top Naeffstraat
origins.en: Anthonetta van Rhijn born Naeff (1878-1953), novelist and theater critic. Wrote biographies of Willem Royaards and Sarah Bernhardt, among others.

origins.name: Top Rinckerstraat
origins.en: Friedrich Johannes Wilhelm Rincker (1877-1939), one of the top figures in Dutch cricket, played in 43 international matches.

origins.name: Topaasstraat
origins.en: A yellow gemstone.

origins.name: Topkapipad
origins.en: Topkapi Museum in Istanbul. One of the most beautifully preserved examples of worldly architecture in Istanbul. Originally the palace of the sultans. Opened as a museum since 1924. The collection consists of the most diverse objects that belonged to the Turkish court, including weapons, porcelain, jewelry, clothing and miniatures.

origins.name: Torensluis
origins.en: The name of this fixed bridge refers to the Jan Roodenpoortstoren, which used to stand next to the gate in the city wall here and was demolished in 1829. The base of the tower is still located on the side of this bridge.

origins.name: Torensteeg
origins.en: The alley leads to the place where once stood the Jan Roodenpoort tower next to the gate in the city wall. After the demolition of the city wall, this tower still existed until 1829. The base of the tower is still located on the side of the bridge, the Tower Lock.

origins.name: Torenven
origins.en: An old local name: a swamp near the tower.

origins.name: Torresstraat
origins.en: Luis Vaez de Torres (1728-1779), Spanish explorer. Discovered the Torresstraat, a sea island named after him, between Australia and New Guinea.

origins.name: Torricellistraat
origins.en: Evangelista Torricelli (1608-1647), Italian physicist, professor in Florence. Inventor of the Torricelli tube, a precursor to the mercury barometer. This street was named Dr. Leydsstraat by the former municipality of Watergraafsmeer (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1921).

origins.name: Tosaristraat
origins.en: Mountain village and plain in East Java. The highest place on the island. During the Dutch rule one of the most popular holiday destinations.

origins.name: Tosarituin
origins.en: Mountain village and plain in East Java. The highest place on the island. During the Dutch rule one of the most popular holiday destinations.

origins.name: Tourniairestraat
origins.en: Bachigaloupi Tourniaire (1850-1921), in his time a particularly beloved actor who excelled in comedic roles, and his son Oscar Tourniaire (1880-1939), who played many Shakespearean roles as an actor.

origins.name: Touwbaan
origins.en: The street was laid out on the site where in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the ropewalks of the Dutch East India Company lay.

origins.name: Touwbaanpark
origins.en: The street was laid out on the site where in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the ropewalks of the Dutch East India Company lay.

origins.name: Touwslagerstraat
origins.en: Occupational name from shipbuilding. The name reminds us of the many shipyards that were established here in earlier centuries.

origins.name: Transformatorweg
origins.en: Device for converting electrical current from one voltage to another

origins.name: Transvaalkade
origins.en: The country across the Vaal River. Formerly an independent Boer Republic and after the 1899-1902 war a province of the Union of South Africa. The street originated from the remainder of Lange Overamstelstraat (formerly named by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel) and Ringstraat (council decision, 1904), the quay was originally named Ringkade by Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Transvaalplein
origins.en: The country across the Vaal River. Formerly an independent Boer Republic and after the 1899-1902 war a province of the Union of South Africa. The street originated from the remainder of Lange Overamstelstraat (formerly named by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel) and Ringstraat (council decision, 1904), the quay was originally named Ringkade by Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Transvaalstraat
origins.en: The country across the Vaal River. Formerly an independent Boer Republic and after the 1899-1902 war a province of the Union of South Africa. The street originated from the remainder of Lange Overamstelstraat (formerly named by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel) and Ringstraat (council decision, 1904), the quay was originally named Ringkade by Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Treilerhof
origins.en: A trawler or trawler is a vessel for marine fishing, where fishing is done with a trawl or scraper net.

origins.name: Tretjakovlaan
origins.en: Named after the Tretyakov Museum in Moscow. Construction was completed in 1900. The collection is based on the art collection of Pavel Tretyakov, which he donated to Moscow in 1892. Famous for the unique collection of icons.

origins.name: Trianonpad
origins.en: The name of two small palaces in the park of Versailles. The Grand Trianon was built at the behest of Louis XIV (1687-1688) and the Petit Trianon at the behest of Louis XV (1762-1768).

origins.name: Trichtstraat
origins.en: Village on the Linge, northwest of Geldermalsen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Trijn Hullemanlaan
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1912-1941), involved in many illegal activities and member of the resistance group 'Krijn Breur'.

origins.name: Trimurtistraat
origins.en: Trimur: independence

origins.name: Troelstralaan
origins.en: Pieter Jelles Troelstra (1860-1930), lawyer and politician, and Frisian poet. Co-founder of the SDAP in 1894, member of the House of Representatives from 1897 to 1924.

origins.name: Troepiaalsingel
origins.en: Brightly colored bird. Usually flies in large flocks (troops), hence the name.

origins.name: Trompenburgstraat
origins.en: Former country house on the Amstel, named after the then owner: fleet commander Cornelis Tromp. After his death in 1691, mayor Nicolaas Witsen moved in there. At the beginning of the twentieth century, the Spijker automobile factory and the Nestelroy-Trompenburg paper factory settled here successively. The name of the street was originally Trompstraat (council decision, 1899).

origins.name: Trouringhstraat
origins.en: Title of a learned poem by Jacob Cats.

origins.name: Truus Wijsmullerbrug
origins.en: Geertruida Wijsmuller-Meyer (1896 - 1978) was already working to bring Jewish refugees from Central Europe to safety through the Netherlands before World War II. For example, she organized weekly transports of 500 children from Frankfurt, Vienna or Prague to England in 1938 and 1939 with the permission of Adolf Eichmann. In August 1939, she organized the evacuation of the Jewish population from Danzig in Poland After the outbreak of the war, she guided the transports to Marseille or Spain on a stopover to Palestine. She also provided food packages for Jewish children in Westerbork In addition, she managed to save 50 children from Westerbork from deportation to Poland.

origins.name: tt. Melaniaweg
origins.en: The turbinetanker Melania. This 330-meter-long and 250,000-ton tanker was delivered to Shell in 1969. The ship was built on the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM) in two parts and welded together after launching. Melania is the name of a shell (the trademark of Shell).

origins.name: tt. Melissaweg
origins.en: The turbine tanker Melissa. Built in 1965 by Van der Giessen-De Noord, first owned by N.V. Verenigde Tankkustvaart and then by P.A. van Es & Co. N.V..

origins.name: tt. Neveritaweg
origins.en: Turbine tanker, 110,000 tons. The last tanker built entirely by the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM), built in 1968 on behalf of Koninklijke Shell Groep. At that time the largest ever built supertanker in the Netherlands.

origins.name: tt. Vasumweg
origins.en: The turbine tanker Vasum, built in 1955 at the shipyard of the Dutch Dok- en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij on behalf of the Royal Shell Group. Vasum is the name of a shell (the trademark of Shell). The road was laid on the grounds of the former shipyard of the NDSM.

origins.name: Tugelaweg
origins.en: River in South Africa, the southern defensive line of the Boers in the war of 1899 to 1902, where fierce fighting took place against the English.

origins.name: Tuigerstraat
origins.en: Occupational name for the person who rigs and unrigs ships. (The rigging of a ship includes all the ropework and steel wires for operating masts, winch equipment and davits.) The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Tuilstraat
origins.en: Village on the Waal opposite Zaltbommel (Gelderland).

origins.name: Tuimelaarstraat
origins.en: Dolphin, does not grow longer than 2.5 meters. It is dark, lives in groups and is distributed worldwide. The bottlenose dolphin is very agile and is often kept in dolphinariums.

origins.name: Tuin van Hera
origins.en: Greek goddess of marriage and childbirth. Fold and also sister of Zeus. Hera was also revered as the patroness of herds; The cow was one of the animals dedicated to her.

origins.name: Tuinbouwstraat
origins.en: The cultivation of vegetables, fruits and flowers.

origins.name: Tuinderijlaan
origins.en: Refers to community garden park De Bongerd.

origins.name: Tuinstraat
origins.en: Tuin (garden) here means a yard or enclosed space. The street name comes from the Stadstimmertuin (the city's carpentry yard, the Stadswerf), which lay here from 1612 to 1660 (by the Lijnbaansgracht) and to which the street led.

origins.name: Tulastraat
origins.en: Tula, nicknamed Rigaud, was one of the leaders of the uprising of the enslaved people that broke out in Curaçao in August 1795. In September 1795 he was captured and executed.

origins.name: Turbinestraat
origins.en: Machine in which a screw-shaped rotor is brought into motion by fluid or steam, used among other things for generating electrical energy.

origins.name: Turbón
origins.en: Mountain peak in Spain, 2492 meters high.

origins.name: Turfdraagsterpad
origins.en: When this path still ran through to the (Old) Turfmarkt, the women who worked at the Turfmarkt lived in the houses along this path.

origins.name: Turfsteeg
origins.en: Named after the peat warehouse of the Oudezijds Huiszittenarmen (later the Arsenal), where the alley runs along.

origins.name: Turnerstraat
origins.en: Practitioner of gymnastics, one of the ancient Greek sports.

origins.name: Turnhoutplantsoen
origins.en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Tussen de Bogen
origins.en: Regarding the location between the railway viaducts. The spaces between these viaducts were called arches on site.

origins.name: Tussen Kadijken
origins.en: When a great deal of land had built up through silting outside the old sea dike (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike, or quay dike (kadijk), was built. It was originally called the new sea dike, but that name later fell out of use. When this new dike was raised further, people spoke of the Laagte (low part) and the Hoogte (high part) of the Kadijk. Until 1943 the Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat. This is because it lies in line with the Plantage Kerklaan, although it has never been connected to it.

origins.name: Tussen Meer
origins.en: Named after a former farm on the Uitweg near the Sloterpolder that was demolished in the 1950s for the construction of the Slotermeer district.

origins.name: Tussendek
origins.en: Achterdek (afterdeck): one of the decks of a ship.

origins.name: Tutein Noltheniusstraat
origins.en: Rudolf Peter Johannes Tutein Nolthenius (1851-1939), civil engineer. Designed plans for relocating the mouth of the Maas.

origins.name: Twee Koningskinderenstraat
origins.en: Named after the fairy tale 'The Twee Royal Children' by the Brothers Grimm.

origins.name: Tweede Anjeliersdwarsstraat
origins.en: An anjelier (carnation) is a flower belonging to the pink family.

origins.name: Tweede Atjehstraat
origins.en: The northern part of the Indonesian island of Sumatra (Aceh), known above all for the Aceh War (1873-1904), with which the name of General Van Heutsz is linked.

origins.name: Tweede Bloemdwarsstraat
origins.en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion of 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which it is named. From 1614 to 1878 the windmill 'De Blom' stood on the bastion; it was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

origins.name: Tweede Boerhaavestraat
origins.en: Hermannus Boerhaave (1668-1738), professor of medicine at Leiden. He enjoyed international fame. The street name Boerhaavestraat (First to Fourth) has been changed several times. It was set as Boerhaavestraat on 15 November 1876 and changed to Eerste Boerhaavestraat on 15 November 1882. This change was reversed on 10 December 1884. On 13 October 1897 the street was extended under the same name, and finally, on 19 February 1908, it was split into the present Eerste and Tweede Boerhaavestraat. The Tweede, Derde and Vierde Boerhaavestraat, named in 1882, were replaced by the names Deymanstraat, Ruyschstraat and Blasiusstraat.

origins.name: Tweede Boomdwarsstraat
origins.en: In this part of the Jordaan, streets are named after flowers, shrubs and trees. In the seventeenth century, the street was also called Lindeboomstraat.

origins.name: Tweede Breeuwersstraat
origins.en: A trade name. A breeuwer (caulker) sealed the seams between the planks of a ship's hull. In the seventeenth century many caulkers lived in the Eerste Breeuwersstraat (formerly Breeuwersstraat), working at the shipyards on the Prinseneiland and Realeneiland. In 1895 the parallel street was given the same name, which made the additions Eerste and Tweede necessary.

origins.name: Tweede Ceramstraat
origins.en: An island in Indonesia.

origins.name: Tweede Coehoornstraat
origins.en: Menno baron van Coehoorn (1641-1704). Fortress builder, general engineer of the fortifications.

origins.name: Tweede Constantijn Huygensstraat
origins.en: Poet and prose writer (1596-1687), whose works include 'Hofwijck' and epigrams (sneldichten). He was secretary to several successive stadholders. Before 1894 parts of these streets were called Eerste and Tweede Bilderdijkstraat (council decisions of 15 May 1878 and 19 December 1883).

origins.name: Tweede Disteldwarsstraat
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Tweede Egelantiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Tweede Goudsbloemdwarsstraat
origins.en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

origins.name: Tweede Helmersstraat
origins.en: Jan Frederik Helmers (1767-1813), Amsterdam broker who devoted himself to letters. His works include 'De Hollandsche Natie' (1813). The second part of the Eerste Helmersstraat lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 and was then called Hofdijkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 9 May 1890). The start of this street was originally a short side street of the Nassaukade called Sophiapark.

origins.name: Tweede Hugo de Grootstraat
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

origins.name: Tweede Jacob van Campenstraat
origins.en: Master builder (1595-1659). Designer of the town hall on the Dam, now a royal palace. However, he was not allowed to complete the work. Van Campen also built the Heiligewegse gate in 1636 and a palace for Prince Frederick Henry in 1657 in Rijswijk. The division into Eerste and Tweede occurred after the intervening part of the street was sold to Heineken Brewery in 1930.

origins.name: Tweede Jan Steenstraat
origins.en: Painter (1626-1679), mostly of domestic scenes: merry, untidy interiors. That gave rise to the expression 'a Jan Steen household' (een huishouden van Jan Steen).

origins.name: Tweede Jan van der Heijdenstraat
origins.en: Painter and engineer (1637-1712), inventor of the fire engine with a hose and of a new model of street lamp. Painter of portraits and townscapes.

origins.name: Tweede Keucheniusstraat
origins.en: Levinus W.C. Keuchenius (1822-1893), Anti-Revolutionary statesman and fierce opponent of the state school. Minister of the Colonies from 1888 to 1890.

origins.name: Tweede Kostverlorenkade
origins.en: After the Kostverlorenwetering, dug in 1413 to give a shorter waterway to the Haarlem and Leiden lakes. According to some, the name Kostverloren (cost lost) comes from the heavy legal costs of this channel, which was a bone of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609. The name Kostverloren occurs in several places in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat
origins.en: The southern European ornamental tree (the laurel).

origins.name: Tweede Leeghwaterstraat
origins.en: Jan Adriaanszoon Leeghwater (1575-1650), hydraulic engineer. As overseer and millwright he worked on many land reclamations, including the Beemster. He drew up the first plan to drain the Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Tweede Leliedwarsstraat
origins.en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Tweede Lindendwarsstraat
origins.en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

origins.name: Tweede Looiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

origins.name: Tweede Marnixplantsoen
origins.en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Tweede Nassaustraat
origins.en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. Before it was named in 1879, the quay was called Buitensingel.

origins.name: Tweede Oosterparkstraat
origins.en: Named after the nearby Oosterpark, and originally (council decision of 15 November 1882) named Eerste, Tweede and Derde Parkstraat. The Eerste Oosterparkstraat was earlier called Oetgenspad, after Frans Hendriks Oetgens, a sixteenth-century burgomaster over whose land several paths were laid. Until 1895 the street name applied as far as the Linnaeusstraat. In that year the stretch along the park was given the park's name.

origins.name: Tweede Passeerdersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

origins.name: Tweede Rozendwarsstraat
origins.en: The flower (the rose).

origins.name: Tweede Schinkelstraat
origins.en: The name recalls the old roadside inn Schinkelhaven. Before 1922 the street was part of the Schinkelkade.

origins.name: Tweede Sweelinckstraat
origins.en: Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck (1562-1621), a musician of great renown and organist of the Oude Kerk. He wrote many compositions on the psalms and love songs. Before 1896 part of the Tweede Sweelinckstraat lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel as the Tweede Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 22 August 1890).

origins.name: Tweede Tuindwarsstraat
origins.en: Tuin (garden) here means a yard or enclosed space. The street name comes from the Stadstimmertuin (the city's carpentry yard, the Stadswerf), which lay here from 1612 to 1660 (by the Lijnbaansgracht) and to which the street led.

origins.name: Tweede Van der Helststraat
origins.en: Bartholomeus van der Helst (1612-1670), painter of militia and regents' group portraits.

origins.name: Tweede van Swindenstraat
origins.en: Jean Henri van Swinden (1746-1823), philosopher, mathematician and physicist, professor at Franeker and from 1785 in Amsterdam. He sat on the commission that fixed the metre, after which he worked out the metric system introduced in the Netherlands in 1816.

origins.name: Tweede Vogelstraat
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Tweede Weteringdwarsstraat
origins.en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory.

origins.name: Tweede Weteringplantsoen
origins.en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory.

origins.name: Tweede Wittenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

origins.name: Tweelingenhof
origins.en: The sign of the zodiac.

origins.name: Twellostraat
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Voorst (Gelderland) on the old road Apeldoorn-Deventer. The village is surrounded by a number of estates.

origins.name: Twentestraat
origins.en: The eastern part of the province of Overijssel.

origins.name: Twikkel
origins.en: Castle in Delden (Overijssel), built in 1347, then renovated and expanded several times.

origins.name: Twiskestraat
origins.en: Twiske is the (West) Frisian word for 'between', it refers to the border ditch between the Waterland and the Zaanontginningen. The current recreation area near Oostzaan still bears this name.

origins.name: U.J. Klarenstraat
origins.en: Uilke Jan Klaren (1852-1947), founder of the playground work in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Ubbo Emmiushof
origins.en: Historian (1547-1625). The first rector magnificus of the University of Groningen.

origins.name: Uffizilaan
origins.en: Galleria degli Uffizi in Florence, museum. Most of the building was built between 1560 and 1580. The painting collection is based on the art collection of the de'Medici family. Contains works from the Florentine, Venetian and Dutch school.

origins.name: Uilenburgersteeg
origins.en: The island of Uilenburg, which together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken came to lie within the city in 1593. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known with certainty, but it is likely that the name comes from the swampy land located here, which was called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was created by the merger of the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

origins.name: Uilenburgerwerf
origins.en: The island of Uilenburg, which together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken came to lie within the city in 1593. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known with certainty, but it is likely that the name comes from the swampy land located here, which was called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was created by the merger of the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

origins.name: Uilengouw
origins.en: Owl is the nickname of the Zunderdorpers

origins.name: Uitdammerdijk
origins.en: The hamlet of Uitdam, located on the IJsselmeerdijk north of the municipal boundary. The road came under the name Waterlandse zeedijk in Amsterdam when the former municipality of Ransdorp was abolished in 1921. (Uitdam = outside dam, outside dike.)

origins.name: Uiterwaardenstraat
origins.en: The land along the rivers between the summer and winter dikes, which run underwater in winter.

origins.name: Uitgeeststraat
origins.en: A village in Noord-Holland.

origins.name: Uithoornstraat
origins.en: The North Holland town of Uithoorn is named after this, because at the junction of this street on the Amstel River, the merchant ship of Uithoorn docked.

origins.name: Uitwegpad
origins.en: The Uitweg was for the construction of the Western Garden Cities (westelijke tuinsteden) of Slotermeer and Osdorp a country road between Osdorperweg and Haarlemmerweg, parallel and west of the former Slotermeer (now Sloterplas). Along this road were a number of farms, which are named in another part of this district.

origins.name: Uiverbrug
origins.en: The Uiver is the name of the legendary KLM aircraft, which participated in the London to Melbourne air race in 1934 and won the first prize in the handicap section of this race at the time. Like the Uiver, this bridge is also made of aluminum.

origins.name: Ukkelhof
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Uranusstraat
origins.en: The planet (Mars).

origins.name: Urkstraat
origins.en: Former island in the Zuiderzee, now located in the Noordoostpolder. The island was bought by Amsterdam in 1660 in connection with the control of the shipping route over the Zuiderzee.

origins.name: Utopia
origins.en: From 'ou topos', Ancient Greek for 'no place'. The concept was introduced in 1516 by the English humanist Thomas More, who in his book Utopia writes about a society of the same name, hypothetical with socialist and communist elements.

origins.name: Utrechtsedwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the city of Utrecht. is the new route to Utrecht. The old road ran via Duivendrecht and Abcoude.

origins.name: Utrechtsestraat
origins.en: Named after the city of Utrecht. The street leads to the Frederiksplein, where the Utrecht Gate used to stand (demolished in 1860). The Nieuwe Utrechtseweg is the new main route to Utrecht. The old road ran via Duivendrecht and Abcoude.

origins.name: Vaalmuiden
origins.en: The English port city of Falmouth, on the south coast of Cornwall, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Vaalrivierstraat
origins.en: River (tributary of the Orange River) that formed the border between Orange Free State and Transvaal. Known for the two Boer Wars of Freedom.

origins.name: Vaartstraat
origins.en: Channel.

origins.name: Valburgdreef
origins.en: Location in Gelderland, located near Nijmegen.

origins.name: Valckenierstraat
origins.en: Gillis Valckenier (1623-1680), nine times mayor of Amsterdam between 1665 and 1680. The street was laid out on the culverted section of the Nieuwe Lijnbaansgracht.

origins.name: Valentijnkade
origins.en: Francois Valentine (1666-1727), preacher and writer in the former Dutch East Indies. He wrote the standard work: Old and New East Indies. He also translated the Bible into Malay.

origins.name: Valeriusplein
origins.en: Adriaan Valerius (1575-1626), notary in Veere. Known for the collection of folk songs he established, still known today as 'Nederlandtsche Gedenckclanck'.

origins.name: Valeriusstraat
origins.en: Adriaan Valerius (1575-1626), notary in Veere. Known for the collection of folk songs he established, still known today as 'Nederlandtsche Gedenckclanck'.

origins.name: Valkenburgerstraat
origins.en: The island of Valkenburg or Marken, which came within the city around 1600. The origin of the name Valkenburg is unknown. It is possible that there was once a house with a facade stone or a shipyard with that name here. A facade stone with Valkenburg also occurs elsewhere (Nieuwendijk 62/68).

origins.name: Valkenisseweg
origins.en: Village that disappeared in January 1862 in a storm surge in the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Valkenstein
origins.en: Lost castle, which stood near Poortugaal on IJsselmonde (South Holland).

origins.name: Valkenweg
origins.en: The raptor. The beginning of the Valkenweg disappeared due to the construction of the IJ tunnel. The Valkenweg ferry was therefore renamed Adelaarsweg-pont (now Meeuwenlaan).

origins.name: Valkhof
origins.en: The Valkhof, located near the Waal Bridge in Nijmegen, was originally founded around 800 by Charlemagne. The castle was rebuilt by Emperor Frederick Barbarossa in 1155 and demolished in 1797, with the exception of the now still remaining Carolingian chapel and some wall remains.

origins.name: Valreep
origins.en: The opening in a ship's bulwark where the gangway ladder (valreepstrap) is fixed. Originally, it is the name of a rope ladder (reep = rope).

origins.name: Valschermkade
origins.en: Dutch word for parachute.

origins.name: Valutaboulevard
origins.en: Currency is the general word for currency unit.

origins.name: Van 't Hofflaan
origins.en: Jacobus H. van 't Hoff (1852-1911), chemist. Professor in Amsterdam from 1878 to 1896, then in Berlin. Lay the foundation for stereochemistry. Won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1901. This street was transferred from the municipality of Watergraafsmeer in 1921 under the name Koninginnelaan (council decision of Watergraafsneer, 1902).

origins.name: Van Abbestraat
origins.en: The Stedelijk Van Abbemuseum in Eindhoven. The art collector Henri van Abbe donated a museum for contemporary art to Eindhoven in 1936. The collection consisted mainly of works that Van Abbe himself had purchased. Over the years, the museum has built up an important collection with works by Picasso, Chagall, Mondrian and Appel, among others.

origins.name: Van Alphenstraat
origins.en: Hieronymus van Alphen (1746-1803), poet. Gained particular fame through his children's poetry.

origins.name: Van Baerlestraat
origins.en: Caspar van Baerle or Barlaeus (1584-1648), Reformed preacher, from 1632 professor at the Athenaeum. Renowned speaker and writer of Latin poems. Part of this street was originally called Houbrakenstraat (council decision, 1880) and another part Roelof Hartstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1893).

origins.name: Van Beuningenplein
origins.en: Coenraad van Beuningen (1622-1693), mayor of Amsterdam, statesman and envoy to various foreign courts.

origins.name: Van Beuningenstraat
origins.en: Coenraad van Beuningen (1622-1693), mayor of Amsterdam, statesman and envoy to various foreign courts.

origins.name: Van Bleiswijkstraat
origins.en: Pieter van Bleiswijk (1724-1790), statesman. From 1771 to 1787, he was the council pensionary of Holland. He joined the resistance against Stadhouder Willem V and was removed from office in 1787.

origins.name: Van Boetzelaerstraat
origins.en: Pieter Alexander baron van Boetzelaer (1759-1826), one of the mayors of Amsterdam from 1813 to 1824. After 1824, Amsterdam had a single mayor.

origins.name: Van Bommel-Van Dampad
origins.en: The Museum Van Bommel Van Dam in Venlo. In 1967, Maarten van Bommel and his wife Reina van Bommel-van Dam donated their art collection to the municipality of Venlo, which was housed in a museum named after the couple in 1971. The collection ranges from paintings and drawings by Dutch artists to wooden sculptures from Africa.

origins.name: Van Boshuizenstraat
origins.en: Koenraad van Boshuizen was bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland from 1515 to 1530.

origins.name: Van Bossestraat
origins.en: Peter Philip van Bosse (1809-1879), liberal statesman. Served as Minister of Finance and Colonies on several occasions. Advocated for free trade.

origins.name: Van Brakelstraat
origins.en: Jan van Brakel (1618-1690), naval officer under Admiral De Ruyter (Four-Day Naval Battle, voyage to Chatham).

origins.name: Van Breestraat
origins.en: Johannes Bernardus van Bree (1801-1857), composer, violinist, conductor and music educator. First conductor of the society Caecilia. Composed cantatas and masses.

origins.name: Van de Sande Bakhuijzenstraat
origins.en: The painter family Van de Sande Bakhuijzen, to which Hendrikus (1795-1860), representative of the romantic school, Julius (1835-1925), painter of cityscapes and landscapes and Gerardine (1826-1895), painter of flowers and fruit belong, among others.

origins.name: Van de Veldestraat
origins.en: The brothers Adriaen van de Velde (1636-1672), landscape painter, and Willem van de Velde (1633-1707), painter of seascapes.

origins.name: Van der Boechorststraat
origins.en: Lord Floris van der Boechorst, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland from 1340 to 1347.

origins.name: Van der Duijnstraat
origins.en: Adam F.J.A. Count van der Duijn van Maesdam (1771-1848). One of the trio (with Van Hogendorp and Van Limburg Stirum) who took charge of the government in 1813 and prepared for the restoration of the rule of the stadtholder's family.

origins.name: Van der Helstplein
origins.en: Bartholomeus van der Helst (1612-1670), painter of militia and regents' group portraits.

origins.name: Van der Hoopstraat
origins.en: Joan Cornelis van der Hoop (1742-1825), after the revolution of 1813 chairman of the provisional government of Amsterdam. In 1814 minister of the Navy.

origins.name: Van der Pekstraat
origins.en: Jan Ernst van der Pek (1865-1919), architect. Designed several blocks of workers' housing, mainly in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Van der Vijverstraat
origins.en: Cornelis van der Vijver (1789-1855), historian, in particular of old Amsterdam.

origins.name: Van Diemenkade
origins.en: Anthony van Diemen (1593-1645), Amsterdam merchant, who was governor-general of Dutch East Indies from 1636 to 1645. Together with Tasman, he discovered New Holland (Australia) and Van Diemen's Land. The street was laid out on the former Barentskade (council decision, 1878).

origins.name: Van Diemenstraat
origins.en: Anthony van Diemen (1593-1645), Amsterdam merchant, who was governor-general of Dutch East Indies from 1636 to 1645. Together with Tasman, he discovered New Holland (Australia) and Van Diemen's Land. The street was laid out on the former Barentskade (council decision, 1878).

origins.name: Van Eeghenlaan
origins.en: Christiaan Pieter van Eeghen (1816-1889), Amsterdam merchant, president-commissioner of the Nederlandsche Bank. Initiator of the construction of Vondelpark.

origins.name: Van Eeghenstraat
origins.en: Christiaan Pieter van Eeghen (1816-1889), Amsterdam merchant, president-commissioner of the Nederlandsche Bank. Initiator of the construction of Vondelpark.

origins.name: Van Effenstraat
origins.en: Justus van Effen (1684-1735), literary scholar. He supervised, among other things, the first Dutch translation of Defoe's 'Robinson Crusoe'.

origins.name: Van Gentstraat
origins.en: Willem J. baron van Gent (1626-1672), vice admiral. Rowed up the Thames in 1667 and captured the English admiral's ship (Chatham). Died in the Battle of Solebay in 1672. The street came to Amsterdam in 1921 under the name Piet Heinstraat (council decision of Sloten, 1910).

origins.name: Van Gilsestraat
origins.en: Maarten van Gilse (1918-1943), resistance fighter, born in Munich, executed in Amsterdam, and Jan Hendrik van Gilse (1912-1944), resistance fighter, born in Munich, executed in The Hague.

origins.name: Van Hallstraat
origins.en: Floris Adriaan van Hall (1791-1866), Amsterdam lawyer. As Minister of Finance in 1844 took drastic measures to reduce the enormous national debt. In 1848 leader of the conservative opposition.

origins.name: Van Hanxleden Houwertstraat
origins.en: Johan Coenraad H.F. van Hanxleden Houwert (1906-1945), resistance fighter, born in Medemblik, executed by firing squad in Limmen (North Holland).

origins.name: Van Heemskerckstraat
origins.en: Jacob van Heemskerck (1567-1607), sailor who was sent from Amsterdam in 1596 to search for a sea route to India 'around the north'. Heemskerck later became an admiral and died at Gibraltar against the Spanish. He is buried in the Old Church.

origins.name: Van Heenvlietlaan
origins.en: Jan van Heenvliet, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland 1396/1397.

origins.name: Van Helt Stocadestraat
origins.en: Nicolaas van Helt Stocade (1615-1669), painter, mainly of portraits.

origins.name: Van Hilligaertstraat
origins.en: Paulus van Hilligaert (1595-1640), painter.

origins.name: Van Hogendorpplein
origins.en: Gijsbert Karel van Hogendorp (1762-1834), liberal statesman, pensioner of Rotterdam. Prepared with Van der Duyn van Maasdam and Van Limburg Stirum the restoration of Dutch independence after the fall of Napoleon. Chairman of the Constitutional Commission.

origins.name: Van Hogendorpstraat
origins.en: Gijsbert Karel van Hogendorp (1762-1834), liberal statesman, pensioner of Rotterdam. Prepared with Van der Duyn van Maasdam and Van Limburg Stirum the restoration of Dutch independence after the fall of Napoleon. Chairman of the Constitutional Commission.

origins.name: Van Houweningenstraat
origins.en: Elsje van Houweningen, Hugo de Groot's valet, who helped him escape from Loevestein Castle by bookcase in 1621.

origins.name: Van Karnebeekstraat
origins.en: Jonkheer Abraham Pieter Cornelis van Karnebeek (1836-1925), statesman, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Vice-Chairman of the First Hague Peace Conference and Chairman of the Carnegie Foundation and Mr. Herman Adriaan van Karnebeek (1874-1942), statesman, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Chairman of the League of Nations Assembly and designer of the Belgian treaty.

origins.name: Van Kinsbergenstraat
origins.en: Jan Hendrik van Kinsbergen (1735-1819), admiral during the Battle of Doggersbank in 1781. Reorganized the navy.

origins.name: Van Koetsveldstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Eliza van Koetsveld (1807-1893), preacher and writer. His 'Religious and Moral Novellas' denounced the misery of emerging capitalism. His most famous novel is 'The Pasture of Mastland'.

origins.name: Van Leijenberghlaan
origins.en: Arent van Leyenbergh, around 1400 bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland.

origins.name: Van Limburg Stirumplein
origins.en: Leopold Count of Limburg Stirum (1758-1840), captain of the State army. In 1813 he took over the provisional government with Van Hogendorp and Van der Duyn van Maasdam and prepared the arrival of King William I.

origins.name: Van Limburg Stirumstraat
origins.en: Leopold Count of Limburg Stirum (1758-1840), captain of the State army. In 1813 he took over the provisional government with Van Hogendorp and Van der Duyn van Maasdam and prepared the arrival of King William I.

origins.name: Van Linschotenstraat
origins.en: Jan Huygen van Linschoten (1563-1611), well-known sailor and explorer. Wrote several travel stories about East and West Indies.

origins.name: Van Marumstraat
origins.en: Martinus van Marum (1750-1837), physician and mathematician. Developed an electrostatic generator and wrote a dissertation on fluid movement in plants. Since 1784 director of the Teylers Foundation.

origins.name: Van Middellandtstraat
origins.en: Pieter van Middellandt, rear admiral, fought under Admiral De Ruyter at Etna in 1676. Died in the same year in the Battle of Palermo.

origins.name: Van Miereveldstraat
origins.en: Michiel J. van Miereveld (1567-1641), portrait painter.

origins.name: Van Mierlobrug
origins.en: Henricus Antonius Franciscus Maria Oliva (Hans) van Mierlo (Breda, August 18, 1931 - Amsterdam, March 11, 2010) Dutch journalist and politician. In 1966, together with Hans Gruijters, he was the main initiator of the establishment of the social liberal party Democrats '66. For this party, he served as political leader for two separate periods and was a member of both the House of Representatives and the Senate (Eerste Kamer). In the 1980s, he was also Minister of Defense in the Van Agt II and III cabinets and from 1994 to 1998, he was Minister of Foreign Affairs and Vice Prime Minister in the 'purple' Kok I cabinet, which was partly due to him.

origins.name: Van Moerkerkenstraat
origins.en: Pieter Hendrik van Moerkerken (1877-1951), literary critic and art critic. He was a professor at the Academy of Fine Arts in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Van Mourik Broekmanstraat
origins.en: Gerrit H. van Mourik Broekman (1875-1948), civil engineer. From 1900 professor in Santiago (Chile) and advisor to the Chilean government. From 1924 professor in Delft.

origins.name: Van Musschenbroekstraat
origins.en: Petrus van Musschenbroek (1692-1761), physicist, professor in London, Utrecht and Leiden. He showed the length increase of a heated rod.

origins.name: Van Neckstraat
origins.en: Jacob van Neck (1564-1638), Dutch admiral, who made two trips to the Moluccas for the Dutch East India Company, laying the foundations for Dutch trade in East India. After that, he was mayor of Amsterdam several times.

origins.name: Van Nijenrodeweg
origins.en: Gijsbrecht van Nijenrode, in 1357-1358 bailiff of Amstelland, Waterland and Gooiland. A part of the road was abandoned in 1986 due to the construction of the Beysterveld street.

origins.name: Van Noordtkade
origins.en: Olivier van Noordt (1558-1627), sailor and ship captain, who sailed around the world via the Strait of Magellan from 1598 to 1601. He later documented this journey.

origins.name: Van Noordtstraat
origins.en: Olivier van Noordt (1558-1627), sailor and ship captain, who sailed around the world via the Strait of Magellan from 1598 to 1601. He later documented this journey.

origins.name: Van Oldenbarneveldtplein
origins.en: Van Oldenbarneveldt (1547-1619), statesman, Grand Pensionary of Holland. He gave the impetus for the establishment of the United East India Company. After many years of cooperation with Prince Maurice, he came into conflict and finally ended his life on the scaffold.

origins.name: Van Oldenbarneveldtstraat
origins.en: Van Oldenbarneveldt (1547-1619), statesman, Grand Pensionary of Holland. He gave the impetus for the establishment of the United East India Company. After many years of cooperation with Prince Maurice, he came into conflict and finally ended his life on the scaffold.

origins.name: Van Ollefenstraat
origins.en: Daan van Ollefen (1824-1900) and Christina da Silva (1809-1881), a theatrical actors' couple. Mrs. Van Ollefen-da Silva was one of the three stars of the Leidseplein.

origins.name: Van Ostadestraat
origins.en: Adriaan van Ostade (1610-1685), painter of peasant life. The section between Amsteldijk and Sweelinckstraat used to be called Hoedemakersstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1883) and numbered from Amsteldijk, as Kuipersstraat and other nearby streets that were laid out before 1896 by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel are still numbered today. When this section was named in the Van Ostadestraat in 1904, it had to be renumbered.

origins.name: Van Rappardstraat
origins.en: Willem Louis C. Ridder van Rappard (1798-1862), statesman. In 1847 Minister of Finance.

origins.name: Van Reedestraat
origins.en: Hendrik Adriaan van Reede tot Drakenstein (1636-1693), from an aristocratic family in Utrecht, left in 1656 in service of the VOC for Asia. There he studied the tropical flora to improve the supply of medicines.

origins.name: Van Reenenstraat
origins.en: Jonkheer Gerlach Cornelis Joannes van Reenen (1818-1893), mayor from 1850 to 1853, then minister of the Interior until 1856, and then chairman of the House of Representatives for many years and member of the Council of State.

origins.name: Van Reigersbergenstraat
origins.en: Maria van Reigersbergen (1589-1643), wife of Hugo de Groot.

origins.name: Van Rensselaerstraat
origins.en: Kiliaen van Rensselaer (1580-1646), jeweler, member of the Amsterdam chamber of the West India Company. Founded the colony of Rensselaerswijk near New Amsterdam (New York).

origins.name: Van Riebeeckhavenweg
origins.en: Jan Anthonie van Riebeeck or Riebeek (1618-1708), who in 1652, in the service of the Dutch East India Company, founded the Cape Colony at the Cape of Good Hope.

origins.name: Van Slingelandtplein
origins.en: Simon van Slingelandt (1666-1736), secretary of the Council of State from 1690 to 1725 and Grand Pensionary from 1727 to 1736. Strived for improvement of the state structure. Wrote political writings in four volumes.

origins.name: Van Slingelandtstraat
origins.en: Simon van Slingelandt (1666-1736), secretary of the Council of State from 1690 to 1725 and Grand Pensionary from 1727 to 1736. Strived for improvement of the state structure. Wrote political writings in four volumes.

origins.name: Van Speijkstraat
