origins.en: Jan Carel Josephus van Speyk (1802-1831), an Amsterdam orphan boy, who became a naval officer. During the Belgian uprising in 1831, he had his ship flown into the air near Antwerp because he refused to surrender.

origins.name: Van Spilbergenstraat
origins.en: Joris van Spilbergen (1568-1620), sailor. Made a round-the-world voyage from 1614 to 1617.

origins.name: Van Suchtelen van de Haarestraat
origins.en: Jonkheer Anthon Hendrik Peter Karel van Suchtelen van de Haare (1869-1946), last mayor of the municipality of Sloten (1909-1921).

origins.name: Van Swindendwarsstraat
origins.en: Jean Henri van Swinden (1746-1823), philosopher, mathematician and physicist, professor at Franeker and from 1785 in Amsterdam. He sat on the commission that fixed the metre, after which he worked out the metric system introduced in the Netherlands in 1816.

origins.name: Van Tuyll van Serooskerkenplein
origins.en: Frederik W.C.H. baron van Tuyll van Serooskerken (1851-1924), the first chairman of the Dutch Olympic Committee.

origins.name: Van Tuyll van Serooskerkenweg
origins.en: Frederik W.C.H. baron van Tuyll van Serooskerken (1851-1924), the first chairman of the Dutch Olympic Committee.

origins.name: Van Walbeeckstraat
origins.en: Johannes van Walbeeck (1601-1649), sea captain of the West Indian Company. Leader of the expedition to conquer Curaçao (1634).

origins.name: Van Woustraat
origins.en: Geert van Wou (1460-1524), famous bellfounder from Kampen.

origins.name: Van Zeggelaarstraat
origins.en: Gerrit van Zeggelaar (1868-1934), writer and publicist. Gained fame through his publications and lectures on Waterland. The street was transferred from the municipality of Landsmeer on 1-8-1966 with the names Thorbeckestraat, Borgesiusstraat and Groen van Prinstererstraat.

origins.name: Vancouverstraat
origins.en: George Vancouver (1757-1798), English sailor. He was the first to sail around the island named after him (off the west coast of Canada).

origins.name: Varenweg
origins.en: Plant family, which reproduces by spores.

origins.name: Varikstraat
origins.en: Former municipality on the Waal, in the Tielerwaard (Gelderland). Now falls under the municipality of Neerijnen.

origins.name: Varkenssluis
origins.en: This bridge is named after the pig market, which was held here in the sixteenth century

origins.name: Vasco da Gamastraat
origins.en: Portuguese explorer (1469-1524), found the sea route around Cape of Good Hope in 1497.

origins.name: Vätternkade
origins.en: The second largest lake in Sweden, located in the south of the country.

origins.name: Vechtstraat
origins.en: The river that flows into the IJsselmeer near Muiden.

origins.name: Veelaan
origins.en: Named after the former livestock market.

origins.name: Veemarkt
origins.en: Named after the former livestock market.

origins.name: Veemkade
origins.en: Company that takes goods into custody and operates warehouses. The Dutch vemen grew out of the seventeenth-century guilds of weigh-house porters (waagdragers).

origins.name: Veenbesstraat
origins.en: Red, sometimes white currant, with a fresh taste. There are two types: the small bog currant and the cranberry. The first grows in upland bog areas, the second is common on Terschelling, after a barrel of cranberries washed ashore there in the mid-nineteenth century.

origins.name: Veenendaalplein
origins.en: Location in the Gelderse Valley (Utrecht).

origins.name: Veerstraat
origins.en: A ferry is a place where - and a boat with which - one is taken across a waterway.

origins.name: Veeteeltstraat
origins.en: The sector of the agricultural company that deals with the keeping (and breeding) of livestock.

origins.name: Vegastraat
origins.en: The star Vega or Wega in the constellation Lyra. One of the brightest stars in the northern sky.

origins.name: Velazquezstraat
origins.en: Diego Rodriguez de Silvary Velazquez (1599-1660). Spanish painter of historical works and portraits.

origins.name: Veldbiesstraat
origins.en: Grass species. Mainly found on the northern hemisphere.

origins.name: Veldhuizenstraat
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Vleuten-de Meern (Utrecht).

origins.name: Veldzicht
origins.en: Farm on the former Uitweg, demolished for the construction of the Western Garden Cities (westelijke tuinsteden). Before 1975, this street was called Heijningspad (council decision, 1958), which was withdrawn when the name of the Heining was given.

origins.name: Velserweg
origins.en: The North Holland municipality of Velsen, where the North Sea Canal was dug through the dunes. The road ran, until the excavation of the Van Riebeeckhaven, from Sloterdijk to the municipal border and had the names Middenweg (Grote IJpolder) and Frogerweg before the naming in 1938.

origins.name: Veluwelaan
origins.en: Part of the province of Gelderland between the Gelderse Valley and the Gelderse IJssel.

origins.name: Venetiëhof
origins.en: Italian port city, on which the former KNSM (see KNSM-laan) maintained a scheduled service.

origins.name: Venetiëstraat
origins.en: Italian port city, on which the former KNSM (see KNSM-laan) maintained a scheduled service.

origins.name: Venhuizenstraat
origins.en: The village between Hoorn and Enkhuizen (North Holland).

origins.name: Vennepluimstraat
origins.en: Type of reed.

origins.name: Verbindingsdam
origins.en: Dam in Ertshaven

origins.name: Verbindingstraat
origins.en: The names express the function. The dam is the connection between the IJ island, which was built in 1898, and the Handelskade. The street was built even before the major annexation of 1896, to enable the residents of Nieuwer-Amstel, who lived here on the edge of Amsterdam, to reach their town hall on the Amsteldijk on their own territory.

origins.name: Verdistraat
origins.en: Giuseppe Verdi (1813-1901), Italian opera composer. Composed among others 'Aida', 'Rigoletto' and 'La Traviata'.

origins.name: Verfstraat
origins.en: Reference to the Vettewinkel paint factory, later Sigma, which was located on the Cruquiusterrein from 1934 to 2008.

origins.name: Verlengde Stellingweg
origins.en: A stelling is a gallery on struts around a tall mill. From this gallery the cap is turned into the wind and the sails are taken in. In 1976, for traffic technical reasons, part of the Stellingweg was renamed Molenaarsweg, while another part was added to Appelweg.

origins.name: Verleunstraat
origins.en: Johannes Adrianus Jozef Verleun (1919-1944), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed in The Hague.

origins.name: Veronesestraat
origins.en: Paolo Cagliari, called Veronese (1528-1588), Italian painter of large decorative canvases.

origins.name: Vertrouwen
origins.en: Vertrouwen in achieving the stated goal.

origins.name: Verversstraat
origins.en: This occupational name reminds us of the cloth (laken) industry, an important industry in Amsterdam in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The cloth dyers were only allowed to settle between the Kloveniersburgwal and the Zwanenburgwal after 1593. The Groenburgwal was called Verversgracht at that time.

origins.name: Vervoorenstraat
origins.en: Louis Christiaan Vervooren (1895-1944), resistance fighter, born in Rotterdam, killed in Bruttig (Germany).

origins.name: Vespuccistraat
origins.en: Amerigo Vespucci (1451- 1512), Florentine explorer. He sailed and described the American coasts. It is likely that America was named after him and not after Columbus.

origins.name: Vianenstraat
origins.en: Fortified town on the Lek (South Holland).

origins.name: Victor Rutgersstraat
origins.en: Victor Henri Rutgers (1877-1945), resistance fighter, killed in the Bochum concentration camp (Germany). Rutgers was a lawyer and statesman, Minister of Education in 1925 and from 1928 professor at the Vrije Universiteit in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Victoria Welbystraat
origins.en: Victoria Welby (1837 – 1912) was a prominent British philosopher and linguist

origins.name: Victorieplein
origins.en: The square was named this in 1946 in connection with the victory of the Allied countries. Previously it was called Daniël Willinkplein, after the poet (1676-1722), known for his Amstellandse Arcadia. (council decision, 1922).

origins.name: Vier Heemskinderensluis
origins.en: This bridge is named after the facade stone with the Vier Heemskinderen on the corner building of the Herengracht and the Leidsegracht.

origins.name: Vier Heemskinderenstraat
origins.en: Named after the facade stone with the Vier Heemskinderen on the corner building of the Herengracht and the Leidsegracht.

origins.name: Vierde Vogelstraat
origins.en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

origins.name: Viermasterstraat
origins.en: A sailing ship, usually a barque, with four masts.

origins.name: Vierwindendwarsstraat
origins.en: This peculiar name is probably derived from a facade stone of a house or warehouse, which stood here on the Realeneiland. Such a stone gave the house on the Lindengracht the name of ''t huis in de vier blazende winden'.

origins.name: Vierwindenstraat
origins.en: This peculiar name is probably derived from a facade stone of a house or warehouse, which stood here on the Realeneiland. Such a stone gave the house on the Lindengracht the name of ''t huis in de vier blazende winden'.

origins.name: Vijfde Vogelstraat
origins.en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

origins.name: Vijgepeerpad
origins.en: Old Dutch pear variety. The path is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Vijverhoef
origins.en: Old knight's manor house near Breukelen on the Vecht, originally from 1670, demolished in 1812. Sung by Vondel. The current Vijverhof, on the same site, dates from 1867.

origins.name: Vijzelgracht
origins.en: The name is probably derived from the former inhabitants Cornelis Arents Vijselaar (around 1600) and Jan Vijselaar (around 1632). Vijzelstraat was then a short street and ran to the current Reguliersdwarsstraat. When the street was extended, the name also passed on to this extension. Until the eighteenth century, people spoke of Old and New Vijzelstraat. The Vijzelgracht, dug between 1660 and 1670, was filled in in 1934.

origins.name: Vijzelstraat
origins.en: The name is probably derived from the former inhabitants Cornelis Arents Vijselaar (around 1600) and Jan Vijselaar (around 1632). The Vijzelstraat was then a short street and ran to the current Reguliersdwarsstraat. When the street was extended, the name also passed on to this extension. Until the eighteenth century, people spoke of Old and New Vijzelstraat. The Vijzelgracht, dug between 1660 and 1670, was filled in 1934.

origins.name: Vikingpad
origins.en: Collective name for groups of adventurers, exiles, merchants, settlers from Denmark, Norway and Sweden, who raided the coasts of 'Friesland' in particular in the ninth century.

origins.name: Vilvoordestraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Vincent van Goghstraat
origins.en: Vincent Willem van Gogh (1853-1890) painter and draughtsman. Initially worked in the Borinage and Drenthe, before leaving for France in 1886, where he produced most and most famous paintings. He has been of great significance for the development of painting.

origins.name: Vinkenstraat
origins.en: The strip south of the Haarlemmerdijk, between the current Binnen Oranjestraat and the Haarlemmerplein, was called the Rietvink in the sixteenth century after an old inn. The street laid out here in the seventeenth century was alternately called Rietstraat, Vinkenstraat and Middenstraat. Of these, the name Vinkenstraat finally remained. In 1566, the first public sermon was held for the Protestants on the Rietvink. Within the city, this was not yet allowed at that time.

origins.name: Violette Corneliushof
origins.en: Photographer (1919-1998). Became involved in the artist resistance during World War II. Worked for the illegal magazine 'De Vrije Kunstenaar' and later for the Persoonsbewijzen Centrale. After the war, she developed into an architecture photographer and eventually chose reportage photography.

origins.name: Violettenstraat
origins.en: An outdated name for the flower the violet.

origins.name: Virginiahof
origins.en: Virginia Dementricia, later Virginia Gaai (Aruba, 1842 - after 1867), was a slave and who rebelled against her owners in Aruba. She repeatedly violated the rules imposed on her and was punished with forced labor every time. In 1859 she tried to run away but failed and resulted in more heavy labor and a prison sentence. Shortly after her release, Virginia was arrested again and accused of 'street disorder and resistance to the police'. This time she received a life sentence. Her owner sold her in 1860. In 1863 slavery was abolished. The last thing known about her is that she gave birth to a son in Willemstad on June 2, 1867: Marcelino Martis Gaai.

origins.name: Virginiastraat
origins.en: Virginia Dementricia, later Virginia Gaai (Aruba, 1842 - after 1867), was a slave and who rebelled against her owners in Aruba. She repeatedly violated the rules imposed on her and was punished with forced labor every time. In 1859 she tried to run away but failed and resulted in more heavy labor and a prison sentence. Shortly after her release, Virginia was arrested again and accused of 'street disorder and resistance to the police'. This time she received a life sentence. Her owner sold her in 1860. In 1863 slavery was abolished. The last thing known about her is that she gave birth to a son in Willemstad on June 2, 1867: Marcelino Martis Gaai.

origins.name: Visseringstraat
origins.en: Simon Vissering (1818-1888), professor of political science in Leiden, Minister of Finance. He already campaigned in 1848 for IJmuiden as a new seaport.

origins.name: Viveportenstraat
origins.en: Kapeldorp on Terschelling, disappeared in the sixteenth century due to storm surges.

origins.name: Vlaardingenlaan
origins.en: City in South Holland, on the Nieuwe Maas.

origins.name: Vlaggemast
origins.en: The ship's mast to which the flag is attached.

origins.name: Vlakkerweg
origins.en: Occupational name for someone who flattens metal with a flatter (slechthamer, a flat-faced hammer), that is, makes it smooth. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Vleutenstraat
origins.en: Location in Utrecht.

origins.name: Vliegtuigstraat
origins.en: The means of transport through the air, using surfaces (wings).

origins.name: Vlielandstraat
origins.en: Wadden island (Friesland).

origins.name: Vlierweg
origins.en: Plant, with white flowers and black berries.

origins.name: Vlietstraat
origins.en: Drainage channel.

origins.name: Vlimmerenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Vlothavenweg
origins.en: The nearby Vlothaven, dug in 1931, was originally shallow and part of the timber port intended for timber barges. Around 1960, the harbor was deepened and adapted for sea vessels.

origins.name: Vluchthavenbrug
origins.en: Probably named after that part of the harbor where small ships could dock in case of bad weather.

origins.name: VOC-kade
origins.en: The United East India Company (VOC), founded in 1602 for trade in East India. The management was in the hands of seventeen directors. From Batavia, the administrative Amsterdam-Centrum Asia, a network of trading settlements was established. In 1799 the state took over the company.

origins.name: Voetbalstraat
origins.en: Refers to the sports park that was here with football clubs

origins.name: Voetboogstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out on the shooting range of the Doelen der Voetboogschutters in 1649.

origins.name: Vogelenzangstraat
origins.en: Village in the dune area, on the edge of the Amsterdam waterworks dunes.

origins.name: Vogelkade
origins.en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

origins.name: Vogelplantsoen
origins.en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

origins.name: Vogelplein
origins.en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

origins.name: Volendammerweg
origins.en: Village southeast of Edam, known for its traditional clothing.

origins.name: Volewijkshof
origins.en: The peninsula north of the IJ, directly opposite the center of Amsterdam. As early as 1360, there was a gallows field here, where the bodies of executed people were hung and exhibited. After the arrival of the Batavian Republic in 1795, this practice was prohibited.

origins.name: Volharding
origins.en: Volharding in pursuit of the goal.

origins.name: Volkerakstraat
origins.en: Water between Overflakkee and North Brabant, which was closed off from Haringvliet and Hollands Diep (Hellegatsplein) by a dam in 1970.

origins.name: Voltaplein
origins.en: Alessandro Volta (1745-1827). Italian physicist, professor at Pavia. Made several inventions in the field of electricity. A unit of electrical voltage is named after him, the 'Volt'.

origins.name: Voltastraat
origins.en: Alessandro Volta (1745-1827). Italian physicist, professor at Pavia. Made several inventions in the field of electricity. A unit of electrical voltage is named after him, the 'Volt'.

origins.name: Von Guerickestraat
origins.en: Otto von Guericke (1602-1682), German physicist, inventor of the air pump and the electrostat machine. They are named after him the Maagdenburger (half) spheres, for demonstrating the effect of atmospheric pressure (Von Guericke was mayor of Magdeburg). The street was originally named Wolmaranstraat, established by the municipality of Watergraafsmeer (council decision, 1915). In 1922, all the streets in this neighborhood were given different names.

origins.name: Von Humboldtstraat
origins.en: Alexander baron von Humboldt (1769-1859), natural scientist and scientific explorer. Traveled South America and Siberia. Founder of climatology and plant geography.

origins.name: Von Liebigweg
origins.en: Justus von Liebig (1803-1873), German chemist. Researcher of artificial fertilization. He invented a method for the preparation of meat extract.

origins.name: Von Zesenstraat
origins.en: Philipp von Zesen (1619-1689), German historian. He wrote, among other things, 'Beschreibung der Stadt Amsterdam'.

origins.name: Vondelbrug
origins.en: Joost van den Vondel (1587-1679) was a poet who wrote many tragic plays, the most famous of which is 'Gijsbrecht van Aemstel'.

origins.name: Vondelkerkstraat
origins.en: The street was taken over from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under this name. A decision to name it by that municipality and the reason why has not been found. The Vondelkerk, built in 1873 under the architecture of Pierre Cuypers, is about a kilometer away from here and therefore cannot have been the reason for the naming of this street.

origins.name: Vondelpark
origins.en: Joost van den Vondel (1587-1679), poet. He wrote 24 tragedies, as well as poetry on heroes and heroic deeds. The part of the street that was in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1896 was first called Verlengde Vondelstraat. Under the leadership of C.P. van Eeghen, a number of Amsterdamers designed the plan for the construction of a Riding and Walking Park in 1864, and then carried it out according to a design by L.D. Zocher. The first part was opened in 1865. When a statue of Vondel was placed here in 1867, the park was renamed Vondelpark.

origins.name: Vondelstraat
origins.en: Joost van den Vondel (1587-1679), poet. He wrote 24 tragedies, as well as poetry on heroes and heroic deeds. The part of the street that was in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1896 was first called Verlengde Vondelstraat. Under the leadership of C.P. van Eeghen, a number of Amsterdamers designed the plan for the construction of a Riding and Walking Park in 1864, and then carried it out according to a design by L.D. Zocher. The first part was opened in 1865. When a statue of Vondel was placed here in 1867, the park was named Vondelpark.

origins.name: Voorburgstraat
origins.en: Village in South Holland, suburb of The Hague.

origins.name: Voordek
origins.en: One of the ship decks.

origins.name: Voordewind
origins.en: Ship term, in particular in sailing: the wind directly from behind. The term is also used figuratively a lot.

origins.name: Voorlandpad
origins.en: Former manor house on the Middenweg, built in 1689 as Meerenburg, renamed Voorland in 1722. The manor house was demolished in 1934 to make way for the Ajax stadium De Meer.

origins.name: Voormalige Stadstimmertuin
origins.en: From 1660 to 1899, the City Timberyards were located here (timber workshops and storage facilities for building materials). Today, this site is located on Van Reigersbergenstraat.

origins.name: Voornestraat
origins.en: The western part of the South Holland island of Voorne-Putten.

origins.name: Voorsteven
origins.en: The front part of the ship's hull.

origins.name: Voorthuizenstraat
origins.en: The village in the municipality of Barneveld (Gelderland).

origins.name: Vorselaarstraat
origins.en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Vorticellaweg
origins.en: Microscopically small aquatic creature. Single-celled ciliate with a bell-shaped head and a contractile stalk.

origins.name: Vosmaerstraat
origins.en: Carel Vosmaer (1826-1888), writer and critic. Clerk at the Court of The Hague, then of the Supreme Court. Originally a classicist, later supported the movement of the Eighties. Wrote among other things 'Nanno', and a translation of the Iliad and the Odyssey.

origins.name: Vossenbesstraat
origins.en: Also known as lingonberry (cowberry). Plant from the heath family, native to the Netherlands, and growing in poor soil. The lingonberry is usually processed into compote due to its sour, slightly bitter taste.

origins.name: Vossiusstraat
origins.en: Gerardus Johannes Voss, calling himself Vossius (1577-1649), philologist and historian, professor successively in Heidelberg, Leiden and from 1631 together with Barlaeus at the Amsterdam Athenaeum. His textbook on rhetoric (1648) had a great influence.

origins.name: Vredeman de Vriesstraat
origins.en: Jan Vredeman de Vries (1527-1606), architect and painter, also worked in several foreign cities. Through his designs, books and engravings, he spread the Dutch Renaissance.

origins.name: Vredenburgerbrug
origins.en: Catholic nursing home Vredenburg was built, now converted into houses. Before the inn, there were successively

origins.name: Vredenburgersteeg
origins.en: In the seventeenth century a very well-known inn, which stood on the site where in 1835 the Roman Catholic nursing home Vredenburg was built. Now converted into houses. Before the inn, there was successively a brewery owned by mayor Kornelis Jacobsz and a salt trader's business. Hence the former names Cornelis Jacobsz Brouwersteeg and Zoutkoperssteeg. The name Rottenest also came up.

origins.name: Vredenhofpad
origins.en: Named after the adjacent Vredenhof cemetery on the Haarlemmerweg.

origins.name: Vredenhofweg
origins.en: Named after the adjacent Vredenhof cemetery on the Haarlemmerweg.

origins.name: Vredespleintje
origins.en: The name was chosen in 2016 by the residents and refers to the theme of 'peace' about which at least thirteen eighteenth and nineteenth-century writers named in the neighborhood have written. In the past, the square was the place for the Solidarity Festival, and in 2010 for the festival 'World Citizens of Amsterdam'.

origins.name: Vreelandplein
origins.en: Village on the Vecht (Utrecht). The castle of the same name was demolished in 1529 at the request of Charles V.

origins.name: Vreeswijkpad
origins.en: Utrecht town on the Lek, opposite Vianen. Now part of the municipality of Nieuwegein.

origins.name: Vriesseveem
origins.en: A veem is a company that stores goods in its warehouses and delivers them from there. Each veem had its own emblem, after which it was named. These could be hats of different colours and shapes (among them Blauwhoeden, blue hats, and Klapmutsen). They also took their names from where their workmen came from (among them the Vriesseveem and the Zeeuwse Veem).

origins.name: Vrijburg
origins.en: Former country house on the Haarlemmerweg.

origins.name: Vrije Geer
origins.en: Old name of part of the municipality of Sloten, a triangular area, that extended from the southeast corner of the Slotermeer to the Haarlemmermeer. The area was outside the jurisdiction (1100 rods) of Amsterdam. The inhabitants of the Vrije Geer were traditionally exempt from paying certain fines to the counts of Holland.

origins.name: Vrijheidslaan
origins.en: This lane, which originally was called Amstellaan, was changed to Stalinlaan after World War II, after the Soviet leader Joseph Stalin, because the Soviet Union together with the Allies achieved our liberation. After the Russian intervention in the Hungarian uprising in 1956, the name was changed to Vrijheidslaan.

origins.name: Vrijzicht
origins.en: A former farm in the old municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Vrolikstraat
origins.en: Gerardus Vrolik (1775-1859) and his son Willem Vrolik (1801-1863), both professors of medicine in Amsterdam. They collected an extensive collection of anatomical preparations. The first part of this street is now called Wibautstraat.

origins.name: Vrouwenmantelstraat
origins.en: Plant, native to Europe, North and West Asia, North America and Greenland. Has been traditionally used, among other things, against severe menstrual pain and menopausal complaints.

origins.name: Vuurwerkerplantsoen
origins.en: A pyrotechnician is a profession or was a profession within the metal industry

origins.name: Vuurwerkerweg
origins.en: Occupational name, someone who works with the glowing metal in a forge.

origins.name: W.J. Bijleveldstraat
origins.en: Wolter Jan Bijleveld (1902-1945), resistance fighter, born in Makassar, died in Vaiklingen (Germany). He was head of the Connections and Intelligence Service of the Order Service (O.D.).

origins.name: W.J. Knoopstraat
origins.en: Lieutenant General (1811-1894), co-founder of the Dutch Red Cross.

origins.name: W.L. Penningstraat
origins.en: Willem Levinus Penning (1840-1924), poet under the pseudonym M. Coens.

origins.name: Waagdragerhof
origins.en: Waagdragers (weigh-house porters) were responsible for weighing goods in the Waag. They carried the goods from the warehouses to the Waag to weigh them.

origins.name: Waaigat
origins.en: Old name for an opening in the canal wall. Wave holes were also there on Warmoesstraat and Rapenburgerstraat.

origins.name: Waalenburgsingel
origins.en: Polder on Texel (north of the village of De Waal). Meadow and swamp lands with extensive fauna and flora.

origins.name: Waalseilandbrug
origins.en: Named after the word 'waal' which means a piece of water surrounded by rows of poles in which ships could overwinter or be repaired

origins.name: Waalstraat
origins.en: Branch of the Rhine from Nijmegen to Gorinchem. Then flows together with the Maas, after which it is called the Merwede.

origins.name: Waddendijk
origins.en: Shallow area outside the dikes that falls dry at low tide, especially in the Wadden Sea.

origins.name: Waddenweg
origins.en: Shallow area outside the dikes that falls dry at low tide, especially in the Wadden Sea.

origins.name: Wagenaarstraat
origins.en: Jan Wagenaar (1709-1773), historian, city historian of Amsterdam, wrote among other things 'Fatherland History' (21 volumes) and a history of Amsterdam in three volumes.

origins.name: Wageningendreef
origins.en: Location in Gelderland.

origins.name: Wagenstraat
origins.en: The name recalls the car park - a place for cars that came from outside the city - near the Regulierspoort.

origins.name: Wakkerstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Philippus van Medenbach Wakker (1784-1860), notary and mayor of the municipality of Watergraafsmeer from 1817 to 1853. The street is named after him, because he lived there.

origins.name: Walborg
origins.en: Seventeenth-century country house, located on the Maas in the municipality of Laak (Limburg). Today only a ruin remains.

origins.name: Walcherenstraat
origins.en: One of the Zeeuwse islands. Due to the poldering of the Sloe, now completely connected to Zuid-Beveland.

origins.name: Waldeck Pyrmontlaan
origins.en: A former German princely house. This family produced Queen Emma, the second wife of King William III and mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

origins.name: Waldenlaan
origins.en: 'Walden; or, Life in the Woods', philosophical and socially critical book by the American Henry Thoreau from 1854, which describes his Spartan living conditions in a self-built cottage in nature.

origins.name: Walenpleintje
origins.en: The square owes its name to the Old Walloon Church located here. This church is the old monastery church of the former monastery of the Pauls Brothers. The name had already existed unofficially for centuries. The naming took place on the occasion of the celebration of the fourth centenary of the Alteration of May 26, 1578.

origins.name: Wallestein
origins.en: Former seventeenth-century country house, near Loenersloot (Utrecht). Demolished in the nineteenth century.

origins.name: Wally Moespad
origins.en: Wally Moes (1856-1918), painter of genre scenes and portraits, also made etchings.

origins.name: Walraven van Hallweg
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1906-1945), born in Amsterdam, executed in Haarlem.

origins.name: Walvisvaart
origins.en: The Oostzanerwerf was one of the centers of the whaling industry in the 17th and 18th centuries, where generations of commanders and crew members of whaling ships lived. There was also a lot of activity related to whaling.

origins.name: Wamberg
origins.en: Nobleman's house, whose oldest wing dates back to 1560. Expanded in 1769 and early twentieth century. Located on the Aa outside the village of Berlicum (North Brabant).

origins.name: Wamelplein
origins.en: Village in the Land of Maas and Waal, opposite Tiel (Gelderland).

origins.name: Wamelstraat
origins.en: Village in the Land of Maas and Waal, opposite Tiel (Gelderland).

origins.name: Wannepad
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Liège.

origins.name: Wanningstraat
origins.en: Joannes Wanning, musician, born in Kampen, organist at Danzig (Germany/Poland). Lived at the end of the sixteenth century and beginning of the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Ward Bingleystraat
origins.en: Dutch actor of English birth (1757-1818). Often performed in national tragic plays.

origins.name: Waregemstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

origins.name: Warmelo
origins.en: Fortified noble house near Diepenheim (Overijssel), originally sixteenth and seventeenth century. Restored in 1928. Property of Prince Bernhard and inhabited by his mother Princess Armgard.

origins.name: Warmoesstraat
origins.en: The current Warmoesstraat had two names until the seventeenth century: Kerkstraat for the northern part up to the Oude Kerk, and Warmoesstraat for the southern part, probably after the radish or vegetable market held here. Later, the entire street was given this name. Finally, in the twentieth century, the part where the Krasnapolsky Hotel is located was added to the Dam.

origins.name: Warmondstraat
origins.en: Location in South Holland, north of Leiden.

origins.name: Warnsborn
origins.en: Former estate, now nature reserve located west of Arnhem.

origins.name: Watergangseweg
origins.en: Village on the North Holland Canal, in the municipality of Landsmeer.

origins.name: Waterkeringweg
origins.en: Any natural or artificial barrier that holds back the water, such as a dam, dike or lock. The street is located on the former premises of the Municipal Waterworks, in a neighborhood where all streets begin with 'water'.

origins.name: Waterlandplein
origins.en: Waterland is in broad terms the area between Amsterdam, Zaandam, Purmerend and Monnickendam. In fact a large nature reserve.

origins.name: Waterlooplein
origins.en: Named after the Battle of Waterloo in 1815. The square was created in 1874 by filling in the Houtgracht and the Leprozengracht.

origins.name: Watermaalpad
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Watermanstraat
origins.en: The constellation and zodiac sign.

origins.name: Waterpoortsteeg
origins.en: Recalls the Waterpoort, formerly a small passage in the city wall as a connection to the Lastage, which was located outside the city at the time.

origins.name: Waterpoortweg
origins.en: Gate in a fence. Defensive work built over a moat. The street is located on the former site of the Municipal Waterworks, in a neighborhood where all streets begin with 'water'.

origins.name: Waterschapstraat
origins.en: A water board is a public legal body that manages the maintenance of flood defenses and the drainage of a certain area.

origins.name: Watervoort
origins.en: Corrupted spelling of the Irish port city of Waterford, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Watteaustraat
origins.en: Jean Antoine Watteau (1684-1721), French painter, painted in Rococo style.

origins.name: Waverstraat
origins.en: River on the border of North Holland and Utrecht.

origins.name: Wedderborg
origins.en: The castle at Wedde (Groningen), originally built in 1362 and rebuilt in 1530 at the behest of Charles of Gelder. The remains of the old wall were exposed in 1957.

origins.name: Weegbreestraat
origins.en: The plant family (gentians).

origins.name: Weegschaalhof
origins.en: The zodiac sign and constellation in the zodiac.

origins.name: Weenahof
origins.en: The Weena Castle, first mentioned in 1306. It was a water castle and was located at the mouth of the Rotte, within the current Rotterdam.

origins.name: Weerdestein
origins.en: Castle, mentioned as early as 1340, near Nederlangbroek (Utrecht), in 1548 a knightly manor (ridderhofstad). Single square tower, surrounded by three moats, restored in 1870. The gate building dates from 1642.

origins.name: Weerslootpad
origins.en: Common name for canals in North Holland.

origins.name: Weesperplein
origins.en: The street runs in the direction of - and is therefore named after - the city of Weesp. At the end of the street was formerly the Weesperpoort, and along the extension, outside the Singelgracht, the Weesperpoort station (demolished 1939). The buildings along Weesperstraat were demolished between 1950 and 1960, after which it gained its current width.

origins.name: Weesperstraat
origins.en: The street runs in the direction of - and is therefore named after - the city of Weesp. At the end of the street was formerly the Weesperpoort, and along the extension, outside the Singelgracht, the Weesperpoort station (demolished 1939). The buildings along the Weesperstraat were demolished between 1950 and 1960, after which it gained its current width.

origins.name: Weesperzijde
origins.en: The Weesperzijde was already the main route to the direction of Weesp since the drying of the Watergraafsmeer. The name was given to distinguish it from the other side of the Amstel, which was formerly called the Utrechtsezijde (today Amsteldijk).

origins.name: Weidestraat
origins.en: Agricultural concept: the grassland on which livestock farming is carried out. By council decision in 1974, part of the Weidestraat was added to the Gaffelstraat and the Harkstraat.

origins.name: Weissenbruchstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Johannes Weissenbruch (1825-1903), landscape painter, pupil of Andreas Schelfhout.

origins.name: Weissensingel
origins.en: The lake, the Weissensee, located in Carinthia in Austria.

origins.name: Weissmanstraat
origins.en: Adriaan Willem Weissman (1858-1923), Amsterdam architect. Built the Stedelijk Museum (1895) among other things. Founder and first secretary of the Bond Heemschut.

origins.name: Weldam
origins.en: Stately, rising from the water, noble house near Markelo (Overijssel), built in 1644 using medieval masonry. Surrounded by a garden in eighteenth-century style.

origins.name: Welnastraat
origins.en: Former country house on the Amstel

origins.name: Welsumerstraat
origins.en: Welsumer is a less well-known chicken breed, bred from various other breeds and named after the village of Welsum (north of Deventer).

origins.name: Wembleylaan
origins.en: Stadium in London. Ajax won the final of the European Cup for Champions on June 2, 1971 at this stadium. Ajax-Panathinaikos (2-0).

origins.name: Wenslauerstraat
origins.en: This is probably the name of a landowner or construction company that built here. Before 1896, this street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under the same name.

origins.name: Werengouw
origins.en: A weir is an elongated plot of land between two boundary ditches. The ditch between two posts is also called a weir ditch. By council decision in 1971, part of the road was added to Buikslotermeerplein.

origins.name: Werfkade
origins.en: Refers to the shipyards that used to be here

origins.name: Werfstraat
origins.en: Refers to the shipyards that used to be here

origins.name: Werkendamstraat
origins.en: Village on the Merwede in the Land of Altena (North Brabant).

origins.name: Werkhovenstraat
origins.en: Village on the Kromme Rijn near Bunnik (Utrecht).

origins.name: Werktuigstraat
origins.en: Tools. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Wervershoofstraat
origins.en: Village near Medemblik.

origins.name: Wessel Gansfortstraat
origins.en: Johan Wessel Gansfort (1419-1489), biblical humanist, professor in Heidelberg, returned to the Netherlands in 1479. Through his opposition to the indulgence trade and the infallibility of the Pope, he can be considered a precursor of the Reformation.

origins.name: Wessel Ilckenstraat
origins.en: Jazz musician (1923-1957), drummer. From 1950 onwards, he performed with his own formation. Until his death, he was undisputed the driving force of Dutch modern jazz. The annual Dutch jazz grand prize is named after him.

origins.name: Westbroekplein
origins.en: Village near Maartensdijk (Utrecht).

origins.name: Westbroekstraat
origins.en: Village near Maartensdijk (Utrecht).

origins.name: Westeinde
origins.en: Named after its location: west of the Utrechtsepoort. Also

origins.name: Westelijke Merwedekanaaldijk
origins.en: The Merwedekanaal, now the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal, dug between Amsterdam and Vreeswijk, was completed in 1892 after a long ordeal. This canal was against the wishes of Amsterdam and the Chamber of Commerce, which were in favor of a canal through the Gelderse valley.

origins.name: Westerdok
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Westerdoksdijk
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Westerdokskade
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Westerduinenstraat
origins.en: Nature monument on the island of Texel, between Den Hoorn and De Koog. The area includes dunes, gullies and heathlands.

origins.name: Westergasbrug
origins.en: This steel loading bridge is named after the former Westergasfabriek that operated here from 1885 to 1985

origins.name: Westerhoofd
origins.en: The western harbor head of the Coenhaven.

origins.name: Westerkade
origins.en: The quay is located on the west side of the Lijnbaansgracht. This is probably the reason for the naming.

origins.name: Westerkoggestraat
origins.en: A polder in West-Friesland.

origins.name: Westerlengte
origins.en: The distance in degrees in a westerly direction, measured from the first meridian.

origins.name: Westermarkt
origins.en: When the square was built in 1616, it was named Keizersmarkt, but with the construction of the Westerkerk, completed in 1630, the square came to be known as Westermarkt in popular parlance and thus displaced the official name Keizersmarkt.

origins.name: Westerpark
origins.en: When it was built, the park was located in the western part of the then-city. The park was built on the site where the first station of the Hollandse Spoor stood from 1843 to 1878. The street was part of the Houtmankade before 1979.

origins.name: Westerstraat
origins.en: The name was given in 1861, when the Anjeliersgracht, as the street was previously called, was filled in. Why it became Westerstraat then is not clear.

origins.name: Westertoegang
origins.en: This bridge is located above the water that forms the western entrance to the IJ

origins.name: Westerwoldestraat
origins.en: Region in the southeastern part of the province of Groningen.

origins.name: Westhavenweg
origins.en: This harbor, dug about half in 1937, was initially called the Fordhaven, but soon gained the unofficial name Westhaven. After the harbor was extended by more than a kilometer to its current length in 1961, the name was also officially established, along with that of other harbors. The later built road therefore bore the name earlier than the harbor.

origins.name: Westlandgracht
origins.en: The area west of Delft, an internationally known horticultural area.

origins.name: Westmallepad
origins.en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Westpoortweg
origins.en: Business park and industrial area, near the western harbors of the city.

origins.name: Westrandweg
origins.en: Refers to the western side of Amsterdam

origins.name: Westwouderstraat
origins.en: The village of Westwoud, between Hoorn and Enkhuizen (North Holland).

origins.name: Westzaanstraat
origins.en: Village west of Zaandam (and west of the Zaan).

origins.name: Weteringlaan
origins.en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory.

origins.name: Weteringschans
origins.en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory.

origins.name: Weteringstraat
origins.en: The streets are located in the Weteringbuurt. The names remind us of the Wetering, which originally flowed into the Spui from outside the city. The Boerenwetering is still a remnant of this. The Schans was formerly the wall on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century, the walls and embankments were demolished. Parts have been recreated in promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen) and a road has been built, which first went by the name of Schans in its full length, but was later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was built on the site that became available due to the demolition of the Flour and Bread Factory.

origins.name: Wethouder Abrahamspad
origins.en: Ephraim Joseph Abrahams (1875-1954), a member of the Amsterdam municipal council for 23 years, nine of which as an alderman (1919-1921 and 1927-1934).

origins.name: Wethouder de Roosplein
origins.en: Albertus de Roos (1900-1978), for 17 years a member of the Amsterdam City Council for Arts Affairs. In 1962 he took office in the Council of State.

origins.name: Wethouder De Roosplein
origins.en: Albertus de Roos (1900-1978), for 17 years a member of the Amsterdam City Council for Arts Affairs. In 1962 he took office in the Council of State.

origins.name: Wethouder De Vriesplantsoen
origins.en: Simon de Vries (1869-1961), a member of the municipal council for many years, and an alderman from 1908 to 1918.

origins.name: Wethouder Den Hertogstraat
origins.en: Herman Johannes den Hertog (1872-1952), alderman of Amsterdam from 1914 to 1921.

origins.name: Wethouder Driessenstraat
origins.en: Bernard Herman Maria Driessen (1828-1896), alderman of Amsterdam from 1886 to 1891.

origins.name: Wethouder Ed. Polakstraat
origins.en: Eduard Polak (1880-1962), a member of the Amsterdam municipal council for 22 years, eight of which as an alderman (1923-1927 and 1929-1933).

origins.name: Wethouder Frankeweg
origins.en: Bernardus Cornelis Franke (1889-1953), well-known figure in the Amsterdam socialist movement. Alderman for Labor Affairs from 1939 to 1941 and from 1945 to 1953. After his death, the Nieuweweg (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1904), where he lived for many years, was named after him. A plaque has also been inlaid there.

origins.name: Wethouder in 't Veldstraat
origins.en: Arie in 't Veld (1893-1976), alderman of Amsterdam from 1948 to 1962.

origins.name: Wethouder Insingerstraat
origins.en: Albrecht Fredrik Insinger (1788-1872) was a member of the Amsterdam municipal council for thirty years, seven of which as an alderman (1843-1850).

origins.name: Wethouder Ramstraat
origins.en: Bernard Ram (1894-1982), member of the Municipal Council from 1949 to 1962 and from 1953 to 1958 alderman for Labor Affairs, in which capacity he was confronted with the tram strike of 1953.

origins.name: Wethouder Seegersplein
origins.en: Leendert Seegers (1891-1970), with a break during the war years 1940-1945 for forty years a member of the Amsterdam municipal council for the CPN. From 1945 alderman, but in 1948 dismissed in connection with the discussion around the communist coup in Prague.

origins.name: Wethouder Serrurierstraat
origins.en: Louis Serrurier (1844-1916). During the 26 years he served on the Amsterdam municipal council, he was an alderman for fifteen years.

origins.name: Wethouder Steinmetzstraat
origins.en: Willem Steinmetz (1891-1968), a member of the Amsterdam municipal council for many years (1931-1962), of whom the last fourteen years as an alderman for municipal companies, among others.

origins.name: Wethouder Tabakstraat
origins.en: Johannes Tabak (1904-1978), alderman for Social Affairs from 1962 to 1968.

origins.name: Wethouder van Essenweg
origins.en: Pieter Hendrik van Essen (1902-1965), from 1931 to 1949 and from 1958 to 1965 alderman of the municipality of Haarlemmerliede and Spaarnwoude.

origins.name: Wethouder Van Wijckstraat
origins.en: Franciscus H.C. van Wijck (1901-1970), a member of the municipal council for 27 years and an alderman from 1945 to 1966, among others for the municipal companies.

origins.name: Wethouder Vospad
origins.en: Isidoor Henry Joseph Vos (1887-1943), a member of the municipal council for 22 years. During that period, he was an alderman from 1921 to 1928 and from 1933 to 1935.

origins.name: Wethouder Wierdelsstraat
origins.en: Ferdinandus J.A.M. Wierdels (1862-1935), municipal council member from 1919 to 1931 and alderman from 1919 to 1925.

origins.name: Wevelgemstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

origins.name: WG-plein
origins.en: The former Wilhelmina-Gasthuis, colloquially referred to as the W.G. The square and surrounding streets were laid out after the closure and partial demolition of the hospital, which was founded in 1891 on and adjacent to the grounds of the old Pesthuis. In 1957, the W.G. became an academic hospital and in 1983 the last patients moved to the Academic Medical Center. However, part of the buildings have remained standing and have been renovated for residential functions and commercial spaces.

origins.name: Wiardi Beckmanstraat
origins.en: Herman Barnard Wiardi Beckman (1904-1945) was a Dutch politician and a resistance fighter during World War II. He was also a member of the Senate (Eerste Kamer) on behalf of the Social Democratic Workers' Party.

origins.name: Wibauthof
origins.en: Florentinus Marinus Wibaut (1859-1936), socialist-democratic politician and statesman, from 1914 to 1927 and from 1929 to 1931 alderman. Of great significance for housing construction, social development and the theater life in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Wibautstraat
origins.en: Florentinus Marinus Wibaut (1859-1936), socialist-democratic politician and statesman, from 1914 to 1927 and from 1929 to 1931 alderman. Of great significance for housing construction, social development and the theater life in Amsterdam. The street was laid out after the closure of Weesperpoort station in 1939 on the route of the former railway line. The streets along the railway line that disappeared due to this naming were Miquelstraat, Spoorbaanstraat and the first part of Vrolikstraat.

origins.name: Wiborgeiland
origins.en: Swedish, Russian, Finnish and finally again Russian Baltic Sea port, which was important for the Amsterdam timber trade.

origins.name: Wichersstraat
origins.en: Mr. Hendrik Ludolf Wichers (1800-1853), statesman and lawyer. Was Minister of Justice in the De Kempenaer cabinet in 1849 and then a member of the Council of State.

origins.name: Wiegbrug
origins.en: This bascule bridge is named after the type of bridge it originally represented. A wiegbrug (rocking bridge) is a rolling bascule bridge.

origins.name: Wielewaalstraat
origins.en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

origins.name: Wielingenstraat
origins.en: The gully in the mouth of the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Wierdestraat
origins.en: Artificially raised residential hill, which occurs under this name in the province of Groningen. Occurs in Friesland under the name terp.

origins.name: Wieringerwaardstraat
origins.en: Polder in North Holland (northeast of Schagen), a piece of tidal flat area drained in 1610.

origins.name: Wigbolt Ripperdastraat
origins.en: Geuzenaanvoerder from Groningen, appointed governor of Haarlem by the Prince of Orange during the siege of 1672 to 1673. After the fall of the city, he was beheaded by the Spanish.

origins.name: Wijde Heisteeg
origins.en: The Heisteeg gets its name from a corner house that was called ''t Hayblok'. This house is already mentioned at the beginning of the sixteenth century. The street was laid out on land that came to the city in the middle of the fifteenth century. The Wijde Heisteeg dates back to the next city expansion.

origins.name: Wijde Kapelsteeg
origins.en: Named after the chapel 'ter Heilige Stede', later called Nieuwezijds Kapel. After the demolition of the original church in 1909, the current one was put into use in 1912. Previously there were even more Kapelstegen (chapel alleys), but their names were changed due to confusion.

origins.name: Wijde Kerksteeg
origins.en: After the Oude Kerk, which the alleys lead to from the Warmoesstraat, part of which was originally called Kerkstraat.

origins.name: Wijde Lombardsteeg
origins.en: After the nearby lommerd, or Bank van Lening (pawnshop), founded in 1614.

origins.name: Wijdenesserstraat
origins.en: Named after the village of Wijdenes, east of Hoorn (North Holland).

origins.name: Wijdesteeg
origins.en: The alley was already mentioned under this name in 1564. Compared to other alleys, this one was quite wide. Earlier, the alley was known by the names Witloossteeg (after a resident) and Houtmarktsteeg.

origins.name: Wijenburg
origins.en: Nobleman's house in Echteld (Gelderland) from the sixteenth century with a late medieval tower. Interior renovated in the eighteenth century, now restored. Named after the lords of Wije, lords of Echteld.

origins.name: Wijkergouw
origins.en: A gouw is a village road or village moat. A district can be a residential area, but also a side water. This may be the second meaning. The name 'De Weijcker' already appears here on a map from the seventeenth century (by Gerrit Drogeham).

origins.name: Wijmarkthof
origins.en: Name of the former land outside the dike along the Spaarndammerdijk near Sloterdijk, protected by a summer dike against the water of the former IJ.

origins.name: Wijnand Nuijenstraat
origins.en: Wijnand Jan Joseph Nuijen (1813-1839), painter from the romantic school. Painted seascapes, street and cityscapes. When it was discovered after the council decision was made that the first name was incorrect, the relevant alderman did not consider it worth changing the name.

origins.name: Wijngaardsstraatje
origins.en: The street already appeared under this name in 1430. It is likely that an inn located here at the time with a facade stone was the name giver.

origins.name: Wijnkersstraat
origins.en: Shiny, dark red to brown cherry.

origins.name: Wijnsilostraat
origins.en: Names refer to companies that were based here Wine trade Roders

origins.name: Wijsmullerstraat
origins.en: Jan Hillebrand Wijsmuller (1855-1925), landscape painter.

origins.name: Wijttenbachstraat
origins.en: Daniel Wijttenbach (1746-1820), professor of philosophy in Amsterdam, later professor of ancient languages in Leiden.

origins.name: Wilco Jiskootpad
origins.en: Willem Herbertus Jiskoot (1924-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Haarlem. He was a member of the main group of the illegal newspaper 'Het Parool'.

origins.name: Wildeman
origins.en: Former grain mill on Amstelveenseweg, near Kalfjeslaan.

origins.name: Wildenborch
origins.en: Fortified castle from 1372, of which only a heavy gate tower remains. This tower is now the central part of the current building, which dates from 1782. Located near Vorden (Gelderland).

origins.name: Wildrijkstraat
origins.en: Nature reserve in the municipality of Zijpe. The area includes one of the few deciduous forests in the north of North Holland.

origins.name: Wilgenweg
origins.en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

origins.name: Wilhelmina Bladergroenstraat
origins.en: Wilhelmina Johanna Bladergroen (1908-1983), psychologist and pedagogue, from 1967 to 1978 professor of child psychology of the deviant child at the University of Groningen. Initiator of the development of L.O.M. schools.

origins.name: Wilhelmina Druckerstraat
origins.en: Pioneer of the Dutch women's movement (1847-1925). Founded the Women's Suffrage Association with Aletta Jacobs in 1893.

origins.name: Wilhelminastraat
origins.en: Wilhelmina Helena Pauline Maria, Princess of Orange-Nassau (1880-1962), daughter of King William III and Queen Emma, Queen of the Netherlands from 1898 to 1948.

origins.name: Wilhelmus Leemansstraat
origins.en: Hydraulic engineer (1841-1929), chief inspector of the Dutch Water Authority. He had a stake in the construction of the Nieuwe Waterweg and the waterway from Zwolle to the North Sea (IJsselmeer). A pumping station is named after him in the Wieringermeerpolder.

origins.name: Willaertstraat
origins.en: Adriaen Willaert (1485-1562), South Dutch composer. Working in Venice since 1527, where he founded the so-called Venetian music school.

origins.name: Willebroekstraat
origins.en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Willem Augustinstraat
origins.en: Skating legend (1923-2004). From 1941 he rode the Elfstedentocht every time (nine times)

origins.name: Willem Baerdesenstraat
origins.en: Willem Baerdesen (1528-1601), also written as Bardes or Bardesius, mayor of Amsterdam at the time of the Alteration in 1578.

origins.name: Willem Bartjenshof
origins.en: Schoolmaster (1569-1645), began his career in Amsterdam. Gained great fame through his notebooks, which have been reprinted repeatedly. Lived in Zwolle since 1618.

origins.name: Willem Beukelsstraat
origins.en: The fisherman from Biervliet, who improved the herring cakes (removing the intestines). Died in 1397. The street was called before 1922: Michiel Adr. de Ruijterstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1907).

origins.name: Willem de Zwijgerlaan
origins.en: Nickname of Prince Willem of Orange (1533-1584), also known as 'The Father of the Fatherland'. Son of Willem of Nassau and Juliana of Stolberg. Because he inherited the principality of Orange, he is the ancestor of the House of Orange-Nassau.

origins.name: Willem Fenengastraat
origins.en: Founder of the Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (1848-1930).

origins.name: Willem Frederik Hermansstraat
origins.en: Writer (1921-1995) and polemicist. Was lecturer in physical geography at the Rijksuniversiteit Groningen. His most famous novels include 'The dark chamber of Damocles' and 'Never sleep again'. Chaos and chance play a major role in his work. He established his name as a polemicist with his book 'Mandarins in sulfuric acid', in which he criticized the Dutch literary world. In 1977 he received the Grand Prize of the Dutch Letters.

origins.name: Willem Frogerstraat
origins.en: Willem Antonie Froger (1812-1883), civil engineer, designer of the North Sea Canal opened on 1-11-1876.

origins.name: Willem Gerresepad
origins.en: Willem Frederik Gerrese (1910-1943), resistance fighter, born in The Hague, executed in Leusden. He was affiliated with the illegal newspaper 'Het Parool'.

origins.name: Willem Gertenbachstraat
origins.en: Willem Johannes Gertenbach (1904-1943), resistance fighter, born in Zandvoort, executed by firing squad in Leusden. As a printer, he had an important role in the production of the illegal newspaper 'Het Parool'.

origins.name: Willem Heselaarsstraat
origins.en: Prominent figure in the Roman Catholic labor movement in Amsterdam (1886-1960). Performed important work in the crisis of the 1930s in favor of workers in employment.

origins.name: Willem Kesstraat
origins.en: Musician (1856-1934). First conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra, founded in 1888, succeeded in 1895 by Willem Mengelberg.

origins.name: Willem Kloosstraat
origins.en: Poet (1858-1938), leading figure in the Movement of Eighty, founder and editor of 'De Nieuwe Gids'. As a critic, he made pioneering work, which made him of great importance for the development of Dutch literature.

origins.name: Willem Kraanstraat
origins.en: Wilhelmus Johannes Kraan (1909-1942), resistance fighter, municipal worker and one of the initiators of the February Strike of 1941. Born in Amsterdam, executed in Soest.

origins.name: Willem Kromhoutstraat
origins.en: Architect (1864-1910). Among his works are the Hotel Americain (1900).

origins.name: Willem Landréstraat
origins.en: Guillaume Louis Frédérick Landré (1874-1948), composer. Wrote operas and symphonies. Music critic for many years for various newspapers. His son Guillaume (1905-1968) was also a composer.

origins.name: Willem Leevendstraat
origins.en: Epistolary novel by Betje Wolff and Aagje Deken from 1785. The street was transferred from the former municipality of Sloten in 1921 under the name Prinses Julianastraat (council decision of Sloten, 1910).

origins.name: Willem Molengraaffstraat
origins.en: Jurist in the field of commercial law (1858-1931). Professor at Utrecht and reformer of Dutch maritime law.

origins.name: Willem Mollhof
origins.en: Church historian (1812-1879), professor at the municipal University of Amsterdam. Layed the foundation for modern church history.

origins.name: Willem Mulierhof
origins.en: Athlete, known as Pim Mulier (1865-1954). He is called the father of Dutch athletics and football. Founded the Dutch Football Association in 1889. In 1890 he rode the entire journey by skating alone along the eleven cities of Friesland. He gave the impetus to the famous eleven-city race, which was first organized in 1909.

origins.name: Willem Nakkenstraat
origins.en: Painter (1835-1926), mainly of cattle, sometimes also of figures.

origins.name: Willem Noorlanderkade
origins.en: Architect (1877-1940), designed the Ceintuur Theater on the Ceintuurbaan, completed in 1920. In the 1920s, he designed the residential complex between the Berberisstraat and the Mosveld in Amsterdam Noord, two villas on the Meeuwenlaan and residential blocks around the Andoornstraat.

origins.name: Willem Paaphof
origins.en: Writer and lawyer (1856-1923), co-founder of 'De Nieuwe Gids'.

origins.name: Willem Parelstraat
origins.en: Chief boatswain (hoogbootsman) on the VOC shipyard in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Willem Passtoorsstraat
origins.en: Willem C.J. Passtoors (1856-1916), Amsterdam cigar dealer, who founded the Roman Catholic People's Federation in the Netherlands in 1888, and thus became the founder of the Roman Catholic Workers' Movement in our country. From 1901-1913 he was a member of the House of Representatives.

origins.name: Willem Pijperstraat
origins.en: Composer (1894-1947), teacher at the conservatories of Amsterdam and Rotterdam. As a lyric poet influenced by the French impressionists Franck and Debussy and by Mahler. Pijper wrote symphonies, choral works and stage music, among other things.

origins.name: Willem Roelofsstraat
origins.en: Landscape painter (1822-1892), representative of a new Dutch realism.

origins.name: Willem Royaardsstraat
origins.en: Willem Cornelis Royaards (1867-1929), actor and director. Led his own company for several years before becoming president of the Vereeniging Het Nederlandsch Toneel from 1920 to 1924.

origins.name: Willem Schermerhornstraat
origins.en: Politician and statesman (1894-1977) Prime Minister-President of the Netherlands after World War II, of the Schermerhorn/Drees cabinet (1945-1946). Before 1945 he belonged to the liberal democrats and led the Dutch People's Movement after 1945. Between 1946 and 1963 he was a member of the House of Representatives and the Senate (Eerste Kamer) for the Labour Party.

origins.name: Willem Schoutenstraat
origins.en: Sailor (1580-1625) made a round-the-world trip and discovered the later named islands in New Guinea.

origins.name: Willem Theunisse Blokstraat
origins.en: Master carpenter. Built ships.

origins.name: Willem van Hembyzestraat
origins.en: Leader of the Geuzen during the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Willem van Konijnenburgstraat
origins.en: Willem Adriaan van Konijnenburg (1868-1943), painter, engraver, lithographer, designer of glass and murals and writer about art. He initially painted realistically, later through contacts with Thorn Prikker, Derkinderen and Toorop his work became more stylized.

origins.name: Willem van Weldammelaan
origins.en: Bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland from 1392 to 1395.

origins.name: Willem Witsenstraat
origins.en: Painter (1860-1923) of Amsterdam cityscapes. Close relative of Breitner. The street was originally named Albert Hahnstraat (council decision, 1925).

origins.name: Willemsbrug
origins.en: This bascule bridge is named after King William I (1772-1843), who opened the nearby Willemspoort in 1840

origins.name: Willemskerkestraat
origins.en: In the sixteenth century, a village drowned in Zeelandic Flanders.

origins.name: Willemsparkweg
origins.en: This street leads to the former Willemspark, which was designed in 1881 as a connection to Vondelpark. That neighborhood still belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel at the time, which called this road Parkweg. However, the plans were changed in 1902, after which the current villa district around Emmaplein was created. Willemspark is named after King William I.

origins.name: Willemsstraat
origins.en: King William I (1772-1843). The Goudsbloemgracht was filled in in 1857. On the occasion of the inauguration of the new street created by this (which coincided with the then still widely known birthday of the previous king on August 24), a festival was organized and the filled in Goudsbloemgracht was renamed Willemstraat. The second s in the street name was added after 1909. Since 1918, the name has appeared with double s.

origins.name: Willeskopstraat
origins.en: Named after a village near Oudewater (Utrecht).

origins.name: William Barlowlaan
origins.en: English mathematician (1544-1625), published his famous work 'The navigator's supply' in 1597 and invented a nautical instrument that he called the 'compass of variation'.

origins.name: William Barlowsteiger
origins.en: English mathematician (1544-1625), published his famous work 'The navigator's supply' in 1597 and invented a nautical instrument that he called the 'compass of variation'.

origins.name: William Boothstraat
origins.en: English traveling preacher (1829-1914), originally Methodist. Founded the Salvation Army in 1878 and was its first general.

origins.name: Willinklaan
origins.en: Dirk Jan Willink (1888-1951), prominent figure in the Dutch athletics world. Played a particularly important role in the development of the synthetic tracks. Held numerous sports positions.

origins.name: Willy la Croixstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1906-1944), was involved in many illegal activities.

origins.name: Willy Mullenskade
origins.en: Cinema operator and filmmaker (1880-1952), in the early years of cinema he operated a traveling cinema together with his brother Albert, where he provided the films with commentary with his voice. He made many commissioned films in the Netherlands and India.

origins.name: Willy Pétillonstraat
origins.en: Youth book writer (1885-1948), debuted in 1908 with the boys' book 'The Adventures of a Bengal'. Then followed a large number of girls' books.

origins.name: Willy Sluiterstraat
origins.en: Painter and illustrator (1873-1949), chairman of Pulchri Studio in The Hague for many years.

origins.name: Wilmkebreekpad
origins.en: Named after a pond in North Holland, which was created by a levee breach in the years 1512 and 1518. Dried up in 1933, then flooded several times.

origins.name: Wilnisgracht
origins.en: The commuter village between Mijdrecht and Breukelen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Wiltzanghlaan
origins.en: Poem by Vondel. The first part of the street was previously designated as Zoutmanstraat by the municipality of Sloten (council decision of Sloten, 1910).

origins.name: Wim Ibobrug
origins.en: Wim Ibo (1918-2000) was a cabaretier and writer, who became especially known as a cabaret historian. His book 'And now the morality of this song' is generally considered the cabaret bible.

origins.name: Wim Noordhoekkade
origins.en: Photographer (1916-1995), best known for his special color photography.

origins.name: Wim van Estlaan
origins.en: Cyclist (1923 - 2003), first Dutchman to wear the yellow jersey as leader of the general classification in the Tour de France of 1951. Wim van Est's nicknames were: 'The Locomotive', 'Iron Willem', 'the Knob' and 'the Beul of the Heike'.

origins.name: Windjammerdijk
origins.en: Equipped sailing ship for the big voyage.

origins.name: Windrooskade
origins.en: Star-shaped figure indicating wind directions.

origins.name: Windroosplein
origins.en: Star-shaped figure indicating wind directions.

origins.name: Windtunnelkade
origins.en: In a wind tunnel, certain properties of aircraft are tested by artificially developed high wind speeds.

origins.name: Wingerdweg
origins.en: The climbing plant.

origins.name: Winkler Prinshof
origins.en: Anthony Winkler Prins (1817-1908), preacher and writer. Editor of the Winkler Prins encyclopedia named after him.

origins.name: Winterdijkstraat
origins.en: The outer river embankment, the bandijk, which limits the riverbed in winter and spring.

origins.name: Winterjanpad
origins.en: Old Dutch pear variety. The path is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Winterstraat
origins.en: The season. The street came under the name Rijnstraat in 1966 from the former municipality of Weesperkarspel. (council decision of Weesperkarspel, 1964).

origins.name: Winthontstraat
origins.en: Named after the historic ship the Winthont, with which enslaved people were transported in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Wismarbrug
origins.en: Wismar is a port city on the Baltic Sea in northeastern Germany near Rostock. The names in the Houthavens are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Wisseloord
origins.en: Country house (herenhuis) in 's-Graveland.

origins.name: Wisseloordpad
origins.en: Country house (herenhuis) in 's-Graveland.

origins.name: Wisseloordplein
origins.en: Country house (herenhuis) in 's-Graveland.

origins.name: Wisselstraat
origins.en: The switch between two train tracks, which is operated with a lever and allows trains to switch from one track to another.

origins.name: Witbolstraat
origins.en: Grass species that occurs in Europe, Asia and North Africa.

origins.name: Withoedenveem
origins.en: A veem is a company that is responsible for storing and delivering goods in and out of its warehouses. The veems each had their own license plate, after which they were named. These could be different colors and models of hats (e.g. Withoeden, Cloche hats). They also derived their name from the origin of the workers (e.g. Vriesseveem, Zeeuwse Veem).

origins.name: Witte Boogbrug
origins.en: Named after her appearance, it is a white arch bridge

origins.name: Witte de Withplein
origins.en: Witte Cornelisz de With (1599-1658, vice-admiral of Holland and West Friesland. Fought under Tromp at the Downs (Duins) and at Terheide, among other places. Died in the battle at the Sont against the Swedes.

origins.name: Witte de Withstraat
origins.en: Witte Cornelisz de With (1599-1658, vice-admiral of Holland and West Friesland. Fought under Tromp at the Downs (Duins) and at Terheide, among other places. Died in the battle at the Sont against the Swedes.

origins.name: Witte Katbrug
origins.en: Named after the species

origins.name: Witte Klok
origins.en: Former farmhouse in the old municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Wittenburgergracht
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

origins.name: Wittenburgerkade
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

origins.name: Wittgensteinlaan
origins.en: Ludwig Josef Johann Wittgenstein (1889-1951), British philosopher of Austrian descent. Eminently researched, he developed through mathematics into a renowned and influential logician and linguist.

origins.name: Wodanstraat
origins.en: Wodan was the supreme god of the Germans.

origins.name: Woestduinstraat
origins.en: Country estate near Bloemendaal. Known for the horse races, which were regularly held there at the beginning of the twentieth century and visited by many Amsterdamers.

origins.name: Wognumerpad
origins.en: A village in Noord-Holland.

origins.name: Wognumerplantsoen
origins.en: A village in Noord-Holland.

origins.name: Wognumerstraat
origins.en: A village in Noord-Holland.

origins.name: Woiskistraat
origins.en: Max Woiski sr. (Domburg (Suriname), 1911 - Hoogeveen 1981) was a well-known musician. In the 1930s, he performed in his own club La Cubana in Amsterdam's Leidsestraat under the name José Baretto. In the early stages of his career, he mainly played Latin American music; later also Surinamese music. His biggest hit was B.B. with R. (Brown beans with rice). In the 1960s he had his own production company MMP and moved to Mallorca where he bought a nightclub. In 2018 theater group Orkater together with the Bijlmer Parktheater staged the play Woiski vs. Woiski.

origins.name: Wolbrantskerkweg
origins.en: In 1421, the church village, which was located near the current town of Dubbeldam (South Holland), drowned.

origins.name: Wolderwijdpad
origins.en: One of the Veluwe border lakes (randmeren).

origins.name: Wolter Brandligtstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1901-1943), by profession writer. Born in Kampen, executed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Woltera van Reesstraat
origins.en: Woltera Bertha Johanna Berns van Rees (1841-1926), director of the Burgerziekenhuis and wife of the founder of the hospital, Anton Wilhelm Cornelis Berns.

origins.name: Wolvenstraat
origins.en: A predator belonging to the dog breed. As with more streets in this neighborhood, the naming is related to the hide trade.

origins.name: Wormerveerstraat
origins.en: Location in the Zaanstreek. The street was known as Houtrijkkade (council decision, 1888) before 1913.

origins.name: Woubruggestraat
origins.en: Village near the Braassemermeer (South Holland).

origins.name: Woudrichemstraat
origins.en: Fortified town on the Maas in the Land of Altena (North Brabant)

origins.name: Woutertje Pietersestraat
origins.en: Named after the book 'The History of Woutertje Pieterse' by Eduard Douwes Dekker under his pseudonym Multatuli.

origins.name: Wouwermanstraat
origins.en: Philips Wouwerman de Oude (1619-1668), painter of horses and war scenes.

origins.name: Wyandottestraat
origins.en: Chicken breed of American origin. Wyandotte is a city in the North American state of Michigan.

origins.name: Zaagmolenstraat
origins.en: Named after the many sawmills, which stood here until the end of the nineteenth century.

origins.name: Zaaiersweg
origins.en: The farmer who sows the seed.

origins.name: Zaandammerplein
origins.en: The city of Zaandam, now forming the municipality of Zaanstad with a few other places.

origins.name: Zaandijkstraat
origins.en: The place in the Zaanstreek, now municipality of Zaanstad. From 30-3-1881 to 1913 this was the Eerste Spaarndammerdwarsstraat.

origins.name: Zaanhof
origins.en: The place in the Zaanstreek, now municipality of Zaanstad. From 30-3-1881 to 1913 this was the Eerste Spaarndammerdwarsstraat.

origins.name: Zaanstraat
origins.en: The Zaan River, the main artery of the Zaanstreek. The street first appears under the name Houtrijkkade (council decision, 1888).

origins.name: Zacharias Jansestraat
origins.en: Zeeuwish eyeglass grinder (1580-1620), inventor of the binoculars. The original name Paul Krugerstraat, established by the municipality of Watergraafsmeer (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1900), had to be changed after the annexation of 1921 due to confusion with the street of the same name in the Transvaalbuurt.

origins.name: Zakslootje
origins.en: An old street name, originally a dead-end ditch. No longer included in the street name database from 1875. Due to the need for address indication, this name was included in the street name database again in 1984.

origins.name: Zamenhofstraat
origins.en: Ludwig Lazer Zamenhof (1859-1917), Polish doctor and linguist. In 1887, under the pseudonym Dr. Esperanto, he compiled a auxiliary language, which has continued to exist as Esperanto. Before 1948, the street was called Plaatijzerweg (derived from the steel industry) established on 6-6-1917. However, this was later found to be an unattractive name.

origins.name: Zanddwarsstraat
origins.en: The piece of land over which Zandstraat and Zanddwarsstraat run was originally swampy. In 1593 it was raised. Presumably the origin of the name lies in this sand elevation. By council decision in 1982, Zandstraat, which formerly ran through Reguliersbreestraat, was shortened to the current Zuiderkerkhof.

origins.name: Zandhoek
origins.en: According to a decree of 1634, the sand market was allowed to be held on this corner of the Western Islands.

origins.name: Zandhoeksbrug
origins.en: This double pick-up bridge is named after the Zandhoek. According to a decree of 1634, the sand market was allowed to be held at this corner of the Western Islands..

origins.name: Zandpad
origins.en: As early as 1688, this path is mentioned as the sand path or Muntepad, belonging to Willem de Munt, goldsmith on the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal. It must have been a sandy dirt road at that time.

origins.name: Zandpad-Driemond
origins.en: This is the part of the old Weesper Zandpad, which is located in the village of Driemond. The rest of the Zandpad is now called Provincialeweg. The municipal council of Amsterdam changed the name Zandpad to Zandpad-Driemond due to confusion with the Zandpad in Oud-West.

origins.name: Zandstraat
origins.en: The piece of land over which the Zandstraat and the Zanddwarsstraat run was originally swampy. In 1593 it was raised. Presumably the origin of the name lies in this sand elevation. By council decision in 1982, the Zandstraat, which formerly ran through Reguliersbreestraat, was shortened to the current Zuiderkerkhof.

origins.name: Zandvoortstraat
origins.en: The seaside resort (North Holland).

origins.name: Zandzeggestraat
origins.en: Perennial, native plant from the sedge family. A dune and heath plant, which counteracts sand erosion.

origins.name: Zaventemweg
origins.en: Name of Brussels airport.

origins.name: Zeebergweg
origins.en: Adriaan van Zeebergh (1746-1824), statesman, from 1773 to 1787 pensionary of Haarlem. During the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War (1780-1784), he was one of the leaders of the resistance against Stadhouder Willem V. In 1787 he was removed from office.

origins.name: Zeeburgerdijk
origins.en: The fortress 'Seeburgh', which stood halfway through the seventeenth century at the end of the dike. The Zeeburgerdijk is a part of the original sea dike of the North Sea. Before the Watergraafsmeer was drained, this was the only connection in the direction of Naarden.

origins.name: Zeeburgerkade
origins.en: The fortress 'Seeburgh', which stood halfway through the seventeenth century at the end of the dike. The Zeeburgerdijk is a part of the original sea dike of the North Sea. Before the Watergraafsmeer was drained, this was the only connection in the direction of Naarden.

origins.name: Zeeburgerpad
origins.en: The fortress 'Seeburgh', which stood halfway through the seventeenth century at the end of the dike. The Zeeburgerdijk is a part of the original sea dike of the North Sea. Before the Watergraafsmeer was drained, this was the only connection in the direction of Naarden.

origins.name: Zeeburgerstraat
origins.en: The fortress 'Seeburgh', which stood halfway through the seventeenth century at the end of the dike. The Zeeburgerdijk is a part of the original sea dike of the North Sea. Before the Watergraafsmeer was drained, this was the only connection in the direction of Naarden.
