origins.name: Zeedijk
origins.en: The name expresses the function. Since the founding of the city, this has been the sea wall and also the border of the first settlement on the side of IJ and Zuiderzee. The street still has the function of water dam, albeit as a sleeper dike (a reserve dike behind the front line).

origins.name: Zeelandstraat
origins.en: The province. Located in the middle of streets named after Zeeland castles.

origins.name: Zeemagazijnkade
origins.en: Named after the VOC warehouse in Oostenburg.

origins.name: Zeevaart
origins.en: The practice of shipping at sea.

origins.name: Zeevaarthof
origins.en: The practice of shipping at sea.

origins.name: Zeilmakerstraat
origins.en: Occupational name from shipbuilding. The name reminds us of the many shipyards that were established here in earlier centuries.

origins.name: Zeilstraat
origins.en: The cloth on vessels, for the capture of wind.

origins.name: Zekeringstraat
origins.en: The stop in the electrical line, which is responsible for protecting the network from overload in the event of a short circuit.

origins.name: Zelzatestraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of East Flanders.

origins.name: Zennehof
origins.en: Channel in Belgium, near Brussels.

origins.name: Zenostraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher (342-270 BC), founder of the Stoic school.

origins.name: Zesde Vogelstraat
origins.en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

origins.name: Zieseniskade
origins.en: Johanna Cornelia Ziesenis-Wattier (1762-1827), one of the greatest Dutch actresses of her time. The quay was built on the old Gangpad.

origins.name: Zijkanaal H-weg
origins.en: The road over the dike along Zijkanaal H and formed by the reclamation of the Noorder IJpolder.

origins.name: Zilverberg
origins.en: Nature monument, consisting of forest and oak wood complexes. Located between Oosterbeek and Doorwerth.

origins.name: Zilvermeeuwpad
origins.en: Large, commonly occurring gull species.

origins.name: Zilverplevierstraat
origins.en: Sturdy bird with black beak and black-and-white plumage. The srey plover breeds in the far north, but is especially common in spring and autumn on the mudflat and in the Zeeland delta.

origins.name: Zilverschoonstraat
origins.en: Silverweed, a small plant of the rose family.

origins.name: Zlotylaan
origins.en: The currency of Poland.

origins.name: Zocherstraat
origins.en: Louis Paul Zocher (1820-1915), garden architect. Designer and builder of Vondelpark (1864).

origins.name: Zomerdijkstraat
origins.en: A summer dike is the low dike or quay directly along the riverbed, which in summer - so at low water level - limits the riverbed.

origins.name: Zomerstraat
origins.en: The season. Earlier, the street name was established on 29-11-1957 by the former municipality of Weesperkarspel as Geinstraat.

origins.name: Zonhovenstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Zonnebeke
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

origins.name: Zonnehoekspad
origins.en: In the Netherlands, in summer the sun is much higher above the horizon than in winter. The angle that the rays of the sun make is also called the solar angle.

origins.name: Zonnehof
origins.en: The central body of the planetary system to which the Earth belongs (the sun).

origins.name: Zonneplein
origins.en: The central body of the planetary system to which the Earth belongs (the sun).

origins.name: Zonneweg
origins.en: The central body of the planetary system to which the Earth belongs (the sun).

origins.name: Zonnewendebrug
origins.en: Zonnewendebrug is a bridge in Oostburg in the Centrum district of Amsterdam. When designing this bridge, attention was paid to light and shadow formation. The fence is 3D printed and has the effect that the perspective of the bridge changes throughout the day and when you walk over it. This bridge has bridge number 2106 which refers to the longest day of the year: the summer solstice.

origins.name: Zonzeelstraat
origins.en: A village that drowned in 1421 during the St. Elizabeth flood in the northwest part of North Brabant.

origins.name: Zoomstraat
origins.en: River in North Brabant, near Bergen op Zoom.

origins.name: Zorgwijkstraat
origins.en: Country estate (hofstede) at the end of the Middenweg corner Oosterringdijk, built in 1696 and demolished in 1820 for the widening of the Middenweg.

origins.name: Zorgzaam
origins.en: The group of women, who regularly holds her silent march on Meiplein in Buenos Aires (Argentina). They want to know the truth about the fate of their men and children, who have disappeared under the general regime. In contrast to the weapons of violence and empty talk, they show in their collectivity and their persistence their struggle for truth, freedom and justice. Around this square, a number of streets are named after the virtues they represent.

origins.name: Zoutberg
origins.en: Farm on the western Ringsloot of the Purmer. Now gone.

origins.name: Zoutkeetsbrug
origins.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, on both sides of this canal stood the zoutketen (salt sheds), which were warehouses where coarse salt was processed for household use.

origins.name: Zoutkeetsgracht
origins.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, on both sides of this canal stood the zoutketen (salt sheds), which were warehouses where coarse salt was processed for household use.

origins.name: Zoutkeetsplein
origins.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, on both sides of this canal stood the zoutketen (salt sheds), which were warehouses where coarse salt was processed for household use.

origins.name: Zuid-Bevelandstraat
origins.en: The Zeeuwse island.

origins.name: Zuid-Hollandstraat
origins.en: The province. The surrounding streets are named after castles from this province.

origins.name: Zuideinde
origins.en: Acquired from the municipality of Oostzaan in 1966. The name indicates its location relative to the village of Oostzaan. In the part that also passed from the municipality of Landsmeer to Amsterdam at the same time, there was also a Zuideinde (relative to the village of Landsmeer), but due to confusion that road was later changed to Kadoelenweg.

origins.name: Zuidelijke Wandelweg
origins.en: Originally built as a walking path between the Amsteldijk and the Amstelveenseweg. Parallel to this, but still further outside the urban development of before 1940, ran the Buitenveldertse Wandelweg, which disappeared due to the construction of the garden city of Buitenveldert. The now still existing remnant of the Zuidelijke Wandelweg only has the name in common. The character of walking path has disappeared.

origins.name: Zuider IJdijk
origins.en: South side of the IJ

origins.name: Zuiderakerweg
origins.en: The location in the Akerpolder. The street was taken over in 1921 under the name Zuiderweg.

origins.name: Zuidergasfabriekbrug
origins.en: This bridge name refers to the Zuidergasfabriek, which stood here from 1909 to 1967.

origins.name: Zuiderkerkhof
origins.en: Named after the original function of this square. The gate that gave access to the old cemetery has now been restored and placed in the entrance from Sint Antoniesbreestraat to the square.

origins.name: Zuidermolenweg
origins.en: Old mill in the former Sloten (suyder Mole), mentioned on the map by Jan Dou from 1687.

origins.name: Zuiderzeepark
origins.en: Zuidzee, after closure in 1932 IJsselmeer.

origins.name: Zuiderzeeweg
origins.en: Zuidzee, after closure in 1932 IJsselmeer.

origins.name: Zuidewijn
origins.en: Ridderhuizinge in Vrijhoeve-Capelle (North Brabant). Partly sixteenth century, partly seventeenth century, renovated in 1763, consisting of two wings built perpendicular to each other with gabled facades.

origins.name: Zuidgorsstraat
origins.en: Nature reserve near Ellewoutsdijk (Zeeland), a landmass outside the dikes in the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Zuidplein
origins.en: The Zuidplein derives its name from its location near Station Zuid and its geographical location in the city. The square forms an important junction in Amsterdam Zuid and is connected to Noord and the Noordplein there via the metro line.

origins.name: Zuivelplein
origins.en: Livestock products (milk, butter and cheese).

origins.name: Zunderdorpergouw
origins.en: The county (village road) leads to the village of Zunderdorp, which has been part of the municipality of Amsterdam since 1-1-1921.

origins.name: Zus Braunstraat
origins.en: Swimmer, won gold in the 1928 Olympic Games in Amsterdam in the 100-meter backstroke.

origins.name: Zutendaalstraat
origins.en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Zwaagstraat
origins.en: Village in North Holland, north of Hoorn.

origins.name: Zwaansvliet
origins.en: Country house (herenhuis) in the Beemster (North Holland). Before 1965, the street was part of the Kastelenstraat.

origins.name: Zwaardemakerstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Zwaardemaker (1857-1930), physiologist, professor in Utrecht. Known for his olfactory and taste studies.

origins.name: Zwaluwstraat
origins.en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

origins.name: Zwanebloemlaan
origins.en: Swamp plant with pink flowers. The name refers to the shape of the pistils, which resemble swans. Grows along canals, waterways and drainage channels, and is planted as an ornamental flower in ponds.

origins.name: Zwanenburgwal
origins.en: Shortly after the land (on which the street and quay were laid out) was brought within the city just before 1600, there is talk of a house 'where the sign of Swanenburg hangs', on the corner of Zwanenburgwal. This will therefore probably have been the name giver. Swanenburg was already a more common name at that time. Gerrit Barents Swanenburgh, for example, built the Muiderpoort, Weesperpoort and Utrechtsepoort in the seventeenth century. By council decision in 1976, a part of the Zwanenburgwal was renamed Sint Antoniesluis. In order to build the Stopera, the Zwanenburgerstraat with adjacent buildings was demolished.

origins.name: Zwanenplein
origins.en: The water bird (the duck).

origins.name: Zwarte Pad
origins.en: Toad species. The black toad is black with irregular light brown spots on back and legs, or brown with black spots

origins.name: Zwartegouw
origins.en: This path was built around 1965, after the construction of the garden town Nieuwendam and the Sportpark de Weeren, for the convenience of access to the adjacent farms. In popular parlance, the path soon took on the name of 'Black path'.

origins.name: Zwenkgrasstraat
origins.en: Rare, native plant from the grass family with plume-shaped flowers.

origins.name: Achter Twiske
origins.en: Twiske is the (West) Frisian word for 'between'. It is not known whether the name refers to the location near the small river Twiske or perhaps to the peat-lake area of the same name.

origins.name: Achtergracht
origins.en: This canal was dug around 1660 behind (achter) the four main canals, hence the name. It connected the Reguliersgracht with the Amstel. In 1870 most of it was filled in.

origins.name: Adenhaven
origins.en: Port city in Yemen, on the Red Sea.

origins.name: Admiralengracht
origins.en: A collective name for the admirals from Holland and Zeeland after whom the streets in the surrounding neighbourhood are named.

origins.name: Afrikahaven
origins.en: Continent. Africa has deserts, steppes, savannas and jungles. About two-fifths of Africa is desert.

origins.name: Alaskahaven
origins.en: Alaska is the largest state of the United States, located in the far north-west of the North American mainland.

origins.name: Albardagracht
origins.en: Johan Willem Albarda (1879-1957), social-democratic politician and statesman. He was Minister of Waterstaat (public works and water management) from 1939 to 1945 (in London from 1940 to 1945).

origins.name: Amerikahaven
origins.en: The continent.

origins.name: Amstel
origins.en: The river to which Amsterdam owes its name and its origin.

origins.name: Amstelkanaal
origins.en: A canal dug around 1920 as part of Berlage's Plan Zuid. It connects the river of the same name with a five-way junction of canals, including the Boerenwetering, the Noorder Amstelkanaal and the Zuider Amstelkanaal.

origins.name: Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal
origins.en: Busy canal, 72 kilometres long, that links the IJ via Utrecht to the Waal near Tiel. It is part of an important route to the Ruhr area.

origins.name: Arendonksingel
origins.en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Ashaven
origins.en: Cargo that was, and still is, shipped through the port of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Australiëhaven
origins.en: The continent.

origins.name: Aziëhaven
origins.en: The largest of the continents.

origins.name: Barnegat
origins.en: Former arm of the sea off the IJ. The name derives from 'barnen', an older form of the verb branden (to burn). This probably refers to the frequent reed fires in the area.

origins.name: Beringhaven
origins.en: The Beringstraat (Bering Strait), a strait between Asia and America. It was discovered in 1741 and named after the Dane Vitus Bering.

origins.name: Beulingsloot
origins.en: Named after one of the residents, Gerrit Jansz Beulinck, who lived here around 1660. He may have made this known with a hanging sign. In the sixteenth century the names Leertouwersstraat and Leertouwerssloot, and also Huidevettersstraat and Huidevetterssloot, occur here (leertouwers and huidevetters were tanners).

origins.name: Bickersgracht
origins.en: These streets are on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr Johan Bicker (1591-1653), a shipbuilder and merchant, and a schepen (magistrate) and burgomaster of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets later laid out on the island automatically took the name of its founder. For the

origins.name: Bijleveldschesluis
origins.en: This name appears in old archives; its exact meaning is unknown.

origins.name: Bilderdijkgracht
origins.en: Willem Bilderdijk (1756-1831), poet and historian. Bilderdijk went against the complacent spirit of his time, which made him a highly controversial figure. The name Bilderdijkstraat originally applied as far as the Vondelstraat. That section, from the Jacob van Lennepkade onwards, is now called Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat (council decision of 21 March 1894). The Bilderdijkpark (park and street) was laid out on the site of the cemetery of the former Roman Catholic church 'De Liefde'.

origins.name: Blauwburgwal
origins.en: Probably named after the Blauwe Brug (blue bridge). The canal was dug at the end of the sixteenth century. The present name occurs from 1614. Before that it was called the canal of the Blauwe brugge outside the Jan Roonpoort, or the cross canal (dwarse burgwal) by the Blauwe brugge. Most bridges at that time were painted red.

origins.name: Bloemgracht
origins.en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion of 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which it is named. From 1614 to 1878 the windmill 'De Blom' stood on the bastion; it was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

origins.name: Boerenwetering
origins.en: The name of the watercourse that originally ran from the Kalfjeslaan to what is now the Koningsplein. It was formerly also called the Oude Wetering, as opposed to the Nieuwe Wetering (Kostverlorenvaart). The Weteringbuurt and the Weteringschans take their names from this wetering (drainage canal).

origins.name: Bosporushaven
origins.en: A strait in Turkey, part of the connection between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean, which separates Europe from Asia.

origins.name: Brantasgracht
origins.en: A river in Indonesia, in East Java, 257 km long.

origins.name: Broekermeerringsloot
origins.en: A ring ditch around the clay polder Broekermeer, which was made around 1628.

origins.name: Brouwersgracht
origins.en: Named after the many breweries found in this neighbourhood in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The prefixes Binnen (inner) and Buiten (outer) refer to the location in relation to the Haarlemmerdijk.

origins.name: Brusselsingel
origins.en: The capital of Belgium, in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Buiksloterkanaal
origins.en: Buiksloot was an independent municipality until 1921, when it was absorbed into Amsterdam. 'Ban' means both a jurisdiction and the authority to judge. The Banne Buiksloot was of old one of the six bannen (jurisdictions) into which the bailiwick of Waterland was divided. After the Batavian Revolution of 1795 the word survived, but referred only to the polder. The Waterland bannen were not abolished until 1936.

origins.name: Buiten-IJ
origins.en: The water east of the Oranjesluizen, joining the IJmeer and the Markermeer.

origins.name: Burgemeester Cramergracht
origins.en: Willem Daniël Cramer (1788-1856), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1836 to 1841.

origins.name: Burgemeester van Tienhovengracht
origins.en: Gijsbert van Tienhoven (1841-1914), alderman from 1874 to 1880 and burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1880 to 1891, and afterwards a minister.

origins.name: Cacaohaven
origins.en: The tropical product, the raw material for chocolate, that is transhipped in the port of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Carel Reynierszhaven
origins.en: Lived from 1604 to 1653. He founded the first settlement of the Dutch East India Company on the Coromandel Coast (India). From 1650 to 1653 he was Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies.

origins.name: Christoffel Plantijngracht
origins.en: Southern Netherlandish printer and lexicographer (1514-1589). His printing and publishing house in Antwerp grew into one of the most famous in Europe (now a museum).

origins.name: Coenhaven
origins.en: Jan Pieterszoon Coen (1587-1629). Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies (1619-1623 and 1627-1629). He founded Batavia, which regained its old name after the transfer of sovereignty.

origins.name: Cornelis Douweskanaal (Oost)
origins.en: Navigator, mathematician and astronomer (1712-1773). Director of the Amsterdam Nautical School (Zeevaartschool).

origins.name: Cornelis Douweskanaal (West)
origins.en: Navigator, mathematician and astronomer (1712-1773). Director of the Amsterdam Nautical School (Zeevaartschool).

origins.name: Da Costagracht
origins.en: Isaäc da Costa (1798-1860), Amsterdam lawyer, poet and prose writer of Portuguese-Jewish descent, who converted to Christianity.

origins.name: Damrak
origins.en: Rak is the old name for a straight stretch of waterway. So here it is the rak, or channel, to the Dam, narrowed on its west side during the eighteenth century. When the road or quay was built (in 1526), the name of the water passed to it. The houses on the Warmoesstraat between the Nieuwebrugsteeg and the Beurs are still called the houses 'aan 't Water' (on the water).

origins.name: De Boelegracht
origins.en: Gerrit de Boele, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland (1354/55).

origins.name: De Leek
origins.en: De Leek is a lake in Amsterdam-Noord.

origins.name: De Rijpgracht
origins.en: Jan Cornelisz de Rijp (1570-1630), navigator, who sailed at the same time as Heemskerk and Barentsz in search of a northern passage, but did not winter on Nova Zembla because he took a route around Spitsbergen. When the street was laid out, the council of the former municipality of Sloten named it Willem Barentsstraat (council decision of Sloten, 8 March 1910).

origins.name: Dijksgracht
origins.en: The street was laid out as a dike at the end of the sixteenth century, after which the surroundings (long a marsh) were filled in with earth (aangeplempt).

origins.name: Distelhaven
origins.en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

origins.name: Duivendrechtsevaart
origins.en: The village of Duivendrecht in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. Duivendrecht comes from Doeve (a man's name) and drecht (a place where ships were hauled overland). When the Watergraafsmeer was still a lake, a ferry ran from where the village now lies to the far side, towards Oetewaal.

origins.name: Durgerdammergouw
origins.en: Named after the village that belonged until 1921 to the municipality of Ransdorp, abolished that year. The name arose by corruption of the oldest name, IJdoringherdam: the dam at the corner of the IJ. (The polder outside the dike here has kept the name IJdoorn.) The Durgerdammerdijk is the stretch of the Waterland sea dike on which Durgerdam lies.

origins.name: Egelantiersgracht
origins.en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

origins.name: Eilandsgracht
origins.en: The canal between the Western Islands and the mainland (eiland: island). It dates from the city's third expansion (1610-1615), when the islands were made, and originally ran between the mainland and two of them, the Prinseneiland and the Bickerseiland. The stretch along the Bickerseiland was filled in in 1928.

origins.name: Entrepotdok
origins.en: Named after its function. The dock was built in 1827; imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid (a bonded warehouse, entrepot). The warehouses have lost their function as an entrepot, and in part of them the upper floors have now been converted into homes (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Entrepotdoksluis
origins.en: Named after its function. The dock was built in 1827; imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid (a bonded warehouse, entrepot). The warehouses have lost their function as an entrepot, and in part of them the upper floors have now been converted into homes (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Entrepothaven
origins.en: Named after its function. The dock was built in 1827; imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid (a bonded warehouse, entrepot). The warehouses have lost their function as an entrepot. In part of them the upper floors have now been converted into homes (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Erasmusgracht
origins.en: Desiderius Erasmus (1467-1536), humanist, who fiercely attacked the abuses in the Roman Catholic Church. His best-known work is 'In Praise of Folly'.

origins.name: Ertshaven
origins.en: Ore boats used to be unloaded at this quay.

origins.name: Fahrenheitsingel
origins.en: Gabriel Daniel Fahrenheit (1686-1736), German by birth, who settled in the Netherlands as a physicist. In 1715 he set the freezing point of the thermometer at 32 degrees and the boiling point at 212 degrees. The Fahrenheitstraat was originally called De Wetstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 31 October 1901).

origins.name: Gaasp
origins.en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp.

origins.name: Gaasperplas
origins.en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp. The Gaasperplas itself is an artificial lake up to 35 metres deep, created by digging sand for building the Bijlmermeer.

origins.name: Geldersekade
origins.en: At the city's second expansion on the east side, today's Geldersekade was the city moat. So the inner bank (on the Zeedijk side) is the oldest, built around 1500. The other side lay outside the city until 1585. In the seventeenth century the old side was called partly Keulse kaai (Cologne quay) and further on Gelderse kaai, and for a short time also Londense kaai or Engelse kaai. The names came from the landing stages here where ships moored that sailed to the towns of Gelderland, to Cologne, London and other English ports. Some remains of the city wall built here around 1500 between the Waag and the Schreierstoren can still be found in the quay wall and by the Bantammerbrug.

origins.name: Gerritsloot
origins.en: The origin of the name is unclear.

origins.name: Gevlewater
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

origins.name: Grimburgwal
origins.en: After the water called the Grim, which formed the city's southern boundary from 1342 to about 1400 (grim = muddy ditch).

origins.name: Groenburgwal
origins.en: The land between the Kloveniersburgwal and the Zwanenburgwal, where the cloth-drying frames stood and which was added to the city in 1593, was then the site of the dye works. This canal was therefore originally called Verwersgracht (dyers' canal). Early in the seventeenth century the name Groenburgwal arose, because there were green dye works here in particular.

origins.name: Groote Braak
origins.en: The name refers to the breach of the Spaarndammerdijk in a north-westerly storm in 1675. The water of the IJ then tore a gap 140 metres wide and almost 10 metres deep in the defences.

origins.name: Grote Die
origins.en: Literally 'great water', to distinguish it from the Kleine Die further on. The overtoom (a place where boats were hauled over a dam) was level with the Nieuwendijk.

origins.name: Grote Haven
origins.en: A harbour on the side canal to Nieuwendam.

origins.name: Haarlemmervaart
origins.en: The canal to Haarlem.

origins.name: Haveneilandschutsluis
origins.en: Named after the adjoining inner harbour, which is connected to the IJmeer by a lock.

origins.name: Havenkom A
origins.en: The name speaks for itself (harbour basin A). Basins B and D have been filled in.

origins.name: Havenkom C
origins.en: The name speaks for itself (harbour basin A). Basins B and D have been filled in.

origins.name: Heiligewegsluis
origins.en: After the Miracle of Amsterdam, the chapel 'Ter Heilige Stede' (later the Nieuwezijds Kapel) was founded between the Rokin and the Kalverstraat. For the pilgrims a road was then laid beside the Heiligewegsevaart (later the Overtoom) from Sloten to the Kalverstraat, called the Heiligeweg (holy way). Our street is what remains of that pilgrimage route. In old documents the Leidsestraat is also called Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Herengracht
origins.en: After the Heren Regeerders (the lords who governed the city; in the old days the city was not administered but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch when in 1612 it was widened into today's canal, the first of the three main canals. The stretch beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658, as does the Nieuwe Herengracht.

origins.name: Het Nauw
origins.en: The narrow passage (nauw: narrows) of water between the Ransdorper Die and the Holysloter Die.

origins.name: Het Slochter
origins.en: Slochter is another word for a navigation channel.

origins.name: Hoekenesgracht
origins.en: A small island in the former IJ. The word nes means a spit of land.

origins.name: Hollandiagracht
origins.en: The first Dutch film company to produce and distribute films and documentaries on a regular basis. The Hollandia film factory was founded in 1912 and expanded with a theatre company in 1913. It went bankrupt in 1922.

origins.name: Holysloter Die
origins.en: A creek south of Broek in Waterland.

origins.name: Hoornsloot
origins.en: Probably named after the town of Hoorn.

origins.name: Hornhaven
origins.en: The former island De Hoorn or Horn in the old IJ. After the Noordzeekanaal was built, the island could still be clearly made out in the landscape of the Grote IJpolder, but the extension of the Westhaven (around 1960) dug it away entirely. 'Horn' means corner and was given to coastal features similar to a 'nes' or 'ham'. This horn's full name was Zaanderhorn: a spit of land belonging to the western part of Zaanden, the forerunner of Zaandam.

origins.name: Houthaven
origins.en: Built in 1873 and enlarged in 1878, for goods shipped through the port of Amsterdam (houthaven: timber harbour).

origins.name: Houthavengracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

origins.name: Houtveemkanaal
origins.en: After the adjoining timber warehouses (houtvemen).

origins.name: Hugo de Grootgracht
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

origins.name: IJhaven
origins.en: The IJ was once an arm of the Zuiderzee. In 1865-1872 it was reclaimed when the Noordzeekanaal was built, and in 1872 it was closed off from the Zuiderzee by the IJdijk and the Oranjesluizen.

origins.name: IJmeer
origins.en: The IJmeer is a border lake in the Netherlands. It lies between the De Nes polder, Pampushaven, the Hollandse Brug and the mouth of the IJ at IJburg, divided between the provinces of Noord-Holland and Flevoland.

origins.name: IJssloot
origins.en: The origin of this name is unknown.

origins.name: Jacob van Lennepkanaal
origins.en: Prose writer (1802-1868), mainly of historical novels, among them 'De roos van Dekama' and 'Ferdinand Huyck'.

origins.name: Jan Massensloot
origins.en: It is not known how this ditch got its name.

origins.name: Jan van Riebeeckhaven
origins.en: Jan Anthonie van Riebeeck or Riebeek (1618-1708), who in 1652, in the service of the Dutch East India Company, founded the Cape Colony at the Cape of Good Hope.

origins.name: Johan van Hasseltkanaal-Oost
origins.en: He lived from 1850 to 1916 and was director of Public Works from 1900 to 1907, and before that director of the Waterworks. He had a large part in organising the ENTOS shipping exhibition of 1913. In 1900 Van Hasselt drew up a design for developing Amsterdam-Noord, with housing districts and a canal. An eastern and a western part of this canal were dug in 1919 and named after him. When a road was built on the undug part, it was named after him too.

origins.name: Kadoelerbreek
origins.en: The name of the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was added to Amsterdam on 1 August 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) appears as early as 1375. In 1429 the manors of Landsmeer and Quadolen are mentioned, which then shared one lord. Old maps show Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterland sea dike (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1 August 1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed because of confusion with the Zuideinde (formerly Oostzaan).

origins.name: Kattenburgervaart
origins.en: A canal named after Kattenburg, the westernmost of the three Eastern Islands in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Kattensloot
origins.en: This name probably refers to the animal (cats).

origins.name: Keizersgracht
origins.en: After Emperor Maximilian, Archduke of Austria, who in 1489 granted Amsterdam the privilege of bearing the imperial crown on its coat of arms.

origins.name: Kinselmeer
origins.en: A lake north of Durgerdam.

origins.name: Kleine Wetering
origins.en: A wetering is a dug watercourse. Called Kleine (little) Wetering because of its size.

origins.name: Kloveniersburgwal
origins.en: The Kloveniersburgwal owes its name to a part of the civic guard called kloveniers, after the firearm its men used, a culverin.

origins.name: Kolberggracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

origins.name: Koningsbergengracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

origins.name: Korte Prinsengracht
origins.en: After 'the princely title', meaning that of the Princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and the plainest in the character of its buildings. It was dug in the expansion of 1612 and built up from the Brouwersgracht to the Leidsegracht. In the expansion of 1658 this canal too was extended across the Amstel (as far as the Entrepotdok). The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for today's Noordermarkt never caught on with the citizens.

origins.name: Kostverlorenvaart
origins.en: After the Kostverlorenwetering, dug in 1413 to give a shorter waterway to the Haarlem and Leiden lakes. According to some, the name Kostverloren (cost lost) comes from the heavy legal costs of this channel, which was a bone of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609. The name Kostverloren occurs in several places in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Krom Boomssloot
origins.en: Named after the sixteenth-century master shipbuilder Cornelis Pietersz. Boom. To connect his yard on the Lastage with the surrounding water he had a canal and a side canal dug.

origins.name: Lamonggracht
origins.en: A river on the Indonesian island of Java.

origins.name: Lauriergracht
origins.en: The southern European ornamental tree (the laurel).

origins.name: Le Mairegracht
origins.en: Jacob le Maire (1585-1616), explorer, who with Willem Schouten discovered the strait at the southern tip of South America named after him, and the cape they called Cape Horn, after Schouten's home town of Hoorn. A Le Mairestraat had been planned and named elsewhere on 20 November 1878, but that council decision was withdrawn on 19 August 1905.

origins.name: Leidsegracht
origins.en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date from the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got its name because it led to the Leidsepoort (Leiden gate). It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Leliegracht
origins.en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Lijnbaansgracht
origins.en: The ropewalks (lijnbanen) of the ropemakers. The Lijnbaanssteeg dates from the fifteenth century, when the Singel was the outermost canal. A ropemaker needed a fairly large site for his trade, which could only be found on the edge of the city. The ropewalks lay on the city side of the moat, so inside the rampart. The Lijnbaansgracht ran right round the city. It has since been filled in in several places and there has taken other names, such as Leidseplein, Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen, Frederiksplein, Maarten Jansz. Kosterstraat, Valckenierstraat and Plantage Muidergracht.

origins.name: Looiersgracht
origins.en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

origins.name: Lozingskanaal
origins.en: A canal running to the Zeeburg pumping station (the name means discharge canal).

origins.name: Lübeckgracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

origins.name: Luiksingel
origins.en: A Belgian city (Liège), in the province of Liège.

origins.name: Machinetocht
origins.en: A canal in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

origins.name: Madagascarhaven
origins.en: An African island, the fourth largest island in the world, south-east of Africa.

origins.name: Mainhaven
origins.en: A tributary of the Rhine, on which the city of Mainz lies (the Main).

origins.name: Majanggracht
origins.en: A river on the Indonesian island of Java.

origins.name: Marssloot
origins.en: A ditch in Amsterdam-Noord, near the Kadoelen.

origins.name: Mauritiushaven
origins.en: An island east of Madagascar, colonised from 1598 by Dutch seamen and later taken over by the French and the English, among others. It is named after Stadtholder Prince Maurits, Count of Nassau.

origins.name: Mechelensingel
origins.en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Mercuriushaven
origins.en: In Roman mythology the god of trade.

origins.name: Merdekagracht
origins.en: Merdeka means free or independent and already formed the forbidden battle cry of the nationalist movement during the colonial period. After the Proclamation of the Republic of Indonesia on August 17, 1945, it became the characteristic battle cry of the independence fighters.

origins.name: Minervahaven
origins.en: In Roman mythology the goddess of wisdom.

origins.name: Moezelhaven
origins.en: Tributary that flows into the Rhine near Koblenz (Germany). Important river for the industries and mines in the Saar region.

origins.name: Neptunushaven
origins.en: In Roman mythology the god of the sea.

origins.name: Nieuwe Achtergracht
origins.en: This canal was dug around 1660 behind (achter) the four main canals, hence the name. It connected the Reguliersgracht with the Amstel. In 1870 most of it was filled in.

origins.name: Nieuwe Diep
origins.en: When the Zuiderzee broke through the Diemerdijk in 1422, the new lake formed below the Bovendiep.

origins.name: Nieuwe Gouw
origins.en: Gouw is a Waterland term for road. The addition Nieuwe indicates that this road is slightly younger than the other Waterland roads. However, the road already appears on the map of Amstellandt and the surroundings of Covens from 1749. In 1957, the name was officially established again.

origins.name: Nieuwe Gouwsloot
origins.en: A county is a Waterland term for road.

origins.name: Nieuwe Herengracht
origins.en: After the Heren Regeerders (the lords who governed the city; in the old days the city was not administered but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch when in 1612 it was widened into today's canal, the first of the three main canals. The stretch beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658, as does the Nieuwe Herengracht.

origins.name: Nieuwe Houthaven
origins.en: Storage yard for the timber trade. Built in 1873 and enlarged in 1878.

origins.name: Nieuwe Keizersgracht
origins.en: After Emperor Maximilian, Archduke of Austria, who in 1489 granted Amsterdam the privilege of bearing the imperial crown on its coat of arms.

origins.name: Nieuwe Meer
origins.en: The water surface was given this name to distinguish it from the Old Lake (see there). The Nieuwe Meer has been enlarged since the 1950s with part of the Riekerpolder and pumped to a depth of thirty meters for sand mining for the Western Garden Cities (westelijke tuinsteden).

origins.name: Nieuwe Prinsengracht
origins.en: After 'the princely title', meaning that of the Princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and the plainest in the character of its buildings. It was dug in the expansion of 1612 and built up from the Brouwersgracht to the Leidsegracht. In the expansion of 1658 this canal too was extended across the Amstel (as far as the Entrepotdok). The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for today's Noordermarkt never caught on with the citizens.

origins.name: Nieuwe Vaart
origins.en: Named after the Nieuwe Vaart dug around 1650 to the IJ and the Oosterdok.

origins.name: Noorder Amstelkanaal
origins.en: Channel that forms a connection between the Amstel and the Schinkel.

origins.name: Noordhollandsch Kanaal
origins.en: A canal that runs from Amsterdam-North, via Purmerend and Alkmaar to Den Helder.

origins.name: Noordzeekanaal
origins.en: The canal provides direct access to the North Sea from Amsterdam and was created by reclaiming the IJ and dredging the dunes near Velsen. The canal was dug to a design by Willem Antonie Froger and opened on November 1, 1876. The construction and operation of the canal and polders were carried out by the Canal Company, whose assets were taken over by the state after its dissolution in 1884. The road was part of the Basisweg and the Zuiderweg in the Grote IJpolder before the naming in 1978.

origins.name: Oesjesduiker
origins.en: The name of this diver comes from the signboard 't Osje, which was formerly attached to a butcher on the corner of the Oostenburgergracht

origins.name: Olympiakanaal
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Onbekendegracht
origins.en: The Onbekendegracht originally gave the Former City Timberyard access to the Amstel. In a notarial deed, drawn up in 1800, the canal was called 'the Unknown or Amstelgragtje'.

origins.name: Oostelijk Marktkanaal
origins.en: Is located on the east side of the Centrale Markthallen.

origins.name: Oostenburgerdwarsvaart
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to public traffic in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and formally abolished in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abolished in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oostenburgervaart
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to public traffic in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and formally abolished in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abolished in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oosterdok
origins.en: The Oosterdok was created by a seawall completed in 1832 on the east side of the city. The quay on and along this dyke was named Oosterdokskade and Oostelijke Handelskade.

origins.name: Oosterdoksdoorgang
origins.en: The water passage located between the name bearer Oosterdokskade.

origins.name: Oostertocht
origins.en: A tow is a connecting ditch between polder ditches and the polder canal.

origins.name: Oostertoegang
origins.en: Eastern access from the Oosterdok to the IJ

origins.name: Open Havenfront
origins.en: Former open waterfront. Filled in for the construction of Central Station.

origins.name: Oranjesluizen
origins.en: Named after the House of Orange-Nassau to which the royal family belongs. The first stone of the Oranjesluizen was laid by the then king William III, on April 29, 1870.

origins.name: Osdorpergracht
origins.en: Named after the neighborhood of Osdorp. On old maps, this neighborhood is mentioned as Oostdorp. In 1957, construction began on the garden city of Osdorp, which was practically completed in 1973. The Osdorperweg used to bear the names Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

origins.name: Oude Houthaven
origins.en: Dug in 1876 for transshipping and storing timber.

origins.name: Oudeschans
origins.en: A rampart is an earthen wall and as such the Oudeschans was built around 1516 for defense against the Gelders. The concept of rampart has long since been lost here, but water and quay have retained the name. The addition 'Old' will have been given, when in the next century a new rampart was built around the enlarged city.

origins.name: Oudezijds Achterburgwal
origins.en: Canal behind the Voorburgwal on the old side.

origins.name: Oudezijds Voorburgwal
origins.en: Before 1385 the Amstel divided the city into two almost equal halves, the old side (with the Oude Kerk) and the new side (with the Nieuwe Kerk). Each side was bounded by a burgwal, a town moat. When new burgwallen were dug behind them around 1385, the existing one became the Voorburgwal and the new one the Achterburgwal, on the old side and the new side alike. After the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal was filled in in 1867, it was renamed Spuistraat. The terms Oudezijds and Nieuwezijds date from the fifteenth century; before that people spoke of the Church side and the Windmill side.

origins.name: Papaverkanaal
origins.en: The plant (poppy), wild and cultivated, also called klaproos.

origins.name: Passeerdersgracht
origins.en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

origins.name: Pereboomsloot
origins.en: The fruits of the pear tree.

origins.name: Pernaugracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

origins.name: Petroleumhaven
origins.en: Named after the port located here for unloading oil tankers and the areas for storing petroleum products. The port was put into use in 1888. The first part of the road was previously named Vlothavenweg (council decision, 1953).

origins.name: Pieter Postsingel
origins.en: Master builder (1608-1669), had a share in the construction of the town hall on the Dam. Other buildings: Mauritshuis and Huis ten Bosch in The Hague, town hall in Maastricht.

origins.name: Plantage Muidergracht
origins.en: The place Muiden. The former Muidergracht began at the Leprozengracht. Part of it was renamed Jonas Daniël Meijerplein after filling in, the second part was later renamed Hortusplantsoen. The part of the Plantage Muidergracht parallel to Sarphatistraat was called Plantage Lijnbaansgracht before 1915.

origins.name: Polygoongracht
origins.en: Film factory, founded in 1919 in Haarlem. Producer of commissioned films, documentaries and weekly cinema news bulletins.

origins.name: Postjeswetering
origins.en: Named after the former Postjeswetering. A postje is a freshwater fish.

origins.name: Prinseneilandsgracht
origins.en: Probably named after the house 'The three Princes', which must have stood here in the seventeenth century. The house had busts of Prince William I, Prince Maurice and Prince Frederick Henry. However, it is not known where this house stood.

origins.name: Prinsengracht
origins.en: After 'the princely title', meaning that of the Princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and the plainest in the character of its buildings. It was dug in the expansion of 1612 and built up from the Brouwersgracht to the Leidsegracht. In the expansion of 1658 this canal too was extended across the Amstel (as far as the Entrepotdok). The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for today's Noordermarkt never caught on with the citizens.

origins.name: Profiltigracht
origins.en: Film factory, founded in 1929 in The Hague. Producer of (commissioned) films, documentaries and cinema newsreels. First counterpart, later partner of Polygoon.

origins.name: Raamgracht
origins.en: The lakenramen (tenter frames for stretching cloth), where the dyed cloth was hung to dry, had to be set up outside the city. When the Kloveniersburgwal was still the city moat, these frames could be found at the height of the current Raamgracht. The nearby Verversstraat also still reminds us of this old Amsterdam industry.

origins.name: Ransdorper Die
origins.en: A stream north of Ransdorp.

origins.name: Rapenburgwal
origins.en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now Oosterdok), Oudeschans, Rapenburgwal and Schippersgrachtje. The main street has taken the name of the island. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

origins.name: Realengracht
origins.en: Reynier Reael, in 1633 alderman (schepen) of the city. He was the owner of the entire Realeneiland.

origins.name: Recht Boomssloot
origins.en: The 16th-century shipbuilder Cornelis Pietersz Boom. To connect his shipyard on the Lastage with the surrounding water, he had a canal and a cross-channel dug. These were then named after him.

origins.name: Reguliersgracht
origins.en: All these names recall the Reguliers monastery (of the Canons Regular), which stood from 1394 to 1532 outside the city gate of the time, where the Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now cross. The city gate, of which the Munttoren is a remnant, was once called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht then ended at that gate. Parts of it were filled in in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Before 1909 the Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

origins.name: Ringsloot
origins.en: Ring-shaped ditch.

origins.name: Ringvaart
origins.en: The water along which the path runs. A Ringvaart is the basin of a polder, into which excess water from the polder is discharged.

origins.name: Rokin
origins.en: We must discard the long-standing theory that this name is a derivation from Rak-in (a rak within the Dam, such as the Damrak outside the Dam). This part of the Amstel, now partially filled in for 2/3 of its length, originally had no embankments. The buildings on Kalverstraat ran right down to the water. When in the sixteenth century the facade along the water of the first part was set back from the Dam (it had to 'ruck in'), a quay was built here, which was designated as Ruck-in in 1559. A few years later this became the Rock-in. With later extension, the entire quay was given this name.

origins.name: Scharrebiersluis
origins.en: Scharrebier was traditionally the drink for ordinary workers. This 'thin' beer type was formerly sold on this collection bridge, because there was often a lot of working people present there

origins.name: Schellingwouderbreek
origins.en: Village Schellingwoude

origins.name: Schinkel
origins.en: A schinkel is a short connecting stretch between two weteringen (drainage channels), in this case the Nieuwe Meer and the Overtoom. It is thought the connection owes its name to its shape: 'schinkel' is a synonym of 'schenkel', the lower leg between foot and knee. The quay was earlier called Visserkade by Nieuwer-Amstel. The municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel had named the streets Visserstraat, Alexanderstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 20 October 1882) and Willemsparkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 30 January 1883), but in 1896 they were changed because of confusion with names that already existed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Schippersgracht
origins.en: In this neighborhood, on the harbor side, the shipowners and sailors made up the majority of the population, which is why the canal and street got this name.

origins.name: Seranggracht
origins.en: A river on the Indonesian island of Java.

origins.name: Singel
origins.en: A singel is a waterway or a road along the outer edge of the city. In Amsterdam, the Singel (Amsterdammers say "het Singel") formed the city boundary in the second half of the fifteenth century, within which the walls with gates were built. At that time, that canal was called 't Singel or the Stedegracht (now Singel, Kloveniersburgwal and Geldersekade). The current Singel has retained the old name. However, in the seventeenth century, the city administration introduced the name Koningsgracht for it, but that name could not be maintained (see also Koningsplein).

origins.name: Singelgracht
origins.en: A singel is a waterway or road along the outer edge of the city. In Amsterdam, the Singel (Amsterdammers say "het Singel") formed the city boundary in the second half of the fifteenth century, within which walls with gates were built. At that time, that canal was called 't Singel or the Stedegracht (now Singel, Kloveniersburgwal and Geldersekade). The current Singel has retained the old name. However, in the seventeenth century, the city administration introduced the name Koningsgracht for it, but that name could not be maintained (see also Koningsplein).

origins.name: Sint Antoniesluis
origins.en: Named after the Sint Antoniesdijk, the sea wall located outside the city until the seventeenth century, which in turn took its name from the Sint Antoniesgasthuis or Leprosy House. The Sint Antoniesluis was part of the Zwanenburgwal before 1976.

origins.name: Sixhaven
origins.en: Jonkheer Willem Six (1859-1919), from 1898 to 1919 chairman of the Royal Sailing and Rowing Association, a great promoter of the construction of the marina in Amsterdam North. Two months before the completion of the harbor, he died, after which the harbor was named after him.

origins.name: Sloterparkbadsingel
origins.en: The name is derived from Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk, which, after being drained more than once, was dug out again into a lake for sand extraction. This water is the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Sloterplas
origins.en: The name is derived from Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk, which, after being drained more than once, was dug out again into a lake for sand extraction. This water is the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Slotervaart
origins.en: The name is derived from Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk, which, after being drained more than once, was dug out again into a lake for sand extraction. This water is the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Smallepadsgracht
origins.en: Ship, flat-bottomed of Frisian origin with leeboards and a gaff-rigged mast. Very suitable for shallow waters. The narrow ship was used to load goods and unload larger ships.

origins.name: Snellerwaardgracht
origins.en: Village on the Hollandse IJssel (Utrecht). The original spelling is Snelrewaard.

origins.name: Snoekjesgracht
origins.en: After a resident from the sixteenth century, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a pike depicted on the facade of his house. Originally, the name was therefore Snoeksgracht/steeg.

origins.name: Sonthaven
origins.en: The sea route between Denmark and Sweden, through which Amsterdam merchant ships have been sailing to the Baltic Sea since the fourteenth century. In 1658, the Dutch fleet under Jacob van Wassenaar defeated the Swedish fleet here at Obdam.

origins.name: Spiegelgracht
origins.en: Named after a well-known Amsterdam family, mostly manufacturers, who had soap factories. In 1564 Lourens Pieters 'in den Spiegel' lived in the corner building of the Oude Spiegelstraat on the Singel and in 1608 Pieter Lourens Spiegel. The intended house is still called Hertspiegel in 1738. The construction of the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat begins in 1665. Again, it is likely that a resident of the Spiegel family is the namesake.

origins.name: Spoorwegbassin
origins.en: The Spoorwegbassin is a harbor. A basin is a harbor basin.

origins.name: Stadiongracht
origins.en: Refers to the adjacent Olympic Stadium.

origins.name: Stoutenburggracht
origins.en: Village south of Hoevelaken (Utrecht). It is named after the former castle that belonged to Van Oldebarneveldt.

origins.name: Stralsundgracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

origins.name: Suezhaven
origins.en: Egyptian port town at the entrance - and namesake - of the Suez Canal opened in 1869.

origins.name: Syphonsluis
origins.en: Lock that works through the lever, a mechanism to pump water away.

origins.name: Texashaven
origins.en: Texas is one of the 50 states of the United States of America.

origins.name: Tolhuiskanaal
origins.en: Named after the Tolhuis, a roadside inn and once a popular spot. Construction dates back to 1662, when a highway was built here and a toll was established. In the garden, the famous concerts were held from 1887 to 1912 by the then popular seventh regiment under the leadership of organist Joh. Zaagmans.

origins.name: Twiske
origins.en: Twiske is the (West) Frisian word for 'between', it refers to the border ditch between the Waterland and the Zaanontginningen. The current recreation area near Oostzaan still bears this name.

origins.name: Uilenburgergracht
origins.en: The island of Uilenburg, which together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken came to lie within the city in 1593. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known with certainty, but it is likely that the name comes from the swampy land located here, which was called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was created by the merger of the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

origins.name: Uitdammer Die
origins.en: The hamlet of Uitdam, located on the IJsselmeerdijk north of the municipal boundary. The road came under the name Waterlandse zeedijk in Amsterdam when the former municipality of Ransdorp was abolished in 1921. (Uitdam = outside dam, outside dike.)

origins.name: Usselincxhaven
origins.en: Willem Usselincx (1567-1647), Flemish merchant and sailor, founder of the West Indian Company in 1621.

origins.name: Van Noordtgracht
origins.en: Olivier van Noordt (1558-1627), sailor and ship captain, who sailed around the world via the Strait of Magellan from 1598 to 1601. He later documented this journey.

origins.name: Vlothaven
origins.en: The nearby Vlothaven, dug in 1931, was originally shallow and part of the timber port intended for wooden barges. Around 1960, the port was deepened and adapted for sea vessels.

origins.name: Voorboezem
origins.en: A bay is an inland body of water without a fixed water level.

origins.name: Weersloot
origins.en: Common name for canals in North Holland.

origins.name: Weespertrekvaart
origins.en: The canal that connects Amsterdam with Weesp. A tow canal was used by barges. The tow canal was built in 1639, using several existing waterways.

origins.name: Westelijk Marktkanaal
origins.en: Was put into use in 1934 for freight transport from and to the Central Market Halls.

origins.name: Westerdok
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Westerdoksluis
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Westerkanaal
origins.en: The canal is located on the west side of the city. This is probably the reason for the naming.

origins.name: Westerkanaalschutsluis
origins.en: This bascule bridge is named after the Westerkanaal, over which it lies, and because it is located in the western part of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Westertoegang
origins.en: The water that forms the western access to the IJ.

origins.name: Westhaven
origins.en: This harbor, dug about half in 1937, was initially called Fordhaven, but soon gained the unofficial name Westhaven. After the harbor was extended by more than a kilometer to its current length in 1961, the name was also officially established, along with that of other harbors. The later built road therefore bore the name earlier than the harbor.

origins.name: Westlandgracht
origins.en: The area west of Delft, an internationally known horticultural area.

origins.name: Weteringpoort
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the Weteringpoort, which stood nearby here from 1688 to 1841. The name recalls the Wetering, which used to enter the city from Kalfjeslaan here and flowed into the Spui. The current Boerenwetering is still a remnant here.

origins.name: Wismargracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

origins.name: Wittenburgervaart
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

origins.name: Zanzibarhaven
origins.en: East African island in the Indian Ocean, which had several colonizers. Here, in 1818, under the rule of the Sultan of Oman, the Dutch monopoly on cloves was broken. Later it became British, and since 1964 it has been part of Tanzania.

origins.name: Zijkanaal I
origins.en: One of the ten side canals A to K. Was put into use in 1876 at the same time as the North Sea Canal.

origins.name: Zouthaven
origins.en: In the past, this location was the Zouthaven for the city.

origins.name: Zoutkeetsgracht
origins.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, on both sides of this canal stood the zoutketen (salt sheds), warehouses where coarse salt was processed for household use.

origins.name: Zuider Amstelkanaal
origins.en: The southern part of the Amstelkanaal. Refers to the water the Amstel.

origins.name: Zwanenburgwal
origins.en: Shortly after the land (on which the street and quay were laid out) was brought within the city just before 1600, there is talk of a house 'where the sign of Swanenburg hangs', on the corner of Zwanenburgwal. This will therefore probably have been the name giver. Swanenburg was already a more common name at that time. Gerrit Barents Swanenburgh, for example, built the Muiderpoort, Weesperpoort and Utrechtsepoort in the seventeenth century. By council decision in 1976, a part of the Zwanenburgwal was renamed Sint Antoniesluis. In order to build the Stopera, the Zwanenburgerstraat with adjacent buildings was demolished.
